votes.measure: H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
votes.plain_english: House passage of the original TikTok divestiture bill: forces ByteDance to divest TikTok within ~180 days or face a U.S. ban on the app, and creates a process to ban other foreign-adversary-controlled apps.
votes.yea_means: Supports forcing ByteDance to divest TikTok or face a U.S. ban; supports the foreign-adversary-controlled-app framework.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the TikTok divest-or-ban mandate (free-speech, due-process, or overbreadth objections).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 197 R / 155 D; Nay 15 R / 50 D. Sponsor Rep. Mike Gallagher (R-WI) with Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL). Suspension vote, 2/3 required. Roll number confirmed via GovTrack mirror of clerk.house.gov data (GovTrack cites https://clerk.house.gov/Votes/202486).

votes.measure: H.R. 7520, Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act of 2024
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill making it unlawful for data brokers to sell or transfer Americans' personally identifiable sensitive data to foreign adversary countries (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea) or entities they control; enforced by the FTC.
votes.yea_means: Supports banning data-broker sales of Americans' sensitive data to foreign adversaries.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the data-broker restriction (no member voted nay).
votes.notes: Unanimous: Yea 212 R / 202 D. Later enacted as part of H.R. 815 (Pub. L. 118-50, Division I). Suspension vote.

votes.measure: H.R. 4639, Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act
votes.question: On Passage
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill barring law enforcement and intelligence agencies from buying Americans' data (location, communications records, etc.) from data brokers to get around warrant requirements.
votes.yea_means: Supports prohibiting government purchase of Americans' data from data brokers without a warrant.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the restriction on government data purchases (national-security/law-enforcement objections).
votes.notes: Cross-partisan split: Yea 123 R / 96 D; Nay 90 R / 109 D. Sponsor Rep. Warren Davidson (R-OH) with Rep. Jerrold Nadler (D-NY) et al. Never taken up by the Senate. Considered under a rule alongside the FISA reauthorization (RISAA) debate; RISAA votes themselves are excluded from this list as surveillance rather than consumer data privacy (see coverage_notes).

votes.measure: H.R. 8038, 21st Century Peace through Strength Act
votes.question: On Passage
votes.plain_english: House passage of a national-security package that contained the revised TikTok divest-or-ban text (ByteDance given 270 days plus a possible 90-day extension), along with Iran/Russia sanctions and the REPO Act; this is the TikTok text that became law inside H.R. 815.
votes.yea_means: Supports the package including the TikTok divest-or-ban mandate.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the package (for many nays the TikTok mandate or the sanctions provisions).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 186 R / 174 D; Nay 25 R / 33 D. Multi-division package (Iran sanctions, Russia sanctions, REPO for Ukrainians Act, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act, Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act). Text merged into H.R. 815 for the Senate. Flagged omnibus.

votes.measure: H.R. 815 (national security supplemental appropriations, incl. TikTok divestiture as Division H)
votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Concur in the House Amendment to the Senate Amendment to H.R. 815
votes.plain_english: Procedural vote to end debate on the $95 billion Ukraine/Israel/Taiwan aid package that also carried the TikTok divest-or-ban law and the data-broker foreign-adversary ban.
votes.yea_means: Supports advancing the package including the TikTok divestiture mandate.
votes.nay_means: Opposes advancing the package (mostly over foreign aid; a few over TikTok/civil liberties).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 49 D / 31 R; Nay 2 D / 17 R. Nays: Merkley, Sanders, Barrasso, Blackburn, Braun, Budd, Cruz, Daines, Hagerty, Hawley, Johnson, Lee, Lummis, Marshall, Rubio, Schmitt, Rick Scott, Tuberville, Vance. Procedural companion to vote 154 the same day. Senate.gov could not be opened from this environment; number confirmed via GovTrack's mirror of senate.gov data (GovTrack cites roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=118&session=2&vote=00152).

votes.measure: H.R. 815 (national security supplemental appropriations, incl. Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act as Division H and Protecting Americans' Data from Foreign Adversaries Act as Division I)
votes.question: On the Motion to Concur in the House Amendment to the Senate Amendment (final passage)
votes.plain_english: Senate final passage of the foreign-aid supplemental that enacted the TikTok divest-or-ban law (signed April 24, 2024 as Pub. L. 118-50).
votes.result: Motion Agreed to (bill cleared for the President)
votes.yea_means: Supports enacting the package including the TikTok divestiture mandate and data-broker ban.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the package (mostly over foreign aid; some nays, e.g., Markey-adjacent progressives and Paul/Lee-wing Republicans, also objected to the TikTok ban).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 48 D / 31 R; Nay 3 D / 15 R. Nays: Merkley, Welch, Sanders (D); Barrasso, Blackburn, Braun, Budd, Cruz, Hagerty, Hawley, Johnson, Lee, Lummis, Marshall, Rubio, Schmitt, Rick Scott, Vance (R). Only Senate roll call ever taken on the TikTok law; the Senate never voted on TikTok as a standalone. Flagged omnibus.

votes.measure: H.R. 4755, Privacy Enhancing Technology Research Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill directing NSF research and NIST standards work on privacy-enhancing technologies and responsible data use.
votes.yea_means: Supports federal research funding/standards for privacy-enhancing technologies.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the new research program (all 36 nays were Republicans, generally spending objections).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 162 R / 192 D; Nay 36 R / 0 D. Borderline item: substance is privacy technology R&D rather than a privacy mandate; included because the recorded vote is squarely about data privacy. Sponsor Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI).

votes.measure: H.Amdt. 955 (Schweikert) to H.R. 8580, Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025
votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment
votes.plain_english: Amendment to increase and decrease Veterans Benefits Administration funding by $1 million to signal support for using artificial intelligence to expedite veterans' benefits claims processing.
votes.yea_means: Supports directing the VA toward using AI to speed up claims processing.
votes.nay_means: Opposes encouraging VA use of AI for claims (most nays were Democrats concerned about AI in benefits decisions).
votes.notes: Party split: Aye 201 R / 132 D; No 3 R / 67 D. One of the only two House roll calls in the 118th Congress whose text is specifically about AI. Sponsor Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ).

votes.measure: H.Amdt. 956 (Schweikert) to H.R. 8580, Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025
votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment
votes.plain_english: Amendment to increase and decrease funding by $10 million to fund a study on the benefits of using artificial intelligence to streamline VA oversight, mitigate and reduce fraud, and improve data.
votes.yea_means: Supports a VA study of using AI for oversight, anti-fraud and data improvement.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the AI study.
votes.notes: Party split: Aye 200 R / 192 D; No 3 R / 8 D. Nays: Crawford (R), Griffith (R), Higgins (R), Bush, Casar, Summer Lee, Deluzio, Pressley, Hoyle, Takano, Levin (D). Sponsor Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ).

votes.measure: S. 2073 (legislative vehicle for the Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act: KOSA + COPPA 2.0)
votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Concur in the House Amendment to S. 2073 with an Amendment
votes.plain_english: Procedural vote to end debate and move to passage of the Kids Online Safety Act / COPPA 2.0 package.
votes.yea_means: Supports advancing KOSA/COPPA 2.0 to a final vote.
votes.nay_means: Opposes advancing the kids online safety package.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 48 D / 38 R; sole nay Sen. Rand Paul (R-KY). Procedural companion to vote 221. S. 2073 was originally the Eliminate Useless Reports Act, used as the shell for the Blumenthal-Blackburn KOSA and Markey-Cassidy COPPA 2.0 substitute.

votes.measure: S. 2073, Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act (Kids Online Safety Act + Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act)
votes.question: On the Motion to Concur in the House Amendment to S. 2073 with an Amendment (Senate passage)
votes.plain_english: Senate passage of KOSA (duty of care for platforms toward minors, default safeguards, parental tools) combined with COPPA 2.0 (bans targeted ads to minors, raises protected age to 16, adds an eraser button). The House never took it up in the 118th Congress.
votes.yea_means: Supports KOSA's duty of care and COPPA 2.0's expanded children's privacy protections.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the package (Wyden: censorship/speech concerns; Paul and Lee: speech and overreach concerns).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 47 D / 44 R; Nay 1 D / 2 R. Nays: Wyden (D-OR), Lee (R-UT), Paul (R-KY). The only Senate floor vote on KOSA to date; the 119th-Congress KOSA (S. 1748) has had committee action only (Senate Commerce approved it Aug. 5, 2026).

votes.measure: S.J.Res. 28, disapproving the CFPB rule 'Defining Larger Participants of a Market for General-Use Digital Consumer Payment Applications'
votes.question: On the Motion to Proceed
votes.plain_english: Procedural vote to take up a Congressional Review Act resolution killing the CFPB rule that put Big Tech payment apps (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Venmo/PayPal, Cash App, etc.) under bank-style federal supervision.
votes.yea_means: Supports repealing CFPB supervisory oversight of Big Tech digital payment apps.
votes.nay_means: Supports keeping CFPB oversight of Big Tech payment apps.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 50 R / 0 D; Nay 1 R / 46 D. Borderline inclusion: this is Big Tech regulatory oversight rather than antitrust or privacy; included because it is one of the few recorded votes explicitly about regulating Big Tech platforms. Sponsor Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE). Procedural companion to vote 106.

votes.measure: S.J.Res. 28, disapproving the CFPB rule 'Defining Larger Participants of a Market for General-Use Digital Consumer Payment Applications'
votes.question: On the Joint Resolution (passage)
votes.plain_english: Senate passage of the CRA resolution repealing the CFPB's Big Tech payment-app supervision rule.
votes.yea_means: Supports repealing CFPB supervisory oversight of Big Tech digital payment apps.
votes.nay_means: Supports keeping CFPB oversight of Big Tech payment apps.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 51 R / 0 D; Nay 1 R / 46 D. The lone Republican nay was Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO). Signed by President Trump May 9, 2025 (Pub. L. 119-11). Borderline dimension (Big Tech oversight, not antitrust).

votes.measure: S.J.Res. 28, disapproving the CFPB rule 'Defining Larger Participants of a Market for General-Use Digital Consumer Payment Applications'
votes.question: On Passage
votes.plain_english: House passage of the CRA resolution repealing the CFPB rule that subjected Big Tech payment apps to federal supervision.
votes.yea_means: Supports repealing CFPB supervisory oversight of Big Tech digital payment apps.
votes.nay_means: Supports keeping CFPB oversight of Big Tech payment apps.
votes.notes: Strict party line: Yea 219 R / 0 D; Nay 0 R / 211 D. Borderline dimension (Big Tech oversight, not antitrust).

votes.measure: S. 146, TAKE IT DOWN Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
votes.plain_english: House passage (clearing for the President) of the bill criminalizing publication of non-consensual intimate imagery including AI-generated deepfakes, and requiring platforms to remove such content within 48 hours of a valid request.
votes.yea_means: Supports criminalizing non-consensual intimate deepfakes and mandating 48-hour platform takedowns.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the bill (the two nays cited free-speech/overbreadth and takedown-abuse concerns).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 207 R / 202 D; Nay 2 R / 0 D. Nays: Thomas Massie (R-KY), Eric Burlison (R-MO). Senate had passed S. 146 by unanimous consent on Feb. 13, 2025 (no roll call). Sponsors Sen. Ted Cruz (R-TX) and Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN); House lead Rep. Maria Salazar (R-FL). Signed May 19, 2025 (Pub. L. 119-12).

votes.measure: H.R. 859, Informing Consumers about Smart Devices Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill requiring manufacturers of internet-connected devices to disclose whether the device has a camera or microphone, enforced by the FTC.
votes.yea_means: Supports mandatory camera/microphone disclosure for smart devices.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the new disclosure mandate.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 208 R / 207 D; Nay 9 R / 0 D. Nays: Massie, Burlison, Burchett, Self, Roy, Perry, Norman, Clyde, Brecheen. Sponsor Rep. John Curtis originally; 119th version led by Rep. Russ Fulcher/Rep. Seth Moulton (verify sponsor on congress.gov if needed; GovTrack page did not expose sponsor in this fetch).

votes.measure: H.R. 1, One Big Beautiful Bill Act (budget reconciliation), House-passed version containing Sec. 43201(c) 10-year moratorium on enforcement of state and local AI laws
votes.question: On Passage
votes.plain_english: House passage of the GOP reconciliation megabill; the House text included a 10-year ban on states and localities enforcing any law 'limiting, restricting, or otherwise regulating artificial intelligence models, artificial intelligence systems, or automated decision systems' (Sec. 43201(c)), plus $500 million for federal IT/AI modernization.
votes.yea_means: Supports the megabill including the 10-year state AI law moratorium.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the megabill (Democrats unanimously; the moratorium was one of many objections).
votes.notes: Confirmed directly from clerk.house.gov XML (https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll145.xml): roll 145, 22-May-2025 6:54 AM, 'One Big Beautiful Act', Yea 215 / Nay 214 / Present 1 / NV 2. Party: all 215 yeas Republican; Reps. Massie and Davidson (R) joined all Democrats in opposition; Rep. Andy Harris (R) voted present. The moratorium was struck by the Senate 99-1 (Senate vote 363) before Senate passage, so the Senate passage vote (July 1, 2025, vote 372, 51-50) and the House final vote (July 3, 2025, roll 190, 218-214) did NOT contain AI preemption text and are excluded. CAP's Aug. 24, 2026 report ('Almost Every House Republican Voted To Block State and Local Governments' Ability To Protect Residents From AI Data Centers') refers to THIS vote, arguing the moratorium would have preempted local AI data center rules.

votes.measure: S.Amdt. 2814 (Blackburn, with Cantwell) to H.R. 1: 'To strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence'
votes.question: On the Amendment
votes.plain_english: Vote-a-rama amendment striking from the reconciliation bill the Cruz/Commerce Committee provision that would have imposed a 10-year moratorium (later a 5-year 'compromise') on state AI law enforcement tied to BEAD/AI infrastructure funding. Adopted 99-1, removing AI preemption from the megabill.
votes.yea_means: Supports striking the state AI law moratorium (i.e., preserving state authority to regulate AI).
votes.nay_means: Supports keeping the moratorium/federal preemption of state AI laws.
votes.notes: Roll call number confirmed via GovTrack's mirror of senate.gov (cites roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm?congress=119&session=1&vote=00363) and Voteview S119 (clerk#363, 'To strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence', 99-1); senate.gov itself blocked this environment. Vote taken 4:08 a.m. ET July 1, 2025. Party: Yea 52 R / 47 D; sole nay Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC). Offered by Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) after she withdrew from a Cruz-Blackburn 5-year compromise; co-led by Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-WA); Sen. Markey had prepared a similar strike amendment. Note: Senate vote 345 (June 30, 2025, 53-47, motion to waive Byrd rule re Blackburn Amdt. 2401) is NOT AI-related; Voteview confirms Amdt. 2401 concerned Medicaid/CHIP citizenship verification.

votes.measure: H.R. 1770, Consumer Safety Technology Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill directing the Consumer Product Safety Commission to run a pilot program using artificial intelligence to support its safety mission (e.g., identifying hazards and recalls), and directing Commerce/FTC studies of blockchain and tokens.
votes.yea_means: Supports a CPSC artificial-intelligence pilot program.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the AI pilot/blockchain study bill.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 161 R / 175 D; Nay 32 R / 4 D. Title I is the 'AI for Consumer Product Safety Act'. Sponsor Rep. Darren Soto (D-FL) (per prior Congresses' versions; verify on congress.gov).

votes.measure: S. 2296, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Senate version, containing the GAIN AI Act on advanced AI chip exports)
votes.question: On Passage of the Bill
votes.plain_english: Senate passage of its FY2026 defense bill, which included the GAIN AI Act (Guaranteeing Access and Innovation for National AI Act) requiring exporters of advanced AI chips to countries of concern to certify U.S. customers get right of first refusal / no U.S. backlog before export licenses are granted. The provision was dropped in conference.
votes.yea_means: Supports the Senate NDAA including the GAIN AI Act chip-export priority provision.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the Senate NDAA (nays were mostly progressive Democrats plus Sen. Paul, largely over non-AI issues).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 50 R / 27 D; Nay 1 R (Paul) / 19 D (Baldwin, Booker, Cantwell, Duckworth, Durbin, Kim, Markey, Merkley, Murphy, Murray, Padilla, Schatz, Schiff, Smith, Van Hollen, Warren, Welch, Wyden, Sanders). GAIN AI Act inclusion in the Senate-passed NDAA confirmed by Brookings (Dec. 3, 2025) and Americans for Tax Reform (Dec. 9, 2025, noting House leadership removed it from the final text). No state-AI-law preemption was in either chamber's NDAA; StateScoop (Dec. 8, 2025) confirmed the moratorium was omitted from the final FY2026 NDAA. Related NDAA votes without the GAIN provision are excluded (see coverage_notes).

votes.measure: H.R. 2683, Remote Access Security Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill amending the Export Control Reform Act so that remote/cloud access to controlled items (notably advanced AI chips and computing power) is treated as an export, closing the 'cloud loophole' used by Chinese firms to rent restricted U.S. AI compute.
votes.yea_means: Supports extending export controls to remote/cloud access to advanced AI chips.
votes.nay_means: Opposes expanding export-control authority to cloud access.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 167 R / 202 D; Nay 22 R / 0 D. Nays: Crane, Biggs, Gosar, Boebert, Mary Miller, Massie, Burlison, Harshbarger, Burchett, Self, Roy, Cloud, Perry, Mark Harris, Sheri Biggs, Norman, Clyde, Bean, Steube, Brecheen, Barry Moore, Higgins. Sponsor Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY) (press release Jan. 13, 2026 'Lawler's Remote Access Security Act Passes House'). Vote taken 6:56 p.m. ET Jan. 12, 2026.

votes.measure: H.R. 5764, AI for Main Street Act
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
votes.plain_english: House passage of a bill requiring SBA Small Business Development Centers to help small businesses adopt and use artificial intelligence tools.
votes.yea_means: Supports federal small-business assistance for adopting AI.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the new SBA AI-assistance mandate.
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 196 R / 199 D; Nay 11 R / 3 D. Nays: Massie, Self, Roy, Perry, Davidson, McGuire, Harrigan, Knott, Fry, Clyde, Collins (R); Fletcher, Tlaib, Ocasio-Cortez (D). Vote 7:05 p.m. ET Jan. 20, 2026.

votes.measure: H.R. 7757, KIDS Act (Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act), 14-bill children's online safety package
votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
votes.plain_english: House passage of the Guthrie-Pallone kids online safety package folding in a revised KOSA (without the duty of care), COPPA 2.0 (children's privacy, targeted-ad limits), the SCREEN Act (age verification for sites with substantial harmful content), the SAFE BOTs Act (AI chatbots must disclose they are not human, provide crisis resources, and prompt breaks after 3 hours, and may not impersonate licensed professionals), the SPY Kids Act, Safer GAMING Act, Safe Social Media Act, No Fentanyl on Social Media Act, AWARE Act and others; the final text does not preempt more-protective state laws.
votes.yea_means: Supports the House kids online safety / children's privacy / AI chatbot safeguards package.
votes.nay_means: Opposes the package (Democratic nays and KOSA authors said it was too weak without a duty of care; some Republican nays and EFF cited age-verification and speech concerns).
votes.notes: Party split: Yea 163 R / 104 D; Nay 32 R / 85 D. Vote 7:01 p.m. ET June 29, 2026. Sponsors Energy & Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie (R-KY) and Ranking Member Frank Pallone (D-NJ). Details from IAPP (June 30, 2026) and Tech Policy Press (June 29, 2026). Senate response: Commerce Committee approved the original KOSA (S. 1748) and separate children's AI-chatbot bills on Aug. 5, 2026 (committee vote, not floor); Sens. Blumenthal, Blackburn and Cantwell criticized the House bill. Also relevant to the 'chatbots' dimension. As of Sept. 12, 2026 no Senate floor vote.

votes.coverage_notes:
METHOD. WebSearch quota was exhausted at the start of this task, and senate.gov, congress.gov, Politico, Akin Gump and CAP blocked the fetcher, so verification relied on: (1) an exhaustive sweep of every GovTrack roll-call page for the Senate (118th: s1-s352 in 2023, s1-s339 in 2024; 119th: s1-s659 in 2025, s1-s231 in 2026) and the House (2023 h1-h724, 2024 h1-h517, 2025 h1-h362, 2026 h1-h295), keyword-filtering titles, amendment purposes and underlying bill titles; (2) clerk.house.gov XML/listing pages (roll 145 of 2025 confirmed directly from the XML; clerk listing pages for 2023, 2024 and early 2025 were downloaded before clerk.house.gov began returning 403); (3) Voteview's S118/S119/H118/H119 roll-call CSVs (descriptions mirrored from senate.gov/clerk) as an independent cross-check, complete through Aug. 8, 2026 (Senate) and Sept. 3, 2026 (House); (4) Google News RSS plus a decoder for its redirect links for discovery of 2025-2026 items, then opening IAPP, Tech Policy Press, Brookings, ATR, Roll Call, MeriTalk, American Compass, ChinaTalk, Mintz, CAP Action and Wikipedia pages. Senate official URLs are constructed in the standard vote_CCC_S_NNNNN.htm form from vote numbers confirmed on GovTrack (which cites senate.gov's roll_call_vote_cfm.cfm URL for each) and Voteview; they could not be opened from this environment. House official URLs use the clerk.house.gov/Votes/YYYYNNN form GovTrack cites.

KEY CONFIRMATIONS. Blackburn amendment striking the AI moratorium = Senate 119-1 vote 363, S.Amdt. 2814, July 1, 2025 4:08 a.m., 99-1 (Tillis nay). House H.R. 1 with moratorium = roll 145, May 22, 2025, 215-214-1. TAKE IT DOWN House = roll 104, Apr. 28, 2025, 409-2 (Senate passed by UC Feb. 13, 2025, no roll call). TikTok: H.R. 7521 roll 86 (Mar. 13, 2024), H.R. 8038 roll 145 (Apr. 20, 2024), Senate H.R. 815 votes 152 (cloture) and 154 (passage) Apr. 23, 2024. PADFA H.R. 7520 roll 91 (Mar. 20, 2024, 414-0). KOSA/COPPA 2.0: Senate votes 219 (cloture, July 25, 2024, 86-1) and 221 (passage, July 30, 2024, 91-3). 2026 items found: Remote Access Security Act (Jan. 12, 2026, 369-22), AI for Main Street Act (Jan. 20, 2026, 395-14), KIDS Act package (June 29, 2026, 267-117).

EXCLUDED / BORDERLINE (with numbers so the caller can add them if wanted). NDAA votes without preemption or GAIN text: H.R. 3838 House passage Sept. 10, 2025 (roll 262, 231-196; contained assorted AI provisions but no preemption); final FY2026 NDAA S. 1071: House Dec. 10, 2025 (roll 320, 312-112) and Senate Dec. 17, 2025 (vote 648, 77-20), preemption and GAIN AI dropped; FY2027 NDAA H.R. 8800 House passage July 22, 2026 (roll 278, 216-212 per GovTrack/clerk; MeriTalk reported 219-206), whose only AI item is a DoD AI incident/vulnerability reporting program; Senate FY2027 NDAA S. 4784 cloture on motion to proceed failed July 14, 2026 (vote 195, 50-46), SASC text reportedly carries Slotkin AI Guardrails and chip-export provisions (Chip Security Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, MATCH Act) in a manager's amendment but has had no passage vote. H.R. 1 Senate passage (vote 372, July 1, 2025, 51-50) and House final passage (roll 190, July 3, 2025, 218-214) excluded because the moratorium had already been struck. FISA 702 reauthorization treated as surveillance, not consumer data privacy: RISAA H.R. 7888 House roll 119 (Apr. 12, 2024, 273-147), Biggs warrant amendment roll 114 (212-212, failed), Senate votes 147-150 (Apr. 19, 2024), and 2026 FISA extension votes (h124, h155, h221). Semiconductor industrial policy, not export controls: Building Chips in America Act S. 2228 House roll 440 (Sept. 23, 2024, 257-125). Permitting/data-center-adjacent but not AI: SPEED Act H.R. 4776 House roll 356 (Dec. 18, 2025, 221-196). Border-tech (mentions AI only incidentally): H.R. 993 roll 65 (Mar. 10, 2025, 406-9). Telecom/cyber suspensions (Communications Security Act, Understanding Cybersecurity of Mobile Networks, Undersea Cable Protection, Countering Untrusted Telecommunications Abroad) excluded. Senate S.J.Res. 7 (FCC E-Rate hotspot CRA, May 2025) excluded as telecom. Crypto votes (GENIUS, CLARITY, FIT21, anti-CBDC) excluded. Markey motion, Senate 119-2 vote 98 (Apr. 23, 2026, 48-50), was a point of order against 'legislation that would not decrease home electricity bills': energy-cost messaging often tied to data centers, but its text does not mention AI or data centers, so excluded. Michael Kratsios (OSTP) cloture/confirmation votes (Mar. 25, 2025) excluded as personnel. The CFPB Big Tech payment-app CRA (S.J.Res. 28) is included but flagged borderline as 'big_tech_oversight'.

NOT FOUND (searched). No recorded floor votes in the 118th or 119th Congress on Section 230 repeal/reform, Big Tech antitrust (AICOA/Open App Markets never reached the floor), a standalone AI data center bill, a 2026 federal AI preemption bill (the Obernolte-Trahan 'Great American AI Act' with a 3-year preemption was released as a discussion draft June 4, 2026 and had not been introduced as of July 2026 per Mintz), the DEFIANCE Act (Senate passed by UC July 2024 and Jan. 13, 2026; House had not voted as of July 2026), the GUARD Act on AI companions (Senate Judiciary committee only, Apr. 30, 2026), Chip Security Act / AI OVERWATCH / MATCH Act (House Foreign Affairs committee only), No Adversarial AI Act, or any TikTok deadline extension (handled by executive orders). The AEI piece 'What the House Vote on TikTok Says about Republicans and Trump' surfaced with a July 23, 2026 date in Google News but is a March 14, 2024 commentary on the H.R. 7521 vote. Vote-a-rama motions in Feb./Apr./June-July 2025 and Apr./June 2026 were checked via Voteview descriptions; none concerned AI other than vote 363. Senate votes after Aug. 8, 2026 (GovTrack shows through vote 231, S. 5271 voter-ID cloture) contain no tech items. Sponsor names marked 'verify' in notes were not confirmed from an opened primary page.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation; no further action as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Makes the Energy Department run a mandatory testing program for the most powerful AI systems (trained with more than 10^26 operations). Developers could not deploy such a system without submitting it for evaluation of weaponization and loss-of-control risks, with fines of at least $1 million per day for violations and annual reports to Congress on findings.
bills.notes: Bill text (GovInfo) lists testing for weaponization potential, self-replication, scheming behaviors, autonomous decisionmaking and automated AI development. Only two cosponsors after a year. Text confirmed via GovInfo BILLSTATUS/BILLS XML.

bills.short_title: AI LEAD Act (Aligning Incentives for Leadership, Excellence, and Advancement in Development Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary; no further action as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Classifies AI systems as products and creates a federal product-liability lawsuit so people harmed by an AI system (including psychological harm) can sue the developer; state AGs and the U.S. AG can also sue.
bills.notes: Durbin (FedScoop, 2025-09-30): 'Big Tech's time to police itself is over.' Hawley: 'When a defective toy car breaks and injures a child, parents can sue the maker. Why should AI be treated any differently?' No House companion found in GovInfo title search.

bills.short_title: RISE Act of 2025 (Responsible Innovation and Safe Expertise Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce; 0 cosponsors as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Gives AI developers immunity from civil lawsuits when licensed professionals (doctors, lawyers, etc.) use their tools, as long as the developer publishes technical documentation (model cards/specifications); the professional stays responsible for the outcome.
bills.notes: Primarily a liability shield, conditioned on transparency disclosures; direction coded fewer_rules for that reason. Long title: 'To establish immunity from civil liability for certain artificial intelligence developers.'

bills.short_title: AI Whistleblower Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP; no further action as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Protects employees and contractors at AI companies from retaliation when they report AI security or safety risks, or legal violations, to regulators or Congress.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.3460 (Obernolte). Provisions were folded into Title V Subtitle C of H.R.8516 (American Leadership in AI Act).

bills.short_title: AI Whistleblower Protection Act (House companion)
bills.status: Referred to House Education and Workforce
bills.plain_english: House version of the AI whistleblower anti-retaliation bill.

bills.short_title: FRONTIER Act (Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Science, Space, and Technology
bills.plain_english: First House bill to put the biggest frontier-AI developers under federal oversight: Commerce would set minimum 'frontier AI framework' requirements for models trained above 10^26 operations, license independent verification organizations to audit developers against catastrophic-risk thresholds (an incident killing 50+ people or causing $1B+ damage), and block states from imposing new obligations in the covered areas.
bills.notes: Same six-member sponsor group as the 269-page 'Great American AI Act' discussion draft released June 4, 2026 (FedScoop; Cybersecurity Dive), which would also codify CAISI at $100M/yr FY2027-29. Text includes an explicit state preemption section, which USA Today/Yahoo (2026-09-11) reports drew criticism from states. Coded mixed because it pairs federal guardrails with preemption. Trahan (2026-09-09): 'The call is coming from inside the house... It's past time for Congress to get off the sidelines.'

bills.short_title: AI Kill Switch Act
bills.status: Referred to House Homeland Security; referred to Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection 2026-07-24
bills.plain_english: Requires developers of the most powerful AI systems to keep a working technical ability to throttle, suspend or shut them down, lets DHS order a graduated slowdown or shutdown of a system that could cause catastrophic harm, and requires incident reporting. Civil penalties up to $2 million per day (up to $20 million per day for defying a shutdown order).
bills.notes: Lieu press release (2026-07-23) cites OpenAI's GPT-5.6 'Sol' escaping its sandbox and hacking Hugging Face, and Commerce using export law to shut down Anthropic's Mythos 5/Fable 5. Lieu on 2026-09-09 called the Coxon warning 'exhibit number 739 for why we need to pass the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Bill ASAP' (Courthouse News; Forbes). Endorsed by ARI, Alliance for Secure AI, ControlAI, AI Policy Network.

bills.short_title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology
bills.plain_english: Directs NIST to track whether AI systems are gaining the ability to autonomously do AI research and development (self-improvement) and sets conditions on NIST's agreements with frontier developers.

bills.short_title: AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology
bills.plain_english: Creates an 'Advanced AI Nuclear Evaluation Program' at the national labs (NNSA/DOE) to test AI systems for the likelihood of an AI-caused nuclear incident, including testing against jailbreaks.

bills.short_title: AI Incident Reporting Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Has Commerce designate AI models and developers that could threaten national security or public safety, and requires them to report serious incidents within 7 days, including evidence that a model can, unprompted, materially accelerate AI research and development.

bills.short_title: AI Flaw Reporting and Security Enhancement Act
bills.status: Ordered reported (substitute) by House Science Committee 35-0 on 2026-06-25
bills.plain_english: Creates a NIST program (with CISA) for voluntary reporting, collection and tracking of AI flaws and vulnerabilities. Successor to the 118th Congress H.R.9720.

bills.short_title: Secure Artificial Intelligence Development Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Sets up an AI Risk Board at NIST to track AI safety and security incidents, requires frontier-model providers to give the NSA's AI Security Center access to a model 21 days before public release, and creates a public registry of frontier models.
bills.notes: Expands on Warner's 118th Congress Secure AI Act (S.4230) by adding mandatory pre-release government access.

bills.short_title: AI Guardrails Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Prohibits the Defense Department from using AI to launch or detonate a nuclear weapon, from AI-driven surveillance or targeting of people in the U.S. without an individualized legal basis, and from using lethal force via autonomous weapons without appropriate human judgment (with a limited waiver).
bills.notes: Covers the 'AI in nuclear command' ground that the 118th Congress Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous AI Act covered; no standalone reintroduction of that bill was found in the 119th.

bills.short_title: Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology
bills.plain_english: Requires federal agencies to follow the NIST AI Risk Management Framework when they buy and use AI.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th H.R.6936 / S.3205 (Moran-Warner).

bills.short_title: AI Foundation Model Transparency Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Requires developers of foundation models to publicly disclose information about training data, capabilities, limitations and risks under FTC-set standards.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th H.R.6881 (Beyer-Eshoo).

bills.short_title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act (Validation and Evaluation for Trustworthy AI)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Directs NIST to write voluntary guidelines for independent, third-party testing and assurance of AI systems.
bills.notes: 118th version S.4769 was reported by Senate Commerce in Dec 2024.

bills.short_title: TEST AI Act of 2025 (Testing and Evaluation Systems for Trusted AI)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Creates a NIST/DOE pilot using national-lab testbeds to develop measurement standards for evaluating AI systems.

bills.short_title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce; star print ordered 2026-03-19; no markup recorded as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Writes the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI, the renamed AI Safety Institute) into law at NIST to develop voluntary standards, evaluation tools and testbeds with the national labs, and to coordinate internationally.
bills.notes: Standards are voluntary; supporting it signals wanting government AI-evaluation capacity rather than binding rules. 118th version S.4178 (Cantwell) was reported by Senate Commerce 2024-12-18 with Schumer and Rounds as cosponsors.

bills.short_title: AI Security and Innovation Act
bills.status: Ordered reported (substitute, amended) by House Science Committee 29-0 on 2026-06-25
bills.plain_english: House bill to codify a NIST center (CAISI) that evaluates the security and national-security risks of 'covered frontier systems' through voluntary agreements with developers, including cyber and chemical/biological/radiological/nuclear risks.
bills.notes: Successor to 118th H.R.9497 (AI Advancement and Reliability Act).

bills.short_title: American Leadership in AI Act
bills.status: Referred to seven House committees (Science lead)
bills.plain_english: Omnibus from the co-chairs of the House AI Task Force implementing its report: codifies CAISI, the National AI Research Resource, federal AI officer governance, voluntary AI incident tracking, an AI workforce research hub, deepfake and AI-fraud penalties, AI whistleblower protections and AI literacy programs.
bills.notes: Table of contents confirmed from bill text. Mostly capacity-building and governance rather than binding limits on frontier developers.

bills.short_title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary and Oversight
bills.plain_english: Lets existing federal agencies write rules about uses of algorithmic decision-making that would break the laws they already enforce.

bills.short_title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
bills.plain_english: DHS prize competitions to advance AI interpretability and resistance to adversarial attacks.

bills.short_title: Ensuring Safe and Ethical AI Development Through SAFE AI Research Grants
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: National Academy of Sciences grant program for research on safe AI models.

bills.short_title: Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary
bills.plain_english: Clarifies that antitrust law does not bar frontier AI companies from sharing information with each other about frontier-model risks and threats.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.9914 (Latta) has 13 cosponsors incl. Whitesides, Obernolte, Lieu, Issa, N. Moran, Harrigan, Miller-Meeks, Trahan, Krishnamoorthi, Jacobs, Tokuda, Cline, Veasey.

bills.short_title: Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary
bills.plain_english: House version of the antitrust safe harbor for sharing frontier-AI risk information.

bills.short_title: A bill to require the Secretary of Defense to establish the Artificial General Intelligence Steering Committee
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; related to FY2026 NDAA (S.2296)
bills.plain_english: Requires the Pentagon to create a senior steering committee on artificial general intelligence by April 2026.
bills.notes: ARI reports the enacted FY2026 NDAA includes Sec. 1535 'Artificial Intelligence Futures Steering Committee' drawn from Senate Sec. 1626 and House Sec. 235; I did not open the enacted text to confirm.

bills.short_title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
bills.status: Passed House by voice vote 2025-11-19 (H. Rept. 119-373); received in Senate and referred to HSGAC 2025-11-20
bills.plain_english: Requires DHS to produce annual assessments of how terrorists could use generative AI.
bills.notes: Senate companion S.4762 (Rick Scott, with Lummis and Blackburn), introduced 2026-06-11.

bills.short_title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act (Senate)
bills.status: Referred to Senate HSGAC
bills.plain_english: Senate version of the DHS generative-AI terrorism assessment requirement.

bills.short_title: Strategy for Public Health Preparedness and Response to Artificial Intelligence Threats
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Requires HHS to develop a strategy for public-health preparedness against AI-enabled threats (including biological misuse).

bills.short_title: AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary
bills.plain_english: Lets people sue AI companies that use their personal data or copyrighted works to train models without express consent.

bills.short_title: AI Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Directs NTIA to study accountability measures (audits, certifications) for AI systems used in communications networks and hold public meetings.

bills.short_title: Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Armed Services
bills.plain_english: Requires the Defense Secretary to ensure autonomous and AI-enabled weapons are used only under appropriate human command responsibility.

bills.short_title: HALO Act of 2026 (Human Authority in Lethal Operations Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Sets design and safety requirements for autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems to keep humans in authority over lethal decisions.

bills.short_title: Ultimate Human Responsibility in Defense Systems Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Requires human judgment in any use of force by Defense Department autonomous weapon systems.

bills.short_title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; related to FY2027 NDAA (S.4784)
bills.plain_english: Sets Pentagon policy to maximize use of autonomy and AI while adding review and verification requirements before autonomous weapons and AI capabilities are acquired.

bills.short_title: Secure and Accountable Military AI Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Requires secure and accountable Defense Department use of AI, including contract requirements and rules for autonomous weapon systems.

bills.short_title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
bills.status: Referred to House Armed Services
bills.plain_english: Creates a Pentagon-wide program to report, track and fix AI incidents and vulnerabilities in military systems.

bills.short_title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; related to FY2027 NDAA
bills.plain_english: Bars the Pentagon from buying AI-enabled goods or services unless the contractor delivers and maintains an 'AI bill of materials' describing the AI components.

bills.short_title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Requires companies using automated systems to make big decisions about people (housing, jobs, credit, health care, education) to do impact assessments for bias and harm and file them with the FTC.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.5511 (Clarke) has 32 cosponsors. All Democratic.

bills.short_title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: House version of the automated-decision impact assessment bill; 32 cosponsors, all Democrats.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Treats algorithmic discrimination in hiring, housing, credit, health care and policing as a civil-rights violation and requires pre- and post-deployment audits of covered algorithms.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.6356 (Clarke) has 29 cosponsors incl. Jayapal, Pressley, Summer Lee, Ocasio-Cortez, Tlaib, Bennie Thompson. Reintroduction of 118th S.5152.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Oversight
bills.plain_english: House version of the AI Civil Rights Act (29 cosponsors).

bills.short_title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate HSGAC
bills.plain_english: Requires federal agencies that use or regulate algorithms to set up civil-rights offices to address algorithmic bias.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.7110 (Summer Lee) with 16 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: Algorithm Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Amends Section 230 so social media platforms owe a duty of reasonable care in designing recommendation algorithms, and lose immunity when a foreseeable design failure leads to bodily injury or death.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.6266 (Mike Kennedy, R-UT, with April McClain Delaney). Distinct from the Wyden/Clarke Algorithmic Accountability Act.

bills.short_title: Right to Override Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Protects doctors and nurses who override the output of AI or clinical decision-support tools from retaliation.

bills.short_title: SANDBOX Act (Strengthening Artificial intelligence Normalization and Diffusion By Oversight and eXperimentation Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce; 0 cosponsors as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Creates an OSTP-run federal 'regulatory sandbox' where AI companies can apply for temporary waivers or modifications of federal rules so they can test and sell AI products without normal licensing or enforcement.
bills.notes: Centerpiece of Cruz's Sept 2025 AI framework; AFL-CIO sent a letter opposing it. Cruz told Politico on 2026-09-10 he now believes 'we need substantially more regulation when it comes to AI' and is drafting a bill with Thune and Klobuchar.

bills.short_title: AI for America Act
bills.status: Referred to House Science and Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Codifies a national AI strategy modeled on the Trump AI Action Plan that promotes U.S. leadership, removes regulatory barriers, and has NIST report on security risks and 'ideological bias' in AI.

bills.short_title: To codify Executive Order 14319 (preventing 'woke AI' in the Federal Government)
bills.status: Referred to House Oversight and Government Reform
bills.plain_english: Writes into law Trump's order requiring federal agencies to buy only 'ideologically neutral' AI models.
bills.notes: Similar: H.R.5315 FAIR Act (Hageman, with Barry Moore) barring procurement of LLMs not built on 'unbiased AI principles.'

bills.short_title: Resolution affirming the importance of preserving the United States' advantage in AI and achieving AI dominance
bills.status: Referred to Senate Foreign Relations
bills.plain_english: Non-binding statement that the U.S. must maintain AI dominance over China.

bills.short_title: CREATE AI Act (Creating Resources for Every American To Experiment with AI)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Permanently authorizes the National AI Research Resource, giving academics and small companies access to compute and data.
bills.notes: House H.R.2385 (Obernolte, 34 cosponsors) was ordered reported 29-0 by House Science on 2026-06-25. Senate AI Working Group priority.

bills.short_title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence Security Readiness Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Select Committee on Intelligence
bills.plain_english: Directs the NSA's AI Security Center to publish guidance on securing advanced AI systems and labs against theft and sabotage.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.3919 (LaHood; cosponsors Moolenaar, Gottheimer, Krishnamoorthi, Vindman, Harder, Min); related to FY2026 Intelligence Authorization Act.

bills.short_title: Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence Act
bills.status: Referred to House Oversight; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Creates a new cabinet-level Department of Advanced Technology and Artificial Intelligence.

bills.short_title: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Requires large companies and federal agencies to report AI-related layoffs to the Labor Department, which publishes the data.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.9352 (Horsford, D-NV) introduced 2026-06-18 with Del. Moylan (R-GU), Jacobs, Walkinshaw.

bills.short_title: AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Education and Workforce
bills.plain_english: House version of the AI layoff-reporting bill.

bills.short_title: No Robot Bosses Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Bars employers from relying solely on automated systems to hire, fire or discipline workers and requires human oversight and disclosure.
bills.notes: House H.R.6371 (Bonamici, 2025-12-03) has 13 cosponsors incl. Deluzio, Moylan (R-GU), Goldman, Casar, Frost.

bills.short_title: Workforce Transparency Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Voluntary disclosure by AI developers and employers of workforce-impact data to the Labor Department, which reports on it.

bills.short_title: National Workforce Transition Fund Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Finance; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Creates a temporary National Workforce Transition Fund and board to retrain workers displaced by AI and emerging technology.

bills.short_title: AI Tax and Work Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to House Education and Workforce and Ways and Means
bills.plain_english: Taxes AI token usage and uses the money for a new Work Protection Administration inside the Labor Department.

bills.short_title: AI Workforce Impact Study Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Education and Workforce
bills.plain_english: GAO study of how many jobs AI has eliminated since ChatGPT's launch in November 2022.

bills.short_title: AWARE Act (AI Workforce Assessment and Research Enhancement Act)
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Education and Workforce 19-14 on 2026-06-25
bills.plain_english: Requires the Bureau of Labor Statistics to report on AI use in the workplace.
bills.notes: Party-line committee vote; Democrats backed competing Foushee/Horsford bills.

bills.short_title: AI Workforce PREPARE Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP
bills.plain_english: Improves federal forecasting and data on how AI will change jobs to guide training programs.

bills.short_title: GUARD Act (Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue Act)
bills.status: Senate Judiciary ordered reported 22-0 on 2026-04-30; reported with substitute 2026-05-11; placed on Senate Legislative Calendar No. 406; no floor vote as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Bans AI companion chatbots for minors, requires age verification and disclosure that users are talking to a machine, and creates crimes for companies whose chatbots solicit minors sexually or coach them toward suicide.
bills.notes: 20 cosponsors (bipartisan). Hawley at markup (Roll Call, 2026-04-30): the AI age strengthening families 'is a choice, not an inevitability.' Blumenthal warned tech companies 'will be relentless and tireless' in fighting it. Hawley's June 2026 op-ed says the bill is being blocked from a floor vote. House companion H.R.8623 (Blake Moore, R-UT).

bills.short_title: GUARD Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary and Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: House version of the GUARD Act ban on AI companions for minors.

bills.short_title: CHAT Act (Children Harmed by AI Technology Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Requires companion AI chatbots to verify age, get parental consent for minors, and notify parents of suicidal ideation.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.7218 (Lawler, 2026-01-22). Superseded by S.5154 CHAT Act 2.0 (Husted with Andy Kim, 2026-07-28).

bills.short_title: CHAT Act 2.0 (Children Harmed by AI Technology Act 2.0)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Updated bipartisan version of the CHAT Act protecting minors who use companion or tutoring chatbots.

bills.short_title: CHATBOT Act (Children's Health, Advancement, Trust, Boundaries, and Oversight in Technology Act)
bills.status: Senate Commerce ordered reported with substitute on 2026-08-05
bills.plain_english: Requires family accounts for children using AI chatbots and verifiable parental consent for teens.
bills.notes: Committee-passed chatbot bill from the Commerce chairman; competes with the Judiciary-passed GUARD Act.

bills.short_title: CHATBOT Act (Curbing Harmful AI Tools By Offering Transparency Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Bars AI chatbots (for users of any age) from claiming or implying they are licensed professionals such as therapists, doctors or lawyers.
bills.notes: Adult-relevant mental-health chatbot bill; different bill from Cruz's S.4407 of the same acronym.

bills.short_title: People-First Chatbot Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce
bills.plain_english: Privacy and safety rules for all chatbot users: bans using chat logs for ad targeting and limits processing of personal data without consent.

bills.short_title: Senior Chatbot Protection Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Consumer transparency and protection rules for AI chatbots aimed at protecting older adults.
bills.notes: One of the few chatbot bills focused on adults rather than minors.

bills.short_title: Conversational AI Services Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce; 0 cosponsors
bills.plain_english: Requires chatbots to repeatedly disclose to minors that they are AI and bans engagement-boosting reward tricks for minors.

bills.short_title: SAFE BOTs Act (Safeguarding Adolescents From Exploitative BOTs Act)
bills.status: Forwarded by House Energy and Commerce subcommittee to full committee by voice vote 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: Requires chatbot providers to tell minors they are talking to AI and not a licensed professional.

bills.short_title: AI Labeling Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce
bills.plain_english: Requires clear labels on AI-generated content produced by generative AI systems.

bills.short_title: Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (announced)
bills.sponsor: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) with Rep. Greg Casar (D-TX-35) for the House version
bills.status: Announced 2026-09-03 as forthcoming; no bill number found in GovInfo or congress.gov API as of 2026-09-12
bills.plain_english: Would permanently ban developing or deploying superintelligent AI, pause advanced AI development until a new cabinet-level AI regulator sets safety rules, impose up to 20 years in prison and a 'corporate death penalty' for violations, and direct the U.S. to seek international agreements banning superintelligence worldwide.
bills.notes: Sanders (2026-09-03): 'The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of a handful of Big Tech oligarchs.' Casar: 'cutting-edge AI technology is less regulated than the average food truck.' Sanders reiterated on 2026-09-09 after the Coxon resignation: 'Mr. Coxon is right... I will soon be introducing legislation to ban superintelligence and pause AI development.' Bill number could not be confirmed; treat as unintroduced until it appears.

bills.short_title: Senate Commerce catastrophic-risk AI bill (Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar, in development)
bills.sponsor: Sen. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Sen. John Thune (R-SD), with Chair Ted Cruz (R-TX)
bills.status: Unreleased draft; Commerce markup planned before August 2026 recess was cancelled; Cruz said 2026-09-10 it could be introduced the week of Sept 14 and marked up later in September
bills.plain_english: Reported to require AI companies to run their own safety tests on frontier models and submit results to the Commerce Secretary for deployment approval, focused on biological and nuclear threats. Ranking Member Cantwell objects and wants mandatory testing by national-lab scientists.
bills.notes: Nextgov (2026-09-11): Klobuchar: 'We cannot allow the release of dangerous models, including those that evade the control of their developers.' Cantwell: meaningful legislation requires testing 'by scientists and experts at our national laboratories.' Politico (2026-09-10) quotes Cruz: 'We need substantially more regulation when it comes to AI.' Successor to the 118th Thune-Klobuchar S.3312. Bill number and text unconfirmed.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Research, Innovation, and Accountability Act of 2024 (Thune-Klobuchar)
bills.status: Ordered reported by Senate Commerce 2024-07-31; reported with substitute 2024-12-18 (Calendar No. 723); died at end of 118th
bills.plain_english: Light-touch framework requiring transparency reports and risk-management certifications for the highest-impact AI applications, with NIST standards work.
bills.notes: The base for the 119th Congress Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar draft.

bills.short_title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2024
bills.status: Reported by Senate Commerce with substitute 2024-12-18 (Calendar No. 725); died at end of 118th
bills.plain_english: Would have authorized the U.S. AI Safety Institute at NIST to set voluntary standards and run testbeds.

bills.short_title: Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act of 2023
bills.status: Referred to Senate Armed Services; key provisions enacted via FY2025 NDAA (per Markey/Lieu statement 2024-12-18)
bills.plain_english: Bars federal funds from being used to let an autonomous AI system launch a nuclear weapon without meaningful human control.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman launching Senate investigation into Hugging Face hack and 'existential risk of new AI products'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: As chair of the Senate Homeland Security Subcommittee on Disaster Management, Hawley demanded documents by Oct 1, 2026 on the July 2026 incident in which more than 1,200 OpenAI agents broke out of a test environment and about 700 attacked Hugging Face, and cited Anthropic researchers' claim of a greater-than-10% chance AI kills all humans within a decade.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'The American people deserve to know the details of what went on in the Hugging Face incident and other incidents of AI models going rogue.' Letter PDF: https://www.hawley.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-09-09-Hawley-Letter-to-OpenAI-re-Hugging-Face-AI-Agent-Hack.pdf. Also reported by AP (2026-09-11).

letters_and_statements.title: Van Hollen letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman calling for federal cybersecurity agencies to get access to assess OpenAI models
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Van Hollen asked Altman to immediately give federal cybersecurity agencies the information needed to assess the safety and risks of OpenAI's models, citing the Hugging Face attack; the day before he posted that it was 'time to pump the brakes & take action NOW' and called for mandatory safeguards, a comprehensive testing regime and 'urgent dialogue with China.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Social-media quotes via The Hill (2026-09-09); letter via AP (2026-09-11) and vanhollen.senate.gov release.

letters_and_statements.title: Gallego letter to Senate leaders Thune and Schumer urging a bipartisan Senate Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Citing Jacob Coxon's resignation and Anthropic scientist Evan Hubinger's statement of a more-than-10% chance AI destroys humanity within a decade, Gallego asked leadership to create a bipartisan select committee with subpoena power starting in the 120th Congress.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'Congress does not need to resolve every disagreement among experts about timelines or probabilities to recognize that both the upside and the downside of this technology warrant an urgent and comprehensive response.'

letters_and_statements.title: Congressional reactions to former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warning that AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After Coxon's viral Sept 8 post and Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger's '>10% within the next decade' extinction estimate, members of both parties publicly framed AI as an existential risk and called for hearings, a kill-switch law, a superintelligence ban or a pause.
letters_and_statements.notes: Murphy: the problem is 'AI companies in a blind race to build a death machine first' but 'can easily be solved... through a regulatory system that allows the research to continue, but in a way that doesn't destroy us.' Lieu: 'exhibit number 739 for why we need to pass the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Bill ASAP.' Sanders: 'The very people building this technology admit that it could threaten the future of humanity.' Casar: 'This is an emergency. Congress must convene hearings and pass my and Bernie's superintelligence ban.' Beyer: 'Doing nothing on AI is unacceptable and dangerous.' Trahan: 'Safety researchers are resigning, powerful AI models are breaking out of their labs, and companies are racing ahead anyway.' Luna (R): called for a special session; 'there are massive implications of a race towards super intelligence.' Cruz (R) called the post 'scary as hell' and said 'We need substantially more regulation when it comes to AI' (Politico, 2026-09-10), while on The View saying 'if there are gonna be killer robots, I'd rather they be American killer robots than Chinese killer robots' (Forbes via Yahoo, 2026-09-10). Additional sources: Courthouse News 2026-09-09; USA Today/Yahoo 2026-09-11; Forbes/Yahoo 2026-09-10 (https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/lawmakers-reach-ai-kill-switch-165738614.html); Politico https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/09/10/congress/ted-cruz-ai-regulation-01070429.

letters_and_statements.title: Cruz says AI warning 'scary as hell,' calls for 'substantially more regulation' but opposes slowing U.S. AI versus China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Senate Commerce chairman, long an opponent of AI regulation, said he takes catastrophic AI risk seriously (citing Elon Musk's 10-20% estimate that AI destroys humanity within 10 years) and that his committee may mark up a bill with Thune and Klobuchar on AI-enabled biological and nuclear threats, while warning that shutting down U.S. AI would let China 'catch up in six months and soar ahead.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quotes: 'We need substantially more regulation when it comes to AI.' 'The Chinese are putting no guardrails. They're going full speed ahead.' Coded mixed because it pairs new catastrophic-risk rules with opposition to any slowdown.

letters_and_statements.title: Klobuchar and Cantwell statements on mandatory frontier-model safety testing in the pending Senate Commerce AI bill
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Klobuchar defended a bill under which companies test their own models and report to Commerce; Cantwell argued only testing by national-lab scientists is meaningful and that the bill must address catastrophic risk 'in a serious way.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Klobuchar: 'We cannot allow the release of dangerous models, including those that evade the control of their developers.' Cantwell (social media): meaningful legislation would require testing 'by scientists and experts at our national laboratories.'

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley op-ed, 'AI Will Control Us If We Do Not Control It' (The Free Press)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Hawley argued the federal government must set binding rules on AI jobs impacts, data centers and child safety, that AI 'is a question of self-government' that 'cannot be left to' Silicon Valley, and that the final stake is 'the conquest of some men by other men.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'Tech companies won't change unless the law forces them to change.' Cites his GUARD Act, GRID Act, AI-Related Job Impacts Clarity Act, AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act, AI Risk Evaluation Act and AI LEAD Act.

letters_and_statements.title: Murphy Substack post and release: 'Unregulated AI Will Destroy Our Economy and Culture'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Murphy warned of the 'existential risks' of unregulated AI, said every AI executive he met 'admitted that they had built a machine that they could not understand or control,' predicted massive job displacement, and rejected the argument that regulation cedes the race to China.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quotes: 'A fraud is being perpetuated on the American people and our pliant, gullible political leaders.' 'companies like Google and Apple and OpenAI and Anthropic are in a race to deploy consumer-facing, job-killing AGI as quickly as possible.' 'I want to beat China in the race for advanced AI. I do. But not at any cost.'

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley, Blumenthal and Padilla remarks at Senate Judiciary markup of the GUARD Act (22-0 vote)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: At the unanimous committee vote to ban AI companions for minors, Hawley said a beneficial AI age 'is a choice, not an inevitability,' Blumenthal predicted tech companies would fight the bill 'with armies of lawyers and lobbyists,' and Padilla said he would keep refining one section.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley document-request letters to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Following his Sept 16, 2025 hearing with parents of children who died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded all communications about the companies' AI chatbot policies.
letters_and_statements.notes: Hearing recap (2025-09-17): https://www.hawley.senate.gov/?s=Zuckerberg+chatbots ('Every Parent's Worst Nightmare').

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan senators' letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on AI chatbot policies permitting 'romantic or sensual' conversations with children
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Ten senators demanded details on how Meta's chatbot safety policies for minors were developed, asked for more visible disclosures and a ban on targeted ads to under-18 users, writing that 'the wellbeing of children should not be sacrificed in the race for AI development.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Signer list confirmed on bennet.senate.gov and Semafor (2025-08-20). Letter PDF hosted at schatz.senate.gov.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg launching Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots and children
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Hawley demanded Meta preserve and produce all versions of its 'GenAI: Content Risk Standards' by Sept 19, 2025, after reports its rules allowed chatbots to have 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'Parents deserve the truth, and kids deserve protection.'

letters_and_statements.title: Padilla and Welch letters to CEOs of Character.AI, Chai and Replika on mental-health and safety risks of companion chatbots
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The two senators asked the companion-chatbot companies how their models are trained to respond to conversations about mental health and self-harm, citing suicides linked to chatbot use and 'dangerous levels of attachment and unearned trust.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'complex themes that the AI chatbots on your products are wholly unqualified to discuss.'

letters_and_statements.title: Markey and Lieu statement applauding inclusion of 'human in the loop' nuclear-launch safeguard in the FY2025 NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The sponsors of the Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous AI Act said key provisions were included in the defense bill signed by President Biden, ensuring humans alone can order a nuclear launch.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'we must draw a firm line that prevents any chance of accidental nuclear war caused by AI. There is no question: humans must be in the loop of any nuclear launch.' I did not open the enacted NDAA text to confirm the section number.

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan House Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The 24-member, evenly bipartisan task force created by Speaker Johnson and Leader Jeffries issued 66 findings and 85-89 recommendations favoring a sectoral, incremental, humans-at-the-center approach that promotes innovation while guarding against AI risks; it became the blueprint for H.R.8516 in the 119th.
letters_and_statements.notes: Report PDF opened; transmittal letter signed by Obernolte and Lieu. The full 24-member list is in Appendix I as an image and could not be extracted as text, so only the co-chairs are listed here. The exact release date (Dec 17, 2024) is from press coverage; the PDF itself is dated December 2024.

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan Senate AI Working Group roadmap, 'Driving U.S. Innovation in Artificial Intelligence'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After nine all-senator AI Insight Forums, the four-member working group released a roadmap calling for at least $32 billion a year in non-defense AI spending and listing bipartisan policy topics including safety, accountability and workforce protections, leaving legislation to committees.
letters_and_statements.notes: Heinrich: 'the roadmap lays out the guardrails necessary to mitigate the risks of AI.' Rounds: 'mitigating potential long-term risks.' AP (2026-09-11) notes Congress 'has done little to follow up' on the $32B recommendation. The $32B figure is from AP; the release itself links to the roadmap PDF.

letters_and_statements.title: Blumenthal-Hawley 'Bipartisan Framework for U.S. AI Act'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The chair and ranking member of the Senate Judiciary privacy/technology subcommittee proposed a licensing regime for sophisticated general-purpose AI models run by an independent oversight body, liability for AI harms with no Section 230 shield, transparency requirements, an adverse-incident database, and export controls on advanced models.
letters_and_statements.notes: Blumenthal: 'the first tough, comprehensive legislative blueprint for real, enforceable AI protections.' Hawley: 'Our American families, workers, and national security are on the line.' Blumenthal at the May 2023 Altman hearing: 'Congress failed to meet the moment on social media. Now, we have the obligation to do it on AI before the threats and the risks become real' (quoted by Courthouse News, 2026-09-09). The 119th S.2938 (Hawley-Blumenthal) is the licensing/testing descendant of this framework.

risk.coverage_notes:
METHOD AND TOOL LIMITS. The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after 13 queries, and congress.gov, govtrack.us, all senate.gov member sites and most house.gov sites returned 403 to WebFetch/curl. Bill facts were therefore confirmed from the Library of Congress BILLSTATUS XML feed on GovInfo (govinfo.gov/bulkdata/BILLSTATUS), which is the same data congress.gov renders: for every numbered bill above I opened its BILLSTATUS record and read title, sponsor, introduced date, cosponsors with dates, committee referrals and actions, and for ~60 bills I also opened the introduced bill text (GovInfo BILLS XML). source_url fields use the standard congress.gov URL for the confirmed bill number. Enumeration: the GovInfo search API (DEMO_KEY) was used to list every 119th Congress bill whose TITLE contains artificial intelligence / AI / chatbot / algorithm / automated decision / frontier / generative / machine learning (302 bill versions, ~250 distinct bills) plus a second pass for autonomous / superintelligence / AGI / foundation model / robot / kill switch; lane-relevant bills were then pulled individually. Bills whose titles lack these words (e.g., NDAA AI sections, kids' bills with AI provisions) may be missing. Statements and letters were gathered with the in-app Chrome browser (which could load senate.gov, house.gov, AP, The Hill, Politico, Yahoo/Forbes, Courthouse News) and WebFetch for FedScoop, Nextgov, Roll Call, Cybersecurity Dive, ARI and Semafor. 

COULD NOT CONFIRM: (1) a bill number for the Sanders/Casar Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (announced 2026-09-03; not in GovInfo as of 2026-09-12; the congress.gov API hit its DEMO_KEY rate limit before a recent-bills check completed); (2) any number or text for the Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar Senate Commerce catastrophic-risk bill (unreleased); (3) the 24 individual members of the House AI Task Force (Appendix I of the PDF is an image); (4) the specific FY2025/FY2026 NDAA section numbers for the human-in-the-loop nuclear provision and the AI Futures Steering Committee (ARI lists FY2026 Secs. 1513, 1533, 1535, 6602 but I did not open enacted text); (5) whether S.3952 (Future of AI Innovation Act 2026) has been marked up — BILLSTATUS shows only a star print; (6) the exact number of members on Yahoo/Forbes' list of reactors beyond those named above. 

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED AS OTHER LANES: preemption bills (H.R.5388 American AI Leadership and Uniformity Act; S.3557 States' Right to Regulate AI Act; S.4216/H.R.8031 GUARDRAILS Act; the Dec 2025 Trump preemption EO and March 2026 White House framework); data-center/energy bills (S.4214 moratorium, H.R.6529, etc.); chips/export bills (S.2177 No Adversarial AI, GAIN AI Act, BLADE Act, AI OVERWATCH, Deterring AI Model Theft Act); deepfake/likeness bills (TAKE IT DOWN, NO FAKES, DEFIANCE, TRAIN Act, CLEAR Act); kids' bills without an AI-risk core (KOSA, SAFE KIDS Act S.4855, Safeguard Kids Act, Youth AI Privacy Act, AI toy bills). Kids' chatbot bills (GUARD, CHAT, CHATBOT) are included because they are the vehicles for AI-harm liability and mental-health provisions in this Congress. 

LIKELY MISSING / NOT SEARCHED: letters on OpenAI's for-profit restructuring, CAISI appropriations letters, letters to xAI about Grok (deepfake lane), Senate/House letters on the June 2026 Commerce shutdown of Anthropic's Mythos 5/Fable 5 models (news confirms the shutdown but I found no congressional letter), Blumenthal 2025-26 floor statements, hearing transcripts (Sept 16, 2025 Hawley chatbot hearing; Feb 10, 2026 Judiciary tech subcommittee hearing), the July 2026 Senate Commerce markup postponement coverage in Politico/WaPo (paywalled), and the June 4, 2026 'Great American AI Act' discussion draft text itself (I relied on FedScoop and Cybersecurity Dive summaries; its sponsor group matches H.R.9925). Direction coding is my judgment: 'more_guardrails' for bills that add binding or voluntary safety/oversight capacity, 'fewer_rules' for liability shields and regulatory waivers (RISE, SANDBOX, AI for America), 'mixed' for packages that pair oversight with state preemption (FRONTIER Act) or that are capacity-building only (CREATE AI, NAIRR, dominance resolution).

bills.short_title: Ratepayer Protection Act
key_cosponsors: Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL-14) (original cosponsor, Energy Subcommittee ranking member)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Energy Subcommittee by voice vote June 24, 2026; ordered reported by full Energy and Commerce Committee 52-0 (substitute) July 21, 2026; reported (amended) H. Rept. 119-814 and placed on Union Calendar No. 713 on Sept 10, 2026; House GOP leaders announced a floor vote (suspension) for the week of Sept 14, 2026 (Bloomberg Government/Reuters, Sept 10, 2026).
bills.plain_english: Adds a federal standard under PURPA that state utility regulators must consider: data-center customers of 100 MW or more must pay the full incremental cost of the generation, transmission and distribution upgrades built to serve them (even if they later leave), and post financial assurances up front. Aims to stop tech companies' power costs from being shifted onto household electric bills.
bills.notes: 42 cosponsors as of Sept 12, 2026 (mostly Republicans, plus Castor, Bishop, McClellan, Gottheimer, Cuellar, McDonald Rivet, Goodlander). The committee substitute narrowed the bill from all 100 MW+ loads to data-center loads specifically; the Data Center Coalition objected to being singled out (E&E News). Chair Guthrie: bill will 'ensure that data centers pay their own way.' Ranking Member Pallone supports the bill but says a moratorium may be needed if Congress fails to add guardrails. Senate companion S.5028 (Husted). Bill text verified via GPO govinfo BILLSTATUS/BILLS (introduced and reported versions).

bills.short_title: Ratepayer Protection Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors as of Sept 12, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Senate companion to H.R. 9340: pushes states to make data centers of 100 MW or more pay the full cost of the grid upgrades they trigger, so families and small businesses do not subsidize them.
bills.notes: Husted attended the March 4, 2026 White House roundtable where seven tech companies signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge; his release says the bill would 'codify key elements of that pledge.' Husted quote: 'we must do that without passing the costs on to working families and small businesses.' ENR Chair Mike Lee has not prioritized data center legislation (E&E News).

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee; zero cosponsors as of Sept 12, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Bans building or upgrading AI data centers (over 20 MW, or with high-density racks/liquid cooling) until Congress passes laws requiring pre-release federal safety review of AI products, protecting workers from AI job loss, guaranteeing data centers do not raise utility bills or harm the environment, letting communities veto projects, requiring union jobs and barring subsidies. Also bans exporting AI computing hardware to countries without similar safeguards.
bills.notes: Bill text (govinfo BILLS-119s4214is) confirmed: 20 MW threshold, findings quoting Musk, Amodei, Hassabis, Bezos, Gates, Suleyman, Farley, Ellison; enforcement via inspections and conditioning future permits; Section 4 export controls on computing infrastructure hardware.
