Sanders quote: 'We need a federal moratorium on AI data centers.' House companion H.R. 9442 (Ocasio-Cortez). Rep. Frank Pallone (top E&C Democrat) separately endorsed a national moratorium on June 24, 2026.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Foreign Affairs Committees; 14 cosponsors as of Sept 12, 2026.
bills.plain_english: House version of the Sanders moratorium: no new or expanded AI data centers until Congress enacts AI safety, worker-protection, utility-bill, environmental and community-consent laws; also restricts AI hardware exports.
bills.notes: Ocasio-Cortez quote: 'We must choose humanity over profit.' Identical to S.4214 per CRS.

bills.short_title: Clean Cloud Act of 2025
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Environment and Public Works Committee; no further action.
bills.plain_english: Sets a declining greenhouse-gas emissions standard for the electricity used by data centers and crypto-mining facilities over 100 kW, with the regional baseline cut 11% a year through 2034 and zero from 2035. Facilities and their utilities exceeding the standard pay a fee ($20 per kW-equivalent, inflation adjusted); fee revenue funds clean firm power, long-duration storage and rebates to lower residential electric bills. Requires annual energy and emissions reporting.
bills.notes: Whitehouse is EPW ranking member. House companion H.R. 6179 (Cohen). CRS summary confirms fee/standard structure.

bills.short_title: Clean Cloud Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 9 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: House version of the Clean Cloud Act: an emissions performance standard and fee on the power used by large data centers and crypto mines, with revenue recycled to clean firm power and lower home electric bills.
bills.notes: Cohen represents Memphis, site of xAI's Colossus data center and gas turbine controversy.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Environment and Public Works Committee.
bills.plain_english: Orders EPA to study the environmental impacts of AI data centers and their energy infrastructure, has NIST convene a consortium to develop measurement standards, and creates an EPA reporting system for AI's environmental footprint (energy, water, emissions).
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th Congress S.3732 (Feb 2024). Markey's June 30, 2026 release describes it as requiring 'data center operators to report the full range of their facilities' environmental impacts.' House companion H.R. 9183 (Beyer).

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology and Energy and Commerce Committees; 21 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: House version: EPA study, NIST consortium and a federal reporting system for the environmental impacts of AI data centers.
bills.notes: Beyer represents Northern Virginia, the world's largest data center market.

bills.short_title: SPEED Act (Standardizing Permitting and Expediting Economic Development Act)
bills.sponsor: Rep. Bruce Westerman (R-AR-4), Natural Resources Chair
bills.status: Ordered reported by Natural Resources 25-18 (Nov 20, 2025); reported H. Rept. 119-395 (Dec 4, 2025); PASSED HOUSE 221-196 on Dec 18, 2025 (Roll Call 356); motion to recommit failed 206-211 (Roll 355); received in Senate and referred to Environment and Public Works Committee Dec 18, 2025; no Senate action.
bills.plain_english: Overhauls the National Environmental Policy Act to shrink what counts as a 'major federal action', shorten environmental reviews and cut the window for lawsuits to 150 days, in order to speed permits for power plants, transmission and AI data centers. Backed by OpenAI, Microsoft and Micron; most Democrats opposed it after GOP leaders added language exempting Trump's renewable-energy permit cancellations.
bills.notes: Roll Call 356 (clerk.house.gov/Votes/2025356): Republicans 210-1, Democrats 11-195. Democrats voting YEA: Jim Costa (CA), Henry Cuellar (TX), Don Davis (NC), Chris Deluzio (PA), Lizzie Fletcher (TX), Jared Golden (ME), Vicente Gonzalez (TX), Adam Gray (CA), John Mannion (NY), Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (WA), Marc Veasey (TX). Republican voting NAY: Brian Fitzpatrick (PA). Westerman: 'The electricity we will need to power AI computing for civilian and military use is a national imperative' (CNBC). Rep. Scott Peters (D-CA), a permitting-reform supporter, voted no, calling the renewable carve-out 'a broken permitting status quo.' Senate companion text: S.3224 (Kennedy). Senate EPW/ENR leaders have not introduced a comprehensive bipartisan permitting bill as of Sept 2026; GOP Senate vehicles are S.4944 (Armstrong) and S.4765 (Barrasso).

bills.short_title: SPEED Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Environment and Public Works Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Senate version of the House SPEED Act's NEPA overhaul to speed environmental reviews for energy and infrastructure projects including data centers.
bills.notes: Official title identical to H.R. 4776 ('to amend NEPA to clarify ambiguous provisions and facilitate a more efficient, effective, and timely environmental review process'). Do not confuse with S.1894/H.R.4059, also nicknamed 'SPEED Act' (Lummis/Hageman), which amend MAP-21 categorical exclusions and are unrelated to data centers.

bills.short_title: DATA Act of 2026 (Decentralized Access to Technology Alternatives Act)
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Creates a new category of 'consumer-regulated electric utilities' that build their own power plants and wires to serve new loads such as data centers while staying physically islanded from the grid; these are exempted from the Federal Power Act (FERC rates, reliability, interconnection, transmission planning), PURPA and PUHCA. Connecting to the grid, even for backup, forfeits the exemption.
bills.notes: Cotton: the bill 'will eliminate outdated federal regulations and enable manufacturers, data centers, and other energy-intensive industries to build customized electricity systems' (Utility Dive, Jan 2026). House companion H.R. 8400 (Begich). Modeled on New Hampshire HB 672.

bills.short_title: DATA Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: House companion to Cotton's bill exempting fully off-grid data-center power systems from federal utility regulation.
bills.notes: Identical to S.3585 per CRS relationship data.

bills.short_title: GRID Act (Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers Act)
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.
bills.plain_english: Requires data centers of 20 MW or more to get all their power, including backup, from sources separate from the public grid (with a 10-year off-ramp for existing facilities), guarantees residential ratepayers priority on the grid and no rate increases due to data centers, and requires operators to publicly disclose current and projected utility usage.
bills.notes: Bipartisan populist pairing. Hawley: 'American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers.' Blumenthal: 'Our GRID Act stops Big Tech's AI-driven drain on family's pocketbooks.' Bill text defines 'Rate Effect Credit' and 'Zero Rate Effect Certificate' mechanisms administered by DOE. Rep. Byron Donalds' H.R. 9777 is a similar off-grid mandate (5 MW threshold) in the House.

bills.short_title: POWER Up Act (Promoting Oversight of Wholesale Energy Reliability Act)
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Clarifies that FERC has jurisdiction over connecting 'large load facilities' (100 MW or more, adjustable by FERC) directly to the interstate transmission grid, subjects those connections to the just-and-reasonable standard, and orders FERC to write standardized large-load interconnection rules within 18 months, including for hybrid on-site-generation-plus-grid projects. Preserves state authority over siting, retail rates and distribution.
bills.notes: Lummis: 'When a facility wants to draw as much power as a city, that is not an ordinary retail question. It is a grid question.' Companion to DOE's Oct 2025 large-load ANOPR and FERC's June 18, 2026 show-cause orders to six RTOs/ISOs. Direction coded mixed: creates federal rules/oversight but aimed at speeding data-center interconnection.

bills.short_title: Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Amends the Federal Power Act to make large loads such as data centers pay 100% of grid network upgrades and reliability services they need, agree to demand flexibility (curtailment at peak) and bring their own power as conditions of connecting to transmission; blocks data centers from siphoning existing plants' output; tightens interconnection queue rules against speculative projects; and tasks DOE national labs with studying data center energy use.
bills.notes: Schiff: 'hard-working Americans should not be left to foot the tab for rising energy costs.' Press reports describe a 50 MW threshold (Washington Signal); bill text adds new FPA section 224 'Management of Large Load Facilities.'

bills.short_title: GRID Savings Act of 2026 (Guarding Ratepayers from Increased Demand-costs Savings Act)
bills.sponsor: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-NM), ENR Ranking Member
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Applies to very large new electricity users (150 MW or more behind one interconnection point) the same rules new power plants face: a FERC-run interconnection study process, paying for the facilities needed to connect them, and financial commitments; lets hyperscalers voluntarily fund backbone transmission upgrades in exchange for service.
bills.notes: Heinrich: 'If a company is driving the need for expensive new facilities, that company should pay for it.' Notable because Heinrich is the top Democrat on the committee of jurisdiction; Chair Lee and Heinrich jointly backed DOE's large-load ANOPR in Nov 2025.

bills.short_title: Power for the People Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; 8 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Directs states to consider creating a separate data-center rate class and 'large load queues', directs FERC to ensure data centers pay for the transmission upgrades their demand causes, and rewards projects that bring their own new generation, storage or demand flexibility so other customers' bills and grid reliability are protected.
bills.notes: Sense-of-Congress text says 'households and businesses are subsidizing data center development.' Warner's June 2, 2026 release: co-sponsored to 'rein in the rising electricity costs Virginians are facing.' House companion H.R. 8241 (Tonko).

bills.short_title: Power for the People Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 26 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: House companion: data-center rate classes, load queues, and FERC direction to make data centers pay for the transmission they cause.
bills.notes: Tonko is a senior E&C Democrat; at the July 2026 markup he said 'We are not doing what this moment demands of us.'

bills.short_title: SHIELD Act (Stopping Hikes In Electricity from Large Load Demands Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 14 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Makes facilities over 75 MW their own PURPA customer class that must fully repay grid upgrade costs (even if they shut down early), and has utilities prioritize large loads that use efficiency, storage, demand response and 100% zero-emission power.
bills.notes: Democratic precursor to the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act's PURPA approach.

bills.short_title: FAIR Data Act (Fair Allocation of Infrastructure Responsibility for Data Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Prohibits investor-owned utilities from recovering any costs associated with data centers over 75 MW, including grid upgrades, from residential or small-business customers; states must implement within set deadlines.
bills.notes: Bipartisan (Van Drew). Stronger than H.R. 9340: a flat prohibition rather than a standard states must 'consider.'

bills.short_title: Data Center Fair Share Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Transportation and Infrastructure Committees.
bills.plain_english: Requires large-load customers (100 MW+) to pay the full incremental cost of grid upgrades up front or via a dedicated rate class, and withholds federal highway funds from states that do not adopt the standard.
bills.notes: Subramanyam represents Loudoun County ('Data Center Alley'). Uses highway-fund leverage to make the Ratepayer Protection Act approach mandatory rather than 'consider.'

bills.short_title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Energy Subcommittee (amended) June 24, 2026; ordered reported by full Energy and Commerce Committee 44-0 on July 21, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Requires FERC to hold a commissioner-led technical conference within 90 days with DOE, utilities, states, consumer advocates and data centers on rate structures to protect residential and small-business customers from large-load costs, and report recommendations to Congress.
bills.notes: One of eight electricity bills in the June 24, 2026 Energy Subcommittee data-center package. Griffith (R-VA) is the lone GOP cosponsor.

bills.short_title: No Harm Data Centers Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Gives FERC sole authority to approve retail electricity rates charged to data centers over 50 MW, requiring them to be just and reasonable and to make data centers bear the costs they impose on the bulk power system rather than residential and small commercial customers.
bills.notes: Unusual federal preemption of state retail ratemaking for data centers.

bills.short_title: Protecting Ratepayers Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Within 180 days, bars any company from building or operating a data center of 5 MW or more unless all its power (including backup) comes from captive or on-site generation off the grid and all its water comes from sources outside the public water system; also gives Trump's March 2026 Ratepayer Protection Pledge proclamation the force of law.
bills.notes: Donalds is the Trump-endorsed candidate for Florida governor. Most aggressive GOP off-grid mandate (5 MW threshold vs 20 MW in Hawley's GRID Act). Cites Proclamation 'Ratepayer Protection Pledge' (91 Fed. Reg. 11439).

bills.short_title: Power and Water for Families Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Ways and Means and Energy and Commerce Committees; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: A GOP 'all-of-the-above' package: declares AI leadership over China a national priority, adds PURPA standards so 100 MW+ large-load facilities pay incremental infrastructure costs and bring additive generation, and creates incentives for water reuse at data centers.
bills.notes: Baumgartner also sponsors the deregulatory Protect American AI Act (H.R. 8037) and cosponsors H.R. 9340; this bill pairs ratepayer protection with pro-buildout policy statements.

bills.short_title: PRICE Act (Preventing Rate Inflation in Consumer Energy Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Requires every data center using 50 MW or more to generate all the electricity it consumes, with 75% from clean sources by 2035 and 100% by 2040; violators face civil penalties up to $100,000 per day.
bills.notes: Introduced the same day as Menendez's Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984).

bills.short_title: Data Center Transparency Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 14 cosponsors including two Republicans.
bills.plain_english: Requires EPA to report quarterly on data centers' water use, water reuse, water pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, and the Energy Information Administration to report every six months on data center electricity use by state and its effect on household bills.
bills.notes: Bipartisan cosponsors Fitzpatrick and Lawler. Complements the Warren-Hawley March 2026 letter urging EIA to mandate data center reporting.

bills.short_title: Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Requires data center operators to file annual reports on on-site electricity and water use (including PUE and WUE metrics) with their state or EPA, DOE and USDA, with public disclosure.
bills.notes: Introduced the same day as the Sanders moratorium and the Rick Scott pledge resolution (March 25, 2026). House companion H.R. 9825 (Underwood). Trackers describe a 25 MW threshold.

bills.short_title: Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: House companion to Durbin's mandatory annual energy and water reporting for data centers.
bills.notes: Identical to S.4213 per CRS.

bills.short_title: POWER Act (Public Oversight of Water and Energy Reporting Act)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Directs DOE, with EPA, to report to Congress every year on water and electricity use by data centers that are 'qualifying projects' under Trump's data-center permitting executive order (EO 14318), including who paid grid-connection costs and how many self-generate.
bills.notes: Conservative transparency bill; findings say construction 'should not come at the sacrifice of our nation's water resources or valuable farm and ranchland' and government should not subsidize data centers 'that would not be viable otherwise.' Roy quote: 'we need to be mindful of our water and energy resources.'

bills.short_title: Data Center Resource Disclosure Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Has NTIA run an annual voluntary survey of every U.S. data center's energy and water use, publish results on an interactive map, name operators that did not respond, and recommend regulatory improvements.
bills.notes: Scholten: 'Accountability starts with transparency.'

bills.short_title: Defending Our Energy and Water Act
bills.status: Referred to House Oversight and Government Reform and Armed Services Committees.
bills.plain_english: Updates federal (including DoD) data center efficiency requirements to protect water resources, requires water-saving cooling at new federal data centers, and reauthorizes DoD's expiring authority to set data center water-efficiency standards.
bills.notes: Applies to government data centers, not private ones.

bills.short_title: Ratepayer Bill of Rights Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Education and Workforce Committees.
bills.plain_english: For data centers with 50 MW+ demand or 100,000+ gallons/day of water, guarantees ratepayers rights to know projected and actual power/water use and infrastructure costs before approval, bars shifting any project-driven cost onto households, farms, schools and hospitals (with refunds plus interest), and requires binding cost-recovery agreements and financial security.
bills.notes: Cuellar also cosponsors the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) and voted for the SPEED Act, an unusual pairing.

bills.short_title: Data Center Tax Accountability and Disclosure Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Finance Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Denies bonus depreciation to AI data centers (where at least 20% of the facility develops or runs AI) unless they earn LEED Gold/Platinum or an equivalent DOE/EPA efficiency standard, and requires covered data centers to publicly report electricity and water use, sources, efficiency metrics and supply agreements to EPA.
bills.notes: Warner represents the largest data center state; the bill uses the tax code rather than utility law.

bills.short_title: Data Center Community Reinvestment Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Ways and Means, Energy and Commerce, and Science Committees; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Imposes a federal excise tax of 1 cent per kilowatt-hour on electricity used by data centers over 1 MW, with proceeds split among the Land and Water Conservation Fund, Housing Trust Fund, Superfund, Highway Trust Fund and other community programs.
bills.notes: First federal data-center electricity tax proposal.

bills.short_title: AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 10 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Requires AI data center developers to publicly disclose location, resource needs and an independent environmental impact analysis at least 180 days before taking definitive steps, engage local media and residents in multiple languages, and limit NDAs with governments; enforced by the FTC as an unfair or deceptive practice.
bills.notes: Targets the secrecy and NDA practices that have driven local backlash.

bills.short_title: Data Center Community Impact Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 15 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Orders a DOE study, with EPA and Commerce, of how data centers' energy use, water use and pollution affect communities of color and low-income communities, citing the xAI facility in Memphis.
bills.notes: Environmental-justice framing; findings cite 17 billion gallons of cooling water in 2023.

bills.short_title: Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Has EPA commission a National Academies assessment of data centers' noise, air pollution, water use, carbon emissions and e-waste, with mitigation recommendations due in 180 days.
bills.notes: Landsman's third data center bill (with H.R. 6529 and H.R. 8033).

bills.short_title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
bills.status: Referred to House Natural Resources Committee; 8 cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Prohibits building or operating AI data centers (AI-scale facilities, or over 20 MW with high-density racks/liquid cooling) on any federal land and orders agencies to cease and remove existing ones within 30 days, with CERCLA-consistent site restoration. A direct rebuke of the administration's push to site AI data centers on DOE and DoD land.
bills.notes: Responds to DOE's 2025 selection of federal sites (e.g., Oak Ridge, Idaho, Paducah, Savannah River) and Army/Air Force data center leasing plans. No Republican support.

bills.short_title: Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; 4 Republican cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Bars federal agencies from overriding state or local zoning, siting or permitting authority over data centers on non-federal land, or conditioning federal funds on giving up that authority.
bills.notes: Republican anti-preemption bill; signals GOP frontliner resistance to any federal override of local data center fights. Barrett also cosponsors H.R. 9340.

bills.short_title: No Data Center NDAs Act
bills.status: Referred to Committee on House Administration.
bills.plain_english: Prohibits members of Congress from signing nondisclosure agreements with governments or companies as a condition of receiving information about data center projects.
bills.notes: Reaction to NDAs used in Michigan data center deals (e.g., Saline Township).

bills.short_title: Local Control Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to House Ways and Means and Judiciary Committees.
bills.plain_english: Strips federal courts of jurisdiction over challenges to local governments' recorded-vote denials of data center projects, bars federal permits for developers suing to overturn local zoning denials, and conditions federal tax credits for data centers on an enforceable community benefit agreement and local workforce plan.
bills.notes: Republican frontliner from northeastern Pennsylvania, a data center hot spot.

bills.short_title: (No short title) Prohibit federal financial benefit for data centers on prime farmland
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Bars any federal agency from providing financial benefits for building or expanding data centers on prime farmland and certain other farmland.
bills.notes: Rural-conservative angle on data center siting.

bills.short_title: Data Center Bill of Rights resolution
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Judiciary Committees; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Sense of the House that communities should have the right to ban data centers within 2,500 feet of homes and schools, reject projects, adopt statewide pauses until ratepayer and water protections exist, demand no rate increases, require clean energy and pollution limits, and receive independent impact reports before approval.
bills.notes: Source URL should read congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-resolution/1471. Khanna, a Silicon Valley Democrat, endorsing statewide pauses is notable.

bills.short_title: Concurrent resolution endorsing the Ratepayer Protection Pledge
bills.status: Referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.
bills.plain_english: Declares that the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge signed at the White House on March 4, 2026 by Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI (pay separate rate structures and pay-whether-used for infrastructure) is sound national policy as AI and data center infrastructure expands.
bills.notes: Endorses a voluntary industry pledge rather than binding rules; Markey and colleagues called the pledge 'vague and insufficient.' Marshall also cosponsors Hawley's binding GRID Act.

bills.short_title: Responsible Data Center Siting Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce Committee.
bills.plain_english: Directs DOE, with FERC and DoD, to publish best practices for siting data centers considering grid impacts and electricity prices, water use, air and water quality, noise and light, national security, workforce and tax effects.
bills.notes: Introduced alongside H.R. 10322.

bills.short_title: Smart Data Center Policy Act
bills.status: Referred to House Transportation and Infrastructure, Armed Services, and Energy and Commerce Committees.
bills.plain_english: Commerce Department study of the costs, grid, water and environmental impacts of siting data centers at or near military installations, rail hubs, airports and industrial zones, and possible federal incentives to steer them there.
bills.notes: Steering, not restricting, siting.

bills.short_title: Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act
bills.status: Ordered reported (substitute, amended) by House Science, Space, and Technology Committee 34-1 on June 25, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Has NIST develop best practices for measuring data center energy use and study the data needed to improve electricity demand forecasting.
bills.notes: Bipartisan (Obernolte, House AI Task Force co-chair). One of few data center bills to clear a committee.

bills.short_title: Unleashing Low-Cost Rural AI Act
bills.status: Referred to House Science, Space, and Technology Committee.
bills.plain_english: DOE national lab study of how AI and data center growth affects energy supply, costs, land and water use, especially in rural areas, including how to expedite NEPA reviews and permitting for data centers and their power infrastructure.
bills.notes: Bipartisan, pro-buildout framing with a study on consumer costs; Costa voted for the SPEED Act.

bills.short_title: Securing Reliable Power for Advanced Technologies Act
bills.status: Referred to House Financial Services Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Amends the Defense Production Act to let the President designate 'critical AI infrastructure' (AI data centers of 50 MW+ and dispatchable baseload plants of 100 MW+ serving them) as priority national defense projects to accelerate them.
bills.notes: Barr is a 2026 Kentucky Senate candidate. Uses DPA priority powers to fast-track data centers and gas/nuclear generation.

bills.short_title: Protect American AI Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary and Energy and Commerce Committees; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Prevents environmental lawsuits (under NEPA, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, ESA, Natural Gas Act) from invalidating permits for data centers and their supporting infrastructure; courts must remand rather than vacate approvals.
bills.notes: Strongest House litigation shield specific to data centers.

bills.short_title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce and Science Committees; 11 bipartisan cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: GAO technology assessment of liquid cooling for AI compute clusters (which cuts energy and water use) plus government-wide best-practice guidance for federal agencies.
bills.notes: Senate companion S.3269 (McCormick; cosponsors Coons, Budd, Schiff) had an ENR Energy Subcommittee hearing April 15, 2026 (S.Hrg. 119-366).

bills.short_title: Load Forecasting Enhancement Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Energy Subcommittee June 24, 2026; ordered reported by full committee 47-0 on July 21, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Requires FERC to set up regional boards with state utility commissions to identify best practices for forecasting electricity demand (a response to speculative and double-counted data center load requests) and requires states to consider adopting them.
bills.notes: Part of the June 24, 2026 E&C data-center electricity package (with H.R. 9340, 6529, 9339, 9335, 6633, 2986, 9338).

bills.short_title: High-Capacity Grid Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Energy Subcommittee June 24, 2026; ordered reported (amended) by full committee 49-0 on July 21, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Has FERC presume that using best-available advanced transmission conductors on interstate lines is prudent and cost-recoverable, to move more power over existing corridors as data center demand grows.
bills.notes: Grid-capacity bill marked up in the data center package; not a data-center regulation per se.

bills.short_title: Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Energy and Commerce Committee 44-0 on July 21, 2026.
bills.plain_english: DOE assessment of using AI and high-performance computing to increase the capacity, reliability and efficiency of the bulk power system.
bills.notes: AI-for-the-grid, not data center regulation; included because it moved in the data center package.

bills.short_title: Advanced Transmission Technology to Reduce Rates Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Energy Subcommittee June 24, 2026; ordered reported 39-10 on July 21, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Promotes grid-enhancing and advanced transmission technologies to lower rates as demand grows; part of the E&C data center electricity package.
bills.notes: Only bill in the package with significant opposition (39-10); no CRS summary available yet.

bills.short_title: Expediting Generator Interconnection Procedures Act of 2025
bills.status: Forwarded (amended) by E&C Energy Subcommittee to full committee by voice vote June 24, 2026.
bills.plain_english: Speeds the process for connecting new power generation to the grid, marked up as part of the E&C response to data-center-driven demand.
bills.notes: Not yet ordered reported by full committee as of Sept 12, 2026.

bills.short_title: American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Environment and Public Works Committee; 17 Republican cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Senate GOP permitting bill streamlining reviews under the Natural Gas Act, Clean Water Act and NEPA for energy and mineral projects; the Senate's principal Republican vehicle in the permitting debate that the House SPEED Act started.
bills.notes: Bill text (80,000+ chars) contains no mention of data centers or AI; included because Senate permitting reform is the vehicle proponents cite for powering AI data centers. No Democratic cosponsors, so it lacks the 60 votes needed.

bills.short_title: Let America Build Act of 2026
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.
bills.plain_english: Broad energy development and permitting reform package from the Senate GOP whip.
bills.notes: Text does not mention data centers or AI; successor to Barrasso's 2024 Manchin-Barrasso effort.

bills.short_title: Making Reviews Certain Act
bills.status: Referred to House Natural Resources Committee; no cosponsors.
bills.plain_english: Democratic NEPA bill clarifying scope of review and limiting judicial review of environmental documents for energy infrastructure.
bills.notes: Signals a Democrat open to permitting reform; Gottheimer voted against the SPEED Act but cosponsors H.R. 9340 and H.R. 5332. Text does not mention data centers.

bills.short_title: NEW HORIZON Act
bills.status: Read twice and referred to Senate Armed Services Committee.
bills.plain_english: Requires DoD to run a pilot evaluating commercially available orbital data centers and space-based cloud computing for national security missions.
bills.notes: Space-based data centers are pitched partly as an answer to terrestrial power and water constraints; tangential to the ratepayer debate.

bills.short_title: Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act
bills.status: Referred to Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection (May 8, 2026).
bills.plain_english: CISA and DoD strategy to identify and defend data centers from attacks and protect surrounding communities.
bills.notes: Security rather than energy; included for completeness of Subramanyam's data center agenda.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2024
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee; died at end of 118th Congress.
bills.plain_english: First federal bill to require EPA to study and NIST to develop standards for measuring AI's environmental footprint, with a voluntary reporting system.
bills.notes: Reintroduced as S.4727 in June 2026 with a mandatory reporting system. House companion H.R.7197 (Eshoo; cosponsors Beyer, Phillips, Levin, Barragan).

bills.short_title: Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024 (Manchin-Barrasso)
bills.status: Ordered reported favorably (substitute) by Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee July 31, 2024; reported with S. Rept. 118-336 and placed on Senate calendar Dec 19, 2024; no floor vote; died at end of 118th Congress.
bills.plain_english: Bipartisan permitting overhaul to speed transmission, pipelines, leasing and renewable projects and cut NEPA litigation windows; widely cited as the template for powering AI data centers, but it never reached the floor.
bills.notes: Committee vote tally not confirmed from an opened primary page; press widely reported 15-4. Heinrich cited his 2024 vote for it in his 2026 GRID Savings Act release.

bills.short_title: ADVANCE Act of 2023 (enacted via S.870, Public Law 118-67)
key_cosponsors: 19 cosponsors on S.1111 (bipartisan; reported by EPW Chair Carper)
bills.status: Reported by EPW July 10, 2023 (S. Rept. 118-182); attached to S.870 (Fire Grants and Safety Act); S.870 as amended passed House 393-13 (Roll no. 194) May 8, 2024; Senate concurred June 18, 2024; signed into law July 9, 2024 as P.L. 118-67.
bills.plain_english: Streamlines and lowers fees for Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing of advanced reactors, speeds siting at brownfield and retired plant sites, and modernizes the NRC mission. Enacted before the AI framing took hold but now the main legal foundation cited for 'nuclear for AI' data centers.
bills.notes: Final Senate vote tally on June 18, 2024 not confirmed from an opened page. Related House bill H.R.6544 Atomic Energy Advancement Act (Rep. Jeff Duncan, R-SC) passed House 365-36 (Roll no. 55) on Feb 28, 2024.

letters_and_statements.title: Letter from 12 members of Congress to PJM Board Chair David Mills on data center load, capacity costs and mandatory backstop
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Lawmakers from PJM states told the grid operator that data centers added $16 billion in capacity costs in two years and could add $163 billion by 2033, criticized PJM for dropping a mandatory curtailment 'backstop' for new large loads under pressure from data center interests, and demanded a large-load queue, better load forecasting, priority for projects that bring their own generation, and an extension of the capacity price collar.
letters_and_statements.notes: Full letter text on Van Hollen's site; press release dated Nov 6, 2025. Quote: 'it is unduly discriminatory to force our constituents to subsidize data center development through astronomical rates and costs.'

letters_and_statements.title: New Jersey congressional delegation letter to PJM on capacity-auction-driven 17% rate increase
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Nine New Jersey lawmakers asked PJM what it is doing to speed interconnection of new generation and avoid price spikes after the 2024 capacity auction, which they attributed to data center demand plus slow new generation, added $14.7 billion in costs.
letters_and_statements.notes: Signer list confirmed from PJM's June 9, 2025 response letter (pjm.com) addressed to these nine members. Focus is on speeding supply rather than restricting data centers, hence coded mixed.

letters_and_statements.title: Seven Democratic senators' letter to FERC Chair Laura Swett urging action to stop data-center-driven rate hikes
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Senators urged FERC to reject transmission filings that spread data-center costs across regions, investigate cost allocation and PJM practices, resist queue-jumping for large fossil generators, standardize load forecasting, and prioritize residential ratepayers in the DOE-requested large-load interconnection rulemaking.
letters_and_statements.notes: Warnock's office re-publicized the same letter on Jan 5, 2026 (warnock.senate.gov). Quote: 'American households simply cannot afford inaction from FERC.'

letters_and_statements.title: Six New England senators' letter to ISO New England CEO Vamsi Chadalavada on protecting ratepayers from data center growth
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Senators asked the New England grid operator how it will keep tech companies, not families, paying for data center load, citing a 13% rise in residential prices in 2025 and PJM's capacity price spike as a warning.
letters_and_statements.notes: Also posted by Welch and Markey. Quote: 'the multi-billion-dollar AI industry should be responsible for these costs.'

letters_and_statements.title: Letter from Senators Markey, Blumenthal, Van Hollen and Booker to NARUC President Ann Rendahl on state PUC action against data center cost-shifting
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Two days after the White House's voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge, the senators called it 'vague and insufficient' and asked state utility regulators' association what guidance it gives PUCs to reject rate filings that make households subsidize data centers.
letters_and_statements.notes: NARUC replied March 18, 2026 (pubs.naruc.org).

letters_and_statements.title: Maryland congressional delegation letter to FERC Chairman Swett on PJM transmission cost allocation for out-of-state data centers
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Maryland's Democratic senators and representatives asked FERC to reform PJM cost allocation after roughly $2 billion in transmission costs for projects primarily serving out-of-state (Virginia) data centers were assigned to Maryland ratepayers, and backed the Maryland People's Counsel complaint.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter PDF at vanhollen.senate.gov (maryland_congressional_delegation_letter_to_ferc_on_pjm_transmission_costs.pdf). Estimated $1.6 billion over ten years for Maryland customers.

letters_and_statements.title: Warren, Van Hollen and Blumenthal investigation letters to Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix on data centers and electricity bills
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Three senators opened an investigation demanding the companies explain how much of their data centers' grid and generation costs are passed to households, and pressed them to pay a greater share up front; responses were due Jan 12, 2026.
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: 'American families bankroll the electricity costs of trillion-dollar tech companies.' Warren's office said it secured 'new commitments' from companies in January 2026.

letters_and_statements.title: Warren-Hawley bipartisan letter to EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey urging mandatory annual energy-use reporting by data centers
letters_and_statements.plain_english: A left-right pair asked the Energy Information Administration to require data centers and other large loads to report hourly and peak consumption, prices paid, deposits, demand flexibility, AI vs. cloud energy use, and who pays for triggered grid upgrades, so the public can check compliance with the voluntary Ratepayer Protection Pledge.
letters_and_statements.notes: Response requested by April 9, 2026. Quote: 'Without this data, policymakers, utility companies, and local communities are operating in the dark.'

letters_and_statements.title: House Energy and Commerce Democratic leaders' letter to FERC on DOE large-load interconnection ANOPR
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Pallone and Castor urged FERC to hold families harmless in any large-load rulemaking: data centers must pay fully for grid upgrades, offer load flexibility, preserve open grid access for all generators, respect state jurisdiction, and FERC must stay independent of DOE and White House pressure and use a full notice-and-comment process.
signers_or_speakers: Rep. Frank Pallone (D-NJ-6), E&C Ranking Member
Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL-14), Energy Subcommittee Ranking Member
letters_and_statements.notes: Quote: data centers 'cannot be built out on the backs of the power bills of American families across the country.' Letter PDF: democrats-energycommerce.house.gov december-2025-ferc-data-centers-letter.pdf.

letters_and_statements.title: Letters from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Twenty House Democrats asked regulators, utilities and the data center industry how they will keep grid upgrade costs off household bills, whether contracts and tariffs will be transparent, whether load forecasts are realistic, and what cost-allocation tools (minimum usage commitments, separate rate classes, upfront cost recovery) Congress should consider.
letters_and_statements.notes: Cites $4.3 billion in PJM transmission costs passed to customers in 2024 and $7.3 billion (82%) higher PJM generation costs. Beyer's release lists Menendez as NJ-13; he represents NJ-8.

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan letter from Senate ENR Chair Mike Lee and Ranking Member Martin Heinrich to FERC supporting DOE's large-load interconnection proposal
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The top Republican and Democrat on the Senate energy committee backed FERC taking up Energy Secretary Wright's Section 403 proposal for federal rules on connecting large loads (data centers) to the grid, stressing customer affordability, fair cost allocation, and respect for state authority.
signers_or_speakers: Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-NM), ENR Ranking Member
letters_and_statements.notes: Lee: addressing large-load interconnection 'will be key to ensuring American energy dominance as well as enabling advancements in AI.' Heinrich: 'ensure that costs are allocated fairly so that households aren't left covering the increased demand from large new energy users.'

letters_and_statements.title: New Democrat Coalition letter to House appropriators requesting FY2027 report language directing DOE to develop a National Strategic Data Center Plan
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Fourteen New Democrats asked the Energy-Water appropriations leaders to direct DOE, with Commerce, DHS, FERC and EPA, to produce an 18-month national plan on data center electricity demand, grid reliability and consumer cost impacts, water efficiency and geographic diversification, framing data centers as vital but in need of managed growth.
letters_and_statements.notes: Addressed to Chairman Tom Cole, Ranking Member Rosa DeLauro, Subcommittee Chair Chuck Fleischmann and Ranking Member Marcy Kaptur. Signers extracted from the PDF.

letters_and_statements.title: Senator Markey letter to EPA Administrator Zeldin opposing pre-construction of data centers without Clean Air Act NSR permits
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Markey objected to EPA's reinterpretation letting data centers and their gas generation begin construction before securing New Source Review air permits, calling it likely unlawful and harmful to communities.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter PDF: markey.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/ai_caa_nsr_letter.pdf. Markey also hosted a July 2025 roundtable, 'The Data Center Next Door.'

letters_and_statements.title: Markey-McClellan bicameral letter to EPA urging withdrawal of proposed rule letting data centers and power plants begin construction before air permits
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Sixteen lawmakers told EPA to withdraw its May 2026 proposal redefining 'begin actual construction' so data centers and fossil plants can pour foundations and install wiring before New Source Review permits, saying it turns the Clean Air Act's preconstruction safeguards 'on its head.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter dated June 29, 2026 per Markey site PDF. EPA finalized permitting guidance expanding islanded generation for data centers on July 27, 2026 (EPA release).

letters_and_statements.title: Reps. Dwight Evans and Madeleine Dean letter to FERC on oversight of data center power demand
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Two Pennsylvania Democrats asked FERC how it is overseeing rising data center demand, grid reliability (including NERC's large-load alert) and costs passed to home consumers, and how the administration's cancellation of clean energy projects affects supply; answers requested by June 30, 2026.
letters_and_statements.notes: Press release page returned 'Access Denied' to automated fetching; details confirmed from the release excerpt indexed by search engines and Center Square coverage (June 2, 2026).

letters_and_statements.title: Senator Jon Ossoff letter to FERC Chairman Swett opening an inquiry into AI data centers' impact on Georgia power bills
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Ossoff told FERC his office is investigating how the AI data center boom is driving up Georgians' power bills and asked the commission for information and action; Georgia PSC commissioners replied with their own letter to FERC a week later.
letters_and_statements.notes: PDF exists (opened in browser, title '26.04.20 Letter to FERC finalized') but text could not be extracted; contents summarized from the indexed excerpt ('My office is investigating AI data centers' impact on rising power bills in Georgia and nationwide') and coverage by 11Alive, USA Today and Broadband Breakfast (Apr 20-24, 2026). Ossoff is up for re-election in 2026.

letters_and_statements.title: Rep. Frank Pallone opening statement endorsing a national AI data center moratorium at E&C Energy Subcommittee markup
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The top Democrat on House Energy and Commerce said the eight data center bills being marked up were 'a useful first step' but that he favors 'a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don't harm our nation's air, water, and power bills.'
letters_and_statements.notes: First senior mainstream Democrat to back a moratorium; The Hill and E&E News covered it June 24, 2026. Pallone reiterated at the July 21 full-committee markup that a moratorium may be needed if guardrails are not enacted.

letters_and_statements.title: Senator Dave McCormick's Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit with President Trump (pro-data-center statement)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: McCormick convened energy and AI executives at Carnegie Mellon with President Trump and touted more than $90 billion in announced investments in data centers, gas plants, nuclear uprates, hydropower and grid upgrades, positioning Pennsylvania to 'power the AI and energy revolution.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Announcements included Blackstone $25B data center/energy in NE Pennsylvania, CoreWeave $6B Lancaster data center, PPL $6.8B grid buildout for data centers, Constellation Limerick uprate, Westinghouse 10 reactors by 2030. McCormick held a second summit in July 2026 and released an 'American AI' vision July 29, 2026. Coded fewer_rules as a pro-buildout, deregulatory-aligned event.

letters_and_statements.title: Senator Jon Husted statement at White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge roundtable and on codifying it
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Husted joined President Trump as Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Oracle and xAI signed a voluntary pledge to pay the full cost of energy and infrastructure for new data centers; he later introduced S.5028 to codify key elements, saying America must build AI energy infrastructure 'without passing the costs on to working families.'
letters_and_statements.notes: The pledge itself is Proclamation 11014 of March 4, 2026 (91 Fed. Reg. 11439); the White House said on July 23, 2026 the coalition grew to 187 organizations including 23 Republican governors (POWER Magazine). Husted's opponent Sherrod Brown attacks him over data center costs.

data_centers.coverage_notes: METHOD: The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the first ~14 queries, and congress.gov blocks automated fetches (Cloudflare), so bill facts were verified from the GPO govinfo BILLSTATUS bulk XML (the same Library of Congress data feed congress.gov displays; downloaded all 18,244 119th-Congress bill status files plus 118th hr/s) and govinfo bill texts. I grepped every 119th bill title, official title, CRS summary and subject term for 'data center', 'large load', 'ratepayer', 'PJM', 'co-location', 'AI + energy/grid/nuclear', 'federal land', NEPA/permitting; 40 bills have 'data center' in a title, and all are covered above. Senate.gov and some house.gov pages block curl/WebFetch; I read them through the user's Chrome browser (Markey, Sanders, Husted, Van Hollen, Booker, Reed, Welch, Warnock, Warren, Hawley, Lummis, Schiff, Heinrich/ENR, McCormick, Beyer, Pallone, E&C Democrats). The SPEED Act roll call (356) was read directly from clerk.house.gov. STATUS DATE: all statuses and cosponsor counts are as of GPO data updated Sept 8-12, 2026. PENDING: House GOP leaders told Reuters/Bloomberg Government (Sept 10, 2026) that H.R. 9340 gets a suspension floor vote the week of Sept 14; that vote had not occurred as of Sept 12. NOT CONFIRMED FROM PRIMARY PAGES (flagged, not asserted): the 15-4 ENR committee tally for S.4753 (2024); the Senate concurrence vote tally for S.870/ADVANCE Act (June 18, 2024); an E&C GOP May 20, 2026 letter authored by Chairs Guthrie and Jason Smith on AI data center electricity demand (appears on energycommerce.house.gov member pages but I could not open it); the House FY2027 NDAA provision by Rep. Cory Mills barring DoD land leases for data centers containing adversary-made components (reported by Federal News Network/E&E, July 2026, pages blocked); the E&C Environment Subcommittee's Sept 3, 2026 hearing on a discussion draft barring water utilities from recovering data center costs from other customers (Roll Call); Chairman Guthrie's July 22, 2026 'POWER Act' permitting discussion draft (NACo); Warren's June 15, 2026 letters to private equity firms on data center investments (banking.senate.gov, not opened). EXCLUDED as out of lane or not data-center-specific: H.R.3616 Reliable Power Act (passed House 225-203, Dec 17, 2025) and H.R.3632 Power Plant Reliability Act (passed House 222-202, Dec 16, 2025), grid-reliability bills passed alongside the SPEED Act; S.1894/H.R.4059 'SPEED Act' (MAP-21 categorical exclusions); S.3839 Cotton (preempting state climate mandates); H.R.5896 Van Drew GRID Act (EV charging); H.R.9700 Kaptur (utility misconduct); H.R.10261 Fitzpatrick Edgely Act (NEPA, no data center text); H.R.6275/S.5382 China AI Power Report Act (AI capability, not electricity); 118th S.933/H.R.5218 Federal Data Center Enhancement Act (federal IT efficiency); H.R.1 reconciliation (state AI-law moratorium, separate lane). POSSIBLE GAPS: bills whose titles and CRS summaries never say 'data center' (e.g., generic transmission or nuclear bills motivated by AI demand) may be missed; no 119th bill explicitly pairing nuclear power with AI data centers was found by title or summary, so 'nuclear for AI' is represented only by the enacted 118th ADVANCE Act and the Westinghouse/Constellation announcements at McCormick's summit. Letters were found via senate.gov/house.gov searches and news coverage; Republican-led letters to FERC/PJM/utilities on data center costs were searched for but none was found beyond the Lee-Heinrich and Warren-Hawley bipartisan letters and the unconfirmed Guthrie-Smith letter. Cosponsor lists above are complete for bills with 15 or fewer cosponsors and complete (42) for H.R. 9340; direction codes reflect whether backing the item signals wanting more guardrails on data center/AI buildout (cost-shifting rules, disclosure, moratoria, local control) versus fewer rules (permitting streamlining, litigation shields, off-grid deregulation, pro-buildout events).

bills.short_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (House-passed version, Sec. 43201(c) 10-year AI moratorium)
bills.sponsor: Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX-19) (reconciliation vehicle; AI title drafted by House Energy and Commerce under Chair Brett Guthrie (R-KY))
bills.plain_english: The House-passed budget bill contained a 10-year ban on states enforcing laws that regulate AI models, systems or automated decision systems. The Senate removed that ban 99-1 before the bill became law.
bills.notes: House-engrossed text Sec. 43201 'Artificial intelligence and information technology modernization initiative', subsection (c) 'Moratorium', confirmed in govinfo EH text. House passed H.R.1 with the moratorium on May 22, 2025, Roll Call 145 (On Passage, 215-214; clerk.house.gov/Votes/2025145). Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene said June 3, 2025 she would have voted no had she known the moratorium was in it. In the Senate, Commerce Chair Cruz rewrote it as a 5-year 'pause' tied to BEAD/$500M AI-infrastructure funds; a Cruz-Blackburn compromise collapsed June 30-July 1, 2025 and the Senate struck the section 99-1 (S.Amdt. 2814, Roll Call Vote 363, July 1, 2025). Enacted as Public Law 119-21 without any AI moratorium. Sponsor/cosponsor data is not a stance signal for this omnibus; the May 22 House passage vote and the Senate vote 363 are the on-the-record positions.
bills.status: Became Public Law 119-21 (July 4, 2025) with the AI moratorium removed by the Senate on July 1, 2025

bills.short_title: Blackburn amendment to strike the AI moratorium from H.R.1
bills.plain_english: An amendment that deleted the proposed multi-year ban on state AI laws from the Republican budget bill. It passed 99-1, with only Sen. Thom Tillis voting no.
bills.notes: Not a bill but the lane's key recorded vote. Senate Roll Call Vote 363, July 1, 2025, 4:08 AM, 'On the Amendment (Blackburn Amdt. No. 2814)', statement of purpose 'To strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence', Agreed to 99-1. Every senator voted Yea except Tillis (R-NC) Nay; Cruz himself voted Yea. Cosponsor names come from the Senate Commerce Democrats' release and Nextgov, not from the congress.gov amendment page (blocked to automated fetch). Cantwell and Markey had filed a strike-all amendment June 30 before joining Blackburn's on July 1.
bills.status: Agreed to 99-1 on July 1, 2025

bills.short_title: SANDBOX Act (Strengthening Artificial intelligence Normalization and Diffusion By Oversight and eXperimentation Act)
bills.plain_english: Lets AI companies ask the White House science office (OSTP) to waive or modify federal rules so they can test and sell AI products; waivers start at 2 years and can be renewed. It was the first bill of Cruz's five-pillar AI framework, which also calls for a single national standard over state AI laws.
bills.notes: Zero cosponsors as of the govinfo bill-status file updated 2026-09-08. Introduced with Cruz's Sept. 10, 2025 'AI Policy Framework' (commerce.senate.gov). The bill waives FEDERAL rules (initial 2-year waiver term per bill text; press describes renewals up to 10 years); it does not itself preempt state law, but it is the legislative piece of the framework whose preemption pillar Cruz has pursued via H.R.1 and the NDAA. The White House March 20, 2026 legislative framework endorsed regulatory sandboxes. Not marked up as of Sept. 2026; the Aug. 5, 2026 Commerce markup covered kids' online safety bills instead.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (Sept. 10, 2025); no further action

bills.short_title: American Artificial Intelligence Leadership and Uniformity Act
bills.plain_english: Would codify President Trump's AI executive order and bar states and localities for five years from enforcing laws that limit or regulate AI models and systems in interstate commerce, with carve-outs for generally applicable criminal law and state contracting. It is the only standalone House bill written to put AI preemption into statute.
bills.notes: Bill text Sec. 6 'State law preemption; temporary moratorium' imposes a 5-year moratorium (govinfo BILLS-119hr5388ih). Zero cosponsors as of bill-status file updated 2026-07-18. Referred to Science, Space and Technology plus 12 other committees; referred to Homeland Security's Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection Subcommittee (2025-09-17) and Veterans' Affairs O&I Subcommittee (2025-12-19). Baumgartner press release Sept. 19, 2025: 'we will lose that edge if we let California or Brussels write the rules for us.'
bills.status: Referred to committees/subcommittees; no hearing or markup as of Sept. 2026

bills.short_title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
bills.plain_english: Blocks federal funds from being used to carry out Executive Order 14365, the Dec. 11, 2025 order that set up a Justice Department task force to sue states over their AI laws and threatened broadband funding.
bills.notes: All 10 cosponsors joined Dec. 17, 2025. Markey also filed the text as an amendment to the Senate appropriations package (Markey release Dec. 17, 2025); no floor vote on that amendment was found. Markey's March 20, 2026 statement urged passage in response to the White House framework.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (Dec. 17, 2025)

bills.short_title: GUARDRAILS Act (Guaranteeing and Upholding Americans' Right to Decide Responsible AI Laws and Standards Act)
bills.plain_english: Repeals Executive Order 14365 so that states keep the power to pass and enforce their own AI safety laws until Congress enacts federal protections.
bills.notes: 35 cosponsors total, all Democrats; introduced the same day the White House released its legislative framework. Senate companion S.4216 (Schatz). Beyer: the White House 'aims to kill state AI laws without setting even minimally acceptable federal guardrails.'
bills.status: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on the Judiciary (March 20, 2026); no further action

bills.short_title: GUARDRAILS Act (Senate companion)
bills.plain_english: Senate version of the bill to cancel the Dec. 11, 2025 executive order targeting state AI laws and to block federal money from implementing it.
bills.notes: Schatz press release dated March 27, 2026 describes 'a group of six senators'; govinfo lists five cosponsors, all joining March 26, 2026.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation (March 26, 2026)

bills.short_title: Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 (discussion draft)
bills.sponsor: Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA-23) and Rep. Lori Trahan (D-MA-3)
bills.plain_english: A 269-page bipartisan draft that would set federal safety, audit and disclosure rules for the biggest frontier AI developers, and in exchange would block states for three years from enforcing laws that specifically regulate the development of AI models (states could still regulate how AI is used). Released for comment, not yet introduced.
bills.notes: Draft released June 4, 2026; no bill number because it has not been formally introduced (checked the 119th bill index through Sept. 10, 2026; no matching title). Preempts state laws 'specifically regulating the development of any artificial intelligence model' with a sunset in Dec. 2029; savings clauses for laws of general applicability and for deployment/use. Trahan: 'I will preempt, but only if we're setting the strongest possible federal standard.' Opposed on preemption by House Democrats including the House Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy (Lieu, Foushee, Gottheimer), the AFL-CIO, ACLU, Public Citizen and Americans for Responsible Innovation; criticized by some Republicans and the White House for not preempting enough (Global Policy Watch, July 7, 2026). 203 state lawmakers (104 D, 98 R, 1 I) wrote Congress June 16, 2026 opposing the preemption section. Majority Leader Scalise said June 9, 2026 he would look to E&C Chair Guthrie rather than Obernolte for AI legislation. Roll Call/Covington assessment: unlikely to advance as drafted in the 119th.
bills.status: Discussion draft, not introduced as of Sept. 12, 2026

bills.short_title: TRUMP AMERICA AI Act (discussion draft)
bills.plain_english: A roughly 291-page omnibus draft meant to codify the Dec. 11, 2025 executive order and create 'one federal rulebook' for AI, combining kids' safety duties, creator/copyright protections, anti-censorship audits, AI liability and workforce reporting; it preempts state law only title-by-title and in several places lets states go further. Still a draft.
bills.notes: Released as a discussion draft March 18, 2026 (Mintz; Global Policy Watch says it does not expressly preempt all state AI laws and explicitly allows stricter state rules in places). Blackburn's April 22, 2026 release still calls it a discussion draft; The Hill reported June 16, 2026 that Blackburn was negotiating text of an AI preemption package with the White House. No numbered bill found in the 119th bill index through Sept. 10, 2026. Blackburn was the senator who led the 99-1 strike of the H.R.1 moratorium, so her draft is the Republican attempt at preemption paired with guardrails.
bills.status: Discussion draft, not introduced as of Sept. 12, 2026

letters_and_statements.title: Matsui-led House Democratic letter to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and the planned executive order
letters_and_statements.plain_english: 81 House Democrats told congressional leaders not to revive the state AI-law moratorium in the defense bill and not to use an executive order or BEAD broadband money to override state AI laws, noting the Senate had already rejected the idea 99-1.
letters_and_statements.notes: 81 signatures extracted directly from the letter PDF (states added from public rosters; the letter itself lists names only). Key line: trying to revive the moratorium in the NDAA or by executive action 'is an attempt to quietly jam through an idea that has already been rejected.'

letters_and_statements.title: Clarke-led House Democratic letter to House and Senate Armed Services leaders urging no AI moratorium or preemption in the FY26 NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: 44 House Democrats asked the defense-bill negotiators to keep any state AI-law preemption or moratorium out of the NDAA, calling a moratorium 'wildly irresponsible given the lack of any federal legislation.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Clarke release says she 'led 43 of her colleagues' (44 signers). States added from public rosters.

letters_and_statements.title: Congressional Progressive Caucus official position opposing AI preemption or a moratorium in the NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The roughly 100-member Progressive Caucus voted by a super-majority to oppose attaching any state AI-law preemption or moratorium to the defense bill, saying state laws are consumers' only current protection from AI harms.
signers_or_speakers: Congressional Progressive Caucus (super-majority internal vote; no individual names published)
letters_and_statements.notes: Vote taken Nov. 25, 2025; statement released Nov. 26 (The Hill). Caucus statement, not an individual-signer letter.

letters_and_statements.title: Markey-Warren 'Dear Colleague' letter urging Senate Democrats to oppose any NDAA containing an AI moratorium
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Two senators asked all Senate Democrats to commit to voting against the defense bill if it included a ban on state AI laws: 'Congress should not give Big Tech a multi-year holiday from state oversight.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quoted in The Hill (Dec. 2, 2025) and referenced in Markey's Dec. 11 and Dec. 17, 2025 releases.

letters_and_statements.title: Cantwell and Senate Commerce Committee Democrats letter to Chairman Cruz demanding a markup of the reconciliation Commerce title, flagging the AI moratorium
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Twelve Commerce Committee Democrats told Cruz the AI moratorium 'tramples states' rights and holds the $42 billion BEAD program hostage' and asked for regular committee consideration instead of a fast-tracked floor vote.
letters_and_statements.notes: Release also notes a House Freedom Caucus memo of June 9, 2025 to Senate Republicans opposing the moratorium.

letters_and_statements.title: House Freedom Caucus memo/letter to Senate Republicans opposing the 10-year state AI-law moratorium in H.R.1
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Hard-line House conservatives told Senate Republicans that 'the federal government should not prevent states from being able to regulate artificial intelligence for the next 10 years,' calling AI something Congress 'does not fully understand.'
signers_or_speakers: House Freedom Caucus (individual signers not published in available sources)
letters_and_statements.notes: Quoted in the Senate Commerce Democrats' June 11, 2025 release and described by The Hill (June 18, 2025) as a letter from 'a group of hard-line conservatives' sent 'last week.' Primary copy not located; date is the Monday cited by the Cantwell release.

letters_and_statements.title: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene statements opposing the H.R.1 AI moratorium
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Greene said she did not know the 10-year state-preemption section was in the bill she voted for, called it 'a violation of state rights,' and said she would vote no on final passage if it stayed in: 'If you are destroying state rights, I'm out.'
letters_and_statements.notes: X post June 3, 2025 (The Hill via Yahoo); follow-up quotes to reporters in The Hill, June 18, 2025.

letters_and_statements.title: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene statement opposing AI preemption in the FY26 NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Greene wrote that 'there should not be a moratorium on states rights for AI' and that 'federalism must be preserved' as House GOP leaders weighed adding preemption to the defense bill.
letters_and_statements.notes: X post in late November 2025 quoted by The Hill (Dec. 2, 2025); exact posting date not confirmed from the primary post. The same article says Reps. Chip Roy (TX) and Thomas Massie (KY) 'previously have expressed concerns about AI preemption.'

letters_and_statements.title: Republican senators' June 2025 statements on the H.R.1 AI moratorium (Johnson, Hawley, Scott, Cornyn, Rounds, Cruz, Blackburn)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: As the Senate rewrote the budget bill, Sen. Ron Johnson said 'let the states experiment,' Sen. Hawley said he would offer an amendment to strip the moratorium, Sen. Rick Scott said he 'likes states' rights,' Sen. Cornyn wrote 'doubtful it survives,' Sen. Rounds said 'I support getting the moratorium in place,' Cruz defended it under the Commerce Clause, and Blackburn said 'until we pass something that is federally preemptive, we can't call for a moratorium.'
signers_or_speakers: Sen. Rick Scott (FL) - noncommittal, 'likes states' rights'
Sen. John Cornyn (TX) - skeptical it survives Byrd rule
Sen. Marsha Blackburn (TN) - opposed absent federal framework
letters_and_statements.notes: Individual directions noted per speaker; The Hill, June 18, 2025. Blackburn's quote is from a May 2025 Commerce hearing.

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ted Cruz statement defending the H.R.1 AI moratorium
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Cruz said the moratorium 'preserves the rights of states to protect consumers and content creators without giving the Left a backdoor to push their woke social agenda through AI regulation.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Statement shared with Nextgov before the July 1 vote; Cruz then voted Yea on the strike amendment after his compromise with Blackburn collapsed.

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn statement withdrawing from the Cruz compromise and moving to strike the moratorium
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Blackburn said the revised 5-year language 'is not acceptable to those who need these protections the most' and joined Cantwell, Collins and Markey to strike it entirely, citing 'kids, creators, and conservatives.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Also see Goodwin alert (July 3, 2025) on the collapse of the Cruz-Blackburn deal (5-year pause, $500M contingent funds, 'undue or disproportionate burden' exception).

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ed Markey and Sen. Maria Cantwell statements after the 99-1 vote
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Markey: the vote 'sent a clear message that Congress will not sell out our kids and local communities in order to pad the pockets of Big Tech billionaires.' Cantwell led the Democratic effort and Commerce Democrats' release credited a bipartisan coalition.
letters_and_statements.notes: Markey quote via Nextgov July 1, 2025; Commerce Democrats release July 1, 2025.

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ted Cruz AI Policy Framework announcement (five pillars incl. a national standard) with SANDBOX Act introduction
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Cruz released a light-touch AI framework and said 'executive orders alone aren't sufficient,' introducing the SANDBOX Act as its first bill; the framework's pillars include preempting the state 'patchwork.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Committee press release.

letters_and_statements.title: Rep. Michael Baumgartner statement introducing H.R.5388
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Baumgartner said America 'will lose that edge if we let California or Brussels write the rules for us' and framed his 5-year moratorium as codifying Trump's AI executive order.

letters_and_statements.title: House Majority Leader Scalise and Senate Majority Leader Thune remarks as NDAA preemption push stalled
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Scalise said the NDAA 'wasn't the best place' but leaders are 'still looking at other places' to block state AI laws 'like California'; Thune called preemption 'controversial' and said 'both sides are kind of dug in.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Scalise's position is fewer_rules; Thune's is neutral. This is the closest thing to a public whip read on the NDAA attempt: no majority support was ever demonstrated and the provision was dropped from the Dec. 7, 2025 conference text.

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Josh Hawley X post after preemption was dropped from the NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Hawley posted 'Good. This is a terrible provision and should remain OUT.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quoted by The Hill (Dec. 9, 2025), NPR (Dec. 11, 2025) and Fisher Phillips (Dec. 5, 2025).

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ted Cruz and Rep. Steve Scalise support for the Dec. 11, 2025 executive order on state AI laws
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Cruz posted on X that those who disagreed with Trump's planned order 'would cede ground to China' and stood beside Trump at the signing; Scalise backed the order and said Congress could 'codify some of the things the President is trying to do.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Cruz post Dec. 9, 2025; Scalise remarks Dec. 10, 2025; signing Dec. 11, 2025 (Executive Order 14365, 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence').

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ed Markey statement on the Dec. 11, 2025 executive order
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Markey said Big Tech 'has finally received the return on its ample investment in Donald Trump' and vowed to use 'every tool available to challenge this indefensible and irresponsible power grab.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Markey also issued a Dec. 8, 2025 statement when the order was announced and introduced S.3557 on Dec. 17.

letters_and_statements.title: Ranking Member Cantwell statement on the Dec. 11, 2025 executive order
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Cantwell said the order's 'overly broad preemption threatens states with lawsuits and funding cuts' and urged Congress to 'pass a bipartisan national AI framework that both leads on innovation and protects consumers.'

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Adam Schiff remarks against federal preemption of state AI protections
letters_and_statements.plain_english: At a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing Schiff said that 'in the absence of federal leadership, the states can and must exercise the power they have to protect their residents.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Schiff later cosponsored S.3557.

letters_and_statements.title: Johnson, Scalise, Guthrie, Jordan, Babin joint statement pledging to implement the White House National AI Framework
letters_and_statements.plain_english: House Republican leaders and three committee chairs said the Trump framework, which calls for preempting state AI laws, 'gives Congress a roadmap' and that House Republicans 'look forward to working across the aisle to enact a national framework.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Issued the day the White House released its Legislative Recommendations for a National Policy Framework for AI (calls for preempting state laws regulating AI development while preserving generally applicable and child-safety laws).

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn statements releasing the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act discussion draft
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Blackburn said Congress must create 'one federal rulebook for AI' to end the state patchwork, but paired preemption with duties of care, kids' protections and creator rights, and said she worked with the White House and child-safety advocates on legislation 'that can garner bipartisan support.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Draft released March 18, 2026; April 22, 2026 'What They Are Saying' release lists outside supporters only, no congressional cosponsors.

letters_and_statements.title: Sen. Ed Markey statement on the White House AI legislative framework
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Markey said Trump was 'proposing to block states from protecting their communities from AI-related harms' and urged Congress to pass his States' Right to Regulate AI Act instead.

letters_and_statements.title: Reps. Beyer, Matsui, Lieu, Jacobs and McClain Delaney statements introducing the GUARDRAILS Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Beyer said the White House 'aims to kill state AI laws without setting even minimally acceptable federal guardrails'; Lieu said 'any attempt by Donald Trump to create laws through executive order is a sham.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Quotes from Beyer and Lieu reported by Biometric Update; the five are the original H.R.8031 sponsors per the Beyer/Jacobs releases indexed by Bing.

letters_and_statements.title: Reps. Obernolte, Trahan, Franklin, Subramanyam, Houchin and Peters statements releasing the Great American AI Act discussion draft
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The six members framed the draft as a national standard for frontier AI development that preserves states' ability to protect children; Houchin said America should not 'regulate ourselves into falling behind China through a patchwork of fifty different state laws.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Trahan (Tech Policy Press, June 14, 2026): 'A preemption provision in a bill with no meaningful federal standard is a moratorium, and I won't sign onto that.'

letters_and_statements.title: House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy statement rejecting the Great American AI Act draft
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Democratic commission led by Reps. Lieu, Foushee and Gottheimer said the Obernolte-Trahan draft 'does not meet the enormity of the moment' and 'cannot serve as the basis for productive dialogue,' with preemption a central objection.
letters_and_statements.notes: Lieu said the commission will propose its own framework to Leader Jeffries by end of 2026. Same article: Scalise said June 9, 2026 'preemption at the federal level on bad local policies is something really important that we're looking at' and that he would look to E&C Chair Guthrie for AI legislation (fewer_rules).

letters_and_statements.title: House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence final report (118th Congress) - Federal Preemption of State Law chapter
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The 24-member bipartisan task force found that preempting state AI laws 'is complex,' has 'benefits and drawbacks,' can be done via floors or ceilings, and must use precise definitions; its only preemption recommendation was that Congress commission a study of existing federal and state AI regulations. It did not endorse a moratorium.
letters_and_statements.notes: Membership from the Feb. 20, 2024 Johnson/Jeffries announcement as reported by FedScoop (https://fedscoop.com/house-leaders-announce-new-bipartisan-ai-task-force/). Chapter 'Federal Preemption of State Law' at report pp. 23-30 (key findings p. 29, recommendation p. 30). The report is the main 118th-Congress artifact in this lane; several members later split (Obernolte/Franklin drafted GAAIA preemption; Lieu, Clarke, Beyer, Foushee, Jacobs, Bonamici, Foster, Bera, Ocasio-Cortez signed anti-preemption letters or cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act).
