preemption.coverage_notes: SEARCH SCOPE: Covered H.R.1 (House Sec. 43201(c) moratorium, Cruz 5-year rewrite, Blackburn Amdt. 2814 and Senate Roll Call Vote 363), the SANDBOX Act, Baumgartner's H.R.5388, Markey's S.3557, House/Senate GUARDRAILS Acts, the Obernolte-Trahan Great American AI Act draft, Blackburn's TRUMP AMERICA AI Act draft, the FY26 NDAA preemption attempt (Nov 17-Dec 7, 2025), Executive Order 14365 (Dec 11, 2025) and reactions, the White House Legislative Recommendations (Mar 20, 2026), and 2026 committee activity. Primary sources used: govinfo BILLSTATUS XML (cosponsors/status; congress.gov and govtrack returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches), senate.gov roll-call page, govinfo bill texts, clerk.house.gov XML (via cached file), member and committee press releases (commerce.senate.gov, markey.senate.gov, blackburn.senate.gov, speaker.gov, clarke/matsui/trahan/obernolte/baumgartner.house.gov), the Matsui letter PDF, the Task Force report PDF; secondary: The Hill, Roll Call, Nextgov, NPR, Politico headline, Global Policy Watch (Covington), Goodwin, Mintz, Fisher Phillips, Biometric Update, Tech Policy Press. A 119th-Congress bill index current through 2026-09-10 (18,244 bills) was keyword-scanned for preempt/moratorium/state-AI titles and summaries; the only in-lane numbered bills found are the six listed. That scan also confirms neither the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act nor the Great American AI Act had been formally introduced as of Sept 10, 2026. 2026 STATUS: No preemption bill has been marked up or voted on in either chamber in 2026. Senate Commerce's Aug 5, 2026 executive session (Cruz had floated an AI markup in July) advanced only kids' online safety bills (S.1748 KOSA, S.4407 CHATBOT Act, S.4199 Youth AI Privacy Act, S.5171 Children's AI Toy Safety Act, S.737 SCREEN Act), not the framework or SANDBOX Act. The Hill (Jun 16, 2026) reported Blackburn negotiating an AI preemption package with the White House; no text or bill number has appeared. Scalise (Jun 9, 2026) said House AI/preemption legislation would run through E&C Chair Guthrie. No published whip count exists; the only whip-like reads are Thune's Dec 2, 2025 'both sides dug in' and Covington/Roll Call's July 2026 assessment that GAAIA is unlikely to advance in the 119th. FY27 NDAA: I scanned the House Rules Committee pages for H.R.8800 (rules failed 198-224 on Jun 30, 2026; second rule adopted Jul 21, 2026) and found no AI-preemption amendment; the Senate FY27 NDAA was not checked. COULD NOT CONFIRM / MISSING: (1) No member-of-Congress-signed letter FOR preemption was found; pro-preemption positions are individual statements (Cruz, Scalise, Rounds, Baumgartner, Houchin) and the Mar 20, 2026 Johnson/Scalise/Guthrie/Jordan/Babin joint statement. (2) The House Freedom Caucus June 9, 2025 memo is documented only through the Cantwell release and The Hill; no primary copy or signer list. (3) Cosponsors of S.Amdt.2814 (Cantwell, Collins, Markey) come from press releases, not the congress.gov amendment page. (4) House Roll Call 145 tally (215-214) is from the clerk XML yea total plus contemporaneous reporting. (5) No 2026 Hawley or Blackburn letter on preemption located; no Senate Democratic letter to Trump on the EO located beyond individual statements. (6) Obernolte's and Guthrie's own Dec 2025 EO reactions not located (their sites block automated fetch). (7) Markey's S.3557 text was filed as an appropriations amendment; no roll call found. (8) Chip Roy and Thomas Massie opposition is sourced only to The Hill's characterization ('previously expressed concerns'). (9) The IAPP Nov 20, 2025 and Politico Jul 22/Aug 5, 2026 articles were paywalled/blocked. EXCLUDED AS NON-CONGRESSIONAL: letters from 260/280/290 state legislators (Jun/Nov 2025), 203 state lawmakers (Jun 16, 2026), 36-40 state attorneys general, 17 Republican governors (Jun 27, 2025), Texas state senators to Cruz/Cornyn (Nov 24, 2025), and Govs. DeSantis, Sanders and Cox statements. 118TH CONGRESS: No standalone bill to preempt state AI laws was found; the major item is the Dec 17, 2024 House Bipartisan AI Task Force report (listed under statements). Adjacent bills with their own preemption clauses (NO FAKES Act, KOSA, CHATBOT Act, App Store Accountability Act) belong to the deepfakes and kids-safety lanes and were not enumerated here. Also noted for other lanes: Sept 10-12, 2026 letters urging Speaker Johnson to act on AI-risk warnings (Axios/Punchbowl) are AI-risk-control items, not preemption.

bills.short_title: Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA)
bills.status: Ordered reported favorably with an amendment in the nature of a substitute by Senate Commerce, 2026-08-05 (voice vote per sponsors' statement); awaiting floor action
bills.plain_english: Makes big platforms used by kids under 17 take reasonable care to prevent harms like addiction, bullying and sexual exploitation, turn on the strongest privacy settings by default, and give parents controls; enforced by the FTC. Supporting it signals wanting stronger federal rules on Big Tech.
bills.notes: 76 cosponsors (bipartisan, includes both party leaders). Senate version keeps the 'duty of care' the House version drops. Predecessor passed Senate 91-3 in July 2024 as part of S.2073 (118th). Data: LOC BILLSTATUS via govinfo.

bills.short_title: Kids Online Safety Act (House / Energy and Commerce version)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade Subcommittee to full committee (amended) by 13-10 party-line vote, 2025-12-11; later folded into H.R.7757 (KIDS Act)
bills.plain_english: House Republicans' narrower rewrite of KOSA: platforms must have policies to prevent a shorter list of specific harms to minors and offer safeguards, but the Senate's broad 'duty of care' is removed and state laws are preempted. Supporting it signals wanting some federal kids-safety rules, but a lighter-touch version than the Senate bill.
bills.notes: Zero cosponsors. Subcommittee vote 13-10 was party line; Ranking Member Pallone (D-NJ) voted no citing weaker knowledge standard and broad preemption (Roll Call, 2025-12-11). Sens. Blumenthal and Blackburn criticized it as weaker than the Senate bill.

bills.short_title: Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act (KIDS Act)
bills.status: Passed House 267-117 under suspension (Roll no. 228), 2026-06-29; received in Senate and referred to Commerce, 2026-07-13
bills.plain_english: House package combining 14 kids-online-safety bills: age checks for porn-heavy sites (SCREEN Act), parental controls and default protections on social media and video games, a ban on disappearing messages for minors, AI chatbots must tell minors they are not human and show crisis-hotline info (SAFE BOTs/AWARE), plus a data-broker registry and kids' privacy protections added in the June 2026 Guthrie-Pallone compromise. It drops KOSA's 'duty of care', so supporting it signals backing federal kids' rules but a lighter version than the Senate's; opponents came from both progressives (too weak, preemption) and libertarian Republicans (too much regulation).
bills.notes: Roll call 228 breakdown (govtrack CSV): Yea 163 R + 104 D; Nay 32 R + 85 D; Not voting 24 R + 23 D. Nays (R): McClintock, Gosar, Schweikert, Austin Scott, Andy Harris, DesJarlais, Massie, Perry, Loudermilk, Davidson, Biggs, Arrington, Norman, Cloud, Fulcher, Burchett, Roy, Barry Moore, Boebert, Clyde, Crane, Luna, Rich McCormick, Burlison, Ogles, Self, Hageman, Downing, Mark Harris, Harrigan, Gill, Patronis. Nays (D): Bishop, Danny Davis, DeLauro, Doggett, Larson, McGovern, Bobby Scott, Adam Smith, Velazquez, Gwen Moore, Matsui, Courtney, Hank Johnson, Clarke, Carson, Pingree, Titus, Bonamici, Huffman, Ruiz, Takano, Vargas, Meng, Pocan, DeSaulnier, Watson Coleman, Boyle, Beyer, Evans, Khanna, Krishnamoorthi, Raskin, Espaillat, Jayapal, Scanlon, Stanton, Harder, Neguse, Crow, McBath, Chuy Garcia, Casten, Underwood, Pressley, Stevens, Tlaib, Omar, Ocasio-Cortez, Escobar, Golden, Jacobs, Nikema Williams, Leger Fernandez, Ritchie Torres, Pat Ryan, Frost, Tokuda, Jonathan Jackson, McGarvey, Ivey, Thanedar, Foushee, Hoyle, Salinas, Summer Lee, Deluzio, Crockett, Casar, Balint, McIver, Ansari, Simon, Whitesides, Friedman, Min, McBride, Bell, Goodlander, Latimer, Dexter, Bynum, Subramanyam, Randall, Adelita Grijalva, Mejia. Component titles per LOC: SCREEN Act, SAFE BOTs Act, Kids Online Safety Act, SPY Kids Act, Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act, Safe Social Media Act, No Fentanyl on Social Media Act, Assessing Safety Tools for Parents and Minors Act, Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act, AWARE Act. Full committee advanced it in March 2026 on a party-line vote per Roll Call (tally not confirmed).

bills.short_title: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0)
bills.status: Passed Senate with amendments by unanimous consent, 2026-03-05; held at the desk in the House since 2026-03-16
bills.plain_english: Updates the 1998 children's privacy law: bans targeted ads to kids and teens under 17, adds an 'eraser button' to delete data, and requires consent before collecting data from 13-16 year olds. Supporting it signals wanting stronger privacy rules for tech companies.
bills.notes: 21 cosponsors. Ordered reported by Senate Commerce 2025-06-25; reported 2026-01-27 (S. Rept. 119-99). Senate-passed version has not been taken up by the House.

bills.short_title: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (House version)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee to full committee by 14-10 vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: House Republican version of COPPA 2.0 that strengthens kids' and teens' data protections but broadly preempts state privacy laws; Democrats on the panel called it too friendly to Big Tech because of the preemption. Supporting it signals backing federal kids' privacy rules in exchange for overriding state laws.
bills.notes: Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL) objected at the 2025-12-11 markup that it would preempt state children's privacy and consumer-protection laws (Roll Call). Kids' privacy provisions were later added to the KIDS Act compromise.

bills.short_title: App Store Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-05-01; no further action
bills.plain_english: Requires Apple and Google app stores to verify users' ages and get verifiable parental consent before minors can download apps or make in-app purchases. Supporting it signals wanting a new federal age-verification mandate on Big Tech.
bills.notes: No Senate cosponsors as of LOC data. Modeled on Utah and Texas state laws; Pinterest endorsed it (Dec 2025 Lee release). House companion is H.R.3149.

bills.short_title: App Store Accountability Act (House)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee to full committee (amended) by voice vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: House companion requiring app stores to age-verify users and get parental consent for minors' downloads. Supporting it signals wanting an age-verification mandate on app stores.
bills.notes: Part of the 18-bill E&C kids' safety subcommittee markup on 2025-12-11.

bills.short_title: Kids Off Social Media Act (KOSMA)
bills.status: Reported by Senate Commerce without amendment, 2025-06-30 (S. Rept. 119-33); on Senate calendar
bills.plain_english: Bans social media accounts for kids under 13, bars algorithmic feeds for users under 17, and limits social media use in schools receiving E-Rate funds. Supporting it signals wanting hard federal limits on how platforms treat minors.
bills.notes: Chairman Cruz chose it as the Commerce Committee's first markup of the 119th Congress (2025-02-05). House versions by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna: H.R.7399 (2026-02-05) and H.R.7433 (2026-02-09, cosponsor Kim Schrier).

bills.short_title: Kids Off Social Media Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-02-09
bills.plain_english: House companion to the Senate bill banning under-13 social media accounts and algorithmic feeds for minors. Supporting it signals wanting hard limits on platforms' treatment of kids.
bills.notes: Luna also introduced an earlier H.R.7399 on 2026-02-05 with no cosponsors.

bills.short_title: SCREEN Act (Shielding Children's Retinas from Egregious Exposure on the Net)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce; considered at the 2026-08-05 markup but not reported (see notes)
bills.plain_english: Requires websites with content 'harmful to minors' (mainly porn sites) to use real age-verification technology, not self-attestation, and to check VPN traffic. Supporting it signals wanting a federal age-verification mandate for adult content.
bills.notes: A secondary source (cunicula.com) reports the Commerce Committee voted 15-13 for it on 2026-08-05 but the bill did not advance for lack of a quorum; LOC data shows no reported action, so the vote detail is unconfirmed. Its text is included in the House-passed KIDS Act (H.R.7757).

bills.short_title: GUARD Act (Guidelines for User Age-verification and Responsible Dialogue)
bills.status: Ordered reported by Senate Judiciary with substitute amendment, 2026-04-30; reported 2026-05-11 (Calendar No. 406)
bills.plain_english: Bans AI 'companion' chatbots for minors, requires age verification for chatbot access, makes chatbots repeatedly disclose they are not human, and creates criminal penalties for chatbots that solicit sexual content from or encourage self-harm by minors. Supporting it signals wanting strict federal rules on AI chatbot companies.
bills.notes: 20 cosponsors, bipartisan. Judiciary advanced it unanimously per secondary reports. House companion H.R.8623 (Blake Moore).

bills.short_title: GUARD Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary and Energy and Commerce, 2026-04-30
bills.plain_english: House companion to Hawley's bill banning AI companion chatbots for minors and requiring age verification and disclosures. Supporting it signals wanting strict rules on chatbot companies.
bills.notes: Same short title as S.3062; long title confirms it is the age-verification chatbot bill.

bills.short_title: CHAT Act (Children Harmed by AI Technology Act)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-09-04
bills.plain_english: Requires AI companion chatbots to verify ages, get parental consent for minors, block sexual content for minors, and alert parents when a minor discusses suicide. Supporting it signals wanting new federal rules on chatbot companies.
bills.notes: Superseded by Husted-Kim CHAT Act 2.0 (S.5154). House version H.R.7218 (Lawler).

bills.short_title: CHAT Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-01-22
bills.plain_english: House companion requiring AI chatbots to verify ages and add protections for minors.
bills.notes: No cosponsors in LOC data.

bills.short_title: CHAT Act 2.0
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-07-28
bills.plain_english: Bipartisan rewrite requiring companion-chatbot companies to take reasonable steps so their bots do not encourage self-harm, engage minors sexually, pretend to be human or licensed professionals, or foster emotional dependency; FTC and state AGs enforce. Supporting it signals wanting a federal framework regulating AI companions.
bills.notes: Tiered, risk-based approach per Husted release; builds on S.2714.

bills.short_title: CHATBOT Act (Children's Health, Advancement, Trust, Boundaries, and Oversight in Technology Act)
bills.status: Ordered reported favorably with substitute by Senate Commerce, 2026-08-05
bills.plain_english: Requires AI chatbot services to put children under 13 on family accounts, get verifiable parental consent for teens, and bans targeted advertising to kids and teens based on chatbot data. Supporting it signals wanting federal rules on how chatbot companies treat minors.
bills.notes: Commerce Chairman Cruz's chatbot bill; advanced at the same 2026-08-05 markup as KOSA. A House bill with the same acronym, H.R.7985 (Mullin), has different content.

bills.short_title: CHATBOT Act (House, Mullin)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-03-18
bills.plain_english: Prohibits AI chatbots from marketing or providing professional services (like therapy or legal advice) without the appropriate licenses. Supporting it signals wanting consumer-protection limits on chatbots.
bills.notes: Different substance from Cruz's S.4407 despite same acronym.

bills.short_title: Youth AI Privacy Act
bills.status: Ordered reported favorably with substitute by Senate Commerce, 2026-08-05
bills.plain_english: Requires companies that let minors use AI chatbots to build in safe-design features and limit collection and use of minors' personal data. Supporting it signals wanting privacy and design rules on AI chatbot companies.
bills.notes: No cosponsors in LOC data but advanced by committee at the Aug 5, 2026 markup.

bills.short_title: SAFE KIDS Act (Safeguarding AI Features to Ensure Kids' Informed Digital Safety)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-06-23
bills.plain_english: Requires AI chatbot providers to design for child safety, offer parental settings, undergo independent audits, and bans targeted ads to children and sale of their data. Supporting it signals wanting new obligations on AI companies.

bills.short_title: AWARE Act (AI Warnings And Resources for Education)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee (substitute) by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Directs the FTC to publish educational resources for parents, teachers and kids on safe use of AI chatbots. It is an awareness measure rather than a mandate on companies.

bills.short_title: SAFE BOTs Act (Safeguarding Adolescents From Exploitative BOTs)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Requires chatbots used by minors to clearly disclose they are AI, not a person, to never claim to be a licensed professional, and to surface suicide and crisis hotline information. Supporting it signals wanting disclosure rules on chatbot companies.
bills.notes: Its text is the chatbot section of the House-passed KIDS Act.

bills.short_title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered reported favorably with substitute by Senate Commerce, 2026-08-05
bills.plain_english: Orders a federal study of AI-enabled toys and a joint action plan on how they are marketed and sold to children. A study bill rather than a mandate.

bills.short_title: Ban on AI chatbots in children's toys (no short title)
bills.status: Referred; sponsor introductory remarks 2026-04-21
bills.plain_english: Prohibits manufacturing or selling children's toys or child-care articles that contain an AI chatbot, enforced under the Consumer Product Safety Act. Supporting it signals wanting a hard product ban.

bills.short_title: Sammy's Law
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: Forces large social media platforms to open real-time APIs so parents can plug in third-party child-safety software to monitor and manage their kids' accounts. Supporting it signals wanting an interoperability mandate on platforms for child safety.
bills.notes: 22 bipartisan cosponsors. Named for Sammy Chapman, who died after buying fentanyl-laced drugs via Snapchat.

bills.short_title: Sammy's Law (Senate)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-03-20
bills.plain_english: Senate companion requiring big platforms to give parents' safety apps API access to their children's accounts.

bills.short_title: Digital Age Assurance Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-07-22
bills.plain_english: Makes operating-system providers (Apple, Google, Microsoft) collect users' ages and send an age-bracket signal that apps, websites and browsers must request, so services know when a user is a minor. Supporting it signals wanting a device-level age-verification system.

bills.short_title: Parents Over Platforms Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-04-20
bills.plain_english: Sets age-assurance rules across the mobile ecosystem (app stores, operating systems, apps) to protect minors. Supporting it signals wanting age-verification obligations on tech companies.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.6333.

bills.short_title: Parents Over Platforms Act (House)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: House version of the mobile-ecosystem age-assurance bill.

bills.short_title: Promoting a Safe Internet for Minors Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Amends the children's privacy law to add online-safety protections for minors.

bills.short_title: Kids Internet Safety Partnership Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Creates a Commerce Department partnership to develop best practices for kids' online safety. A soft, non-mandate measure.

bills.short_title: SPY Kids Act (Stop Profiling Youth and Kids)
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee (substitute) by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Prohibits market or product-focused research on children and minors by online platforms.

bills.short_title: Safe Social Media Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Requires an FTC study of teenagers' social media use.

bills.short_title: Assessing Safety Tools for Parents and Minors Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11; folded into KIDS Act
bills.plain_english: Requires an FTC report on industry efforts to protect minors online.

bills.short_title: SMK Act of 2025
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: Bans disappearing-message features for minors and requires parental controls over who can direct-message a minor on social media.
bills.notes: Ephemeral-messaging ban for minors appears in the KIDS Act summary.

bills.short_title: Algorithmic Transparency and Choice Act
bills.status: Forwarded by E&C subcommittee by voice vote, 2025-12-11
bills.plain_english: Requires platforms to tell minors when a personalized recommendation algorithm is choosing their content and to offer a non-personalized option.

bills.short_title: Parental Approval for Youth Social Media Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-08-04
bills.plain_english: Requires social media platforms to get parental consent before children can create or keep accounts.

bills.short_title: STOP CSAM Act of 2025
bills.status: Reported by Senate Judiciary with substitute, 2025-06-26 (Calendar No. 106)
bills.plain_english: Lets victims of child sexual abuse material sue platforms that knowingly host or promote it, carving an exception out of Section 230 immunity, and adds reporting duties and penalties. Supporting it signals wanting to narrow Big Tech's liability shield.
bills.notes: 28 cosponsors. Hawley/Durbin cite unanimous committee passage. House companion H.R.3921 (Barry Moore, 28 cosponsors). Encryption advocates oppose.

bills.short_title: STOP CSAM Act of 2025 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-06-11
bills.plain_english: House companion letting CSAM victims sue platforms and narrowing Section 230.
bills.notes: 28 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-07-22
bills.plain_english: Has NIST develop a framework for detecting, removing and reporting child sexual abuse material in the datasets used to train AI models.

bills.short_title: Sunset Section 230 Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-12-17
bills.plain_english: Repeals Section 230, the law shielding platforms from lawsuits over user content, two years after enactment to force Congress to write a replacement and let people harmed online sue companies. Supporting it signals wanting to strip Big Tech's liability shield.
bills.notes: All nine cosponsors are original. Judiciary Chair Grassley and Ranking Member Durbin both on it. Sen. Wyden (D-OR), Section 230's author, continues to defend the law (KLCC interview, Feb 2026).

bills.short_title: Sunset Section 230 Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-09-10
bills.plain_english: House companion repealing Section 230.
bills.notes: Introduced two days before this research date.

bills.short_title: Sunset To Reform Section 230 Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2025-12-16
bills.plain_english: Makes Section 230 expire after December 31, 2026 unless Congress reforms it.
bills.notes: Text confirmed on govinfo: adds subsection (g) sunset.

bills.short_title: Algorithm Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-11-18
bills.plain_english: Amends Section 230 so social media companies lose immunity unless they exercise reasonable care in designing recommendation algorithms to prevent foreseeable bodily injury or death. Supporting it signals wanting a duty of care on algorithms.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.6266 (Mike Kennedy R-UT-3, cosponsor April McClain Delaney D-MD-6).

bills.short_title: Deepfake Liability Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2025-12-01
bills.plain_english: Conditions Section 230 immunity on platforms running a reasonable process to address cyberstalking and intimate-image abuse, and broadens the TAKE IT DOWN Act's definition of sexually explicit digital forgeries. Supporting it signals wanting to narrow the liability shield for deepfake abuse.

bills.short_title: AI LEAD Act (Aligning Incentives for Leadership, Excellence, and Advancement in Development)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2025-09-29
bills.plain_english: Treats AI systems as products and creates a federal product-liability cause of action so developers and deployers can be sued for harms, voids unconscionable liability waivers, and requires foreign AI providers to register. Supporting it signals wanting AI companies to face lawsuits for harms.
bills.notes: Overlaps the AI-risk lane; included because it is the main AI liability vehicle from the Judiciary Committee's ranking member.

bills.short_title: American Innovation and Choice Online Act (AICOA)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2026-06-10
bills.plain_english: Bars dominant platforms like Amazon, Apple, Google and Meta from favoring their own products over rivals on their platforms (self-preferencing). Supporting it signals wanting tough antitrust rules on Big Tech.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of the 117th/118th Klobuchar-Grassley bill; now led by Judiciary Chair Grassley.

bills.short_title: Open App Markets Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2025-06-24
bills.plain_english: Forces Apple and Google to allow third-party app stores, sideloading and alternative payment systems, and bans punishing developers who offer cheaper prices elsewhere. Supporting it signals wanting antitrust rules on app-store gatekeepers.
bills.notes: Passed Judiciary in 2022 but never got a floor vote.

bills.short_title: App Store Freedom Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2025-05-06
bills.plain_english: Requires app stores with 100M+ US users to allow third-party app stores and payment systems, let users change defaults and delete pre-installed apps, and give developers equal access to tools. Supporting it signals wanting antitrust limits on Apple and Google.
bills.notes: A second identical-title bill, H.R.5313 (Russell Fry R-SC-7), was introduced 2025-09-11.

bills.short_title: Big Tech Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary and Energy and Commerce, 2026-09-04
bills.plain_english: Creates a federal crime for knowingly spreading fraudulent civic misinformation with liability for publishing entities that aid it, and aims to curb amplification of disinformation and commercial exploitation of personal data. Supporting it signals wanting strong new liabilities on platforms.
bills.notes: No cosponsors; brand new.

bills.short_title: Platform Accountability and Transparency Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-12-01
bills.plain_english: Requires large platforms to give vetted independent researchers privacy-protected access to internal data so outsiders can study platform harms. Supporting it signals wanting transparency mandates on Big Tech.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th S.1876.

bills.short_title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2025-09-19
bills.plain_english: Directs the FTC to require companies to run impact assessments on automated decision systems used for housing, jobs, credit and other critical decisions. Supporting it signals wanting oversight of AI decision-making.
bills.notes: 32 cosponsors, all Democrats. Senate companion S.2164 (Wyden; cosponsors Warren, Booker, Heinrich, Lujan, Merkley, Hirono, Schatz).

bills.short_title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (Senate)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-06-25
bills.plain_english: Senate version requiring FTC-mandated impact assessments of automated decision systems.

bills.short_title: Consumer Data Privacy and Security Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-03-25
bills.plain_english: A comprehensive federal consumer privacy law: companies may collect personal data only with consent or for permitted purposes, consumers get rights to know and control their data, with FTC enforcement and rules on how it relates to state laws. Supporting it signals wanting a national privacy standard.
bills.notes: No cosponsors. The closest thing to an APRA successor found in the 119th Senate; no ADPPA/APRA-style House bill was located (House E&C privacy working group has not filed a bill in LOC data).

bills.short_title: Online Privacy Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, Judiciary, and Science, 2026-03-19
bills.plain_english: Creates individual privacy rights, imposes data-security duties on companies, and establishes a new Digital Privacy Agency to enforce them. Supporting it signals wanting a strong federal privacy regulator.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of Lofgren-Eshoo bill; no cosponsors in LOC data.

bills.short_title: Data Care Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-12-18
bills.plain_english: Imposes fiduciary-style duties of care, loyalty and confidentiality on online services regarding user data. Supporting it signals wanting binding data obligations on tech companies.
bills.notes: 14 cosponsors, all Democrats/independents.

bills.short_title: DELETE Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-04-03
bills.plain_english: Creates a one-stop system for people to demand all data brokers delete their personal information. Supporting it signals wanting privacy rules on the data-broker industry.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.2612 (Lori Trahan D-MA-3).

bills.short_title: AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2025-07-21
bills.plain_english: Creates a federal tort letting individuals sue anyone who uses their personal data or creative works without express prior consent, explicitly including training generative AI models. Supporting it signals wanting AI companies to face liability for scraping data and copyrighted works.
bills.notes: Introduced after the Hawley-led Judiciary subcommittee hearing 'Too Big to Prosecute?' on AI training on copyrighted works (S.Hrg. 119-202).

bills.short_title: People-First Chatbot Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-07-09
bills.plain_english: Requires AI chatbot providers to protect users' data privacy and security.

bills.short_title: Senior Chatbot Protection Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-07-23
bills.plain_english: Sets consumer transparency and protection requirements for AI chatbots, aimed at protecting older adults.

bills.short_title: AI Advertising Disclosure Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-08-24
bills.plain_english: Requires AI tools to disclose when their output is sponsored content or advertising.

bills.short_title: Online Consumer Protection Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2025-04-10
bills.plain_english: Requires social media platforms and online marketplaces to publish and follow consumer-protection policies in their terms of service, with FTC enforcement.

bills.short_title: TAKE IT DOWN Act
bills.status: Became Public Law 119-12, signed 2025-05-19
bills.plain_english: Makes it a federal crime to publish real or AI-generated intimate images of someone without consent, and requires platforms to remove such images within 48 hours of a victim's request, enforced by the FTC. Supporting it signals wanting binding takedown duties on platforms.
bills.notes: Passed Senate by UC 2025-02-13; passed House 409-2 on 2025-04-28 (Roll no. 104) with the only Nays from Reps. Thomas Massie (R-KY) and Eric Burlison (R-MO). Platform takedown duty became enforceable 2026-05-19; first criminal conviction 2026-04-09 per Commerce Committee release. Backed by First Lady Melania Trump.

bills.short_title: TAKE IT DOWN Act (House companion)
bills.status: Ordered reported by E&C 49-1, 2025-04-08; reported (H. Rept. 119-82) and placed on Union Calendar 2025-04-28; Senate bill S.146 was the enacted vehicle
bills.plain_english: House companion to the enacted TAKE IT DOWN Act.
bills.notes: 41 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits)
bills.status: Passed Senate by unanimous consent, 2026-01-13; held at the desk in the House
bills.plain_english: Gives victims of sexually explicit deepfakes a federal right to sue the people who create, distribute or solicit them. Supporting it signals wanting legal remedies against deepfake abuse.
bills.notes: Senate also passed the 118th version (S.3696) in July 2024; House has not acted either time. Reps. Ocasio-Cortez and Laurel Lee held a Jan 22, 2026 press event with Paris Hilton urging a House vote.

bills.short_title: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-05-21
bills.plain_english: House version creating a civil right of action for victims of sexually explicit deepfakes.
bills.notes: 65 bipartisan cosponsors.

bills.short_title: NO FAKES Act of 2026
bills.status: Ordered reported by Senate Judiciary with substitute, 2026-06-18; reported 2026-06-24 (Calendar No. 446)
bills.plain_english: Creates a federal right for every person to control AI 'digital replicas' of their voice and likeness, with liability for those who make or distribute unauthorized replicas and for platforms that knowingly host them, while preempting future state replica laws. Supporting it signals wanting new legal protections against AI impersonation.
bills.notes: 15 cosponsors. Supersedes S.1367 (2025 version). Backed by recording industry, SAG-AFTRA, and companies including OpenAI and YouTube per sponsors; some digital-rights groups oppose the notice-and-takedown provisions.

bills.short_title: NO FAKES Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2025-04-09; superseded by S.4591
bills.plain_english: Earlier 2025 version of the digital-replica rights bill.
bills.notes: 13 cosponsors; useful for cosponsorship tracking before the 2026 reintroduction.

bills.short_title: NO FAKES Act of 2026 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2026-05-20
bills.plain_english: House companion to the 2026 digital-replica rights bill.
bills.notes: Earlier 2025 House version H.R.2794 (Salazar; cosponsors Dean, Moran, Balint, Morelle, Laurel Lee, Susie Lee, Wittman, Friedman, Max Miller, Moskowitz).

bills.short_title: NO FAKES Act of 2025 (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-04-09; superseded by H.R.8915
bills.plain_english: Earlier House version of the digital-replica rights bill.

bills.short_title: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-03-06
bills.plain_english: Criminalizes sharing sexually explicit deepfakes without consent and gives victims a civil remedy. Supporting it signals wanting penalties for deepfake abuse.
bills.notes: 11 cosponsors; 118th version H.R.3106 had 59.

bills.short_title: Protect Victims of Digital Exploitation and Manipulation Act of 2025
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-04-01
bills.plain_english: Makes producing or distributing intimate digital forgeries of identifiable people a federal crime.
bills.notes: Mace also introduced H.R.2373 (Increased Accountability for Nonconsensual Pornography Act) on 2025-03-26.

bills.short_title: COPIED Act (Content Origin Protection and Integrity from Edited and Deepfaked Media Act of 2025)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-04-09
bills.plain_english: Requires AI tools to let creators attach provenance information (where content came from) and bans platforms from stripping it, giving creators a way to protect work from unauthorized AI use. Supporting it signals wanting provenance and labeling rules for AI content.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th S.4674; Cantwell is Commerce ranking member.

bills.short_title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
bills.status: Ordered to be reported (substitute) by committee 35-0, 2026-06-25
bills.plain_english: Has NIST create task forces to set standards for identifying AI-generated content and requires disclosures on AI-generated audio and video. Supporting it signals wanting labeling rules for AI content.
bills.notes: Which committee held the 35-0 vote was not confirmed (referred to E&C and Science). Earlier version H.R.8479 introduced 2026-04-23. 118th predecessor was Eshoo's H.R.7766.

bills.short_title: Spot the Fakes Act
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2026-07-02
bills.plain_english: Requires AI-generated content to carry an indelible AI label in its metadata, with FTC enforcement.

bills.short_title: TRAIN Act (Transparency and Responsibility for Artificial Intelligence Networks)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2025-07-24
bills.plain_english: Lets copyright owners use an administrative subpoena to find out whether their works were used to train an AI model. Supporting it signals wanting transparency obligations on AI developers.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th S.5379. Blackburn and Welch held an artists' roundtable for it on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: CLEAR Act (Copyright Labeling and Ethical AI Reporting)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2026-02-10
bills.plain_english: Requires AI developers to file a notice with the Copyright Office listing the copyrighted works used to build generative AI models. Supporting it signals wanting disclosure mandates on AI training data.
bills.notes: Senate successor to Schiff's 118th House bill, the Generative AI Copyright Disclosure Act (H.R.7913).

bills.short_title: CREATOR Act
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2026-06-02
bills.plain_english: Gives visual artists an exclusive right to authorize commercial use of AI 'stylistic impersonations' of their work. Supporting it signals wanting new rights for creators against AI.

bills.short_title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Rules and Administration, 2025-03-31
bills.plain_english: Bans knowingly distributing materially deceptive AI-generated audio or video of federal candidates to influence an election or raise money, with a carve-out for parody and news, and lets candidates sue to remove it. Supporting it signals wanting federal limits on election deepfakes.
bills.notes: 118th version S.2770 was reported by Rules in May 2024. House companion H.R.5272.

bills.short_title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act (House)
bills.status: Referred to House Administration, 2025-09-10
bills.plain_english: House companion banning deceptive AI media about federal candidates.

bills.short_title: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to House Administration, 2026-07-23
bills.plain_english: Requires political ads to include a disclaimer when images, audio or video were substantially generated by AI. Supporting it signals wanting disclosure rules for AI in campaigns.
bills.notes: No 119th Senate version found; 118th Senate version S.3875 (Klobuchar/Murkowski) was reported by Rules.

bills.short_title: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Rules and Administration, 2025-07-17
bills.plain_english: Has the Election Assistance Commission write voluntary guidelines for election officials on AI risks and uses. A guidance bill rather than a mandate on tech companies.

bills.short_title: FAIR Elections Act (Fraudulent Artificial Intelligence Regulations)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Rules and Administration, 2026-06-11
bills.plain_english: Prohibits distributing false AI-generated election media and bars voter-roll purges based on unverified challenge databases. Supporting it signals wanting limits on AI in elections.
bills.notes: Democratic-only cosponsors.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2025-12-16
bills.plain_english: Targets fraud enabled by AI, such as voice-clone scams.

bills.short_title: AI Fraud Accountability Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2026-03-04
bills.plain_english: Creates protections against digital impersonation fraud using AI.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.7786 (Vern Buchanan R-FL-16; cosponsors Darren Soto, Jefferson Van Drew).

bills.short_title: AI Fraud Deterrence Act
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2025-11-25
bills.plain_english: Increases criminal penalties for financial crimes committed using AI.

bills.short_title: SAFE AI Act (Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, 2026-07-21
bills.plain_english: Prohibits federal agencies from using certain AI image and video generation models (those tied to fabricated sexual exploitation content) across the federal government.
bills.notes: Bill text confirms it covers models that generate realistic image or video outputs; exact model criteria not fully reviewed.

bills.short_title: Kids Online Safety Act (118th)
bills.status: Reported by Senate Commerce with substitute, 2023-12-13; text passed Senate 91-3 via S.2073 in July 2024; House never voted
bills.plain_english: Original KOSA with a duty of care on platforms toward minors. Supporting it signaled wanting strong federal rules on Big Tech.
bills.notes: 72 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: Kids Online Safety and Privacy Act (KOSPA vehicle for KOSA + COPPA 2.0)
bills.status: Senate concurred in House amendment with amendment (KOSA + COPPA 2.0 text) by 91-3 (Record Vote 221), 2024-07-30; House never acted
bills.plain_english: The vehicle that carried KOSA and COPPA 2.0 through the Senate 91-3 in July 2024, the biggest Senate vote on tech regulation in decades. Voting yes signaled wanting strong federal kids' safety and privacy rules.
bills.notes: Vote 221 breakdown (govtrack): Yea 47 D + 44 R; Nay: Ron Wyden (D-OR), Rand Paul (R-KY), Mike Lee (R-UT); 6 not voting. Speaker Johnson declined to bring it up in the House.

bills.short_title: Kids Online Safety Act (118th House)
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by E&C by voice vote, 2024-09-18; no floor vote
bills.plain_english: The bipartisan 118th House KOSA that the full Energy and Commerce Committee advanced but leadership never brought to the floor.
bills.notes: 64 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0, 118th)
bills.status: Reported by Senate Commerce 2023-12-13; text passed Senate via S.2073 in July 2024
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the kids' privacy update (ad ban, eraser button, teen consent).
bills.notes: 22 cosponsors including then-ranking member Cruz.

bills.short_title: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (118th House)
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by E&C by voice vote, 2024-09-18
bills.plain_english: 118th House version of COPPA 2.0.
bills.notes: 28 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: American Privacy Rights Act of 2024 (APRA)
bills.status: Referred to House Energy and Commerce, 2024-06-25; never received a committee vote
bills.plain_english: The bipartisan comprehensive federal privacy bill negotiated by McMorris Rodgers and Sen. Cantwell: data minimization, consumer rights, a private right of action, and preemption of state laws. Supporting it signaled wanting a national privacy law.
bills.notes: Its full-committee markup was called off in late June 2024 (widely reported; not re-verified here). No numbered successor bill from the 119th House E&C privacy working group was found in LOC data.

bills.short_title: American Innovation and Choice Online Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2023-06-15; no action
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the anti-self-preferencing Big Tech antitrust bill.

bills.short_title: Journalism Competition and Preservation Act of 2023
bills.status: Reported by Senate Judiciary, 2023-07-18; no floor action
bills.plain_english: Lets news publishers collectively bargain with Google and Meta for payment for their content, an antitrust exemption aimed at Big Tech. Supporting it signaled wanting to rebalance power away from platforms.
bills.notes: 20 cosponsors. No 119th reintroduction found.

bills.short_title: DEFIANCE Act of 2024
bills.status: Passed Senate with amendment by voice vote, 2024-07-23; House did not act
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the deepfake civil-remedy bill, introduced after the Taylor Swift deepfake episode.

bills.short_title: TAKE IT DOWN Act (118th)
bills.status: Passed Senate with amendment by voice vote, 2024-12-03; House did not act before the 118th ended
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the nonconsensual-intimate-image takedown law later enacted as S.146 in 2025.
bills.notes: 20 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: NO FAKES Act of 2024
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2024-07-31
bills.plain_english: First formal NO FAKES bill creating a federal digital-replica right.
bills.notes: House version H.R.9551 (Salazar; cosponsors Dean, Moran, Morelle, Wittman, Schiff, Ferguson, Kustoff, DelBene, Smucker, Suozzi, Magaziner).

bills.short_title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act (118th)
bills.status: Reported by Senate Rules and Administration with substitute, 2024-05-15; no floor vote
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the election-deepfake ban; one of three AI election bills the Rules Committee advanced in May 2024.
bills.notes: House version H.R.8384 (Kilmer; cosponsors Gonzales, Houlahan, Fitzpatrick).

bills.short_title: AI Transparency in Elections Act of 2024
bills.status: Reported by Senate Rules and Administration with substitute, 2024-05-15
bills.plain_english: Requires disclaimers on political ads made with generative AI.

bills.short_title: Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act (118th)
bills.status: Reported by Senate Rules and Administration with substitute, 2024-05-15
bills.plain_english: Voluntary EAC guidance for election officials on AI.

bills.short_title: Generative AI Copyright Disclosure Act of 2024
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2024-04-09; no action
bills.plain_english: Would have required AI developers to file a notice with the Copyright Office listing copyrighted works used to train generative models. The direct ancestor of Schiff's 119th CLEAR Act.
bills.notes: No cosponsors in LOC data despite industry and union endorsements.

bills.short_title: TRAIN Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2024-11-21
bills.plain_english: First version of the copyright-owner subpoena bill for AI training data.

bills.short_title: Kids Off Social Media Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2024-04-30
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the under-13 ban and algorithmic-feed limits for minors.

bills.short_title: Protecting Kids on Social Media Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2023-04-26
bills.plain_english: Would have required age verification for social media, banned under-13 accounts, and required parental consent for teens.

bills.short_title: STOP CSAM Act of 2023
bills.status: Reported by Senate Judiciary with substitute, 2023-05-15; no floor vote
bills.plain_english: 118th version letting CSAM victims sue platforms and narrowing Section 230.

bills.short_title: EARN IT Act of 2023
bills.status: Reported by Senate Judiciary with amendments, 2023-05-15; no floor vote
bills.plain_english: Would have removed Section 230 immunity for platforms in child sexual abuse material cases and created a national commission on best practices. Supporting it signaled wanting to narrow the liability shield.
bills.notes: 24 cosponsors. No 119th reintroduction located in LOC/govtrack data.

bills.short_title: COPIED Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2024-07-11
bills.plain_english: First version of the content-provenance and anti-tampering bill.

bills.short_title: No AI FRAUD Act
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2024-01-10
bills.plain_english: Would have created a federal right against unauthorized AI clones of a person's voice and likeness; forerunner of the House NO FAKES bills.

bills.short_title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to E&C subcommittee, 2024-03-22
bills.plain_english: NIST standards and disclosure requirements for AI-generated content; predecessor to Foushee's 119th bill.
bills.notes: 18 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act (118th)
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary, 2023-05-05
bills.plain_english: Criminalized nonconsensual sexual deepfakes; gained 59 cosponsors after the Taylor Swift and New Jersey high school deepfake incidents.
bills.notes: 59 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: REPORT Act
bills.status: Became Public Law 118-59, signed 2024-05-07
bills.plain_english: Requires platforms to report child sex trafficking and enticement to NCMEC, raises fines for failing to report CSAM, and extends evidence-retention periods. One of the few enacted kids' online safety laws of the 118th.
bills.notes: Passed Senate by UC 2023-12-14; passed House by voice vote 2024-04-29.

bills.short_title: Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divest-or-ban)
bills.status: Passed House 352-65 (Roll no. 86), 2024-03-13; referred to Senate Commerce; its text was later enacted through the foreign-aid package H.R.815 (Public Law 118-50, April 2024; not re-verified in this session)
bills.plain_english: Forces ByteDance to divest TikTok or face a US ban, the most consequential Big Tech regulation vote of the 118th Congress. Voting yes signaled willingness to impose hard rules on a major platform.
bills.notes: Roll 86 breakdown (govtrack): Yea 197 R + 155 D; Nay 15 R + 50 D; 1 Present. Republican Nays included Massie, Gaetz, Greene, Biggs, Davidson, Perry, Higgins, Steube, Mace, Schweikert, McClintock, Mooney, Bishop, Barry Moore, Duarte. Also overlaps the China lane.

bills.short_title: Sammy's Law of 2023
bills.status: Referred to E&C subcommittee, 2023-09-29
bills.plain_english: 118th version of the third-party child-safety-software API mandate.
bills.notes: 20 cosponsors.

bills.short_title: No Section 230 Immunity for AI Act
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce, 2023-06-14
bills.plain_english: Would have made clear that Section 230 does not protect companies from claims over generative AI outputs. Supporting it signaled wanting AI companies exposed to lawsuits.
bills.notes: No numbered 119th reintroduction found; the 119th AI LEAD Act covers similar ground via product liability.

bills.short_title: Digital Consumer Protection Commission Act of 2023
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary, 2023-07-27
bills.plain_english: Would have created a new federal regulator with licensing power over dominant tech platforms. Supporting it signaled wanting a dedicated Big Tech regulator.
bills.notes: Unusual Warren-Graham pairing; not reintroduced in 119th per govtrack search.

bills.short_title: DEEPFAKES Accountability Act
bills.status: Referred to Homeland Security subcommittee, 2023-09-20
bills.plain_english: Would have required labels and watermarks on deepfakes with criminal penalties for malicious unlabeled deepfakes.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley letter to Mark Zuckerberg opening Senate Judiciary subcommittee investigation into Meta AI chatbots' 'romantic' and 'sensual' exchanges with children
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After Reuters reported Meta's internal AI rules allowed chatbots to flirt with children, Sen. Hawley demanded Meta preserve and hand over documents and announced a formal investigation by the Crime and Counterterrorism Subcommittee he chairs.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter demanded Meta produce responsive documents; Hawley later held a Sept 16, 2025 subcommittee hearing with bereaved parents.

letters_and_statements.title: Schatz-led bipartisan letter of 10 senators to Zuckerberg on safeguards for children using Meta AI chatbots
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Ten senators told Meta they were 'alarmed' by its chatbot policies, asked how its minor-safety rules were developed, and demanded Meta ban targeted ads to under-18s, improve disclosures and add mental-health referrals.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter PDF dated 8-19-2025; press release 2025-08-20. Also posted by Sens. Gallego and Welch.

letters_and_statements.title: Grassley, Blackburn, Hawley letter to Zuckerberg on Meta's emotional targeting of teens and alleged COPPA violations
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Judiciary Committee chairman and two members demanded answers on a 2014 Facebook study of teens' emotional triggers for ads and on FTC allegations that Meta let under-13s onto Horizon Worlds without parental consent.
letters_and_statements.notes: Follows Grassley's April 16, 2025 letter to Meta on emotional targeting.

letters_and_statements.title: Markey letter to Zuckerberg urging Meta to bar minors from AI chatbots
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Sen. Markey told Meta to stop letting minors use its AI chatbots, noting he had warned Meta in 2023 not to roll chatbots out to teens and citing privacy risks when teens use bots as therapists.
letters_and_statements.notes: Date from Markey press release (Sept 8, 2025) as reproduced by PublicNow; letter PDF hosted on markey.senate.gov.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley document requests to Character.AI, Google, Meta, OpenAI and Snap on AI chatbot policies after Judiciary subcommittee hearing
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Following testimony from parents whose children died after chatbot interactions, Hawley demanded five companies turn over all communications about their chatbot policies by Oct 17, 2025, writing 'children are dead. Families are broken.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Expands the August Meta probe; press release notes Zuckerberg declined to testify.

letters_and_statements.title: Padilla and Welch letters to CEOs of Character.AI, Chai and Luka (Replika) on companion-chatbot safety for children
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Two senators asked three AI companion companies how they train models to handle self-harm and mental-health conversations and what safety measures they use, citing the Florida teen's suicide linked to Character.AI.

letters_and_statements.title: Padilla and Schiff letter to FTC Chairman Ferguson urging the AI chatbot inquiry to address risks to children
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After the FTC opened its 6(b) inquiry into companion chatbots, the two California senators asked it to examine crisis detection, parental tools, deceptive marketing and sexual-exploitation risks, and requested a briefing by Oct 31, 2025.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter dated Oct 21, 2025; release Oct 22. Cites the Adam Raine case.

letters_and_statements.title: Castor-led House Democrats' letter to Zuckerberg urging Meta to halt AI companion bots for users under 18
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Six House Energy and Commerce Democrats told Meta to stop deploying AI companion bots to minors and any bots impersonating children, citing a Wall Street Journal investigation into sexual role-play with minors.

letters_and_statements.title: Guthrie and Pallone joint statement supporting FTC inquiry into AI companion chatbots
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The House Energy and Commerce chairman and ranking member jointly said they were 'alarmed' by incidents involving minors and chatbots, backed the FTC probe, and pledged bipartisan legislation to protect children online.

letters_and_statements.title: Wyden, Markey and Lujan open letter to Apple and Google to remove X and Grok from app stores over AI-generated sexual images
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Three Democratic senators told Apple and Google to pull X and Grok from their app stores until Elon Musk stops Grok from generating nonconsensual sexualized images of women and children, saying inaction would 'make a mockery' of their moderation claims.
letters_and_statements.notes: Signers and quotes confirmed via NBC News and CNBC (Jan 9, 2026); official release located on wyden.senate.gov and lujan.senate.gov.

letters_and_statements.title: Blunt Rochester-led letter of 8 senators to Alphabet, Meta, X, TikTok, Snap and Reddit on sexualized AI-generated images
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Eight Democratic senators demanded the platforms explain their policies for AI 'undressing' deepfakes, including of minors, preserve related documents, and describe how they remove images and notify victims.
letters_and_statements.notes: Prompted by the Grok episode; TechCrunch reported the letter's document demands.

letters_and_statements.title: Pallone and Castor statements opposing House Republicans' rewritten KOSA and COPPA 2.0 at E&C subcommittee markup
letters_and_statements.plain_english: At the subcommittee markup, Ranking Member Pallone said he could not support the House KOSA 'in its current form' because of its weaker knowledge standard and broad state-law preemption, and Rep. Castor said the House COPPA 2.0 preemption went against prior bipartisan work; the House KOSA advanced 13-10 on party lines.
letters_and_statements.notes: Secondary source (Roll Call) quoting members at the markup; Subcommittee Chair Bilirakis (R-FL) defended dropping the duty of care as protection against First Amendment challenges.

letters_and_statements.title: Blumenthal and Cantwell press call urging the House to reject the KIDS Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The KOSA co-author and the Senate Commerce ranking member said the House package strips the duty of care, narrows covered platforms and could preempt the state lawsuits now holding Meta and YouTube liable, with Blumenthal saying 'big tech is behind the House bill.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Secondary source; also covered by IAPP and Roll Call. Cantwell also warned against tying kids' safety to state AI-law preemption.

letters_and_statements.title: Blackburn and Blumenthal statement on House passage of the KIDS Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Senate KOSA authors called the House-passed bill 'a pale imitation of Big Tech accountability' for stripping the duty of care and vowed not to 'greenlight hollow reforms.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Notable Republican-Democrat split with House GOP leadership over the KIDS Act.

letters_and_statements.title: Speaker Johnson, Leader Scalise and Chairman Guthrie statements on House passage of the KIDS Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: House Republican leaders hailed the 267-117 passage of the KIDS Act as protecting children while 'protecting free speech,' and Guthrie and Pallone jointly said it 'creates strong protections with new rules for design features, default settings, and kids' privacy.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Guthrie-Pallone joint statement quoted by IAPP (2026-06-30); Rep. Castor (D-FL) also called it 'a meaningful step' per IAPP. Direction reflects supporters' framing; Senate KOSA authors call it weaker.

letters_and_statements.title: Blumenthal and Blackburn statement on Senate Commerce Committee passage of KOSA by voice vote
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The sponsors called the committee's voice-vote approval of the duty-of-care version of KOSA 'a major victory' and said the Senate has repeatedly shown bipartisan support for a version with a duty of care.
letters_and_statements.notes: Same markup advanced Cruz's CHATBOT Act, Markey's Youth AI Privacy Act and Duckworth's AI toy study.

letters_and_statements.title: Cruz and Klobuchar statements marking one year of the TAKE IT DOWN Act as FTC enforcement begins
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The law's authors said platforms must now remove nonconsensual intimate images and deepfakes within 48 hours, with Cruz saying 'Big Tech can no longer look the other way' and Klobuchar noting platforms can no longer 'turn a blind eye.'
letters_and_statements.notes: Release notes the first conviction under the law on 2026-04-09 and FTC warning letters to more than a dozen companies.

letters_and_statements.title: Hawley and Durbin letter to Roblox CEO opening Judiciary subcommittee investigation into child sexual abuse on Roblox
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The subcommittee chair and Judiciary ranking member told Roblox it 'appears to prioritize revenue and engagement metrics over the safety and well-being of our children,' cited 65,381 suspected exploitation reports in 2025, and directed it to preserve all child-safety records.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter dated Aug 12, 2026; release Aug 13.

letters_and_statements.title: Ocasio-Cortez and Laurel Lee press conference with Paris Hilton urging House passage of the DEFIANCE Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After the Senate passed the DEFIANCE Act unanimously, the bipartisan House co-leads and survivors publicly pressed Speaker Johnson to bring the deepfake civil-remedy bill to the floor.
letters_and_statements.notes: Other House members attended but are not named in the release text captured.

letters_and_statements.title: Blackburn and Welch roundtable statement with artists supporting the NO FAKES Act and TRAIN Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: During the Recording Academy's advocacy day, the two senators said the NO FAKES Act would protect creators from deepfakes and the TRAIN Act would let them find out when their copyrighted works train AI models, urging Congress to pass both.

letters_and_statements.title: Wyden interview defending Section 230 against repeal efforts
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Section 230's co-author said the law rightly makes individuals, not platforms, responsible for what they post and that he still stands by it as more than a dozen repeal or sunset bills circulate.
letters_and_statements.notes: Press interview rather than a formal statement; included because Wyden is the leading congressional opponent of the Sunset Section 230 Act and one of three Nays on KOSPA in 2024.

letters_and_statements.title: Blackburn and Blumenthal statement on House Energy and Commerce Committee passage of KOSA (118th Congress)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Senate sponsors called the House committee's approval 'a positive step' while noting 'more work to do' on KOSA and thanked Chair McMorris Rodgers and Reps. Bilirakis and Castor.
letters_and_statements.notes: 118th Congress item; the House bill never reached the floor.

tech_regulation.coverage_notes: METHOD AND SOURCES. The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after 16 queries and congress.gov, senate.gov, house.gov, clerk.house.gov and most committee sites returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl. Bill facts (numbers, titles, sponsors, full cosponsor lists with dates, actions, public-law numbers) were therefore taken from the Library of Congress BILLSTATUS bulk XML served by govinfo.gov (the same data behind congress.gov) for every bill listed, cross-checked against the govtrack.us API and bill pages; source_url fields point to govtrack pages for readability. Roll-call breakdowns and Nay lists come from govtrack's vote CSV exports (House 119-228, 119-104, 118-86; Senate 118-221). Bill text excerpts were read on govinfo for bills lacking CRS summaries. Letters and statements were found via DuckDuckGo run inside the in-app browser and confirmed by opening the official senate.gov/house.gov press release in that browser, except where notes say a secondary source (Roll Call, Broadband Breakfast, IAPP, NBC, CNBC, KLCC) was used. Discovery searches on govtrack covered: kids safety, chatbots, age verification, Section 230, app stores, antitrust, privacy, algorithms, deepfakes, digital replicas, copyright/training data, elections, scams. WHAT COULD NOT BE CONFIRMED FROM PRIMARY SOURCES: the reported 15-13 SCREEN Act vote failing for quorum at the 2026-08-05 Commerce markup (secondary source only); which committee held the 35-0 vote on H.R.8893; enactment of the TikTok bill via H.R.815/P.L. 118-50 and the cancellation of the June 2024 APRA markup (general knowledge, not re-opened); the tally of the House E&C full-committee party-line vote on the KIDS Act in March 2026. LIKELY GAPS: no numbered 119th APRA/ADPPA successor exists in LOC data (only Moran's S.4211 and Lofgren's H.R.8014); no 119th EARN IT, JCPA, SAFE TECH, PACT, or Digital Consumer Protection Commission reintroductions were found; the House companion to Cruz's CHATBOT Act does not appear to exist (H.R.7985 shares the acronym but differs). Letters not located despite searching: congressional letters on AI copyright/fair use (only the Blackburn-Welch roundtable and Hawley's hearing-driven bill were found), letters to DOJ/FTC on Big Tech antitrust remedies, any Lee/James letter to Apple and Google on age verification, Klobuchar FEC letters in the 119th, and 118th-Congress letters generally (only one 118th statement included). The Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing of Sept 16, 2025 on AI chatbot harms and the House E&C Oversight hearing of Nov 18, 2025 are referenced in sources but member statements from them were not individually captured. A background Wayback CDX crawl of senator sites also surfaced Hawley's Dec 17, 2025 release on new GUARD Act cosponsors and a 2023 Hawley-Blumenthal letter to Meta on the LLaMA leak (118th, AI-risk lane), neither included as separate entries. Off-lane bills surfaced but excluded: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act (S.3680/H.R.7110), Privacy Protection Updates Act (S.4268), Safeguard Kids Act (S.4958, school AI curriculum), STRONG Kids Act (H.R.9839), SOCIAL MEDIA Act (S.626), Voluntary Consumer AI Disclosure Pilot Act (H.R.9439), No Fentanyl on Social Media Act (S.3618/H.R.6259).

bills.short_title: Chip Security Act
bills.plain_english: Requires advanced AI chips to carry location-verification and other anti-diversion features before export, and requires exporters to report to Commerce if chips are diverted or tampered with, to stop smuggling to China.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking (2025-05-08); no committee action as of 2026-09-12. 21 bipartisan cosponsors.
bills.notes: Bill number and cosponsor roster confirmed via GPO BILLSTATUS XML (congress.gov data feed). Cotton press release 2025-05-09 at cotton.senate.gov. House companion H.R.3447.

bills.short_title: Chip Security Act
bills.plain_english: House version of the Chip Security Act: Commerce must require location-verification on export-controlled advanced chips and exporters must report diversion, so US chips cannot be smuggled to China.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute, 42-0, on 2026-03-26. Awaiting floor action. 41 cosponsors.
bills.notes: Moolenaar statement on committee passage 2026-03-26 (chinaselectcommittee.house.gov). Cotton and Huizenga letter to Lutnick 2026-03-20 asked Commerce to start implementing the bill's anti-diversion provisions administratively.

bills.short_title: GAIN AI Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Gives American customers a right of first refusal on advanced AI chips: chipmakers could not get licenses to ship advanced chips to China or other arms-embargoed countries while US buyers' orders go unfilled.
bills.status: Standalone bill referred to Senate Banking 2025-11-06. The Banks-Warren GAIN AI amendment was carried in the Senate-passed FY2026 NDAA (S.2296, passed 77-20 on 2025-10-09, Record Vote 570) but was dropped from the final NDAA (S.1071, Public Law 119-60, signed 2025-12-18).
bills.notes: Nextgov (2025-10-09) reported Senate passage of the GAIN AI amendment via the NDAA; Nextgov (2025-12-03) reported it was not expected to make the final NDAA, with Nvidia and the Semiconductor Industry Association opposed and Microsoft and Americans for Responsible Innovation in support. Punchbowl (2025-12-01) headline: GAIN AI all but dead in NDAA. Bloomberg reported White House asked Congress to drop it (per TECHi 2025-11-20). PL 119-60 text confirmed to contain no GAIN AI provisions. Banks says GAIN's core principles were incorporated in Commerce's January 2026 H200 rule.

bills.short_title: GAIN AI Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: House companion to the GAIN AI Act: US customers get first claim on advanced AI chips before they can be exported to China.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-10-31.

bills.short_title: Remote Access Security Act
bills.plain_english: Closes the cloud loophole: export controls would apply when a foreign person accesses controlled US chips or technology remotely over the internet or a cloud service, not just when hardware physically ships.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 51-0 (2025-04-09). Passed House under suspension 369-22 (Roll Call 13) on 2026-01-12. Received in Senate and referred to Banking 2026-01-13.
bills.notes: Roll Call 13 (2026-01-12) is a recorded per-member vote. Senate companion S.3519. A 118th-Congress version (H.R.8152) passed the House by voice in Sept 2024.

bills.short_title: Remote Access Security Act
bills.plain_english: Senate companion: applies export controls to remote/cloud access to controlled US chips and technology by foreign persons.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2025-12-17.

bills.short_title: SAFE Chips Act of 2025 (Secure and Feasible Exports of Chips Act)
bills.plain_english: Locks in current chip export limits: Commerce must deny licenses for 30 months for any AI chip to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea that is more powerful than chips already allowed, blocking sales like Nvidia's H200.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2025-12-04.
bills.notes: Introduced four days before Trump's 2025-12-08 announcement allowing H200 sales to China. Ricketts release 2025-12-04 quotes Ricketts, Coons, Cotton, Shaheen and Kim.

bills.short_title: AI OVERWATCH Act
bills.plain_english: Gives Congress an arms-sales-style check on advanced AI chip exports to China and other countries of concern: licenses required (no blanket approvals), Commerce must certify exports will not shortchange US supply or enable remote access, and the most advanced chips stay barred.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute, 42-2, on 2026-01-21. 43 cosponsors.
bills.notes: Introduced ten days after Trump's H200 announcement. Select Committee report (2026-04-16) recommends passage. House-passed FY2027 NDAA (H.R.8800, passed 216-212 on 2026-07-22) text does not contain OVERWATCH language (grep of engrossed text).

bills.short_title: AI OVERWATCH Act
bills.plain_english: Senate AI OVERWATCH Act: codifies and extends for 18 months the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to countries of concern, requires licenses and congressional certifications for less-advanced chips, and orders an American AI Victory Strategy.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2026-04-30. Banks announced (2026-07-14) it was included in the Senate Armed Services-reported FY2027 NDAA (S.4784); cloture on the motion to proceed to S.4784 failed 50-46 on 2026-07-14 (Record Vote 195).
bills.notes: Banks/Warren joint release 2026-05-04 (banking.senate.gov minority) with quotes from Banks, Warren, Cotton, Cortez Masto, Shaheen.

bills.short_title: No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: No advanced AI chip could be exported to China unless Commerce approves after an interagency review and Congress passes a joint resolution approving the sale.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-08-22.
bills.notes: Introduced after the July 2025 H20 reversal. Text confirmed from govinfo introduced version.

bills.short_title: RESTRICT Act (Restoring Export and Security Trade Restrictions for Integrated Circuit Technologies Act)
bills.plain_english: Writes into law a ban on selling the most advanced AI chips (ECCN 3A090/4A090-class, data-center chips) to China and other countries of concern, reversing Trump's H200 decision, while easing transfers to approved US persons abroad.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-12-18. All 16 cosponsors are Democrats.
bills.notes: Export Compliance Daily (2025-12-19) described it as Meeks leading 13 other House Democrats to block the H200 sale. Text confirmed from govinfo.

bills.short_title: Stop Stealing our Chips Act
bills.plain_english: Creates a whistleblower reward and protection program at Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security for people who report chip export-control violations.
bills.status: Banking Committee discharged and bill passed Senate with an amendment by unanimous consent on 2026-05-20; received in House and held at the desk 2026-05-21.
bills.notes: House companion H.R.6322 (Kean) ordered reported by HFAC 43-1 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Stop Stealing our Chips Act
bills.plain_english: House version of the BIS whistleblower-reward bill for chip export-control violations.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 43-1 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: MATCH Act (Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware Act)
bills.plain_english: Closes gaps in controls on chipmaking equipment: the US must first seek matching allied restrictions and then use foreign direct product rules, US-content thresholds or end-use controls to stop China buying chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing tools.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute (amended), 36-8, on 2026-04-22. 29 cosponsors.
bills.notes: Recommended in the Select Committee's 2026-04-16 report 'Buy What It Can, Steal What It Must'. Baumgartner introduced 2026-04-02; Moolenaar cosponsor release 2026-04-03.

bills.short_title: MATCH Act (Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware Act)
bills.plain_english: Senate MATCH Act: aligns US and allied export controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment so China cannot buy chokepoint chipmaking tools from allies that the US already restricts.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2026-04-13.
bills.notes: Announced by Kim and Ricketts 2026-04-02 and by Risch/Ricketts/Kim 2026-04-08 (foreign.senate.gov); Schumer also announced support (democrats.senate.gov 2026-04-03).

bills.short_title: SCALE Act (Semiconductor Controls Adjusted to Limit Exports Act)
bills.plain_english: Sets an objective, rolling export threshold: Commerce and the DNI publish metrics on China's AI chip capability, and exports are allowed only up to 110 percent of what adversaries can mass-produce themselves, with a presumption of denial if adversary AI hardware would exceed 5 percent of the US base.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence 2026-04-15. No cosponsors.
bills.notes: Moolenaar release 2026-04-21 (chinaselectcommittee.house.gov).

bills.short_title: Cloud Security Act
bills.plain_english: Targets the cloud loophole: lets US cloud providers report suspected misuse by customers tied to adversaries to Commerce without legal risk, and pushes identity verification of cloud users so China cannot rent restricted AI chips.
bills.status: Referred to House Judiciary 2026-06-30.
bills.notes: Gottheimer/Moolenaar release dated 2026-06-26; bill formally introduced 2026-06-30 per BILLSTATUS.

bills.short_title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Authorizes sanctions on foreign adversaries that steal American AI models, including through industrial-scale 'distillation' of US frontier models by Chinese labs.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 43-0 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
bills.plain_english: Codifies the Trump administration's program to promote exporting the American 'full AI stack' (chips, data centers, models, cloud) to allies, with security requirements on foreign buyers to prevent transfer to adversaries.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute, 37-7, on 2026-04-22 (the only export-control bill at that markup with notable opposition).
bills.notes: Export-promotion bill implementing the July 2025 AI exports executive order; AI Now Institute urged HFAC to oppose it. Direction marked mixed because it promotes exports while adding buyer security conditions.

bills.short_title: BIS License Fee Prohibition Act
bills.plain_english: Bans the government from collecting revenue-sharing or fees as a condition of an export license and requires refunds, a direct response to Trump's 15 percent cut of Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-11-07.
bills.notes: Findings state export controls on China should rest on national-security assessments, not revenue. Marked mixed because it does not itself tighten controls; politically it opposes the pay-to-export deal.

bills.short_title: Semiconductor Controls Effectiveness Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Requires an assessment of how well US semiconductor export controls are working.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 43-0 on 2026-04-22.
bills.notes: Bill text not reviewed; description from title. Direction marked neutral pending text.

bills.short_title: Export Controls Enforcement Act
bills.plain_english: Puts BIS's overseas Export Control Officer program into law and requires at least 20 officers posted at embassies to catch chip diversion.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute, 41-3, on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Ten-year statute of limitations for export control violations (ECRA amendment)
bills.plain_english: Extends the time to prosecute export-control violations from 5 to 10 years.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 44-0 on 2026-04-22. Identical Senate bill S.5380 (Husted, with Warner) introduced 2026-08-07.

bills.short_title: Increase ECRA civil penalties (Export Control Reform Act amendment)
bills.plain_english: Raises the maximum civil fine for export-control violations to $1.2 million or four times the transaction value.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 44-0 on 2026-04-22. Related Senate bill S.4883 (Kennedy, with Andy Kim) introduced 2026-06-24.

bills.short_title: Export Control Enforcement and Enhancement Act
