bills.plain_english: Speeds up Entity List additions by letting any End-User Review Committee member force a vote within 30 days, and creates a presumption of denial for exports involving listed parties.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute 44-0 on 2026-04-22. Senate companion S.4840 (Blackburn, with Mark Kelly) introduced 2026-06-18.

bills.short_title: ADVERSARIES Act
bills.plain_english: Expands export-control coverage to Chinese military companies (1260H list), Entity List and Military End-User parties, and any subsidiary they own 50 percent or more, wherever located.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute 44-0 on 2026-04-22. Senate companion S.5381 (Husted, with Warner) introduced 2026-08-07.

bills.short_title: Bureau of Industry and Security License Administration Enhancement Act
bills.plain_english: Requires BIS to run licenses triggered by 'is informed' letters through the normal interagency process and adds reporting on those letters.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 43-1 on 2026-04-22. Senate companion S.4835 (Cramer, with Andy Kim) introduced 2026-06-18.

bills.short_title: BIS Licensing Efficiency Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Sets a 90-day deadline for BIS export-license decisions and quarterly reporting to Congress on license processing.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 44-0 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Strengthening Export Controls Compliance Act
bills.plain_english: Requires BIS to help small and mid-sized businesses comply with export controls and to do industry outreach before major new rules.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 39-5 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Interagency Coordination in Export Controls Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Lets State, Defense and Energy propose new export-control rules directly to the Export Administration Review Board (forcing a vote within 30 days) rather than leaving rulemaking to Commerce alone, and orders a study of China's military-civil fusion.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs in the nature of a substitute on a party-line 25-19 vote, 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Export Dispute Resolution Act
bills.plain_english: Changes how interagency disputes over export licenses are resolved (majority vote on the Operating Committee, including for arms-embargoed countries).
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 44-0 on 2026-04-22.

bills.short_title: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act
bills.plain_english: Requires BIS to report annually to Congress on export licenses, enforcement actions and other authorizations involving entities in China and other Country Group D:5 destinations.
bills.status: ENACTED. Passed House by voice under suspension 2025-05-05; passed Senate by unanimous consent 2025-07-22; signed 2025-08-19 as Public Law 119-34.
bills.notes: Senate companion S.744 (Banks, with Warner). The 118th-Congress version H.R.6614 passed the House in Sept 2024 but died in the Senate.

bills.short_title: Strategic Export Controls and Border Security Enhancement Act
bills.plain_english: Authorizes a State Department Office of Export Controls and Border Security to help partner countries stop diversion of US critical technologies.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2026-05-07.

bills.short_title: China AI Power Report Act
bills.plain_english: Requires Commerce to report annually on China's AI chip capabilities (Huawei, Cambricon and others) so Congress can keep export controls current; includes a sense of Congress that controls must be dynamic.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 47-0 on 2026-01-21. Senate companion S.5382 (Husted, with Warner) introduced 2026-08-07.

bills.short_title: China Advanced Technology Monitoring Act
bills.plain_english: Requires the Pentagon to report annually on China's semiconductor manufacturing capabilities and the impact of US and allied export controls.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-09-10.

bills.short_title: Semiconductor Sovereignty Act
bills.plain_english: Requires Commerce/BIS reports on critical inputs, offshoring trends and bottlenecks for semiconductor manufacturing and research.
bills.status: Referred to Foreign Affairs, Energy and Commerce, and Science 2025-09-10.

bills.short_title: China Technology Transfer Control Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Controls exports to China of technology and intellectual property deemed important to the national interest, including tech that would aid China's military or human-rights abuses.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs and Ways and Means 2025-02-07. No cosponsors; sponsor resigned from Congress in 2025.

bills.short_title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Would make it a crime for US persons to import or export AI technology to or from China, do AI research with Chinese entities, or invest in Chinese AI development.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Judiciary 2025-01-29. No cosponsors.
bills.notes: Introduced days after DeepSeek R1's release.

bills.short_title: No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
bills.plain_english: Requires OMB to order DeepSeek (and any successor app from High Flyer) removed from federal government devices.
bills.status: Referred to House Oversight 2025-02-07. 32 cosponsors. Related: FY2026 NDAA (PL 119-60) Sec. 6604 prohibits use of DeepSeek on intelligence community systems.
bills.notes: Senate companion S.765 (Rosen, with Husted and Ricketts) introduced 2025-02-27, referred to HSGAC.

bills.short_title: No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act
bills.plain_english: Senate companion requiring removal of DeepSeek from federal devices.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs 2025-02-27.

bills.short_title: No Adversarial AI Act
bills.plain_english: Directs the Federal Acquisition Security Council to list AI systems made by foreign adversaries (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea) and bars federal agencies from buying or using them, with narrow research and national-security exceptions.
bills.status: Referred to House Oversight 2025-06-25. Identical Senate bill S.2177 (Rick Scott, with Gary Peters) referred to HSGAC.

bills.short_title: No Adversarial AI Act
bills.plain_english: Senate companion barring federal agencies from acquiring or using AI developed by foreign adversaries such as DeepSeek.
bills.status: Referred to Senate HSGAC 2025-06-25.

bills.short_title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Bars federal contractors from using DeepSeek to perform federal contracts and orders a Commerce/Defense report on national-security threats from AI platforms based in countries of concern.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce 2025-05-07.

bills.short_title: Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act
bills.plain_english: Requires the State Department to assess annually how foreign adversaries use generative AI for malicious activity and to pursue diplomacy on it.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs 45-0 on 2026-03-26.

bills.short_title: China AI Threat Assessment Act
bills.plain_english: Orders a National Intelligence Estimate on Chinese AI systems, including embedded bias and use for influence operations.
bills.status: Referred to House Intelligence 2025-12-18.

bills.short_title: FIGHT China Act of 2025 (Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart China Act)
bills.plain_english: Outbound investment guardrails: requires US investors to notify Treasury of, and lets Treasury prohibit, investments in Chinese firms in sensitive technologies such as AI and semiconductors, and authorizes sanctions on Chinese defense and surveillance tech firms.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2025-03-13. Its outbound-investment provisions were largely enacted through the COINS Act title of the FY2026 NDAA (PL 119-60).
bills.notes: House companion H.R.2246 (Barr) with Moolenaar, McCaul, Golden, Suozzi, Wagner, LaHood.

bills.short_title: FIGHT China Act (Foreign Investment Guardrails to Help Thwart China Act)
bills.plain_english: House outbound-investment bill: notification and prohibition authority over US investment in Chinese AI, chips and other sensitive tech, plus sanctions on Chinese military and surveillance companies.
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs and Financial Services 2025-03-21.

bills.short_title: Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security (COINS) Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Creates a statutory outbound-investment regime requiring notification of, and allowing prohibition of, US investments in Chinese AI, semiconductor, quantum and other national-security technologies.
bills.status: Standalone bill referred to Senate Banking 2025-12-17; ENACTED as Title LXXXV (Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, Secs. 8501-8531) of the FY2026 NDAA, S.1071, Public Law 119-60, signed 2025-12-18.
bills.notes: Inclusion confirmed by grep of PL 119-60 text (govinfo). Senate agreed to the House amendment to S.1071 77-20 on 2025-12-17 (Record Vote 648); cloture 76-20 (Record Vote 647) on 2025-12-15.

bills.short_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Public Law 119-60)
bills.plain_english: The annual defense bill that became the vehicle for the outbound-investment COINS Act (Title LXXXV) and a ban on DeepSeek on intelligence community systems (Sec. 6604); the Senate-passed GAIN AI chip provision was stripped before final passage.
bills.status: Became Public Law 119-60 on 2025-12-18. Senate concurred in House amendment 77-20 (Record Vote 648, 2025-12-17).
bills.notes: Direction marked neutral because an omnibus defense vote is not a clean signal on chip policy. The Senate's own NDAA (S.2296) passed 77-20 on 2025-10-09 (Record Vote 570) with the GAIN AI amendment; the House NDAA (H.R.3838, passed 2025-09-10) did not include GAIN AI.

bills.short_title: Chip EQUIP Act (Chip Equipment Quality, Usefulness, and Integrity Protection Act of 2025)
bills.plain_english: Bars CHIPS Act grant recipients from buying completed semiconductor manufacturing equipment made by Chinese or other foreign-entity-of-concern firms.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce 2025-12-02. House companion H.R.6207 (Lofgren) forwarded by Energy and Commerce subcommittee by voice vote 2026-09-01.
bills.notes: Reintroduction of 118th-Congress S.4585/S.5002 (Kelly) and H.R.8826 (Lofgren).

bills.short_title: Chip EQUIP Act
bills.plain_english: House Chip EQUIP Act: CHIPS Act-funded fabs may not buy Chinese-made chipmaking equipment.
bills.status: Forwarded by Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade to full committee (amended) by voice vote 2026-09-01.

bills.short_title: Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act
bills.plain_english: Directs Commerce's SelectUSA program to work with state economic development agencies to attract foreign investment into US semiconductor manufacturing (CHIPS follow-on).
bills.status: Reported by Senate Commerce (S. Rept. 119-18); passed Senate by unanimous consent 2025-05-20; held at the desk in House. House companion H.R.2480 (Landsman) passed House by voice 2025-04-28.

bills.short_title: Semiconductor Superiority Act
bills.plain_english: Tax bill (Finance Committee) on semiconductors; identical House bill H.R.8959 (Buchanan) referred to Ways and Means. Appears to be a CHIPS investment-credit follow-on.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Finance 2026-06-11. H.R.8959 (Buchanan, with Sewell, DelBene, Steube, Carol Miller, Fong, Neguse, Moolenaar, Tenney, Grothman) referred to Ways and Means 2026-05-21.
bills.notes: Bill text not reviewed; policy area 'Taxation' per BILLSTATUS. Treat description as provisional.

bills.short_title: Dismantling Ideological Policies for Semiconductors and Science Act
bills.plain_english: Repeals diversity, equity and inclusion requirements and positions created by the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act.
bills.status: Referred to Senate HELP 2025-05-13.
bills.notes: CHIPS Act follow-up; not an export-control bill.

bills.short_title: CHIPS Training in America Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Semiconductor workforce-training follow-on to the CHIPS Act.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce 2026-06-17. Reintroduction of 118th S.4657.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed.

bills.short_title: Memory Chip Competitiveness Assessment Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Requires an assessment of US competitiveness in memory chips amid the AI-driven DRAM shortage and Chinese memory-chip expansion.
bills.status: Forwarded by Energy and Commerce subcommittee to full committee by voice vote 2026-09-01.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed; description from title.

bills.short_title: China Subsidy Response and Export Competitiveness Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Expands the Export-Import Bank's China and Transformational Exports program (including semiconductor machinery and printed circuit boards) to counter Chinese subsidies.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2026-06-08.

bills.short_title: Securing Innovation and Research from Adversaries Act
bills.plain_english: Bars federally funded researchers from collaborating with entities on US government restricted lists (such as the Entity List) or people tied to them, with a national-security waiver.
bills.status: Referred to House Science 2026-05-19. Senate companion S.4525 (Banks) referred to HSGAC 2026-05-14.
bills.notes: Research-security bill adjacent to the export-control lane (uses BIS Entity List as trigger).

bills.short_title: Divesting from Communist China's Military Act of 2026
bills.plain_english: Requires Treasury to put every Pentagon-designated Chinese military company on the investment-ban (NS-CMIC) list, cutting US capital to Chinese defense-linked tech firms.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2026-01-14. Identical House bill H.R.7075 (Scott Perry).

bills.short_title: Resolution condemning and calling for reversal of the decision to allow advanced AI chip exports to the UAE
bills.plain_english: Senate resolution condemning President Trump's decision to allow advanced AI chip exports to the UAE, citing national-security risk and the UAE's $500 million stake in the Trump family crypto firm.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking 2026-02-05.

bills.short_title: Resolution affirming the importance of preserving the US advantage in artificial intelligence
bills.plain_english: Bipartisan sense-of-the-Senate resolution that the US must achieve and maintain AI dominance over China.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Foreign Relations 2025-11-06.
bills.notes: Resolution text not reviewed beyond title.

bills.short_title: Semiconductor Supply Chain Security and Diversification Act of 2025
bills.plain_english: Directs US development-finance and diplomatic efforts to diversify semiconductor supply chains away from China (reintroduction of 118th H.R.8414).
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2025-02-11.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed; description from title and 118th predecessor.

bills.short_title: ENFORCE Act (Enhancing National Frameworks for Overseas Restriction of Critical Exports Act)
bills.plain_english: Would have given Commerce clear authority to control exports of AI models (model weights) and related technology to China under the Export Control Reform Act.
bills.status: Ordered reported (amended) by House Foreign Affairs 43-3 on 2024-05-22; died at end of 118th Congress.
bills.notes: No Senate companion bill number was confirmed.

bills.short_title: Remote Access Security Act
bills.plain_english: First version of the cloud-loophole bill applying export controls to remote access of controlled items.
bills.status: Ordered reported by HFAC by unanimous consent 2024-05-16; passed House by voice vote under suspension 2024-09-09; died in Senate Banking.

bills.short_title: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act
bills.plain_english: Annual BIS reporting to Congress on export licenses to China and other D:5 countries (later enacted in the 119th as PL 119-34).
bills.status: HFAC 43-0 (2023-12-13); passed House by voice 2024-09-09; died in Senate Banking.

bills.short_title: Outbound Investment Transparency Act of 2023
bills.plain_english: Requires US investors to notify Treasury before investing in Chinese (and Russian, Iranian, North Korean) semiconductor, AI and other sensitive-technology firms.
bills.status: Standalone bill referred to Senate Banking. Adopted as the Cornyn-Casey amendment to the Senate FY2024 NDAA (S.2226) by a 91-6 vote on 2023-07-25; dropped in the final FY2024 NDAA conference.
bills.notes: 91-6 tally per Cornyn release (2023-07-25) and CSIS analysis (2023-08-02); the amendment number and Senate roll-call number were not confirmed from a primary source.

bills.short_title: Preventing Adversaries from Developing Critical Capabilities Act
bills.plain_english: House outbound-investment bill: would prohibit or require notification of US investment in Chinese AI, semiconductor, quantum and hypersonic capabilities.
bills.status: Ordered reported by House Foreign Affairs by voice vote 2023-11-29; no floor action.

bills.short_title: COINS Act of 2024 (Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act)
bills.plain_english: End-of-Congress outbound-investment bill after the provision was dropped from the FY2025 NDAA; became the template for the 2025 COINS Act enacted in the FY2026 NDAA.
bills.status: Referred to Foreign Affairs and Financial Services 2024-12-24; died at end of Congress. Identical Senate bill S.5648 (Cornyn, with Tim Scott) introduced 2024-12-20.
bills.notes: Barr release (2025-01) describes Barr/Moolenaar introduction; 118th BILLSTATUS lists Moolenaar as sole cosponsor.

bills.short_title: Export Controls Enforcement Improvement Act of 2024
bills.plain_english: Bipartisan bill to strengthen BIS export-control enforcement capacity.
bills.status: Referred to Senate Banking; HSGAC subcommittee hearing 2024-04-10.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed.

bills.short_title: Building Chips in America Act of 2023
bills.plain_english: CHIPS Act follow-up that streamlined federal environmental (NEPA) review for CHIPS-funded semiconductor projects.
bills.status: ENACTED: passed Senate by UC Dec 2023; passed House 257-125 (Roll Call 440) on 2024-09-23; signed 2024-10-02 as Public Law 118-105.
bills.notes: House Roll Call 440 is a recorded per-member vote. Direction 'fewer_rules' refers to environmental-review streamlining, not export controls.

bills.short_title: Chip EQUIP Act of 2024
bills.plain_english: Original Chip EQUIP Act: bars CHIPS grant recipients from buying Chinese-made chipmaking equipment (reintroduced as S.5002 and H.R.8826 by Lofgren).
bills.status: Referred to Senate Finance 2024-06-18; died.

bills.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Acquisitions Act of 2024
bills.plain_english: Restricts federal acquisition of AI from foreign adversary sources (precursor to the 119th No Adversarial AI Act).
bills.status: Referred to Senate Commerce 2024-08-01; died.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed; description inferred from title.

bills.short_title: Closing Loopholes for the Overseas Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence Act
bills.plain_english: Early attempt to apply export controls to Chinese remote/cloud use of US AI chips (the cloud loophole).
bills.status: Referred to House Foreign Affairs 2023-07-17; died.
bills.notes: Text not reviewed; description from title.

letters_and_statements.title: Ricketts-led Republican senators' letter to Commerce Secretary Lutnick urging withdrawal of the Biden AI Diffusion Rule
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Seven GOP senators asked Commerce to scrap the Biden-era AI Diffusion export rule before its May 15, 2025 compliance date and replace it with a lighter alternative, arguing it hurt US companies' global sales.
letters_and_statements.notes: Release dated 2025-04-14 says the letter was sent 'Friday' (2025-04-11). Commerce rescinded the rule 2025-05-13. Companion releases on wicker.senate.gov (2025-04-16) and tuberville.senate.gov (2025-04-15).

letters_and_statements.title: Warren letter to Lutnick urging Commerce to block Nvidia H20 exports to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Warren pressed Commerce to proceed with restricting H20 chip exports after reports it paused the plan following a Nvidia CEO dinner with Trump.

letters_and_statements.title: House Select Committee on the CCP report 'DeepSeek Unmasked' and letter to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Bipartisan committee report found DeepSeek funnels US data to China, censors output, and was built on tens of thousands of Nvidia chips possibly obtained around export controls; leaders sent Nvidia a letter demanding sales data for China and Southeast Asia.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter to Nvidia dated 2025-04-16 posted at https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/letters/nvidia-letter-mr-jensen-huang-ceo (posted 2025-05-01).

letters_and_statements.title: Joint statement of Senate and House Democrats on Trump's UAE and Saudi AI chip deals
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Seven Democrats said exporting very large volumes of advanced AI chips to the Gulf without credible security assurances threatens national security, could leak compute to China, and offshores the US AI buildout.

letters_and_statements.title: Schumer and Warren-led Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick and Rubio urging reconsideration of Middle East chip deals
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Eight Senate Democrats urged the administration to reconsider the Saudi and UAE AI chip deals absent enforceable protections against diversion to China, and raised Trump-family financial conflicts.

letters_and_statements.title: Meeks and Lofgren letter to Lutnick on multilateral export controls on chips and chipmaking equipment
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The top Democrats on Foreign Affairs and Science warned Commerce not to pull back from allied coordination on semiconductor and SME export controls after the AI Diffusion Rule rescission.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar letter to Lutnick objecting to resumption of Nvidia H20 sales to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The Select Committee chairman said Commerce 'must hold the line' on the H20 ban, cited use of H20s by DeepSeek and Tencent, requested a briefing, and proposed a floating technical benchmark pegged just above China's domestic chip capability.
letters_and_statements.notes: Full letter PDF: https://ari.us/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Moolenaar-Letter-to-Lutnick-7-18-25.pdf (3 pages, signed by Moolenaar alone). Reuters covered it 2025-07-18.

letters_and_statements.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to Lutnick on decision to resume H20 (and AMD MI308) sales to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Five senior Senate Democrats expressed 'grave concern' at reversing the April 2025 H20 ban, said restricting leading-edge chips is the defining barrier to Chinese AI parity, and objected to trading export controls in trade talks without consulting Congress.

letters_and_statements.title: Meeks and Krishnamoorthi letter to Lutnick: export controls should not be bargaining chips in China trade talks
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The ranking members of Foreign Affairs and the China Select Committee condemned using H20 export controls as a 'negotiating chip', said it contradicted Under Secretary Kessler's testimony, and noted the reversal followed Jensen Huang's White House meeting.

letters_and_statements.title: Top Senate Democrats' letter to President Trump on the 15 percent fee deal for Nvidia and AMD chip sales to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Six Senate Democrats urged Trump to reverse the deal letting Nvidia and AMD sell AI chips to China in exchange for a 15 percent cut, arguing it harms national security and that export law bars fees tied to licenses; they demanded answers by Aug. 22.

letters_and_statements.title: Cotton letter to Lutnick on smuggling of export-controlled US chips through Malaysia
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Cotton asked Commerce to address and investigate large-scale diversion of controlled US AI chips through Malaysia to China.
letters_and_statements.notes: Letter PDF located on cotton.senate.gov (dated by filename 10-30-25 and opening sentence in search snippet); full text was not opened, so details beyond the request for a Commerce investigation are unconfirmed. Covered by MeriTalk 2025-11-03.

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the GAIN AI Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Six senators from both parties introduced the standalone GAIN AI Act after the Banks-Warren amendment passed the Senate in the NDAA on Oct. 9, 2025, arguing US customers should not wait behind Chinese tech giants for advanced chips.
letters_and_statements.notes: Release dated 2025-11-07 on banking.senate.gov minority site; bill S.3150 introduced 2025-11-06.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar statement: DOJ chip-smuggling indictment shows urgent need for the Chip Security Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: After DOJ indicted three Chinese nationals for routing chips through Thailand and Malaysia to China, Moolenaar called for passing the Chip Security Act's location-verification mandate, noting 30 bipartisan cosponsors.

letters_and_statements.title: Bipartisan senators' statement introducing the SAFE Chips Act to lock in AI chip export limits on China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Six senators introduced a bill to codify current chip export limits on China for 30 months, with Ricketts, Coons, Cotton, Shaheen and Kim quoted opposing any loosening for chips like the H200.

letters_and_statements.title: Warren, Schumer and colleagues' letter to Lutnick on the decision to allow Nvidia H200 sales to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Seven Senate Democrats said approving H200 exports disregarded DOJ warnings that these chips are building blocks of AI superiority, and questioned Nvidia lobbying and donations preceding the decision.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar letter to Lutnick on Nvidia H200 chips: US is winning the AI race against a weak Chinese chip sector
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Moolenaar argued China lags far behind in aggregate compute, that Huawei's flagship chip was made abroad via a TSMC shell company, and that approving cutting-edge chip sales to Chinese companies risks undercutting the US lead; requested a Commerce briefing.

letters_and_statements.title: House Foreign Affairs Chairman Mast opening statement at hearing on the H200 export rule
letters_and_statements.plain_english: At a hearing the day after BIS formally allowed H200 sales to China (with a 25 percent revenue cut), Mast warned that if Nvidia chips were sold freely the CCP would likely overtake the US in the AI arms race.
letters_and_statements.notes: Nextgov reports Democrats charged the H200 move was a trade bargaining chip while some Republicans argued it keeps China dependent on second-tier US chips; only Mast is quoted by name in the portion reviewed.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar and Mast bipartisan letter to Rubio and Lutnick supporting stronger allied export controls on chipmaking tools
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Eight House members from both parties urged countrywide (not entity-specific) controls on chokepoint semiconductor manufacturing equipment and closer work with the Netherlands and other allies, citing doubling Dutch lithography sales to China.
letters_and_statements.notes: HFAC releases dated 2026-02-09; Select Committee release 2026-02-10. Letter PDF at democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov (sme-controls-letter-02.09.26.pdf).

letters_and_statements.title: Ro Khanna (new Select Committee ranking member) signals openness to Nvidia H200 sales to China
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Khanna told reporters he is open to sales of older-generation (Hopper) Nvidia chips to China, a shift from predecessor Krishnamoorthi, who cosponsored legislation to block them.
letters_and_statements.notes: Reuters, Stephen Nellis. Khanna stopped short of endorsing the H200 decision itself.

letters_and_statements.title: Cotton and Huizenga letter to Lutnick urging implementation of Chip Security Act anti-diversion measures after Super Micro smuggling indictments
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The lead sponsors of the Chip Security Act asked Commerce to begin requiring location verification and other anti-diversion tools administratively, citing Operation Gatekeeper and other smuggling cases.

letters_and_statements.title: House Select Committee report 'Buy What It Can, Steal What It Must: China's Campaign to Acquire Frontier AI Capabilities'
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Committee investigation found China remains the largest buyer of chipmaking equipment, lawfully buys large volumes of AI chips, runs sophisticated smuggling networks, and distills US frontier models at industrial scale; it recommends passing the MATCH Act (H.R.8170) and AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R.6875).

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar statement backing House Foreign Affairs passage of export-control bills (MATCH Act, Stop Stealing Our Chips Act, Deterring American AI Model Theft Act)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Moolenaar praised the committee's bipartisan approval of bills restricting chipmaking-equipment sales, rewarding chip-smuggling whistleblowers, and sanctioning AI model theft.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar and Garbarino letters to Airbnb and Anysphere launching investigation into use of Chinese AI models
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The chairs of the China Select Committee and Homeland Security opened a joint probe into US companies' use of PRC-developed models (DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, MiniMax), citing distillation of US frontier models and cybersecurity risk.
letters_and_statements.notes: Probe continued 2026-07-31 per homeland.house.gov; a related DoorDash Chinese-AI inquiry appears on the Select Committee site (not opened).

letters_and_statements.title: Banks and Warren joint statement introducing the AI OVERWATCH Act
letters_and_statements.plain_english: A bipartisan group introduced the Senate AI OVERWATCH Act to codify the ban on exporting the most advanced AI chips to China; Warren said selling advanced chips to China is 'bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

letters_and_statements.title: Warren statement on Commerce easing export controls on AI chips to the UAE (G42/MGX)
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Warren called the license-free access for G42 a 'corrupt deal' tied to the UAE royal's stake in the Trump family crypto firm and demanded Lutnick and Kessler testify.

letters_and_statements.title: Banks statement securing the AI OVERWATCH Act in the Senate FY2027 NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Banks announced his bill codifying Trump's restrictions on the most advanced AI chip exports to adversaries was included in the Senate Armed Services NDAA, and said GAIN AI's principles had been incorporated in Commerce's January 2026 H200 rule.
letters_and_statements.notes: Cloture on the motion to proceed to S.4784 failed 50-46 the same day (Record Vote 195); the bill's fate is unresolved as of 2026-09-12.

letters_and_statements.title: Moolenaar and Whitesides letter to Lutnick urging Commerce not to allow US purchases of Chinese memory chips
letters_and_statements.plain_english: A bipartisan pair urged Commerce to hold firm against letting Apple and other US firms buy DRAM from Chinese, military-linked memory makers despite the AI-driven memory shortage, and to expand export controls on Chinese memory producers.

letters_and_statements.title: Warren letter to BIS Under Secretary Kessler invoking ECRA to compel documents on the Foundry Due Diligence loophole
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Warren used her statutory authority under the Export Control Reform Act to demand records on gaps created by the AI Diffusion Rule rescission, especially whether BIS is enforcing the worldwide licensing requirement that stopped Huawei from ordering millions of TSMC chips via a shell company.

letters_and_statements.title: Kamlager-Dove and Meeks letter to Lutnick on financial conflicts behind loosening UAE export controls
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Two senior Foreign Affairs Democrats demanded answers on BIS's July 10, 2026 upgrade of the UAE to trusted-partner export status, citing G42 diversion risks to China and the Abu Dhabi royal's 49 percent stake in the Trump family's World Liberty Financial.
letters_and_statements.notes: Release says a first letter on the same conflicts was sent in February 2026.

letters_and_statements.title: Gallagher, McCaul, Hagerty and Young Kim letter to Commerce Secretary Raimondo: export controls are non-negotiable, abandon US-China working group
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Four Republicans told Raimondo before her China trip not to create a working group with Beijing on chip export controls and that China should expect more, not fewer, controls.

letters_and_statements.title: Cornyn and Casey statement on Senate passage (91-6) of their outbound investment amendment to the FY2024 NDAA
letters_and_statements.plain_english: The sponsors hailed the Senate's 91-6 adoption of the Outbound Investment Transparency Act amendment requiring notification of US investments in Chinese semiconductor, AI and other sensitive technologies.
letters_and_statements.notes: 91-6 tally per CSIS (2023-08-02); the Cornyn release text reviewed did not itself state the number. Roll-call number not confirmed.

letters_and_statements.title: Brown, Reed, Menendez and Warner letter to President Biden urging a significant BIS funding increase in the FY2025 budget
letters_and_statements.plain_english: Senate Banking Chairman Brown and three senior Democrats asked the White House to seek a large increase for BIS export-control administration and enforcement.

chips_china.coverage_notes: METHOD AND CONSTRAINTS. The WebSearch tool budget was exhausted before this task began, and congress.gov, senate.gov, most house.gov member sites, Politico, The Hill and Reuters block the WebFetch tool and curl. Bill numbers, sponsors, full cosponsor rosters, dates, committee votes and roll calls were therefore confirmed from the GPO/govinfo BILLSTATUS XML bulk feed (the congress.gov legislative data feed; source_url fields point to the canonical congress.gov page for each bill) plus govinfo bill text where noted. Bill discovery used the GovTrack API keyword search (119th and 118th) across ~40 queries (chip, semiconductor, export control, DeepSeek, adversarial AI, outbound investment, BIS, Huawei, remote access, AI exports, entity list, cloud, MATCH, SCALE, model theft, etc.). Letters and statements were located via Bing in a real Chrome tab and read directly from the primary press pages (Select Committee on the CCP, HFAC minority, Senate Banking minority/majority, member sites, democrats.senate.gov). The FY2026 NDAA public law text (PL 119-60) and the House-passed FY2027 NDAA (H.R.8800) engrossed text were grepped directly. CONFIRMED VOTES USEFUL FOR A PER-MEMBER TRACKER: House Roll Call 13 (2026-01-12) Remote Access Security Act 369-22; Senate Record Vote 570 (2025-10-09) passage of S.2296 FY26 NDAA carrying the GAIN AI amendment 77-20; Senate Record Votes 647 (cloture 76-20) and 648 (77-20) on final S.1071 FY26 NDAA with COINS Act; House Roll Call 440 (2024-09-23) Building Chips in America Act 257-125; Senate Record Vote 195 (2026-07-14) cloture on FY27 NDAA S.4784 failed 50-46; House Roll Call 278 (2026-07-22) FY27 NDAA H.R.8800 passed 216-212; HFAC committee votes as listed. NOT CONFIRMED / GAPS: (1) the exact amendment number and Senate roll-call number for the 2023 Cornyn-Casey 91-6 outbound-investment vote (tally from Cornyn release and CSIS only); (2) no Senate companion to the 118th ENFORCE Act was found; (3) Sen. Ted Cruz's position on the GAIN AI Act could not be confirmed from a primary source (White House and Nvidia opposition confirmed via Nextgov/press); (4) Cotton's 2025-10-30 Malaysia letter was identified from its PDF on cotton.senate.gov and a search snippet but the full text was not opened; (5) Rep. Krishnamoorthi's own December 2025 H200 statement page was not opened (his position is evidenced by his No Advanced Chips bill and RESTRICT Act cosponsorship); (6) the Select Committee's Dec 2023 'Reset, Prevent, Build' report and its Netherlands/Futurewei letters, the DoorDash Chinese-AI letters, a Warren 2026-08-05 UAE letter, Lawler's Jan 2026 passage statement, and Rounds/Warner May 2026 passage statements were seen only in search results and not opened, so they are omitted; (7) whether the SASC-reported FY27 NDAA text (S.4784) actually contains AI OVERWATCH rests on Banks's release; (8) BIS appropriations levels for FY26/FY27 were not confirmed (FY27 request reportedly adds ~$215M per trade press; Kessler testified to HFAC 2026-07-14); the only BIS-funding letter found is the 118th Brown letter; (9) bill texts for S.4750/H.R.8959 Semiconductor Superiority Act, H.R.8287, S.4976, H.R.1215, H.R.4683, S.4085 and S.Res.490 were not reviewed, so plain_english is from titles and directions are provisional; (10) H.R.3838 (House FY26 NDAA) content on chips was not checked beyond press reports that it lacked GAIN AI; (11) Ro Khanna's Feb 2026 remarks are the only 'fewer_rules' member statement found on the H200 question besides the April 2025 GOP diffusion-rule letter; Republican members who defended the H20/H200 sales are referenced generically by Nextgov but not named there. Bills outside the lane that surfaced (preemption H.R.5388, AI data-center moratorium, Liquid Cooling for AI) were excluded.

caucuses.coverage_notes:
METHOD AND LIMITS. The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the first batch of 8 searches, so most work used direct fetches, curl, an in-Chrome browser tab, and DuckDuckGo/Brave via curl (both eventually rate-limited/captcha'd). Every *.senate.gov committee site, commerce/judiciary/armed-services/help/energy.senate.gov, and several Akamai-fronted house.gov sites (newdemocratcoalition, financialservices, congressionalblockchaincaucus) returned 403 to WebFetch and curl; heinrich.senate.gov, rounds.senate.gov, democrats.senate.gov, help.senate.gov and congress.gov were successfully opened in Chrome instead. Where a committee's own site was unreachable, GovTrack (primary-derived, opened via curl) plus clerk.house.gov were used and cross-checked against Wikipedia. LegiStorm caucus rosters are paywalled and were not used.

CONFIRMED FROM OPENED PRIMARY PAGES: all 24 AI Task Force members + committees (Lieu release + report Appendix I images); full 83-name Congressional AI Caucus roster (caucus site) and its four officers (CHA CMO list 4/23/26 PDF, text-extracted); Senate AI Caucus 18-name roster (Heinrich page); the Senate 'gang of four' (Schumer floor remarks 5/15/2024); E&C privacy working group (E&C release 2/12/2025); RSC Emerging Tech Task Force (RSC release 4/7/2025); House Democratic AI Commission leaders (Jeffries release 12/9/2025); GAAIA draft six (Trahan release 6/4/2026) and H.R. 9925 sponsor/cosponsors (congress.gov); S. 2750 sponsor/date/0 cosponsors (congress.gov); House GOP leadership AI statement (Scalise release 3/20/2026); Clerk profiles for E&C, CMT, Science, R&T, Judiciary, Courts/IP/AI, HASC CITI, Select CCP.

SECONDARY-ONLY: HFSC 118th AI working group roster (Husch Blackwell); Klobuchar-Thune-Cruz/Cantwell negotiation (Nextgov 9/11/2026); Khanna's Jan 5, 2026 CCP ranking-member start date (Wikipedia). Party affiliations for the 79 rank-and-file AI Caucus members were added by the researcher because the caucus site lists only districts.

NOT FOUND / NULL: no formal 'House AI Task Force 2.0' in the 119th (Beyer said in June 2025 members were lobbying Speaker Johnson for one); no formal Energy & Commerce AI working group beyond the GOP privacy working group; no formally chartered Senate Commerce or Senate Republican AI working group (Cruz's framework is a chair-only document; the 2026 bill is a Klobuchar-Thune-Cruz negotiation); no Senate Democratic AI task force in 2025-2026 (Schumer's 2026 task force is on elections, not AI); New Democrat Coalition AI Working Group 119th leadership unconfirmed (site blocked; 118th chair Kilmer/vice chair Stevens known only from an unopened snippet, so left out of data); Congressional Blockchain Caucus is not on the 4/23/26 CMO list and its site is blocked, so only the Crypto Caucus officers are asserted; the Great American AI Act omnibus itself has no bill number (only its FRONTIER Act title, H.R. 9925, was introduced). The Senate AI Caucus page is partly stale (lists ex-Senators Braun and Romney; includes Husted). Recommended manual follow-ups: New Dem AI WG 119th officers; whether HFSC re-formed its AI working group under Chair Hill; any Senate Commerce markup or text release of the Klobuchar-Thune bill after Sept 11, 2026; Mikie Sherrill's current House status on the AI Caucus roster.

events.headline: Trump signs EO 14409 creating voluntary 30-day pre-release federal cyber review of frontier AI models; Hawley says he would go further
events.plain_english: The executive order 'Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security' (postponed from May 21) lets frontier developers voluntarily submit models to Treasury/NSA/CISA up to 30 days before release, creates an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse, and directs CISA binding directives. It does not mandate licensing. Hawley said the reporting and monitoring should be mandatory, via his bill with Blumenthal.

members_involved.name: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: "I would go farther. I think we ought to enact my legislation that I have with Senator Blumenthal that would make that sort of reporting and monitoring mandatory."

members_involved.name: Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)

events.headline: Obernolte and Trahan release 269-page Great American AI Act discussion draft with 3-year preemption of state AI-development laws
events.plain_english: The bipartisan House E&C draft would put NIST's CAISI in statute ($100M/yr FY27-29), require large frontier developers ($500M+ revenue) to publish safety frameworks, undergo semi-annual audits by licensed Independent Verification Organizations, and report critical incidents (24 hours for catastrophic, 15 days otherwise), with penalties up to $1M/day. It preempts state laws 'specifically regulating the development' of AI models for three years (sunset Dec 2029) but not deployment/use laws. The House Democratic AI Commission chairs said it 'does not meet the enormity of the moment.'

events.headline: Commerce imposes export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models; lawmakers protest 'no law, no process, no oversight'
events.plain_english: After Amazon flagged a jailbreak, Commerce's BIS sent Anthropic a letter (June 12; some outlets date the action June 13) restricting Fable 5/Mythos 5 for foreign nationals, effectively taking both models offline worldwide. On June 25 Beyer called the approach 'haphazard'; a bipartisan group of four House members wrote Lutnick (June 18) demanding the legal basis. Commerce partially restored Mythos 5 to ~100 vetted entities (June 26/27) and rescinded controls June 30, with Lutnick 'reserving the right to reevaluate.'

events.headline: Senate cloture on FY27 NDAA (S. 4784) fails 50-46 as Democrats protest Iran war; chip-export bills stranded in manager's package

Schumer said Democrats would not treat the NDAA as 'business as usual' without authorization for Iran operations. The manager's amendment had folded in the AI OVERWATCH Act (SA 6575), Chip Security Act (SA 6683), MATCH Act (SA 6585) and a Schiff-Banks adversarial-threats provision (SA 6561), none adopted. As of Sept 12 the Senate had taken no further NDAA action.

summer_2026.coverage_notes:
METHOD AND LIMITS: The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after ~20 queries, so discovery relied on Google News RSS queries (hundreds) plus direct WebFetch/curl of primary pages, congress.gov API (DEMO_KEY, rate-limited), GovTrack, clerk.house.gov roll-call XML, and Wayback copies of Akamai-blocked senate.gov pages. Politico, Punchbowl, Axios, WaPo, Reuters, CNBC (partly), NYT, Bloomberg, LA Times, Guardian, and most senate.gov/house.gov press pages could not be opened; where an item rests only on a headline/date from Google News, the event text says so ("not opened"). Dates are exact where taken from congress.gov/clerk/senate XML; a few (Senate Banking hearing June 10 vs 11; Anthropic export order June 12 vs 13; Fall resignation announced July 20/departed July 31) carry the discrepancy in-text.

KEY VERIFIED VOTES: House KIDS Act H.R. 7757 passed June 29, roll 228, 267-117 (R 162-32, D 104-85). House NDAA H.R. 8800 passed July 22, roll 278, 216-212 (R 209-7, D 6-205; names listed); H.Res. 1398 failed June 30 (roll 231, 198-224); H.Res. 1438 passed July 21 (roll 254, 214-211); recommit failed 213-216 (roll 277). Senate cloture on S. 4784 failed July 14, Record Vote 195, 50-46 (50 R yea, 45 D + 1 R nay; the GOP nay not identified). E&C reported H.R. 9340 52-0 (July 21) and filed H. Rept. 119-814 (Sept 10). Senate Commerce Aug 5 markup outcomes from the committee's own release (via Wayback). Senate passed FY27 CR H.R. 6500 90-6 (Aug 8).

NOT FOUND / NULLS: No Commerce Department list of "onerous" state AI laws, no FCC preemption NPRM, and no new DOJ AI Litigation Task Force lawsuit against a state frontier-AI law (CA SB 53, NY RAISE, IL SB 315) was found June 1-Sept 12; the Task Force's only observed activity is the April Colorado intervention (pre-window) and the Aug 19 Minnesota amicus. Text of the Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar bill was not public as of Sept 12 (no bill number). Bill numbers unconfirmed: Sanders-Casar Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, Sanders AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, Lummis POWER Up Act, Gottheimer-Lawler Stop Rogue AI Act, Guthrie-Palmer Water Cost Accountability Act (discussion draft). Sponsors of the House NDAA AI sections (Sec. 240 AGI Preparedness Initiative, Sec. 1502 incident reporting) were not identified. Only 4 of the 16 Republicans in Public First Action's $15M project are named (Hawley, Cotton, Moody, Donalds; Punchbowl paywalled). The four House signers of the June 18 Lutnick letter beyond Trahan were not identified. Newsweek's Sept 1 "Republicans breaking with Trump on data centers" list, the July 30 Punchbowl "Thune's AI plan clashes with Anthropic" details, and the WaPo July 28 "Dems' strategy for the AI markup" could not be opened. GUARD Act (S. 3062) saw no floor action after its April 30 Judiciary vote. The Senate Judiciary tech-CEO hearing planned for late July was reportedly delayed by Sen. Lindsey Graham's death (July 2026); whether it was held was not confirmed. Senate Appropriations marked up FY27 CJS on June 25 (AIP listing) but NIST/CAISI AI funding details were not confirmed. Senate Commerce has an executive session scheduled Sept 16 (JAWBONE Act and Ali Revival Act listed); no AI framework bill was on that agenda as of Sept 12. Primary results for Hern (June 16), McKinney (Aug 4), Markey (Sept 1), Menendez (June 2) rest on wire/local headlines with LTF/PFA backing confirmed from opened sources.

PRE-WINDOW CONTEXT USED: the 99-1 Senate vote killing the state AI moratorium was July 1, 2025 (not 2026); CAP Action's Aug 24, 2026 article about "almost every House Republican" voting to block state/local data center authority refers to the May 22, 2025 OBBBA vote and is excluded.
