events.headline: Sen. Tom Cotton introduces the DATA Act of 2026 to let AI data centers build fully off-grid power and escape FERC/DOE regulation
events.plain_english: Cotton's bill would create 'consumer-regulated electric utilities' that can serve data centers if they are physically isolated from the bulk power grid, exempting them from Federal Power Act and Energy Department rules. It is the deregulatory answer to the data center electricity-price fight, versus Democratic bills making data centers pay grid costs.

members_involved.name: Tom Cotton (R-AR)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the DATA Act of 2026 on Jan. 8, saying it 'will eliminate outdated federal regulations and enable manufacturers, data centers, and other energy-intensive industries to build customized electricity systems without impacting existing power grids.'

events.headline: House passes the Remote Access Security Act (H.R. 2683) to close the cloud loophole in AI chip export controls
events.plain_english: The House passed a bill letting the Commerce Department extend export controls to remote access of controlled US technology — aimed at Chinese firms renting US AI chips through cloud services instead of buying them. The Select Committee on the CCP applauded passage.

members_involved.name: House Select Committee on the CCP (Chairman John Moolenaar, R-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Applauded House passage as a way to 'restrict foreign adversaries' ability to access technologies, including AI chips, remotely through cloud computing services.'

events.headline: Senate passes the DEFIANCE Act by unanimous consent in direct response to Grok deepfakes
events.plain_english: The Senate passed Sen. Durbin's bill letting victims sue over AI-generated nonconsensual intimate images. Durbin explicitly tied it to X and Grok generating sexualized images of real people, including children.

members_involved.name: Dick Durbin (D-IL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor; sought and won unanimous consent. Said the bill gives victims 'the tools to fight back against those who would exploit them,' and criticized X for not stopping Grok from creating 'exploitive images.'

events.headline: Commerce formalizes the H200-to-China rule; House Foreign Affairs members split on the record
events.plain_english: BIS announced the rule allowing licensed sales of Nvidia H200 chips to China (Trump had confirmed approval with a 25% cut to the US). Republicans and Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee attacked or hedged on it the same week.

members_involved.name: Brian Mast (R-FL), HFAC Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Nvidia has made such good chips that if they were sold freely to the [Chinese Communist Party], the CCP would likely overtake us in the AI arms race.'

members_involved.name: Bill Huizenga (R-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Said he appreciated the rule but that 'the devil's in the details' and 'rules and regulations are only as good as your willingness to enforce them.'

members_involved.name: Gregory Meeks (D-NY), HFAC Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Called the policy 'a strategic mistake that degrades national security.'

members_involved.name: Jim Costa (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Said the rule's non-military-use requirement 'rings hollow' because of China's Military-Civil Fusion strategy.

events.headline: House Science research subcommittee hearing: OSTP's Kratsios testifies on the AI Action Plan and the December preemption executive order
events.plain_english: In the administration's first Hill appearance after Trump's December 2025 executive order on state AI laws, Kratsios gave few specifics on the promised national standard. Obernolte pushed a 'federal lane/state lane' framing; Lofgren called the order unconstitutional and attacked federal payments to Musk's Grok.

members_involved.name: Jay Obernolte (R-CA), Research and Technology Subcommittee Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Chaired the hearing. Said 'there should be a federal lane, and that there should be a state lane,' with the federal government going first in defining preemptive guardrails, and pressed Kratsios on what those guardrails would be.

members_involved.name: Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), full committee Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Said she believes the December executive order is unconstitutional; attacked federal equity stakes in AI/tech firms as 'socialism'; on federal purchases of Grok said 'Essentially we're paying Elon Musk to give perverts access to a child pornography machine.'

events.headline: Senate Commerce hearing 'Plugged Out' turns into an AI-and-kids hearing; Cantwell links it to opposing preemption
events.plain_english: Cruz's screen-time hearing produced expert testimony that AI companion apps are a bigger risk to children than social media. Cantwell used it to argue Congress cannot tell states to stand down on protecting kids. The same morning Cantwell, Klobuchar and Markey wrote to the CPSC about AI chatbots embedded in children's toys.

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX), Senate Commerce Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Convened the Jan. 15 full committee hearing 'Plugged Out: Examining the Impact of Technology on America's Youth' and promoted the Kids Off Social Media Act with Sen. Schatz.

members_involved.name: Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'We need meaningful safeguards on AI to address the harms they cause... That is why we cannot tell states to stand down from protecting their kids.'

members_involved.name: Amy Klobuchar (D-MN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-led a letter to CPSC Acting Chairman Peter Feldman on AI chatbots in children's toys.

members_involved.name: Ed Markey (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed the CPSC letter warning that 'AI poses significant risks when used by children, especially without safeguards in place.'

events.headline: Sen. Van Hollen introduces the Power for the People Act, the first big Democratic data center ratepayer bill of the year
events.plain_english: The bill would make data centers supply their own power, pay for local transmission upgrades, and push states toward a separate rate class for them, with FERC directed to keep those costs off ordinary ratepayers. Seven other Senate Democrats backed it.

members_involved.name: Chris Van Hollen (D-MD)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor. 'Although they are not the only factor causing electricity prices to rise, it is clear that new data center energy demand is having a significant and growing impact on Americans' utility bills.'

members_involved.name: Dick Durbin (D-IL); Cory Booker (D-NJ); Tammy Duckworth (D-IL); Tina Smith (D-MN); Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD); Peter Welch (D-VT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Named among the seven Democratic senators supporting the bill.

events.headline: Markey and Rep. Summer Lee reintroduce the BIAS Act to require AI civil rights offices at federal agencies
events.plain_english: The bill would require federal agencies that use, fund or oversee AI to stand up civil rights offices staffed by experts to police bias and discrimination, and report to Congress.

members_involved.name: Ed Markey (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Reintroduced the Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems (BIAS) Act in the Senate.

members_involved.name: Summer Lee (D-PA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Reintroduced the House companion.

events.headline: Eight Senate Democrats demand answers from X, Meta, Alphabet, Snap, Reddit and TikTok on sexualized deepfakes
events.plain_english: A second Grok-driven letter, this one to six platform CEOs, demanding their policies, enforcement approach, technical safeguards, detection, monetization controls and victim notification procedures for nonconsensual sexual deepfakes.

members_involved.name: Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE); Tammy Baldwin (D-WI); Richard Blumenthal (D-CT); Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY); Mark Kelly (D-AZ); Ben Ray Luján (D-NM); Brian Schatz (D-HI); Adam Schiff (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Signed the letter: 'many AI systems claim to block explicit pornography. In practice, however... users are finding ways around these guardrails. Or these guardrails are failing.'

events.headline: House Foreign Affairs advances the AI Overwatch Act 42-2-1, giving Congress arms-sale-style veto power over AI chip exports
events.plain_english: The central chip-export fight of the window. Mast's bill would give Congress 30 days to review and block advanced chip exports to China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and Cuba, revoke existing licenses, and impose a temporary ban until the administration submits a national security strategy. White House AI czar David Sacks opposed it.

members_involved.name: Brian Mast (R-FL), HFAC Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor. 'If we are selling another country anything that could give them an advantage on the battlefield, it requires congressional notification.' Also: 'Companies like Nvidia are requesting to sell millions of advanced AI chips... to Chinese military companies like Alibaba and Tencent.'

members_involved.name: Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Voted yes: 'While I wish the bill before us today directly prohibited the sale of H200s, it nevertheless puts in place robust guardrails that would delay those sales and allow for congressional review.'

members_involved.name: Andy Barr (R-KY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: One of only two committee members to vote no.

members_involved.name: Rich McCormick (R-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: The other no vote.

members_involved.name: Darrell Issa (R-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Voted present, warning the bill would put Congress in the 'position of being a regulator': 'Let me assure you, Congress is not a good regulator.'

members_involved.name: John Moolenaar (R-MI); Bill Huizenga (R-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Original cosponsors of the bill (15 cosponsors at markup).

events.headline: Moolenaar says Nvidia helped DeepSeek build models later used by China's military, and demands strict H200 rule enforcement
events.plain_english: The Select Committee on the CCP chairman wrote that documents showed Nvidia gave DeepSeek extensive technical support that let it squeeze frontier performance out of export-controlled H800 chips, and argued this justifies enforcing the H200 rule even if that blocks H200 exports to China entirely.

members_involved.name: John Moolenaar (R-MI), Chairman, Select Committee on the CCP
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Wrote that 'rigorous enforcement of the Department's H200 export rule... is essential – even if such enforcement effectively prevents H200 exports to the PRC altogether,' and that Nvidia's DeepSeek work shows Military-Civil Fusion makes commercial/military distinctions impossible.

events.headline: House E&C Energy Subcommittee holds FERC oversight hearing framed around winning the AI race and data center costs
events.plain_english: Latta chaired FERC's first Hill appearance under the Trump commissioners, arguing data center growth can stabilize the grid and lower prices, while members pressed on pipelines, transmission and post-Winter Storm Fern price spikes.

members_involved.name: Bob Latta (R-OH), Energy Subcommittee Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Winning the AI race, reshoring manufacturing jobs, and lowering energy costs are not mutually exclusive... the growth of large energy users like data centers and manufacturing facilities can help stabilize the grid and make electricity more affordable.'

members_involved.name: August Pfluger (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Pressed FERC Chairman Swett on states blocking pipelines and the effect on affordability.

members_involved.name: Troy Balderson (R-OH)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned FERC on pipeline capacity and Northeast price spikes after Winter Storm Fern.

events.headline: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei lobbies the Hill; Warren and Banks announce a Senate companion to the AI Overwatch Act
events.plain_english: Amodei met Senate Banking Republicans and then Warren privately. Warren said her bill with Banks will be a Senate version of the AI Overwatch Act, including a two-year ban on Nvidia Blackwell sales to China, and described it as a rework of the GAIN AI Act. She also said she would join Cotton on a chip-tracking bill.

members_involved.name: Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Senate Banking Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Met Amodei; said 'We had a good conversation about the importance of keeping high-tech chips here in the U.S.' and 'Selling these chips to the Chinese is bad in the short run and worse in the long run.'

members_involved.name: Jim Banks (R-IN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Partner on the Senate AI Overwatch companion with a two-year Blackwell ban.

members_involved.name: Tom Cotton (R-AR)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Named by Warren as her partner on a bill to track advanced chips to prevent adversary misuse.

events.headline: Ossoff leads Senate Democrats questioning the Pentagon's use of Grok
events.plain_english: Six Democrats wrote to Defense Secretary Hegseth citing Grok's antisemitic outputs and its generation of sexual deepfakes of children, asking what rules govern DoD's use of the model and what safeguards and data protections exist.

members_involved.name: Jon Ossoff (D-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Led the letter: 'Grok's generation of such content has triggered various investigations of the platform and the potential use of this model by a federal agency is troubling.'

members_involved.name: Chris Van Hollen (D-MD); Adam Schiff (D-CA); Dick Durbin (D-IL); John Hickenlooper (D-CO); Raphael Warnock (D-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed the letter to Hegseth.

events.headline: Hawley and Blumenthal introduce the GRID Act, the first bipartisan bill to stop data centers from raising consumers' power bills
events.plain_english: The bill guarantees no data-center-driven consumer rate increases, gives consumers first priority on the grid, requires new data centers to use off-grid generation (10-year off-ramp for existing ones), and mandates public disclosure of their electricity use.

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor: 'American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country. This is unacceptable.'

members_involved.name: Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Our GRID Act stops Big Tech's AI-driven drain on family's pocketbooks... Families should not be forced to bankroll Big Tech's electricity and infrastructure costs.'

events.headline: Anthropic puts $20 million into Public First Action, creating a counterweight to the pro-AI super PAC network
events.plain_english: Anthropic funded a new bipartisan 501(c)(4) led by former Reps. Brad Carson (D-OK) and Chris Stewart (R-UT), tied to Democratic and Republican super PACs. Its stated priorities include opposing preemption of state AI laws without a strong federal standard, chip export controls, and AI-bio risk rules. Its first ads backed two Republicans.

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Beneficiary of Public First Action's first six-figure ad buy, supporting her Kids Online Safety Act and the TRUMP America AI Act.

members_involved.name: Pete Ricketts (R-NE)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Beneficiary of the other first ad buy; cited for introducing legislation to limit advanced US chip sales to China.

members_involved.name: Brad Carson (former Rep., D-OK); Chris Stewart (former Rep., R-UT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead Public First Action. Carson: Leading the Future is 'driven by three billionaires who are close to Donald Trump... We believe it should be more democratically accountable.'

events.headline: Leading the Future pledges $5 million for Rep. Byron Donalds' Florida governor bid, its first state-level race
events.plain_english: The pro-AI super PAC backed a sitting House member running for governor, in a state where Gov. DeSantis was pushing AI regulation the industry opposed.

members_involved.name: Byron Donalds (R-FL-19)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Received the $5M pledge. His chief strategist said 'Byron believes we should be a standard-bearer for responsible innovation while also protecting Floridians.'

events.headline: E&C Democrats open an investigation into Elon Musk and xAI over Grok's nonconsensual sexual images
events.plain_english: Three senior House Energy and Commerce Democrats wrote to Musk demanding when he learned Grok was generating explicit images, what guardrails existed at the Edit Image launch, image counts, law enforcement/NCMEC takedown requests, and copies of responses to other regulators, with a March 5 deadline.

members_involved.name: Frank Pallone (D-NJ), E&C Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Led the letter: 'We are deeply concerned about xAI's refusal to put a stop to the creation of nonconsensual sexualized images, particularly of children.'

members_involved.name: Jan Schakowsky (D-IL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed as Commerce, Manufacturing and Trade Subcommittee Ranking Member.

members_involved.name: Yvette Clarke (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed as Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee Ranking Member.

events.headline: Anthropic-funded Public First Action spends $450,000 for Alex Bores as Leading the Future spends $1.1 million attacking him
events.plain_english: The NY-12 primary to replace Rep. Nadler became the first proxy war between the two AI super PAC networks. Bores authored New York's RAISE Act, the frontier AI safety law the industry wanted preempted.

members_involved.name: Alex Bores (NY State Assembly, candidate NY-12)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Target of $1.1M in Leading the Future attack ads over his sponsorship of New York's RAISE Act; backed with $450,000 from Anthropic-funded Public First Action.

events.headline: House Science oversight panel holds a data center infrastructure hearing as Trump announces a 'ratepayer protection pledge' in the State of the Union
events.plain_english: Republicans and industry witnesses pushed permitting reform and more generation; the subcommittee chair acknowledged residential ratepayers could end up subsidizing upgrades that serve data centers. Trump the same day announced tech companies would commit to providing their own power.

members_involved.name: Rich McCormick (R-GA), Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee Chair
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Data centers consume vast amounts of electricity, sometimes 10 to 50 times more per square foot than traditional buildings... That raises serious questions of whether residential ratepayers could end up subsidizing upgrades that primarily serve high-intensity users.'

events.headline: House passes the Small Business AI Advancement Act (H.R. 3679)
events.plain_english: A bipartisan bill directing NIST to build AI resources for small businesses cleared the House and went to the Senate — one of the few AI bills to actually pass a chamber in this window.

members_involved.name: Mike Collins (R-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor of H.R. 3679, which passed the House Feb. 23-24.

members_involved.name: Haley Stevens (D-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-lead sponsor.

events.headline: House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing on export control enforcement highlights DeepSeek training on smuggled Blackwell chips
events.plain_english: Huizenga used the hearing to argue China's AI progress depends on stolen US technology — smuggled chips, distillation of US models, and smuggled chipmaking equipment.

members_involved.name: Bill Huizenga (R-MI), South and Central Asia Subcommittee Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Opening remarks: 'China's AI chips cannot compete with ours, so Beijing is resorting to theft instead,' citing reporting that DeepSeek's latest model was trained on smuggled Nvidia Blackwell chips and that Chinese models are distilling US labs' models.

events.headline: Senators from both parties demand the Pentagon back off its ultimatum to Anthropic
events.plain_english: As DoD threatened Anthropic over contractual limits banning mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous lethal weapons, senators publicly said Congress, not the Pentagon alone, should set those rules. Outside groups formally asked Congress to investigate.

members_involved.name: Thom Tillis (R-NC)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Why in the hell are we having this discussion in public?... this is sophomoric.' Added: 'It's fair to say that Congress needs to weigh in if they have a tool that could actually result in mass surveillance.'

members_involved.name: Gary Peters (D-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'The deadline is incredibly tight... That should not be the case if you're dealing with mass surveillance of civilians. You're also dealing with the potential use of lethal force without a human in the loop.'

events.headline: Mast accuses Nvidia's CEO of asking Washington to trust the CCP as House pushes chip export limits
events.plain_english: In a CNBC interview tied to the AI Overwatch Act, the Foreign Affairs chairman escalated directly against Jensen Huang, framing the chip fight as Congress versus the White House and Nvidia.

members_involved.name: Brian Mast (R-FL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'The joke here is, Jensen wants us to trust the CCP. Anybody watching this should laugh.'

events.headline: Cantwell, Young, Hickenlooper and Blackburn reintroduce the Future of AI Innovation Act
events.plain_english: The bill would authorize NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (formerly the AI Safety Institute) to write voluntary guidance, standards and benchmarks, and create an AI testbed program with DOE and NSF.

members_involved.name: Maria Cantwell (D-WA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor: the bill 'brings together private sector and government experts to develop voluntary standards for AI, create new assessment tools, and conduct testing.'

members_involved.name: Todd Young (R-IN); John Hickenlooper (D-CO); Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-sponsors of the reintroduced bill.

events.headline: Coons condemns the Pentagon labeling Anthropic a supply chain risk
events.plain_english: After Hegseth directed DoD to designate Anthropic a supply chain risk — a label usually reserved for foreign adversaries like Huawei — the top Democrat on Senate Appropriations Defense called it an attack on free enterprise that will be thrown out in court.

members_involved.name: Chris Coons (D-DE), Ranking Member, Senate Appropriations Defense Subcommittee
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'The Trump administration's decision to label Anthropic a supply chain risk to national security weakens free enterprise, harms innovation, and makes Americans less safe... when this administration takes a page out of Xi Jinping's playbook and tells our leading companies to embrace the party line or lose its contracts...' He urged immediate reversal.

events.headline: AI-linked super PACs spend about $2 million in North Carolina primaries
events.plain_english: PACs tied to the AI industry spent heavily for Rep. Valerie Foushee in NC-04 and Republican Laurie Buckhout in NC-01 in the closing days of the primaries — an early demonstration that the money flows to both parties and that the ads mostly avoid mentioning AI.

members_involved.name: Valerie Foushee (D-NC-04)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Backed by AI-industry-linked PAC spending in her contested primary.

events.headline: E&C Chairman Guthrie suggests China may be behind US anti-data-center sentiment
events.plain_english: Speaking at the ACA Connects summit, the Energy and Commerce chairman said adversaries like China and Russia might be feeding misinformation to sour Americans on data centers as a way to slow the US in the AI race.

members_involved.name: Brett Guthrie (R-KY), E&C Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'If you're China, what would you want to do to keep Americans from building data centers, how do you do that? You use our system of free press and freedom of information to influence people.' He also previewed the KIDS Act markup.

events.headline: House Energy and Commerce advances the GOP kids online safety package 28-24 after bipartisan talks collapse
events.plain_english: The committee approved the Kids Internet and Digital Safety (KIDS) Act — which folds in a weakened KOSA plus the SAFE BOTs Act requiring AI chatbots to disclose they are not human — along with the App Store Accountability Act and COPPA 2.0. Democrats objected mainly to the preemption language and the removal of KOSA's duty of care.

members_involved.name: Brett Guthrie (R-KY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Called the KIDS Act 'the most serious, comprehensive piece of legislation to address online safety to date' and said 'the absence of a bipartisan consensus cannot be an excuse for inaction.'

members_involved.name: Frank Pallone (D-NJ)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'These bills would leave our kids less safe online than they are today,' arguing Republicans handed Big Tech a gift by weakening preemption standards and the knowledge standard.

members_involved.name: Jake Auchincloss (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Called the session a 'Meta markup' and the App Store Accountability Act a 'false flag operation by Meta.'

events.headline: Thirty former defense and intelligence officials ask Congress to investigate the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic; Gillibrand calls it dangerous misuse
events.plain_english: A bipartisan coalition including former CIA director Michael Hayden told lawmakers the supply chain risk authority was meant for adversary-controlled firms, not American companies refusing to drop safeguards. Gillibrand, on both Armed Services and Intelligence, publicly condemned the designation.

members_involved.name: Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Called the designation 'a dangerous misuse of a tool meant to address adversary-controlled technology' and 'shortsighted, self-destructive, and a gift to our adversaries.'

events.headline: Sen. Mark Kelly presses Pentagon officials on AI in targeting decisions at a Senate Armed Services hearing
events.plain_english: Kelly asked whether AI systems assisted targeting in Operation Epic Fury drone strikes and who validated them, and noted Congress has set no statutory framework for AI in lethal military operations while companies publish their own safety frameworks.

members_involved.name: Mark Kelly (D-AZ)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned Maj. Gen. Steven M. Marks on autonomous capabilities in the LUCAS drone system: 'Are AI systems being used to assist in targeting decisions during this operation?' and stated 'Congress has not yet set any kind of clear statutory framework for how AI can be used in lethal military operations.'

events.headline: Warner and Hawley lead a bipartisan letter demanding federal data on AI's labor market impact
events.plain_english: Senators asked the Labor Department, BLS and Census to expand the Current Population Survey, JOLTS and the youth longitudinal survey to capture AI's effect on jobs, arguing federal statistics are inadequate for the moment.

members_involved.name: Mark Warner (D-VA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-led the letter: 'At a time when the U.S. workforce is approaching an inflection point due to the acceleration of artificial intelligence, adaptable and responsive federal statistical agencies are necessary.'

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-led the letter to Labor Secretary Chavez-DeRemer and statistical agency heads.

events.headline: Cantwell and Moran introduce the NSF AI Education Act of 2026
events.plain_english: A bipartisan bill authorizing NSF scholarships, fellowships, AI Centers of Excellence and a land-grant university grant program to build the AI workforce.

members_involved.name: Maria Cantwell (D-WA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor: 'Demand for AI expertise is already high and will continue to grow, and we must meet that demand if we are to out-compete China.'

members_involved.name: Jerry Moran (R-KS)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-sponsor: 'As the capabilities of AI increase, we must make certain the next generation can utilize its full potential.'

events.headline: Sen. Slotkin introduces the AI Guardrails Act to limit Pentagon AI use after the Anthropic fight
events.plain_english: The bill would ban DoD from firing autonomous weapons without human authorization, from using AI for domestic mass surveillance, and from using AI to launch nuclear weapons — codifying exactly the limits Anthropic had insisted on contractually.

members_involved.name: Elissa Slotkin (D-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the AI Guardrails Act: 'Congress is behind in putting left and right limits on the use of AI, and the first place to start should be at the Pentagon.'

events.headline: Sen. Blackburn releases the TRUMP AMERICA AI Act discussion draft, a ~300-page preemption package built around kids, creators and conservatives
events.plain_english: Blackburn's draft is the Senate's main attempt to trade preemption for substance: it folds in KOSA, the GUARD Act, the NO FAKES Act, a duty of care on chatbot developers, third-party audits for political viewpoint discrimination, a DOE-housed Advanced AI Evaluation Program, and a sunset of Section 230 protections.

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Released the discussion draft: 'Instead of pushing AI amnesty, President Trump rightfully called on Congress to pass federal standards... Congress must answer his call to establish one federal rulebook for AI to protect children, creators, conservatives, and communities.' At a Commerce hearing she said 'The president asked me to take a shot at drafting this.'

members_involved.name: Lindsey Graham (R-SC)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: His bill sunsetting Section 230 liability protections two years after enactment was incorporated into the draft.

events.headline: Senate Commerce holds a Section 230 at 30 hearing; senators in both parties balk at full repeal
events.plain_english: The hearing mattered for AI because the repeal/sunset of Section 230 was being folded into AI preemption packages. Cruz was skeptical of full repeal and Blackburn used the hearing to introduce her framework.

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Chaired the hearing; reported as skeptical of a full Section 230 repeal.

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Used the hearing day to roll out her AI framework draft, which sunsets Section 230 protections.

events.headline: White House releases its national AI framework calling for broad preemption; House GOP leadership immediately commits to act
events.plain_english: The four-page framework asked Congress for broad preemption of state AI laws, no open-ended liability for AI firms, regulatory sandboxes, streamlined data center permitting, and no new AI regulator, with carve-outs for generally applicable state laws, zoning and state procurement. Speaker Johnson and four committee chairs issued a joint statement the same day.

members_involved.name: Mike Johnson (R-LA), Speaker; Steve Scalise (R-LA), Majority Leader; Brett Guthrie (R-KY), E&C Chairman; Jim Jordan (R-OH), Judiciary Chairman; Brian Babin (R-TX), Science Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Joint statement: 'To ensure we continue to harness its potential and beat China in the global AI race, Congress must take action... House Republicans look forward to working across the aisle to enact a national framework.'

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Over the last few months, I have worked diligently with the White House, conservative leaders, child safety advocates, members of the creative community, and AI innovators to develop legislation that can garner bipartisan support and accomplish the President's goals.'

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Long-promised preemption legislation; his sandbox bill (SANDBOX Act) is the model for the framework's regulatory sandbox proposal.

events.headline: Speaker Johnson pledges 'regulate only where we must' at the Hill and Valley Forum
events.plain_english: Johnson laid out the House Republican posture on AI: speed, deregulation, and American dominance, days after the White House framework landed.

members_involved.name: Mike Johnson (R-LA), Speaker
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'We have to move at the speed that victory demands. Inaction is unacceptable... simplify and streamline where we can, regulate only where we must, and pave the way for American dominance.'

events.headline: Banks and Warren demand Commerce suspend Nvidia export licenses after the Super Micro smuggling charges
events.plain_english: A bipartisan letter to Secretary Lutnick urged pausing or suspending all active export licenses for advanced Nvidia chips and servers bound for China and Southeast Asian intermediaries, and questioned whether Jensen Huang's public denials of chip diversion misled US officials.

members_involved.name: Jim Banks (R-IN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed: urged 'the immediate pausing, suspension, or other reconsideration of all active export licenses covering advanced Nvidia AI chips and server systems' destined for China and intermediaries in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Singapore.

members_involved.name: Elizabeth Warren (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed; the letter said Huang's statements 'were not simply wrong in hindsight. They were contradicted by reporting available at the time and potentially misled U.S. officials.'

events.headline: Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez unveil the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (S. 4214)
events.plain_english: The most aggressive AI bill of the window: a national moratorium on new AI data center construction until Congress passes safeguards on safety, workers, consumers, civil rights and the environment, plus a ban on exporting AI computing infrastructure to countries without such safeguards.

members_involved.name: Bernie Sanders (I-VT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced S. 4214 on March 25: 'We cannot sit back and allow a handful of billionaire Big Tech oligarchs to make decisions that will reshape our economy, our democracy and the future of humanity... We need a federal moratorium on AI data centers.'

members_involved.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-announced: 'Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society. We must choose humanity over profit.'

events.headline: Sen. Warner calls the AI data center moratorium 'idiocy' and attacks Hegseth's unilateral power over Anthropic
events.plain_english: At the Axios AI+DC Summit, the Senate Intelligence vice chairman publicly split with Sanders and AOC on data centers while also saying one cabinet official should not be able to designate an American AI company a supply chain risk.

members_involved.name: Mark Warner (D-VA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'That would be idiocy... A data center moratorium simply means China is going to move quicker.' On Anthropic: 'you give one guy the ability to declare any company, American company, a global supply chain risk — that is the equivalent of a death sentence.'

events.headline: Hawley uses the Axios AI+DC Summit to demand a chatbot ban for minors and break with his party on AI
events.plain_english: Hawley pushed the GUARD Act as the minimum Congress should do and framed AI companies as needing to be told that profit does not justify harming children.

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'The first thing we need to do is we need to pass legislation that would prevent AI chatbots from targeting minor children... Our message to the companies has got to be no amount of profit justifies destroying children's lives.'

events.headline: Senate Energy and Natural Resources hearing on the bulk power system and load growth after Winter Storm Fern
events.plain_english: Senators examined interregional transmission and permitting as AI-driven demand collides with grid reliability; Sen. King refused to engage on permitting reform while the administration attacks renewables.

members_involved.name: Angus King (I-ME)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'I feel like I'd be dumb to agree to permitting reform which only affected one half of the equation,' declining to participate in reform talks until the administration stops attacking renewable projects.

members_involved.name: Martin Heinrich (D-NM), ENR Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned witnesses on the power system and energy affordability at the March 25-26 proceedings.

events.headline: Warren and Hawley ask EIA to mandate annual data center energy disclosures
events.plain_english: The bipartisan pair asked the Energy Information Administration to require comprehensive annual energy-use reporting from data centers and publish it, going beyond EIA's new voluntary pilot, partly to verify tech companies' Ratepayer Protection Pledge commitments.

members_involved.name: Elizabeth Warren (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed the letter urging EIA to 'establish a mandatory annual reporting requirement for data centers.'

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-signed, arguing the data is 'essential for accurate grid planning.'

events.headline: House Foreign Affairs advances the Chip Security Act requiring location verification on exported AI chips
events.plain_english: The committee unanimously advanced Huizenga's bill directing Commerce to build chip security mechanisms (including location verification) into exported advanced chips, as part of a broader export-control markup.

members_involved.name: Bill Huizenga (R-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor: 'The Chip Security Act enhances protections on AI chip exports by scaling up best security practices and encouraging innovative technologies.'

members_involved.name: Brian Mast (R-FL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'If we're going to export advanced AI chips, we need confidence that they don't end up in the hands of the Chinese military.'

members_involved.name: John Moolenaar (R-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'The Chip Security Act will make it harder to steal from us and protect American jobs and industry.'

events.headline: Markey releases a 'Ratepayer Roadmap' discussion draft as energy prices spike
events.plain_english: Markey's three-part plan to cut household energy bills is the Democratic framing device for the electricity-price politics that AI data centers intensified, including support for state and federal regulators protecting ratepayers from unfair rate hikes.

members_involved.name: Ed Markey (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Released the Ratepayer Roadmap: 'Americans' energy bills are skyrocketing... these increasing costs are a choice being made by the Trump administration and by Republicans in Congress.'

events.headline: Gottheimer announces the bipartisan Parents Decide Act for device-level age verification covering AI platforms
events.plain_english: The bill would require Apple, Google and other OS developers to verify ages at device setup and pass age and parental settings to apps and AI platforms, explicitly to block inappropriate AI chatbot interactions with children.

members_involved.name: Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Announced the Parents Decide Act on April 2, requiring operating system age verification and controls that flow to 'apps and AI platforms.'

events.headline: Leading the Future reports $15M in Q1 and $140M for the cycle; endorses five House Democrats, who are then pressured to disavow it
events.plain_english: The pro-AI network's money became a live issue for Democratic incumbents: a coalition led by the Tech Oversight Project wrote to the five endorsed Democrats asking them to 'disavow' the PAC.

members_involved.name: Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future; targeted by the disavowal letter.

members_involved.name: Sam Liccardo (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future; targeted by the disavowal letter.

members_involved.name: Yvette Clarke (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future despite having proposed regulation of high-impact AI systems in housing, employment and credit.

members_involved.name: Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future; targeted by the disavowal letter.

members_involved.name: Jimmy Gomez (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future; targeted by the disavowal letter.

events.headline: Sen. Ossoff opens an investigation into AI data centers' effect on Georgia power bills, writing to FERC
events.plain_english: Facing reelection in a state with a data center boom, Ossoff wrote to FERC Chairman Laura Swett asking who bears the cost of Georgia Power's approved 9,885 MW capacity increase to serve large customers like data centers. Georgia's PSC pushed back on the inquiry.

members_involved.name: Jon Ossoff (D-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sent a letter to FERC Chairman Laura Swett on April 20 launching an inquiry into AI data centers' impact on Georgia ratepayers.

events.headline: Obernolte and Jacobs introduce the Economy of the Future Commission Act, House companion to Warner-Rounds
events.plain_english: A bipartisan, bicameral commission to study how AI is transforming the economy and recommend policy on workforce, education, federal AI adoption and competitiveness.

members_involved.name: Jay Obernolte (R-CA-23)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-introduced: 'Artificial intelligence will reshape every sector of our economy, and Congress has a responsibility prepare for those changes.'

members_involved.name: Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-introduced: 'I'm constantly hearing from young people who are absolutely terrified that AI will take their jobs and make their degrees irrelevant.'

members_involved.name: Mark Warner (D-VA); Mike Rounds (R-SD)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Senate sponsors of the companion bill. Warner: 'The question isn't whether these changes are coming — it's whether we are prepared.'

events.headline: House Foreign Affairs advances the MATCH Act to cut China off from advanced chipmaking equipment
events.plain_english: Baumgartner's bill, part of what the committee called the largest export control markup in its history, directs Commerce and State to identify chokepoint controls and Chinese advanced-node fabs, targeting semiconductor manufacturing equipment including DUV lithography.

members_involved.name: Michael Baumgartner (R-WA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor: 'The United States cannot afford to leave open back doors that allow the Chinese Communist Party to acquire the tools it needs to leap ahead in semiconductor manufacturing.'

members_involved.name: Brian Mast (R-FL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Without these tools, China can't make their own chips, and they likely won't be able to for years to come.'

events.headline: Commerce Secretary Lutnick tells Senate appropriators no H200s have been sold to China
events.plain_english: At a Senate Appropriations CJS subcommittee hearing on the FY2027 budget, Coons asked whether H200s had been exported; Lutnick said 'We have not sold them any chips as of yet,' a statement that conflicted with Jensen Huang's March comments about having approvals and restarting manufacturing.

members_involved.name: Chris Coons (D-DE)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned Lutnick at the April 22 hearing about whether any H200 chips had been exported to China.

events.headline: House E&C Republicans pivot to legislating on data center power costs, announcing an 'AI and the Grid' hearing
events.plain_english: After months of arguing the issue was mostly state and local, Guthrie and E&C Republicans rallied around concrete ratepayer-protection proposals — the first time GOP leadership did so.

members_involved.name: Brett Guthrie (R-KY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'It's clearly interstate commerce that we have to look at where the federal action should be... We want to make sure people don't pay more for their personal electricity because a data center locates in their community.'

events.headline: Lieu and Obernolte introduce the American Leadership in AI Act, the bipartisan non-preemption package
events.plain_english: The bill codifies NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation ($10M) and the National AI Research Resource, modernizes federal AI procurement, creates an AI Workforce Research Hub, protects AI industry whistleblowers, and adds deepfake remedies and AI fraud penalties. Anthropic-aligned ARI praised it while warning it must not become a justification for preemption.

members_involved.name: Ted Lieu (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-introduced the American Leadership in AI Act on April 27, drawing on the bipartisan House AI Task Force recommendations.

members_involved.name: Jay Obernolte (R-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-introduced the bill.

events.headline: Cruz, Schatz, Curtis and Schiff introduce the CHATBOT Act requiring parental 'family accounts' for kids' AI use
events.plain_english: The Senate Commerce chairman's own chatbot bill: mandatory family accounts for under-13s, parental consent for teens, parental controls over time limits and privacy settings, restrictions on manipulative design, and a ban on targeted ads to minors. It is the parental-control alternative to Hawley's prohibition-based GUARD Act.

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead sponsor: 'The rapid development of sophisticated chatbots has left many parents in the dark... Congress has an opportunity to put parents back in control.'

members_involved.name: Brian Schatz (D-HI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-sponsor; said AI chatbots pose 'real risks for kids,' pointing to harmful interactions and social isolation.

members_involved.name: John Curtis (R-UT); Adam Schiff (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-sponsors of the CHATBOT Act.

events.headline: House E&C Energy Subcommittee holds 'AI and the Grid: Meeting Growing Power Demand While Protecting Ratepayers'
events.plain_english: A legislative hearing on six bills including H.R. 6529, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (Rep. Landsman), which would require FERC to hold a technical conference on protecting residential ratepayers from large-load costs.

members_involved.name: Bob Latta (R-OH)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Chaired: 'the American people are understandably uneasy. Many question whether AI, and the data centers that power it, will ultimately do more harm than good, particularly when it comes to individual energy costs. These concerns deserve to be taken seriously.'

members_involved.name: Frank Pallone (D-NJ); Kathy Castor (D-FL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Delivered Democratic opening statements as full committee and subcommittee ranking members.

members_involved.name: Greg Landsman (D-OH-1)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor of H.R. 6529, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act, considered at the hearing.

events.headline: Marjorie Taylor Greene, now out of Congress, says AI could eliminate 50% of jobs
events.plain_english: In a Tucker Carlson interview, the former congresswoman tied AI job loss to her broader populist critique of the Republican Party — continuing the anti-AI lane she occupied while in office.

members_involved.name: Marjorie Taylor Greene (former Rep., R-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Argued AI could eliminate 50% of jobs and linked AI disruption to public frustration and GOP priorities.

events.headline: Senate Judiciary unanimously advances Hawley's GUARD Act banning AI companions for minors
events.plain_english: The biggest kids-and-chatbots milestone of the window: the committee voted unanimously to ban AI companions for under-18s, require chatbots to disclose they are not human, and create criminal penalties for chatbots that push sexual content or self-harm to minors. Several senators voted yes while flagging age-verification privacy concerns.

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor. Described the bill as one of the first to 'hold accountable AI companies when they push to our children sexually explicit material, when they tell our children they should commit self-harm.'

members_involved.name: Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Cosponsor of the GUARD Act.

members_involved.name: Katie Britt (R-AL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Lead cosponsor; spoke before the vote: 'They should do it anyway. It is sick that we're having...' urging companies to build guardrails.

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Voted yes but said the bill needs 'some revisions,' worried it could ban all AI chatbots for minors.

members_involved.name: Alex Padilla (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Voted yes but flagged 'potential privacy and security risks' in the age-verification component, suggesting it may need to be 'fine-tuned.'

members_involved.name: John Cornyn (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Backed the GUARD Act at the markup: 'Unregulated AI companions have harmed children all across the country, including Texas.'

members_involved.name: Blake Moore (R-UT); Valerie Foushee (D-NC)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the House companion the same day. Moore: 'Parents and policymakers alike need to ground our children's development in real-world interactions.' Foushee: AI chatbots 'continue to put the lives and mental health of children at risk.'

events.headline: Schiff and Rounds introduce the LIFT AI Act for K-12 AI literacy
events.plain_english: An NSF grant program to build AI literacy curriculum, evaluation tools and teacher training, with a House companion.

members_involved.name: Adam Schiff (D-CA); Mike Rounds (R-SD)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the LIFT AI Act in the Senate.

members_involved.name: Tom Kean Jr. (R-NJ); Gabe Amo (D-RI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the House companion.

events.headline: Hegseth calls Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei an 'ideological lunatic' at a Senate Armed Services hearing
events.plain_english: Asked by Sen. Rosen about the Pentagon's treatment of Anthropic, the Defense Secretary attacked Amodei personally and defended DoD's AI use — escalating the fight in front of the committee that writes the NDAA.

members_involved.name: Jacky Rosen (D-NV)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned Hegseth at the SASC hearing about the Anthropic dispute, prompting his 'ideological lunatic' remark.

events.headline: Coons presses Lutnick in writing over contradictory H200 statements
events.plain_english: Coons wrote to Lutnick asking how many H200s had been licensed, shipped, and were planned for licensing, saying the secretary's testimony appeared to contradict Jensen Huang's March 17 statement that Nvidia had US and Chinese approvals and was restarting manufacturing for China.

members_involved.name: Chris Coons (D-DE)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sent the letter: 'Your statements before the committee appear to contradict Huang's comments.' Said he remains 'deeply concerned' and that allowing any Chinese companies to buy these chips 'presents a serious risk to our national security and economic leadership.'

events.headline: Leading the Future endorses three more House Democrats: Hoyle, Menendez and Torres
events.plain_english: The pro-AI network expanded its Democratic footprint. Within days Rep. Hoyle distanced herself from the endorsement — then backtracked — showing the political cost of industry money amid AI backlash.

members_involved.name: Val Hoyle (D-OR-4)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed; then told Transformer 'AI must be regulated so that it does not harm labor or people' and said she 'did not seek out the endorsement,' before reversing course. She had called NDAA preemption efforts 'outrageous' and a 'Big Tech backroom deal.'

members_involved.name: Rob Menendez (D-NJ-8)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed; Think Big, the network's Democratic arm, later reported $661,899 in expenditures supporting him (reported May 21).

members_involved.name: Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed by Leading the Future.

events.headline: Cruz promises a Commerce markup of kids online safety bills at a Capitol rally, then endorses KOSA
events.plain_english: At a Mother's Day-timed rally by parents who lost children, Cruz committed to advancing four kids' bills, and the next day backed Blackburn's Kids Online Safety Act — a significant shift for the chairman who had been the leading preemption advocate.

members_involved.name: Ted Cruz (R-TX)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'If we do nothing else in Washington, we need to be protecting our kids,' promising a markup of four bills including his own Kids Off Social Media Act; the next day he backed KOSA.

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN); Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: KOSA's sponsors, whose bill gained Cruz's support; no Commerce markup had been scheduled as of mid-May.

events.headline: Senate Judiciary privacy subcommittee uses landmark social media verdicts to push KOSA
events.plain_english: Hearing on jury verdicts finding Meta and Google liable for youth harms, used by senators to argue for proactive federal law rather than reactive litigation, and to attack the weaker House package.

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), subcommittee chair
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Said it is 'up to Congress to prevent future harm to our children' and pass KOSA.

members_involved.name: Richard Blumenthal (D-CT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Warned advocates not to accept the 'watered-down shadow legislation' moving through House Energy and Commerce.

members_involved.name: Katie Britt (R-AL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Urged House colleagues to pass the Senate's version.

events.headline: House Appropriations approves the FY27 Commerce-Justice-Science bill funding AI research and research security
events.plain_english: The bill maintains support for AI, quantum and advanced manufacturing research and funds efforts to counter Chinese theft of American research and technology — the appropriations-side expression of the AI competition agenda.

members_involved.name: House Appropriations Committee (Chairman Tom Cole, R-OK)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Approved the FY27 CJS bill, which prioritizes 'artificial intelligence, quantum, and advanced manufacturing' and research security against China.

events.headline: Anthropic briefs the House Homeland Security panel behind closed doors on its Mythos model and cyber risk
events.plain_english: Even while blacklisted by the Pentagon, Anthropic briefed a House committee on frontier model cyber capabilities, setting up a later public hearing on AI security.

members_involved.name: House Homeland Security Committee (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection Subcommittee)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Received a closed-door briefing from Anthropic about Mythos and related cyber risks.

events.headline: Senate Judiciary leaders summon tech CEOs for a June hearing on social media and AI risks to children
events.plain_english: Meta, Alphabet, TikTok and Snap CEOs were called to testify, keeping the kids-safety pressure on through the midterm run-up.

members_involved.name: Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Senate Judiciary Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Joined in summoning the CEOs to testify about social media's risks for children.

events.headline: Sen. Schiff introduces the Energy Cost Fairness and Reliability Act
events.plain_english: Schiff's bill would make data centers pay for all grid upgrades needed to power them, require demand flexibility and battery storage prioritization, block them from consuming existing public power supply, and direct DOE labs to study their energy use.

members_involved.name: Adam Schiff (D-CA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sponsor: 'that growth cannot come at the cost of consumers or society. There need to be guardrails that protect Americans' pocketbooks.'

events.headline: Kelly presses the Pentagon on the contradiction of blacklisting Anthropic while using its AI for operations
events.plain_english: At another Senate Armed Services hearing, Kelly highlighted that DoD had branded Anthropic a supply chain risk while its models were being used operationally.

members_involved.name: Mark Kelly (D-AZ)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Pointed out the contradiction in the Pentagon's decision to brand Anthropic a risk while using its AI for operations.

events.headline: NO FAKES Act reintroduced in both chambers with expanded industry backing
events.plain_english: The bill would create a federal property right in a person's voice and visual likeness and make unauthorized AI digital replicas actionable — a core piece of the 'creators' pillar of the preemption packages.

members_involved.name: María Elvira Salazar (R-FL-27)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: House lead: 'you own your identity—not Big Tech, not scammers, not algorithms.'

members_involved.name: Madeleine Dean (D-PA-4)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: House co-lead: 'The use of AI is only growing, and Congress must catch up with common sense, common ground regulations.'

members_involved.name: Marsha Blackburn (R-TN); Chris Coons (D-DE)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the Senate companion.

events.headline: Leading the Future endorses a second slate of ten House Republicans including Majority Leader Scalise and E&C Chairman Guthrie
events.plain_english: The pro-AI network moved from primaries into leadership, endorsing the members who would write and move any federal AI framework. Its first House GOP slate (12 members, including Obernolte and Emmer) had come earlier in April.

members_involved.name: Steve Scalise (R-LA), Majority Leader
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed: 'Artificial intelligence has the potential to strengthen our economy and ensure America outcompetes China to remain the global leader in innovation.'

members_involved.name: Brett Guthrie (R-KY), E&C Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed in the second slate.

members_involved.name: Richard Hudson (R-NC); Julie Fedorchak (R-ND); French Hill (R-AR); Michael Baumgartner (R-WA); Andy Barr (R-KY); Kevin Hern (R-OK); Lance Gooden (R-TX); Julia Letlow (R-LA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Also endorsed; Barr, Hern and Letlow were simultaneously running for Senate. Baumgartner is the MATCH Act sponsor; Barr was one of two HFAC votes against the AI Overwatch Act.

events.headline: House Armed Services releases the FY27 NDAA chairman's mark and subcommittee prints with new AI provisions
events.plain_english: The $1.15 trillion defense bill (H.R. 8800, introduced May 13) would create a DoD AI incident and vulnerability reporting program and an AI model rapid deployment framework for enterprise AI platforms. Markup followed June 4, outside this window.

members_involved.name: Mike Rogers (R-AL), HASC Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Released the chairman's mark and subcommittee prints on May 26 ahead of the June 4 full committee markup.

members_involved.name: Adam Smith (D-WA), HASC Ranking Member
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Joined in releasing the draft legislative proposals.

members_involved.name: Don Bacon (R-NE), Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation Subcommittee Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Authored the CITI print containing the AI incident reporting and AI rapid deployment provisions.

events.headline: Leading the Future puts $2 million into Senate primaries and $750,000 into House primaries
events.plain_english: The network expanded to Senate races in Louisiana, Montana and Oklahoma plus House primaries in California and Washington, after claiming wins in North Carolina, Texas, Illinois and Georgia.

members_involved.name: Leading the Future (Zac Moffatt, co-strategist)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Announced $2M for Senate primaries in LA, MT and OK (with $1.5M deployed immediately) and $750K for House primaries in CA and WA.

events.headline: Marjorie Taylor Greene attacks federal agencies over reported monitoring of anti-AI activists and data center protesters
events.plain_english: Responding to a WIRED report on more than 1,000 pages of FBI, DHS and fusion center documents describing 'anti-tech violent extremism' tracking, Greene said AI critics and data center protesters were being treated like dangerous extremists.

members_involved.name: Marjorie Taylor Greene (former Rep., R-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Publicly blasted the FBI/DHS over reported surveillance of anti-AI activists and data center protesters.

events.headline: A pro-Trump group's AI deepfake attack ad against Rep. Thomas Massie draws a Take It Down Act complaint from Greene
events.plain_english: An ad used AI-generated video to depict Massie in a romantic liaison with Reps. Ocasio-Cortez and Omar. Greene said it violated the Take It Down Act, making AI deepfakes a live intra-GOP campaign issue.

members_involved.name: Thomas Massie (R-KY-4)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Target of the AI-generated attack ad in his primary.

members_involved.name: Marjorie Taylor Greene (former Rep., R-GA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Posted 'TAKE IT DOWN' and called the ad an AI-generated lie violating the law criminalizing nonconsensual digital forgeries.

members_involved.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY); Ilhan Omar (D-MN)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Depicted without consent in the AI-generated ad.

events.headline: Leading the Future announces its first slate of state legislative endorsements, all Republicans
events.plain_english: The network moved below the federal level, endorsing 19 Republican state legislators and candidates across Arizona, Florida, Georgia, Michigan, Mississippi, Pennsylvania, Texas and Utah, with a Democratic slate promised.

members_involved.name: Leading the Future (network of pro-AI super PACs)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Endorsed state legislators including Florida House Speaker Daniel Perez, Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall, Georgia state Sens. John Albers and Shawn Still, and Pennsylvania state Sen. Tracy Pennycuick.

events.headline: Senate Judiciary hearing on Chinese IP theft becomes a broader AI oversight moment
events.plain_english: At 'Stealth Stealing: China's Ongoing Theft of U.S. Innovation,' Hawley questioned whether the government should be helping AI companies at all, and witness Helen Toner told senators there is an unprecedented mismatch between AI's strategic importance and the government's limited involvement.

members_involved.name: Thom Tillis (R-NC)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Chaired in Grassley's place; warned China is evolving 'from imitator to innovator.'

members_involved.name: Josh Hawley (R-MO)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Questioned whether it is worth the government's time to help AI companies that may be working against the American people.

members_involved.name: Dick Durbin (D-IL)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Asked whether government should be more involved in developing AI technologies.

events.headline: Warren opens an investigation into DoD retaliation against Anthropic
events.plain_english: Warren wrote to Hegseth demanding details on whether DoD is 'weaponizing bipartisan national security statutes to retaliate against an American company' after Anthropic refused to drop contractual bans on mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous lethal weapons. The letter also posed detailed questions about OpenAI's competing DoD agreement.

members_involved.name: Elizabeth Warren (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Sent the March 23 letter: the supply chain risk label is 'historically reserved for foreign adversaries such as Huawei' and its use here 'appears to be an unprecedented abuse of longstanding national security authorities.'

events.headline: Meeks and Warren say the first approved H200 license undercuts US national security
events.plain_english: After Commerce finally provided information on the first license approval (made public by Nvidia on Feb. 25), the top Foreign Affairs Democrat and the top Banking Democrat jointly said they are 'more concerned than ever' that the administration is undercutting national security.

members_involved.name: Gregory Meeks (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Joint statement: 'We've finally received information about the administration's first license approval and are now more concerned than ever that the Trump administration is undercutting U.S. national security by approving this sale.'

members_involved.name: Elizabeth Warren (D-MA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Co-issued the statement, following their December 2025 statutory demand for license information.

events.headline: Senate Commerce subcommittee hearing on deploying AI for workforce, healthcare and industry
events.plain_english: Sen. Budd chaired a hearing framing AI as a productivity and healthcare opportunity — the optimistic Republican counterpoint to the risk-focused hearings elsewhere.

members_involved.name: Ted Budd (R-NC), Science, Manufacturing and Competitiveness Subcommittee Chairman
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: 'Artificial Intelligence will undoubtedly usher in significant improvements in quality of life for the American people,' citing manufacturing, semiconductors and healthcare diagnostics.

members_involved.name: Tammy Baldwin (D-WI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Subcommittee ranking member at the hearing.

events.headline: Cantwell leads bipartisan grilling of Trump's NIST nominee over CHIPS and manufacturing cuts
events.plain_english: NIST runs the Center for AI Standards and Innovation and the CHIPS R&D program, so the nomination hearing became a fight over whether the administration is gutting the institutions that would implement any federal AI standard.

members_involved.name: Maria Cantwell (D-WA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Pressed nominee Arvind Raman on Lutnick's cancellation of $7.4B in semiconductor R&D funding and the halt to Manufacturing Extension Partnership funding: 'semiconductor innovation is the foundation of who will win the future in AI.'

events.headline: Warner warns at Hill and Valley that new-graduate unemployment could spike to 35% and tells AI CEOs to stop fear-mongering
events.plain_english: One of the Senate's most AI-engaged Democrats publicly put a number on the labor shock and named Amodei and Altman, showing how AI-and-jobs moved into mainstream Senate rhetoric.

members_involved.name: Mark Warner (D-VA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Warned new college grad unemployment will spike dramatically within two years and pointedly referenced 'Dario, Sam' in urging AI leaders to change their approach.

events.headline: Sanders calls on Jeff Bezos to testify before Congress about AI-driven job elimination
events.plain_english: Sanders publicly demanded Bezos explain plans tied to AI-driven automation and job loss, part of his broader AI-and-labor campaign that also produced the data center moratorium bill.

members_involved.name: Bernie Sanders (I-VT)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Called on Bezos to testify before Congress about an AI-driven manufacturing fund and its implications for workers.

events.headline: MATCH Act introduced in the House to ban sales of key AI chipmaking equipment to China
events.plain_english: Introduced before its April 22 committee advance, the bill tightens restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment — a chokepoint even more consequential than chip sales. Lawmakers scaled it back in mid-April after industry pushback.

members_involved.name: Michael Baumgartner (R-WA)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the MATCH Act to ban exports of key chipmaking equipment to China.

events.headline: Sen. Slotkin urges the Pentagon to use Anthropic's Mythos model to find cybersecurity gaps despite the blacklist
events.plain_english: Even as DoD kept Anthropic designated a supply chain risk, a Democratic Armed Services member publicly pushed the department to use its frontier model for defensive cyber work.

members_involved.name: Elissa Slotkin (D-MI)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Said the Pentagon should use Anthropic's Mythos to spot cybersecurity gaps.

events.headline: Rep. Tonko introduces the Power for the People Act in the House
events.plain_english: The House companion to Van Hollen's Senate bill shifting data center grid costs away from consumers, expanding the ratepayer-protection push to the House.

members_involved.name: Paul Tonko (D-NY)
members_involved.what_they_did_or_said: Introduced the Power for the People Act to shield consumers from rising energy costs.

spring_2026.coverage_notes:
SOURCING METHOD: Google News RSS (date-bounded) plus Wayback CDX enumeration of member/committee sites were used for discovery; every event below was confirmed by opening a primary source (house.gov/senate.gov press release, committee page, congress.gov/govtrack) or a named news article. Search-result snippets alone were never used as confirmation.

CONFIRMED-BUT-EXCLUDED / PARTIAL ITEMS (flagged rather than guessed):
1. Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY-17) introduced the CHAT Act on ~Jan 27, 2026 to restrict AI companion chatbots for minors. The lawler.house.gov release could not be opened (site blocks; no archive capture; Google News link resolution failed), so the item is omitted from events rather than dated from feed metadata.
2. A Markey-led letter to NARUC (state utility regulators) on data-center cost impacts was reported around March 9, 2026 (WWLP). Both the WWLP article and markey.senate.gov returned 403 and the CDX enumeration timed out, so the letter's exact date and signer list are unconfirmed and the item is excluded.
3. Politico articles (Feb 5 "The Hill Republican who could get a deal on AI"; Feb 27 "Trump wants to move on data centers"; Mar 11 "Data center moratorium gains traction among Hill progressives"; Mar 27 "Republicans split on how to legislate on data centers"; May 15 "House talks look at blocking some state AI laws"; May 19 "AI attacks may be backfiring in Manhattan House race"; May 26 "The House Democrat taking a big risk to land an AI deal") are all paywalled/Cloudflare-blocked. Their existence and headlines are confirmed via resolved URLs, but no member quotes from them are included.
4. Reuters articles (Jan 21 HFAC vote; Feb 11 "Top Democrat on US House China committee open to Nvidia H200 sales" — i.e., Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi; Apr 16 "lawmakers scale back bill targeting Chinese chipmaking"; Apr 22 Lutnick; Apr 28 "lawmakers take on AI chatbots, fraud"; May 14 "US clears H200 chip sales to 10 China firms") could not be opened (401/JS wall). Where a fact appears in events it is sourced to an openable outlet instead.
5. Leading the Future's FIRST House GOP endorsement slate (12 members: Tom Emmer, Russell Fry, Brandon Gill, August Pfluger, Rich McCormick, John Joyce, Jay Obernolte, Rudy Yakym, Brian Jack, Riley Moore, Mike Haridopolos, Guy Reschenthaler) is confirmed by the May 22 Breitbart piece as having occurred in "April 2026," but no exact date was confirmed, so it is folded into the May 22 event rather than given its own date.
6. Feb 11 Krishnamoorthi openness to H200 sales, and Rep. Ro Khanna's reported openness to older Nvidia chip sales (Feb 11), are headline-confirmed only — excluded.
7. Sen. Hawley's GUARD Act "new cosponsors" release (Cotton, Kelly, Gallego, Hassan, Lankford, Lee, Welch added to original cosponsors Blumenthal, Britt, Murphy, Warner) was opened and its content confirmed, but the page carries no visible date, so it is not given its own dated event; the cosponsor list is reliable.
8. Ricketts-Coons SAFE CHIPS Act was opened but is titled "of 2025" — treated as out of window.
9. FY2027 NDAA: no AI-preemption rider was found in the House chairman's mark within this window. Confirmed AI content is the CITI subcommittee's AI incident/vulnerability reporting program and AI model rapid deployment framework. The full HASC markup (June 4, 44-12) and Senate action fall after May 31.
10. No AI CEO (Altman, Amodei, Huang) testified before Congress during Jan 1 - May 31, 2026. Amodei lobbied the Hill in person on Feb 10; Warren's invitation to Huang and Altman's testimony plans came in June, outside the window.
11. Cruz's promised Senate Commerce AI framework markup did not occur in this window; as of mid-May no markup date had been set (Roll Call, Washington Times). The Obernolte-Trahan Great American AI Act discussion draft (June 4) and the FRONTIER Act (July 23) are both after the window; Obernolte's in-window AI work was the Lieu-Obernolte American Leadership in AI Act (Apr 27), the Economy of the Future Commission Act (Apr 21), his Jan 14 hearing chairmanship, and his Apr 22 SECURE Data Act statement.
12. Dimension values used: preemption, chip_export_controls, data_centers_electricity, kids_and_chatbots, deepfakes, ai_in_government, ai_money_politics, ai_and_jobs, ai_legislation_other, ndaa, appropriations, member_politics.
13. Vote counts confirmed: AI Overwatch Act 42-2-1 (HFAC, Jan 21); House E&C kids package 28-24 (Mar 5); GUARD Act unanimous (Senate Judiciary, Apr 30); DEFIANCE Act by unanimous consent (Senate, Jan 13). No roll-call numbers were located for the House floor passage of H.R. 2683 (Jan 12) or H.R. 3679 (Feb 23-24), so none are asserted.

pacs.name: Leading the Future (super PAC, FEC C00916114) and network affiliates: Think Big PAC (C00923417, Democratic arm), American Mission PAC (C00916692, Republican arm), Build American AI (501(c)(4)), American Mission Florida (state PAC)
pacs.backers: Registered with FEC Aug 15, 2025. Donors per FEC/Transformer tracker: Marc Andreessen $25M, Ben Horowitz $25M, Greg Brockman (OpenAI president) $12.5M, Anna Brockman $12.5M, Perplexity AI $100K; Ron Conway (SV Angel) $500K to Think Big; Lonsdale Enterprises (Joe Lonsdale, Palantir co-founder) $250K to American Mission. Run by Zac Moffatt (Targeted Victory CEO, ex-Romney) and Josh Vlasto (ex-Schumer/Cuomo press, previously advised crypto super PAC Fairshake); Build American AI led by Nathan Leamer; treasurer Britney Gonzalez. Spokesperson Jesse Hunt. White House officials attacked it in Oct 2025 as run by 'Schumer acolytes' (NBC). Tech Oversight Project documents OpenAI political strategist Chris Lehane's role in conceiving it.
pacs.agenda: Elect 'pro-innovation, pro-AI' candidates of both parties; push a single national AI framework / federal preemption over state AI laws; oppose candidates who back state AI-safety statutes (chief target: NY RAISE Act author Alex Bores); frames AI as a race with China. Affiliate websites: 'back Democratic/Republican candidates who champion a pro-innovation, pro-AI vision ... and oppose those who do not.'
pacs.money: LTF raised $75.79M / spent $44.76M / $31.03M cash (FEC, through Jun 30, 2026); network claims $140M+ incl. c4. LTF makes no IEs itself; transferred $20M to Think Big ($5M Dec 15 2025, $10M May 19 2026, $5M Jun 8 2026) and $20M to American Mission ($5M Dec 15 2025, $15M Jun 8 2026). Think Big raised $20.52M, IEs $16.63M as of Sep 12 2026 (incl. $8.16M against Bores); American Mission raised $21.43M, IEs ~$6.07M (Transformer) to $10.9M across 21 GOP candidates (AI Money Watch). Campaign Legal Center FEC complaint (May 2026) alleges both affiliates route ~95% of spending through shell LLCs (Lantern Production Consultants LLC; Summit Ridge Media Group LLC). Also $5M pledged for Byron Donalds (FL gov) via American Mission Florida; $800K for Ty Masterson (KS gov); 18 GOP state-legislative endorsements.
