pacs.coverage_notes:
METHOD AND LIMITS. Research date Sep 12, 2026. The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the first ~16 queries (shared session cap), so the bulk of the work was direct WebFetch of primary/secondary pages already surfaced plus systematic crawling of three FEC-derived trackers: Transformer's elections.transformernews.ai (per-PAC and per-race pages, data as of Sep 12, 2026 01:29 UTC), Demand Progress's aimoneywatch.org (LTF network only), and electhumans.com (Jul 25, 2026 snapshot; its PAC-column attributions were sometimes garbled by the fetch summarizer and are flagged where used). FEC's open API (DEMO_KEY) returned Schedule E for Think Big, American Mission, Jobs and Democracy, Defending Our Values (first 100 rows each) before hitting its daily limit (HTTP 429); Public First super PAC and ARI PAC schedules were not retrieved. Blocked (403/paywall): all OpenSecrets pages, Axios, CNBC (incl. AMP), Politico, Wired, Bloomberg, Houston Public Media, Florida Politics, docquery.fec.gov listings, NOTUS (redirected to washingtonsun.com, which worked). The Campaign Legal Center FEC complaint PDF was downloaded and read via pypdf.

RACE RESULTS. NY-12 (Jun 23, 2026): Micah Lasher won; Alex Bores second (Wikipedia pages for Bores and Lasher, citing NYT). Vote percentages not confirmed. Total AI-PAC spending in NY-12 ~$29.5M: $21.3M for Bores (Jobs and Democracy $15.03M, You Can Push Back $3.41M, Dream NYC $2.48M, Guardrails Alliance $395K) vs. Think Big $8.16M against. Other outcomes are from Transformer race pages ('won', 'lost', 'advanced to general').

CONFLICTS/FLAGS. (1) Kevin Hern is backed by BOTH networks (American Mission $252,902; Defending Our Values $808,341). (2) 'Darline Graham' in FEC IE filings = Sen. Lindsey Graham per trackers/press. (3) 'Felix Moore' (AL-Sen) = Rep. Barry Moore by legal name; inferred. (4) Dan Koh: FEC Schedule E aggregates $705K of Think Big support (Aug 21-26) and Tech Oversight says $705K; Transformer PAC page lags at $99K. (5) Don Davis 'targeted' per Tech Oversight only; FEC trackers show $0 oppose IEs. (6) Kai Newkirk oppose row appears only on electhumans. (7) Moskowitz listed as FL-25 and Maloy as UT-03 in FEC filings (post-redistricting numbering); Amanda McKinney amounts differ across trackers ($215K Transformer vs $779K FEC). (8) Suozzi, Sorensen, Beatty, Conaway, Sykes endorsements rest on a single New Republic sentence (Sep 11, 2026). (9) LTF's five-Democrat endorsement (Gottheimer, Liccardo, Clarke, Subramanyam, Gomez) was reported by CNBC Apr 15, 2026 (page blocked) and is corroborated by aimoneywatch.org/people 'ENDORSED BY LEADING THE FUTURE' labels. (10) Public First Action's 'Conservative AI Consensus' release promised 12 additional members; 11 were captured. (11) Anthropic corporate giving to Public First Action is $40M per Transformer's FEC-derived company page versus the $20M announced Feb 12, 2026.

GAPS. ARI PAC's $329K of candidate/committee contributions: recipients not retrieved. Scott Wiener: Public First support confirmed only qualitatively (Transformer), no amount. Big Tech corporate PAC (Microsoft/Google/Amazon/Meta PAC) AI-specific giving trends: no accessible source; only employee-level data captured via Transformer company pages (OpenAI employees $13.14M, almost all Brockman's $12.5M to LTF; Anthropic employees $5.16M incl. $3.15M to Public First and $790K to Dream NYC; Google employees $581K incl. Kate Woolverton's $250K to Public First; Microsoft employees $120K incl. Brad Smith $30K to Blackburn and Ricketts; Perplexity corporate $100K to LTF). Meta federal-race activity: none found (state-only). Fairshake crossover: Josh Vlasto previously advised Fairshake; Fortune/The Nation cite Fairshake precedents and shared staff; no AI-relevant Fairshake IEs found; the clearest crypto-to-AI money link is Ripple's Chris Larsen ($4.51M to You Can Push Back, $3.5M for Bores per NY1). Other AI-labeled committees with $0 activity as of Sep 12, 2026: Innovation Council (C00922815, David Sacks-linked per Tech Oversight), Building the Future (C00960328), NVPAC (C00960070). State-level items excluded from member lists but noted: LTF's 18 GOP state-legislative endorsements (AZ, FL, GA, MI, MS, PA, TX, UT), $800K for Ty Masterson (KS gov), Byron Donalds (FL gov) via American Mission Florida; Meta's Forge the Future/Making Our Tomorrow state spending. Candidates who distanced from or rejected AI-PAC support: Val Hoyle (distanced then backtracked), Jack Schlossberg (NY-12, touted rejecting AI PAC money), Paul Kendrick (IL state house, rejected Meta PAC); a 'No Big AI Money Pledge' exists (electhumans) but signers were not retrieved. Regulatory: CLC's May 2026 FEC complaint against American Mission and Think Big (shell-LLC sub-vendor concealment; Summit Ridge Media Group LLC / Lantern Production Consultants LLC, both formed Oct 30, 2025).

trackers.name: Congress.gov API v3 (bill sponsors/cosponsors/subjects)
trackers.covers: All federal bills, 93rd-119th Congress. Endpoints verified from LoC GitHub docs: /v3/bill/{congress}/{type}, /v3/bill/{congress}/{type}/{number}/cosponsors, /subjects, /actions, /committees, /text, /amendments. Per-bill policy area and CRS legislative subject terms.
trackers.how_to_harvest: Free API key. Enumerate 119th bills (or start from a curated AI bill list such as Brennan/AAF), pull /cosponsors for each (bioguideId, party, state, sponsorshipDate, withdrawn). To find AI bills, filter on title/text keywords: CRS does NOT appear to use an 'Artificial intelligence' subject term (checked S.3312 and S.4178 of the 118th via BILLSTATUS: subjects were 'Computers and information technology', 'Advanced technology and technological innovations', 'Internet, web applications, social media'; policy area 'Science, Technology, Communications'). The congress.gov website itself is Cloudflare-gated (blocked WebFetch, curl and the browser pane this session); the API root was reachable.
trackers.quality: Authoritative and current; cosponsorship is the best per-member 'position' signal short of a roll call. Website scraping not viable; use API or GovInfo bulk data.

trackers.name: GovInfo Bulk Data BILLSTATUS XML
trackers.covers: Per-bill XML for every bill: sponsors, cosponsors (bioguideId, party, state, date, isOriginalCosponsor), actions, committees, policyArea, legislativeSubjects, titles. Verified live for BILLSTATUS-119hr3460.xml (AI Whistleblower Protection Act; updateDate 2026-05-21) and BILLSTATUS-119s146.xml (TAKE IT DOWN Act: 22 cosponsors, policy area 'Science, Technology, Communications').
trackers.how_to_harvest: No key needed. GET https://www.govinfo.gov/bulkdata/json/BILLSTATUS/119/hr (and /119/s) with Accept: application/json returns a file list with direct XML links (verified); fetch each XML and parse <sponsors>, <cosponsors>, <legislativeSubjects>, <policyArea>. Note the HTML directory URLs (without /json/) returned 'Govinfo Bulkdata Service Error' this session; the /json/ path works.
trackers.quality: Authoritative, mirrors congress.gov nightly. Best bulk source for a script; no scraping needed.

trackers.name: Senate roll-call vote XML (LIS)
trackers.covers: Every Senate roll call. Verified AI/tech votes: 119th-1st #00363 (2025-07-01, Blackburn Amdt. No. 2814 to H.R.1, 'To strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence', Agreed to 99-1); 118th-2nd #00221 (2024-07-30, motion to concur in House amendment to S.2073 with Amdt. 3021 = KOSA/COPPA 2.0 vehicle, 91-3) and #00219 (2024-07-25 cloture, 86-1). 119th-2nd menu (231 votes as of fetch) had no AI/KOSA/deepfake roll calls by keyword; menu XMLs: vote_menu_119_2.xml, vote_menu_118_2.xml.
trackers.how_to_harvest: Parse vote_menu_{congress}_{session}.xml (<vote><vote_number><vote_date><issue><question><title><result><vote_tally>). Per-member positions are in the per-vote XML under /legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote{congress}{session}/vote_{congress}_{session}_{number}.xml (standard LIS pattern; not opened this session). senate.gov is Akamai-protected: curl and WebFetch got 403; fetching from inside a real browser context worked (fetch() from a senate.gov page).
trackers.quality: Authoritative. The 99-1 vote is the single cleanest per-senator record on state-law preemption. Requires a browser-context fetch or whitelisted client.

trackers.name: House Clerk roll-call vote XML
trackers.covers: Every House roll call with per-member votes. Verified: roll 104 (2025-04-28, S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act, suspension, Passed 409-2, 22 not voting). Cross-verified via Voteview/GovTrack: roll 145 (2025-05-22, H.R.1 passage 215-214, House text contained the 10-year state-AI-law moratorium), roll 190 (2025-07-03, motion to concur in Senate amendment to H.R.1, 218-214), 2026 roll 228 (2026-06-29, H.R.7757 KIDS Act, suspension as amended, 267-117).
trackers.how_to_harvest: Pattern https://clerk.house.gov/evs/{year}/roll{NNN}.xml; parse <vote-metadata> and <recorded-vote> (legislator name-id = bioguide, party, state, vote). First request succeeded via curl with a browser UA; later requests got Akamai 'Access Denied', so throttle or fetch from a browser context. 2026 votes live under /evs/2026/.
trackers.quality: Authoritative. Note the H.R.1 votes are omnibus votes, so they are weak evidence of an individual member's AI-moratorium position; TAKE IT DOWN and KIDS Act are cleaner tech votes.

trackers.name: Voteview roll-call and member-vote CSVs
trackers.covers: All House and Senate roll calls with per-member cast codes. Verified live (HTTP 200): /static/data/out/rollcalls/H119_rollcalls.csv (656 rows, through 2026-09-03), S119_rollcalls.csv (890 rows, through 2026-08-08), /static/data/out/votes/H119_votes.csv and S119_votes.csv (congress, chamber, rollnumber, icpsr, cast_code, prob), /static/data/out/members/HSall_members.csv. Confirms Senate roll 363 (99-1, 'To strike the section relating to support for artificial intelligence'), House clerk 104 (S146, 409-2), clerk 228 (HR7757 KIDS Act, 267-117).
trackers.how_to_harvest: Download the CSVs; filter rollcalls on bill_number (HR1, S146, HR7757) or regex on vote_desc/dtl_desc; join votes on (congress, chamber, rollnumber) to rollcalls and on icpsr to HSall_members (has bioguide_id). Note Voteview 'rollnumber' differs from the Clerk's number (clerk_rollnumber column carries the Clerk's).
trackers.quality: Very good, updated within days; the easiest programmatic path to per-member votes because senate.gov and clerk.house.gov block scripts.

trackers.name: GovTrack bill, cosponsor and vote pages
trackers.covers: Per-bill sponsor/cosponsor tables with join dates (S.1748 KOSA: 76 cosponsors, 105 member links on page) and per-vote member tables with CSV export (verified https://www.govtrack.us/congress/votes/119-2026/h228/export/csv for the KIDS Act vote). Bill pages verified: H.R.7757 KIDS Act (Guthrie), H.R.8031 GUARDRAILS Act, H.R.8516 American Leadership in AI Act, H.R.3460 AI Whistleblower Protection Act, S.1748.
trackers.how_to_harvest: curl with a browser User-Agent works (WebFetch gets 403). Scrape /congress/bills/{congress}/{bill}/cosponsors and /congress/votes/{congress}-{year}/{h|s}{n}/export/csv. GovTrack has no public API; the subject-browse URLs guessed here (e.g. /congress/bills/subjects/artificial_intelligence) returned 404, so do not rely on a subject taxonomy.
trackers.quality: Reliable secondary mirror of congress.gov with convenient CSV vote exports; bill pages are JS-heavy so target the /cosponsors and /export/csv endpoints.

trackers.coverage_notes:
METHOD AND LIMITS: The WebSearch budget for this session was already exhausted (200/200) before the task began, so discovery used DuckDuckGo HTML results loaded in the Claude browser pane (JS-extracted), plus WebFetch and curl for verification. Several key hosts block scripts: senate.gov, clerk.house.gov, house.gov, cnbc.com (Akamai 403 to curl/WebFetch; readable in the browser pane, including fetch() of senate.gov XML from a senate.gov page); congress.gov, opensecrets.org, legiscan.com, justfacts.votesmart.org, cdt.org, ncsl.org, akingump.com (Cloudflare challenge; congress.gov/OpenSecrets/LegiScan/VoteSmart also failed in the browser pane). Anything marked unverified above was not opened. No bill number, roll-call number or date in the data was taken from a snippet alone; each was read from an opened page or downloaded file (Senate LIS XML, Clerk XML, Voteview CSVs, GovTrack pages, GovInfo BILLSTATUS XML, letter PDFs).

HEADLINE FINDING: As of 2026-09-12 there is no dedicated per-member AI scorecard or report card for Congress from any advocacy group (ARI, Brennan, Tech Policy Press, Public Citizen, Encode, CAIP, Common Sense, Fight for the Future, Issue One, FLI, ControlAI, Alliance for Secure AI all checked; repeated searches for 'AI scorecard Congress 2026' returned nothing). CAIP shut down (June 2023-May 2025). The only per-member scorecard touching this space is Restore The Fourth/FFTF's Political Surveillance Scorecard (702, encryption, facial recognition, EARN IT and KOSA cosponsorship, through the 119th), plus generic ideological scorecards (Heritage Action) whose AI items are unconfirmed. Existing 'AI trackers' (Brennan, AAF, Steptoe, Integrity Institute, AGORA, Legisletter, StateScape, ai-law-tracker, ailawsbystate) are bill-level; the best give sponsor names and cosponsor counts, none record votes or stances. Brennan (frozen 2025-06-05) and Steptoe (Aug 2025) are stale; AAF (bi-weekly) and Legisletter (days) are current.

PER-MEMBER AI/TECH RECORDS A SCRIPT CAN BUILD FROM PRIMARY DATA: (1) Roll calls: Senate 119-1 #363 (2025-07-01, Blackburn Amdt 2814 to H.R.1, strike AI moratorium, 99-1); House Clerk roll 145 (2025-05-22, H.R.1 passage 215-214, House text carried the 10-year moratorium) and roll 190 (2025-07-03, concur 218-214, moratorium removed) as weaker omnibus signals; House roll 104 (2025-04-28, S.146 TAKE IT DOWN Act, 409-2); House 2026 roll 228 (2026-06-29, H.R.7757 KIDS Act, 267-117); Senate 118-2 #221 (2024-07-30, S.2073 KOSA/COPPA 2.0 vehicle, 91-3). Voteview S119 (through 2026-08-08) shows no other AI-specific Senate roll call; Senate 119-2 LIS menu likewise. (2) Cosponsorships via congress.gov API / GovInfo BILLSTATUS for a seed list of AI bills (take bill numbers from Brennan/AAF/Legisletter; e.g. S.1748 KOSA 76 cosponsors, H.R.3562 DEFIANCE 63, H.R.3460 AI Whistleblower Protection Act, H.R.8031 GUARDRAILS Act, H.R.8516 American Leadership in AI Act, S.4199, S.4407, S.5171). CRS subject terms do not include 'Artificial intelligence' (verified on 118th S.3312 and S.4178), so filter by title/text keywords, not subject. (3) Letters with signatory lists: Matsui letter Nov 26, 2025 (81 House Democrats, PDF parsed: 81 signature blocks) and Clarke letter Dec 3, 2025 (44 House Democrats, names in release) opposing NDAA preemption/moratorium; both are the closest thing to a whip count and are all-Democratic. (4) Rosters: House AI Caucus (82 members, co-chairs Beyer/McCaul, vice-chairs Obernolte/Matsui), Senate AI Caucus (stale page still listing Romney and Braun), House Democratic Commission on AI (co-chairs Lieu, Gottheimer, Foushee; ex officio Lofgren, Pallone). (5) PAC endorsements as proxies: Leading the Future's 22 named House Republicans (Apr 16 and May 22, 2026) plus Democrats Hoyle, Menendez, Torres (May 8, 2026) and opposition to Alex Bores; Public First Action publishes no list.

2026 PREEMPTION STATE OF PLAY (for stance tables): Trump EO on state-AI-law preemption Dec 2025 (Wikipedia cites EO 14365); White House 'Legislative Recommendations for a National Policy Framework for AI' Mar 21, 2026; Blackburn TRUMP AMERICA AI Act discussion draft (Dec 2025, not introduced as of Mar 2026); Obernolte-Trahan Great American AI Act discussion draft Jun 4, 2026, revised bill introduced Jul 23, 2026 with cosponsors Peters, Franklin, Subramanyam, Houchin (bill number not confirmed: null); Lieu critical; GUARDRAILS Act H.R.8031 (repeal EO; Schatz Senate companion); NDAA preemption dropped Dec 2025 after opposition from HASC Chair Rogers and SASC RM Reed; Senate Commerce's broad AI/preemption markup postponed from late July 2026 and still pending (Cruz, Sept 10, 2026: possibly later in September; Sept 16 executive session agenda has no AI bills). METHOD/LIMITS: The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted almost immediately, so discovery was done via Google News RSS and Bing News RSS, with Google-News redirect links resolved in the Chrome pane and pages read via the r.jina.ai reader or the browser. senate.gov and congress.gov blocked direct fetches, so bill sponsorship/cosponsorship comes from GovTrack (bill + /cosponsors pages, checked Sept 11-12 2026) and roll calls from clerk.house.gov (RC 145) and GovTrack vote pages (h356, s363). Member press releases were located via the Wayback CDX index and fetched directly. All quotes are verbatim from pages actually opened; where I could only see a headline, quote is null and the position says so. Dates given as YYYY-MM-DD are confirmed from the page; a few are approximate and flagged.
KEY FEDERAL RECORD ITEMS USED ACROSS STATES: (1) House Roll Call 145, May 22 2025, passage of H.R.1 (OBBBA, 215-214) whose Sec. 43201 carried a 10-year moratorium on state/local AI laws that NCSL/CAP said would preempt state and local data-center rules; every Republican from these 9 states voted Yea except Garbarino (NY-2, Not Voting) and every Democrat voted Nay. (2) Senate vote s363 July 1 2025 on Blackburn Amdt 2814 striking that AI-preemption section (99-1, Tillis lone Nay); all 18 senators from these states voted Yea. (3) House vote h356 Dec 18 2025 on H.R.4776 SPEED Act (permitting bill framed by CNBC/CIO Dive as fast-tracking AI infrastructure): all GOP members Yea except Fitzpatrick (Nay); Democrats Nay except Golden (ME-2, also original cosponsor), Deluzio (PA-17) and Mannion (NY-22) who voted Yea. (4) House E&C full-committee markup July 21 2026 approved the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R.9340, Evans/Castor) unanimously (reported 52-0); I could not retrieve the committee roll call, so individual E&C members from these states (Pallone, Tonko, Kean, Menendez, Joyce, Trahan, Auchincloss, Ocasio-Cortez, Clarke, Langworthy) are not listed as voting, only as cosponsors where applicable. (5) Bills used: S.4214/H.R.9442 AI Data Center Moratorium Act; S.3852 GRID Act; S.1475/H.R.6179 Clean Cloud Act; S.4727/H.R.9183 AI Environmental Impacts Act; S.3682/H.R.8241 Power for the People Act; H.R.9655 FAIR Data Act; H.R.6983 PRICE Act; H.R.6984 Data Center Transparency Act; H.R.7858 Data Center Community Impact Act; H.R.8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act; H.R.9262 Local Control Protection Act; H.R.9340/S.5028 Ratepayer Protection Act; H.R.9939 No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act; H.R.6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act; H.R.8033 No Harm Data Centers Act; H.R.9332 Load Forecasting Enhancement Act; H.R.10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act; H.R.7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (electricity-bill bill, not data-center-specific; used only as a weak signal); S.5159 STRONG GRID Act; S.5074; S.4337; S.3976; S.5306; S.5353; S.4743; S.3269/H.R.5332 Liquid Cooling for AI Act; H.R.8248; H.R.5896 (Van Drew 'GRID Act', text not read); H.R.5600; H.R.6075; S.Res.564.

states.summary: Pennsylvania is the epicenter of the Northeast data-center fight: it sits in PJM, where the 2025/26 capacity auction cleared at a record $269.92/MW-day (driving sharp mid-2025 bill increases), the 2026/27 auction hit the Shapiro-negotiated cap, and the July 14 2026 auction added an estimated $6.3B in costs attributed to data-center load; PJM's board on July 27 2026 proposed a one-time backstop auction and curtailment of new large loads that do not bring their own supply. Sen. McCormick's July 15 2025 Pennsylvania Energy and Innovation Summit with President Trump announced $90B+ (Blackstone/QTS $25B Luzerne County, Amazon/Talen ~$20B at Susquehanna, Homer City $10B+ gas-plus-data-center campus, PAX-1 Carlisle 1.3-1.8 GW, CoreWeave Lancaster, Shippingport conversion, TMI/Crane restart). Local backlash (Archbald, Muncy Twp, Middlesex Twp, Pennhurst, Luzerne County) turned data centers into the defining issue of the PA-1, PA-7, PA-8 and PA-10 House races; Gov. Shapiro signed an Aug 18 2026 executive order he called the nation's strictest data-center guardrails after the state House passed a data-center pause June 25 2026. The delegation splits three ways: pro-buildout senators (Fetterman, McCormick), Republicans who now stress 'local control' (Bresnahan, Meuser, Mackenzie, Fitzpatrick), and Democrats pushing ratepayer-protection and disclosure bills (Deluzio, Dean, Evans, Houlahan, Scanlon, Lee).

fights.issue: Capacity-auction price spikes attributed to data-center load; 2025/26 record $269.92/MW-day, Shapiro-PJM settlement capped bids at $325 for the 2025 and 2026 auctions; July 2026 auction added ~$6.3B; PJM board proposes backstop auction and data-center curtailment (Jul 27 2026)
fights.status: ongoing; FERC review of PJM board proposals

states.summary: New Jersey's electricity politics were remade by PJM: the 2024 capacity auction's $14.7B cost drove 17-20% residential bill increases on June 1 2025, another ~5% followed in 2026, and Democrats rode the issue to the 2025 governorship (Sherrill) and into a rate freeze; Sherrill then signed laws in July-August 2026 making data centers pay for infrastructure and disclose water/energy use. Nearly 100 towns have banned data centers, developers are suing (Andover), and fights rage in Vineland ($17B Microsoft-linked campus), Kenilworth, Manchester, Bayonne, Howell, and Pallone's district (Asbury Park, Red Bank, Old Bridge, Sayreville, New Brunswick). The delegation is unusually active: Kim and Booker led a May 2 2025 delegation letter to PJM; Pallone (E&C ranking member) became the highest-ranking Democrat to endorse a national moratorium (Jun 24 2026); Menendez, McIver and Watson Coleman each introduced data-center bills; Gottheimer led two PJM letters; and Republicans Kean, Van Drew and Smith have cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act and local-control bills while having voted for the House OBBBA AI-preemption provision in 2025.

fights.issue: $14.7B capacity-auction cost driving 17%+ residential bill increases from Jun 1 2025 (17.23-20.20% depending on utility); ~5% more in 2026

fights.issue: Gov. Sherrill signed bills to make data centers pay for infrastructure/energy (Jul 2026) and a transparency law requiring self-reporting of water and energy use to BPU (Aug 27 2026), completing a four-part data-center plan; critics want a statewide moratorium

members_on_record.name: Andy Kim

As you know, there is a $14.7 billion cost to ratepayers, which is in large part driving an expected 17 percent or greater increase in electric utility bills in New Jersey beginning June 1, 2025.

members_on_record.position: Co-led May 2 2025 PJM letter; original cosponsor Power for the People Act (S.3682, Jan 15 2026) making data centers pay grid costs; co-signed Markey's Mar 6 2026 NARUC letter urging state PUCs to protect ratepayers; original cosponsor AI Environmental Impacts Act (S.4727, Jun 9 2026); voted Yea on s363.

members_on_record.position: E&C ranking member; called for a national AI data center moratorium at Jun 24 2026 Energy Subcommittee markup (highest-ranking Democrat to do so); signed May 2 2025 PJM letter; Jul 29 2026 letter to Elon Musk on xAI Colossus; Sept 3 2026 blasted GOP leaders for not bringing Ratepayer Protection Act to the floor; voted Nay RC 145 and SPEED.
members_on_record.quote: That is why I am in favor of a national AI data center moratorium until we can find a way to ensure they don't harm our nation's air, water, and power bills.

states.summary: New York became the first state to halt large data centers: after the legislature passed the Responsible Data Center Development Act (one-year pause on 20 MW+ projects), Gov. Hochul signed a July 14 2026 executive order barring new 50 MW+ hyperscale data centers for up to a year, citing residential electricity prices up ~68% since 2019 and backlash in Lansing (TeraWulf), East Fishkill (1,000 MW proposal; town adopted a 3-year moratorium), the $19.5B Stream/STAMP project in Genesee County and Long Island. Unions and Republicans (Blakeman, Lawler, Assembly GOP) attacked the pause; a Siena poll found 46-21 support. Federally, Ocasio-Cortez carries the House AI Data Center Moratorium Act (14 cosponsors incl. Goldman), Tonko's Power for the People Act is the main Democratic cost-allocation bill, Riley introduced the FAIR Data Act, Gillibrand endorsed the pause and local veto power, Schumer backs data centers if they 'pay their fair share' with enforceable protections, and Lawler has moved from criticizing the moratorium to cosponsoring the Ratepayer Protection and Data Center Transparency Acts.

fights.issue: Hochul executive order (Jul 14 2026) pausing new 50 MW+ data centers up to one year; legislature's Responsible Data Center Development Act (20 MW, one year) awaiting action; Hochul pursuing repeal of data-center sales-tax exemptions; unions and business groups oppose
$19.5B, 500 MW Stream U.S. Data Centers project with ~$1.45B in tax incentives under GCEDC review; community opposition; likely delayed by moratorium
fights.status: pending; planning board vote scheduled Jul 6 2026

members_on_record.quote: will push for what people want, not [President] Trump's toothless, stupid pledge, but strong, enforceable consumer protections

members_on_record.name: Kirsten Gillibrand

members_on_record.quote: It's up to the community to decide, and if the community does not want a data center, they should not have to have a data center in their community

members_on_record.name: Kirsten Gillibrand

members_on_record.quote: This one-year moratorium is fundamentally about trust. Right now, New Yorkers aren't convinced these massive facilities benefit them. Before we move forward, our communities need ironclad guarantees that their energy bills won't spike, their water will be protected, and their air will remain clean.

members_on_record.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez

members_on_record.quote: Congress has a moral obligation to stand with the American people and stop the expansion of these data centers until we have a framework to adequately address the existential harm AI poses to our society. We must choose humanity over profit.

members_on_record.quote: Families are already paying higher prices for everything from groceries to healthcare, to gas, to utilities — they shouldn't be forced to also shoulder the costs for companies building data centers

states.summary: Massachusetts has no hyperscale data centers yet but the first, a $4B, 120-acre Westfield campus (Rep. Neal's district), triggered western-Mass 'Ban! Ban! Ban!' organizing in 2026; a state Senate moratorium stalled in July, and Gov. Healey signed a Sept 8 2026 executive order requiring local approval before data centers can be permitted. Ratepayers already pay among the highest ISO-NE prices. Sen. Markey is the delegation's (and the Senate's) most prolific data-center legislator: AI Environmental Impacts Act (reintroduced Jun 9 2026), Nov 2025 FERC letter, Mar 2026 NARUC letter, a Jul 13 2026 discussion draft creating a federal certificate regime for data centers, and he won a Sept 1 2026 primary against Rep. Moulton in which AI and data centers were debate topics. Sen. Warren has led investigations of hyperscalers' utility costs (Dec 2025) and a bipartisan EIA reporting push with Hawley. Reps. McGovern (moratorium cosponsor), Trahan (Frontier Act, WETA Act) and Auchincloss (permitting to build 'behind the meter') stake out different lanes.

fights.issue: Proposed $4B, 120-acre hyperscale AI data center, the state's first, raising fears of power-bill impacts across western Massachusetts

Healey executive order requiring local approval for data centers before permits (Sept 8 2026); proposed Senate moratorium met resistance (Jul 2026); state data-center tax incentive from 2024 economic development law
Markey vs. Moulton debate (Aug 20 2026) featured AI regulation and whether large data centers belong in Massachusetts; Markey won Sept 1 2026

members_on_record.quote: Communities are organizing and demanding action to protect their air, water, energy bills, and quality of life from the tsunami of data centers around the country

members_on_record.name: Ed Markey
members_on_record.position: Reintroduced AI Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 (reporting requirements with fines; NIST standards; EPA lifecycle study)

We urge you to protect residential ratepayers over corporate profits, as FERC's mission demands.

members_on_record.name: Jim McGovern
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of AOC's AI Data Center Moratorium Act (Jun 24 2026), McIver's Site Selection Transparency Act (Apr 23 2026) and Tlaib's No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act (Jul 23 2026); cosponsored AI Environmental Impacts Act (Jun 24 2026), PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act (Sept 8 2026); Aug 23 2026 Worcester Telegram guest column on fighting data centers' climate threat (headline); attacks GOP over OBBBA Opportunity Zone tax breaks for data centers.

states.summary: Connecticut has some of the nation's highest electricity prices and ~50 small data centers but no hyperscale facility; the marquee fight, NE Edge's proposed 300 MW data center co-located at the Millstone nuclear plant in Waterford, was scrubbed in early 2026, with Gov. Lamont telling the legislature to 'slow down new data centers' unless they add generation, and legislation pending to repeal the 2021 data-center tax incentive that only Cigna has used. Smaller proposals (Killingly gas-plant co-location, Beacon Falls fuel-cell project) continue. Sen. Blumenthal is the delegation's leading voice, co-authoring the bipartisan GRID Act with Hawley (Feb 11 2026) to force new data centers off the grid, joining Warren's hyperscaler probe and Markey's FERC/NARUC letters, and introducing utility-cost bills in Aug 2026; Sen. Murphy reports data centers now come up everywhere on his annual walk. Reps. Larson and Hayes have cosponsored data-center cost bills; Courtney, Himes and DeLauro have no data-center record found.

NE Edge exploring data center co-located with gas-fired plant

Blumenthal and state Consumer Counsel call for federal review of Eversource transmission spending driving bills (Aug 2026)

members_on_record.name: Richard Blumenthal
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of Hawley's bipartisan GRID Act (S.3852, Feb 11 2026): new 20 MW+ data centers must secure power off-grid, existing ones get 10 years and pay 'zero rate effect credits,' $1M/day fines, project labor agreements; original cosponsor Power for the People Act (Jan 15 2026); joined Warren's Dec 2025 hyperscaler investigation; cosigned Nov 13 2025 FERC letter and Mar 6 2026 NARUC letter; original cosponsor Warren's AI Bubble Transparency Act (Jun 10 2026); sponsor of Affordable Electricity Rates Act (S.5306) and No Bonuses for Utility Executives Act (S.5353), both Aug 6 2026; voted Yea s363.
members_on_record.quote: Connecticut has some of the highest energy prices in the country, which makes this bill especially important to us. But consumers in any state deserve protection against data centers swallowing power and sending prices sky high. They should bear the burden of the additional costs they created because they also receive the additional profits that data centers enable.

members_on_record.name: Richard Blumenthal
members_on_record.position: Describing GRID Act's purpose
members_on_record.quote: to make sure that consumers are spared the burden of increased costs resulting from the demands placed on electricity and energy production and transmission

states.summary: Vermont has no data center proposals of scale (state officials call the odds 'slim to none'), but Sen. Sanders made it the national symbol of resistance: he became the first member of Congress to endorse a national data-center moratorium (Dec 16 2025) and introduced the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (S.4214, Mar 25 2026) with AOC, followed by a Sept 2026 proposal to ban 'superintelligence.' atlantic_south.coverage_notes: METHOD/LIMITS: The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the first batch, so discovery ran through Google and DuckDuckGo inside the user's Chrome plus curl; page text was confirmed by opening pages (govtrack, senate.gov via Chrome, news sites). All *.house.gov pages were unreachable (Akamai geo-block/403 for both curl and Chrome; WebFetch 403 after two early successes), so House press releases are cited via govtrack cosponsor records, committee summaries (Daily Energy Insider), or mirrors (WVDN, Quiver, MeriTalk, Florida's Voice). Where a quote could only be seen in a search snippet, the entry says so and the quote field is null or the position text is flagged '(snippet; page not opened)'. Politico, Axios, E&E (most), Baltimore Sun, The State (one URL), Fortune, AP, WLRN, Tampa Bay Times and WRIC pages were not retrievable. VOTES: The only floor roll call found that is squarely tied to the data-center build-out in this period is House Roll Call 356 (Dec 18, 2025) on H.R. 4776, the SPEED Act (NEPA permitting reform, 221-196), which industry and critics both framed as accelerating data center/AI infrastructure; it is not data-center-specific, and is included per member with that caveat (source: govtrack CSV export). The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340, Evans/Castor) cleared House Energy & Commerce 52-0 on July 21, 2026 and is scheduled for a House suspension vote on Tuesday Sept 15, 2026 (Bloomberg Government, USA Today, Politico); individual committee members' presence for the 52-0 vote could not be confirmed, so E&C members from these states (Griffith, McClellan, Hudson, Fry, Carter, Allen, Castor, Bilirakis, Dunn, Soto) are noted as committee members rather than credited with the vote unless they said so themselves (Soto, Bilirakis did). The May 22, 2025 House passage of the OBBBA (with the 10-year state/local AI-law moratorium later stripped in the Senate) is referenced by CAP Action (Aug 24, 2026) as a data-center-relevant vote; not tabulated here. MEMBERSHIP CHANGES verified: Marjorie Taylor Greene resigned Jan 5, 2026 (Clay Fuller, R-GA14, seated Apr 14, 2026); David Scott (D-GA13) died Apr 22, 2026; Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick (D-FL20) resigned Apr 21, 2026; Lindsey Graham (R-SC) died July 2026, Darline Graham appointed and won the Aug 25, 2026 GOP runoff over Rep. Ralph Norman; Eleanor Holmes Norton is retiring. MEMBERS WITH NO DATA-CENTER STATEMENT FOUND (only the SPEED Act vote, if any): DE Sen. states.summary: Ground zero. ~603 data centers statewide (Warner office) with ~4 GW installed in Loudoun and 2-3 GW more in development; the Prince William Digital Gateway needs 2.4-7 GW; Dominion is building a 22-mile 500 kV line in Loudoun. The SCC created a data-center rate class in Nov 2025 (effective Jan 2027; 85% of contracted transmission/distribution demand and 60% of generation demand must be paid) and approved Dominion residential increases (+$11.24/month in 2026). PJM capacity costs tied to data centers (>$21B over three auctions; +$70/month per household by 2028 per Van Hollen/Warner offices) dominate the affordability debate. The 2026 General Assembly passed ~15 data center bills and launched a study of the sales-tax exemption; PJM floated a 'bring your own power' rule in Aug 2026; the NextEra-Dominion merger (2026) drew opposition. Data centers are now an explicit midterm issue in VA-1, VA-7 and VA-10 (E&E Aug 4, 2026; Axios Sept 10, 2026). Delegation is unusually active: Warner co-sponsored the Power for the People Act and introduced a data-center tax/disclosure bill while calling a moratorium 'idiocy'; Kaine signed FERC and PJM letters; Subramanyam filed a four-bill National Data Center Plan; four Republicans (Wittman, Kiggans, McGuire, Cline) and Griffith cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act, Griffith co-leads the Landsman FERC-conference bill; Vindman and McClellan have their own bills/cosponsorships.

states.summary: Maryland is a PJM import state (imports ~40% of power) where the fight is about paying for other states' data centers: PJM assigned roughly $2B of $22B in data-center-driven regional transmission to Maryland ratepayers (Maryland OPC complaint at FERC, Docket EL26-63), and BGE/Pepco bills jumped with the 2024-2025 capacity auctions. In-state fights center on the 2,100-acre Quantum Frederick campus (up to 2.4 GW; management passed from Quantum Loophole to TPG's Catellus), a Frederick County council cap on data-center acreage, and the 70-mile Maryland Piedmont Reliability Project transmission line (PSEG/PJM) opposed across Baltimore, Carroll and Frederick counties. Gov. Moore has shifted toward data centers as Amazon eyes Washington County. The delegation is the most unified in the region: Van Hollen leads the Power for the People Act (S. 3682) with Alsobrooks as original cosponsor and Mfume as House co-lead (H.R. 8241); all nine Democrats plus Republican Andy Harris put statements on record at a March 2026 delegation meeting, and all nine Democrats signed a July 27, 2026 letter asking FERC to relieve Maryland of out-of-state data center transmission costs.

members_on_record.name: Chris Van Hollen
members_on_record.position: Lead sponsor of S. 3682, the Power for the People Act of 2026 (introduced Jan 15, 2026; 8 Democratic cosponsors): data-center rate classes, FERC rule on local transmission upgrades, large-load queue, clean energy and labor standards, load forecasting.
members_on_record.quote: the huge corporations building and running data centers should cover the costs of the energy they need – not push those costs onto the backs of consumers

members_on_record.name: Chris Van Hollen
members_on_record.position: Co-led Nov 2025 letter to PJM (with Beyer, Kaine, Booker, Alsobrooks, Subramanyam, Ivey, Norton, Mfume, Schakowsky, McBride, Dwight Evans) urging a mandatory backstop for new large loads and a large-load queue; led Feb 14, 2025 FERC technical-conference letter; cosigned Markey's Nov 13, 2025 FERC letter and Mar 6, 2026 NARUC letter.
members_on_record.quote: Consumers should not have to pay one dime in additional electricity costs to support data centers for the richest companies on the planet

members_on_record.name: Chris Van Hollen
members_on_record.position: Led July 27, 2026 Maryland delegation letter to FERC Chair Swett backing the OPC complaint over ~$2B in data-center transmission costs assigned to Maryland.
members_on_record.quote: our constituents should not be forced to pay for transmission projects that they did not cause and from which they will not meaningfully benefit

members_on_record.name: Angela Alsobrooks
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of S. 3682 Power for the People Act; signed the Nov 2025 PJM letter and the July 27, 2026 FERC letter.
members_on_record.quote: Data centers are critical to our national security, job creation, and economic development, but we cannot subsidize the costs of these data centers with our energy bills – which are already way too high

members_on_record.name: Andy Harris (MD-1)
members_on_record.position: Only Republican in the delegation; at the March 2026 delegation energy meeting said large users like data centers should build or secure their own electricity rather than shift costs; also called for a moratorium on state energy taxes/fees. Voted Yea on SPEED Act (Roll 356). Maryland Matters (Mar 5, 2026, not opened) quoted him: 'There is bipartisan agreement.'
members_on_record.quote: Large energy users like data centers should be responsible for building or securing the electricity they need instead of shifting those costs onto Maryland ratepayers.

members_on_record.name: Johnny Olszewski (MD-2)
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 8241 (House Power for the People Act) and H.R. 7977; signed July 27, 2026 FERC letter; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: Maryland families are struggling with ever-increasing utility bills. Lowering the cost of living has to be the top priority for all levels of government.

members_on_record.name: Sarah Elfreth (MD-3)
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 8241 and H.R. 7977; signed July 27, 2026 FERC letter; campaign runs 'Stop the Data Center Hikes' petition; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: Billions in data-center-driven transmission upgrade costs have already fallen onto ratepayers. That's why Team Maryland is working together on real solutions so our neighbors aren't caught footing the bill.

members_on_record.name: Glenn Ivey (MD-4)
members_on_record.position: Signed Nov 2025 PJM letter; original cosponsor of H.R. 8241; cosponsor of H.R. 7977 (May 4, 2026); signed July 27, 2026 FERC letter; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: We are paying for data centers that are not located in Maryland nor in the interest of our constituents. We need common sense regulations that save us from this affordability crisis and prevent rolling blackouts on the grid

members_on_record.name: Steny Hoyer (MD-5)
members_on_record.position: Signed July 27, 2026 FERC letter; joined March 2026 delegation meeting; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: it is critical that we continue to combat rising energy prices for working families

members_on_record.name: April McClain Delaney (MD-6)
members_on_record.position: Represents Frederick County (Quantum Frederick, MPRP); original cosponsor of H.R. 8241 and H.R. 7977; signed July 27, 2026 FERC letter; data centers part of her 'Costs Down, Opportunity Up' agenda; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: Rising demand from data centers, extreme weather, and the President's disruptive energy policies are only driving prices higher for working families while benefiting the wealthy.

members_on_record.name: Kweisi Mfume (MD-7)
members_on_record.position: House co-lead (with Tonko) of H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act (Apr 9, 2026); cosponsor of H.R. 9442, the AI Data Center Moratorium Act (joined Aug 27, 2026) - the only member from these nine jurisdictions on the moratorium bill; original cosponsor H.R. 7977; signed Nov 2025 PJM letter and July 27, 2026 FERC letter; voted Nay on SPEED Act.
members_on_record.quote: Working families cannot wait for another study, plan or proposal to address our skyrocketing electricity costs. ... Congress must pass the POWER FOR THE PEOPLE ACT.

members_on_record.name: Kweisi Mfume (MD-7)

members_on_record.name: Jamie Raskin (MD-8)

members_on_record.quote: The Trump economy is crushing Marylanders, especially as energy costs soar

The District's non-voting delegate Eleanor Holmes Norton (retiring; Robert White won the June 2026 Democratic primary to succeed her) is on record through letters and cosponsorships rather than floor votes.

members_on_record.name: Eleanor Holmes Norton (Delegate)
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (Dec 9, 2025); original cosponsor of H.R. 8241 Power for the People Act (Apr 9, 2026) and H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (Mar 18, 2026); cosponsor of H.R. 9372 Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act (July 20, 2026). As a delegate she has no vote on final passage (not recorded on Roll 356).

states.summary: HB 2014 (2025, pushed by Gov. Morrisey) lets data centers build gas-fired microgrids and strips local zoning/noise control and diverts property tax to the state. The flagship fight is Tucker County, where Fundamental Data's 'Ridgeline' campus (up to 10,000 acres between Thomas and Davis with a new gas plant) would use ~10 million MWh/yr, roughly all WV residential consumption; Tucker United leads opposition and says the congressional delegation has not engaged. Other projects: Nscale/Fidelis 'Monarch' in Mason County, a Putnam County proposal citing Ohio River water, and the MARL transmission line that PSC staff say mainly serves Virginia data centers. Markey's FERC letter cited two WV transmission lines expected to add $440M to residents' bills. The delegation is uniformly pro-data-center-with-caveats: Capito and Justice frame data centers as energy opportunity while urging community engagement; Riley Moore cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act citing local frustration; Carol Miller has no located statement.

members_on_record.quote: West Virginia families and American taxpayers should not be forced to foot the bill for massive data centers, and the enormous potential demands they place on our power grid. ... That cost should always be on the companies.

members_on_record.name: Riley Moore (WV-2)

members_on_record.quote: The locals aren't particularly happy because there's not local input. They can say something, but there's not an approval or disapproval process at the local level

states.summary: Duke Energy has 7.6 GW of executed data center agreements and a $103B 2026-2030 capital plan; data centers are ~80-85% of projected Carolinas load growth, and residential bills rose ~30% from 2017-2024 with 16-18% more proposed. Projects: Apple (Catawba), Microsoft's 1,385-acre Person County megasite, Amazon's $10B Richmond County campus, Google (Caldwell), Meta (Rutherford), a $19.2B/900 MW Tarboro campus, and Natelli's 190-acre Apex proposal that dominated the Foushee-Allam primary (won narrowly by Foushee with $1.6M from an Anthropic-funded PAC). 30+ localities (Charlotte, Durham, Wilson, Chatham, Haywood, Surry, Davie) enacted moratoria; an Elon poll found 24% support vs 44% oppose; Gov. Stein's Energy Policy Task Force recommended large-load tariffs and Duke signed Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge (July 2026). The NC House advanced SB 730 data center guardrails (June 2026). Data centers are an issue in the Cooper-Whatley Senate race. Congressional record: Tillis says AI/data centers are a GOP liability but defends off-grid projects; Budd co-sponsored the Liquid Cooling for AI Act; Foushee holds a 'local decision' line and cosponsors three cost bills; Davis embraces AI with community input (and was the only Democrat from these states to vote Yea on the SPEED Act); Murphy calls data centers 'the boogeyman' in an AI arms race; the rest of the GOP delegation has no located statements.

members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of S. 3269, the Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 (McCormick/Coons), framed as easing grid strain and lowering consumer costs while winning the AI race; chairs Commerce subcommittee that held a Sept 2025 'AI've Got a Plan' hearing warning against overregulation.
members_on_record.quote: The United States must win the AI Race against China, but it cannot do so without access to abundant and affordable energy. Liquid cooling of IT equipment at data centers and other advancements can ease electrical grid strain and help lower costs for consumers

members_on_record.name: Don Davis (NC-1)

members_on_record.name: Alma Adams (NC-12)
members_on_record.position: Voted Nay on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (Roll 356); Charlotte enacted a data center moratorium in 2026. No statement located.

members_on_record.name: Virginia Foxx (NC-5), Addison McDowell (NC-6), Mark Harris (NC-8), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Chuck Edwards (NC-11), Brad Knott (NC-13), Tim Moore (NC-14)
members_on_record.position: All voted Yea on H.R. 4776 SPEED Act (Roll 356); David Rouzer (NC-7) did not vote. No data center statements located. states.summary: Santee Cooper imposed an experimental large-load (50 MW+) rate in April 2025; Google announced $9B (Oct 2025) for Berkeley and two Dorchester County campuses; 32+ hyperscale projects are built or planned, and the Spartanburg 'Valara' campus at the old Kohler plant (nearly $3B with a private power plant) drew bus-loads of protesters. The legislature adjourned in May 2026 without passing Sen. Tom Davis's data center framework, which he called 'irresponsible'; the Dominion-NextEra merger case has become a data-center proxy fight. Politics: Rep. Nancy Mace (then a gubernatorial candidate) called for a one-year statewide moratorium (May 18, 2026; renewed July 10); the SC GOP gubernatorial debate asked all candidates about a moratorium. Sen. Lindsey Graham died in July 2026; his sister Darline Graham was appointed and beat Rep. Ralph Norman in the Aug 25, 2026 GOP runoff after both said communities need 'guardrails', with Norman opposing incentives. Sen. Tim Scott applauded Google's investment but says data centers must 'pay their own way' on electricity and water. Rep. Clyburn tied rising bills to Trump and Big Tech. Data center proposals were reported declining by March 2026.

Timmons' Democratic challenger Courtney McClain attacks his lack of a clear stance on the Spartanburg Valara project. No data center statements located.

states.summary: Georgia Power's data center-driven expansion is the state's defining energy fight: the PSC approved ~9,885 MW of new capacity in Dec 2025 (~80% for data centers, $16.5B construction, $50-60B potential ratepayer cost per SELC), a base-rate freeze through 2028 (July 2025), a 100 MW large-load contract rule (effective Feb 2025), and a disputed fuel deal (May 2026); average residential bills are up $43+/month over two years and Democrats won two PSC seats in Nov 2025 on affordability. The legislature's SB 34 ratepayer-protection bill failed and tax-break repeal stalled; DeKalb, Decatur and Floyd counties enacted moratoria; Georgia Power eminent-domain takings for transmission in Coweta/Newnan (Brian Jack's district) drew national coverage; OpenAI's $20B 'Project Camellia' in Effingham County got a 3.2 GW Georgia Power contract (Aug 26, 2026). Senate race: Ossoff opened a FERC inquiry (Apr 20, 2026) and demands transparency; GOP nominee Mike Collins says it's a local decision. Warnock called for a statewide moratorium (Aug 28, 2026). House: Carter, Bishop and Fuller cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act; McCormick says 'Georgia is open for business'; Bishop and Austin Scott want guardrails; Hank Johnson questions why Congress supports data centers at all. MTG (resigned Jan 5, 2026) attacked data center water use in July 2025; David Scott died Apr 22, 2026.

members_on_record.quote: Georgians are suffering from sky-high power bills. The Georgia Public Service Commission says most of the new energy to be brought online through a recently approved generation agreement will serve new large customers such as data centers.

members_on_record.name: Jon Ossoff

states.summary: Data centers are a top-tier issue in Alabama's 2026 governor's race (Sen. Tuberville, R, vs. ex-Sen. Doug Jones, D). At least a dozen hyperscale projects are proposed; Inside Climate News/WBHM (Aug 2026) found the proposed load would exceed all Alabama residential consumption. Flashpoints: Project Marvel in Bessemer (17 buildings, ~90x Bessemer's residential use), Project Red Clay in Lowndes County (1,500 MW request, 100,000 gal/day water, unanimous local Black Belt opposition, in Rep. Sewell's district), a 300 MW Oxmoor Valley/Birmingham build with a redacted PSC contract, and existing Google (Jackson Co.) and Meta (Madison Co.) sites in TVA territory. The Legislature passed SB 270 (effective Oct 1, 2026) requiring PSC public-interest review and full incremental-cost recovery for data center contracts; Alabama Power argues pre-SB 270 projects are exempt. Cullman, Fort Payne, Birmingham, Leeds and Homewood enacted pauses or restrictions in 2026. Southern Co./Alabama Power signed Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge (7/23/26) and won a $26.5B DOE loan (Feb 2026); TVA created a separate ~10% higher data-center rate (8/20/26) affecting north Alabama. Delegation split: Tuberville (pro, 'gold mines', China-propaganda framing, then a Sept 2026 'pay full price' plan), Britt (middle path, codify the pledge), Sewell and Figures (cosponsors of the AI Data Center Moratorium Act), Strong (pro with 'rails').

states.summary: Texas is the most politically volatile data-center state in the country. ERCOT's interconnection queue hit ~474 GW (90% data centers) against a peak-demand record around a fifth of that; the Legislature's SB 6 (2025) created large-load rules, but the 2013 sales-tax exemption now costs $3.2B per biennium. OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank's Stargate campus in Abilene (initial $100B; 85% abatement; ~9,000 construction jobs) produced a housing-cost spike and rural anger, with more Stargate sites in Shackelford and Milam counties; Google pledged $40B (Nov 2025); Meta's 1 GW El Paso campus and a proposed Fort Bliss data center rely on gas turbines; Hood County faces eight proposals; Caldwell County a 4 GW Tract campus; Laredo, Fort Worth, San Marcos, Amarillo and others saw organized opposition. Gov. Abbott reversed course: called for banning new AI data centers in rural neighborhoods (June 30, 2026), then ordered PUCT/ERCOT to audit every queued project and pause interconnections (Aug 3, 2026), demanding self-supplied power and water and an end to state incentives. Data centers now define the open U.S. Senate race (GOP nominee Ken Paxton released a platform Aug 24, 2026 backing Cotton's DATA Act and a rural ban; Democrat James Talarico's plan would give locals veto power). In Congress: Sen. Cruz champions Stargate and blames Chinese 'misinformation' for water fears; Cornyn (defeated in the May 2026 runoff) toured Stargate/Lancium in 2025; Arrington and Pfluger are boosters; Chip Roy filed the POWER Act (data-center water/energy reporting); Cuellar filed a 'Ratepayer Bill of Rights' and says GOP leaders are blocking data-center bills until after the election; Escobar has fought Meta's El Paso project; Casar co-led the PRICE Act and Data Center Transparency Act; Fallon, Van Duyne, McCaul, Weber and De La Cruz cosponsored the House Ratepayer Protection Act; Crenshaw cosponsored the House DATA Act.

members_on_record.position: Toured Project Stargate and the Lancium campus in Abilene and discussed the city's tech future (page paywalled; headline only)

members_on_record.name: Jodey Arrington
members_on_record.position: House Budget chair; hosted Stargate launch, framing West Texas as 'Silicon Prairie' and AI compute as beating China
members_on_record.quote: There's no better place to build the backbone for AI than West Texas because of our abundant and reliable energy, our workforce, our hard-working, God fearing, freedom-loving people, and we have a very good environment for starting businesses and building facilities like this at this scale.

members_on_record.name: Jodey Arrington
members_on_record.position: Press release touting Stargate's $100B Abilene investment
members_on_record.quote: From construction jobs to cutting-edge careers, this project means opportunities for our people, billions in private investment, and a powerful reminder that America - not China - will lead in the technologies of tomorrow.

members_on_record.name: August Pfluger
members_on_record.position: E&C member; at nuclear hearing tied AI race to exponential energy demand and asked how utilities serve data-center load growth at scale; present at 7/20/26 E&C markup
members_on_record.quote: I think what we recognize in this hearing is very significant, because there's a race, and that race is not just for AI, although that is extremely important, but the race is for an assortment of energy needs that demand is going to continue to increase at an exponential rate.

members_on_record.name: Chip Roy
members_on_record.position: As AG candidate, questions whether Texas has enough water and power for data centers; wants them self-sustaining and accountable for water
members_on_record.quote: These are massive sucks on power. We need to know that we're going to have the ability to sustain these things when we get them created and developed.

members_on_record.name: Chip Roy
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of H.R. 9019, POWER Act (Public Oversight of Water and Energy Reporting): DOE to collect and report data-center water and energy use
members_on_record.quote: As data centers spring up across the country, we need to be mindful of our water and energy resources. States like Texas have been enduring extreme drought conditions, and as we build out energy intensive data center infrastructure, we must have a clear picture of how much water and energy these projects are consuming.

members_on_record.name: Greg Casar
members_on_record.position: Co-lead (original cosponsor) of H.R. 6983 PRICE Act (data centers must self-generate/renewables) and H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act
members_on_record.quote: Families should not pay more for utilities so that billionaires can get rich off AI data centers. With this bill, Congressman Menendez and I are saying clearly: AI data centers should not be allowed to jack up your electric bill or poison your environment.

members_on_record.name: Greg Casar
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of H.R. 8568, Lowering Utility Bills Act (caps utility return on equity; 27 cosponsors incl. Al Green, Menefee, Escobar)
members_on_record.quote: They pay basically no risk, but pay themselves more than anybody else can get investing in the stock market, and then you are forced to pick up the tab

members_on_record.name: Henry Cuellar
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act (Evans/Castor)

members_on_record.name: Henry Cuellar
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of H.R. 10139, Ratepayer Bill of Rights Act of 2026: ten protections incl. disclosure of water/power use, ban on cost-shifting, binding cost-recovery agreements, 90-day refunds
members_on_record.quote: The basic promise of this bill is simple: If a data center creates the cost, the data center pays the cost. The family ratepayer does not.

members_on_record.name: Henry Cuellar
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 6529, Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (Landsman)

members_on_record.name: Henry Cuellar
members_on_record.position: Says House GOP leadership is blocking all data-center bills, including the 52-0 committee bill, until after the election
members_on_record.quote: The ranking member of [the Energy and Commerce Committee] told me that the Republican leadership doesn't want to put any data center bills up before the election.

members_on_record.name: Veronica Escobar
members_on_record.position: Letter demanding Meta hold public listening sessions on El Paso data center; cites electricity rate risk, gas turbines, water use
members_on_record.quote: These data centers use an exorbitant amount of energy, and when energy usage increases without increased energy production, rates go up for consumers.

members_on_record.name: Veronica Escobar
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor, H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act; cosponsor H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (5/21/26), H.R. 8568 (8/20/26), H.R. 10139 (8/31/26); H.R. 7977 (5/7/26)

members_on_record.name: Veronica Escobar
members_on_record.position: Offered Appropriations amendment to block EPA New Source Review change letting gas-powered data centers start construction before permits/public comment; rejected by Republicans
members_on_record.quote: In my community, the data center issue is probably the number one front and center issue. And if data centers haven't come to your community yet, they will

members_on_record.name: Pat Fallon
members_on_record.position: Praised Gov. Abbott's data-center audit/pause as responsive to constituents' concerns
members_on_record.quote: I think it was a thoughtful, good step that the governor put in place. He was listening to his constituents, over 30 million of them. They share those concerns, as I do.

members_on_record.name: Pat Fallon
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340, Ratepayer Protection Act

members_on_record.name: Beth Van Duyne
members_on_record.position: Said data-center construction should be decided at the local level (Bloomberg TV; video not opened)
