states.summary: Oklahoma has been mostly pro-development at the top (Gov. Stitt signed SB 480, the 2025 'behind the meter' law letting large loads build their own generation, which the White House later cited as a model for its Ratepayer Protection Pledge), while local fights grew: Google's Stillwater AI campus (revealed Mar 2025; water and county/city splits), Google's $9B statewide expansion (Aug 2025), a contested Google proposal in Sand Springs, an IREN data center near Kiowa (Pittsburg County commissioners paused incentives), and Corporation Commission races focused on data-center costs. State Sen. Kendal Sacchieri (R) filed a three-year moratorium; the state Senate passed a bill shifting data-center energy costs off consumers (Apr 2026). The federal delegation changed mid-stream: Sen. Mullin (who told Sapulpa leaders data centers are a 'game changer' for rural towns) became DHS Secretary in March 2026 and was replaced by ex-Williams CEO Alan Armstrong, who has made permitting reform for AI-era power his signature issue; Rep. Hern won the GOP nomination for the seat. Rep. Brecheen cosponsored Roy's POWER Act and says operators must not drive up electricity costs. No data-center statements were located for Sen. Lankford or Reps. Hern, Bice, Lucas and Cole.

fights.project: Google AI data center campus (400 acres; up to ~$3B)
fights.issue: Water supply, city vs. county officials split, incentives
Tax revenue vs. power and water demand
Local controversy over siting and impacts
Electricity costs; county commissioners paused incentives

fights.project: SB 480 'behind the meter' law; moratorium bill; cost-shift bill
fights.issue: Sacchieri three-year moratorium not heard; Senate passed bill shifting data-center energy costs off consumers (4/29/26); OCC candidates debate costs

fights.project: Interconnection backlog; Inola aluminum smelter power
fights.issue: Sen. Armstrong says 8-15 year interconnection studies push data centers behind the meter

members_on_record.name: Markwayne Mullin
members_on_record.position: (While a senator, before becoming DHS Secretary) urged rural towns to welcome data centers as revenue 'game changers'; acknowledged limited permanent jobs; said federal policy will require grid-connected facilities to generate excess power
members_on_record.quote: It's a game changer. The amount of revenue that brings to your city, into your water and wastewater facilities, into your high schools … it's pretty hard to ignore.

members_on_record.name: Alan Armstrong
members_on_record.position: Appointed senator (Mar 24, 2026) pushing permitting reform as essential to meeting AI-driven electricity demand and competing with China
members_on_record.quote: What we don't have is a permitting process that allows us to get the infrastructure built

members_on_record.name: Alan Armstrong
members_on_record.position: Op-ed: interconnection backlogs are pushing data centers to build private behind-the-meter systems; cites PJM's 76% cost surge; calls for permitting reform
members_on_record.quote: Under the current system, large power consumers like major industrial players and data center developers are increasingly bypassing the public grid entirely, building private "behind-the-meter" energy systems because public infrastructure cannot keep pace.

members_on_record.name: Josh Brecheen
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9019, POWER Act (Roy): DOE reporting on data-center electricity and water use

members_on_record.name: Josh Brecheen
members_on_record.position: At McAlester town hall on the IREN Kiowa project: operators must not drive up electricity costs; Congress should provide information, not a regulatory regime
members_on_record.quote: (Data center operators) have to make sure that they are not driving up people's electricity costs. I think that is something that every Oklahoman ought to know the facts on. So that data center measure that you're talking about (HR9019), Congress is not gonna create the regulatory environment. What we can do is make sure people have information about the data centers.

states.summary: Ohio is the epicenter of the Midwest data center backlash and the clearest case where it is moving federal politics. Average Ohio electric bills rose 53% June 2021-June 2026 (Heatmap/MIT via Ohio Capital Journal); PJM's 2026-27 capacity auction cleared at the $329/MW-day court-imposed cap and PJM came up 6.8 GW short; AEP Ohio's data center tariff (85% minimum-take) took effect July 2025; Signal Ohio found the state lost $1.6B in data-center tax revenue in 2025 (11x forecast) and Gov. DeWine paused new exemptions. Marquee projects: Google/Meta/Amazon/Microsoft campuses in New Albany-Columbus, the proposed 10 GW PORTS/SB Energy-OpenAI campus in Pike County (Piketon) with a $33.3B gas plant, Meta's ~$800M Bowling Green (Wood County) site, Ark Data Centers' Akron/Independence expansion (10 jobs, $4.5M tax break). A BGSU poll found 71% of Ohioans back a moratorium; Conserve Ohio is collecting signatures for a 2027 constitutional amendment. The Husted-Brown Senate race has become a national referendum: Brown's ads call Husted 'the face of data centers,' an NRSC memo (Aug 18, 2026) called data centers 'the anchor hanging around Husted's neck,' and Husted responded with S. 5028 (Ratepayer Protection Act). Sen. Moreno now wants a 100% federal tax on state/local data center incentives. House members split: Landsman (3 bills), Kaptur (floor speech, campaign issue vs. Merrin), Latta/Balderson (E&C grid bills, 'data centers must pay their own way' but blaming foreign influence for opposition), Jordan (PUCO approach 'a good thing'), Davidson (only Midwest Republican to vote no on the May 2025 H.R.1 that carried the state-AI-law moratorium).

fights.issue: Electric bills up 53% since 2021; PJM 2026-27 capacity auction cleared at the $329/MW-day cap and came up 6.8 GW short with data centers the main driver; April 2026 AEP BTCR transmission increase (~$7.90/mo); NRDC projects ~$70/month more by 2028.
fights.project: PJM capacity market / AEP Ohio data center tariff (in force since July 23, 2025)
fights.status: Ongoing; state bill to extend AEP-style tariff statewide stalled in June 2026

fights.issue: Proposed ~10 GW PORTS Technology Campus (SB Energy, OpenAI/Nvidia-backed, reported $500B+), powered by a new $33.3B natural gas plant; billed as 'the world's largest construction project'; FAST-41 status granted June 2026.
fights.project: PORTS Technology Campus / Piketon gas plant
fights.status: Groundbreaking of gas plant March 2026; campus in development

fights.issue: $800M Meta data center rising near Bowling Green; Ohio Democrats staged a Sept. 9, 2026 rally against Sen. Husted at the site.
fights.status: Under construction; campaign flashpoint (TiffinOhio page opened but body not extractable; WTOL coverage blocked)

fights.issue: Ohio Tax Credit Authority approved a $4.5M sales-tax exemption for Ark Data Centers (Carlyle Group) $136M expansion creating 10 jobs; Sen. Moreno demanded Carlyle give the subsidy back.
Ohio EPA draft general permit that would let data centers discharge wastewater/stormwater directly to rivers and streams; condemned by Sen. Moreno (Feb. 27, 2026).
fights.project: Ohio EPA data center wastewater general permit

fights.issue: Conserve Ohio ballot amendment to ban new data centers (fell short of 2026 signatures, aiming for 2027); Ohio Supreme Court allowed an Ashville referendum against a data center project (Aug 2026); Washington Township (Montgomery County) 360-day zoning moratorium (April 2026).
fights.project: Conserve Ohio moratorium amendment; local moratoria

fights.issue: Duke Energy rate increases; 38,000+ disconnections; Landsman backed Hamilton County Commissioner Reece's call for a moratorium on rate increases (letter to DeWine, Aug. 26, 2026).

Brown ads: Husted 'force-fed the massive energy-sucking facilities' and gave '$2.5 billion in out-of-control tax breaks' for 226 data centers; NRSC memo (Aug. 18, 2026) warns Husted loss would make politicians nationwide 'not go near the next one.'
fights.status: Election Nov. 2026; Fox News poll had Brown +8 (Axios, Aug 19)

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Introduced S. 5028, the Ratepayer Protection Act (July 16, 2026), requiring states/PUCs to consider standards making 100 MW+ large loads pay full incremental cost of generation, transmission and upgrades; companion is H.R. 9340 (Evans/Castor), which E&C reported 52-0 on July 21, 2026. 0 cosponsors on S. 5028 per govinfo.
members_on_record.quote: If America wants to lead the world in AI and strengthen our national security, we have to build the energy infrastructure to support it. But we must do that without passing the costs on to working families and small businesses. The Ratepayer Protection Act would keep America globally competitive while protecting Ohioans and Americans from higher electricity bills.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Joined President Trump's White House roundtable where seven tech companies signed the Ratepayer Protection Pledge; pro-data-center framing (AI race with China) plus ratepayer protection.
members_on_record.quote: In places like Ohio, this work matters. If America wants economic and national security dominance, we must lead in technology and AI to stay ahead of adversaries like China. But, this innovation requires energy and Ohio families are concerned about the impact on their own bills.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Defends data centers; says his bill requires them to produce their own power. Continues to advocate development provided it does not burden communities.
members_on_record.quote: What we're requiring the data centers to do is to produce their own power so that the local ratepayers don't have to foot the bill for their expansions. This is something I've been working with President Trump on for six months.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Blames higher electricity prices on Democratic climate policy and plant closures rather than data centers (Cleveland-Cliffs Middletown event with VP Vance).
members_on_record.quote: You want to have lower electricity prices — I want to tell you why they're rising. Because Congress and, under the Obama administration, under the Biden administration, they closed 23 power plants in the state of Ohio, representing half the electricity we use on a daily basis. Radical climate policies did that.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Told Ohio Statehouse News Bureau (Aug. 2026) that data center tax breaks should no longer be awarded and that the industry has 'earned that backlash'; says siting should be a local decision.
members_on_record.quote: They've earned that backlash. They haven't been as forthcoming about the benefits that will come in terms of local jobs and construction worker jobs and reduced property taxes, and they haven't offered things like paying the energy bills for local communities, for the power plants they build.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: On a conservative podcast (July 22, 2026) defended data centers as something every connected consumer uses; earlier (Feb. 2026 at Statehouse) said data centers should produce their own electricity and recycle water. Record as Lt. Gov. 2019-25: championed Google ($600M New Albany, $43.5M tax break), Amazon $7.8B (2023), Google $2.3B (2024).
members_on_record.quote: If you're connected to a wire, you're using the data center. So, understand that when we look in the mirror, we are the problem.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Called the backlash a 'wake up call' after the NRSC memo; says data centers must build trust with local communities (Bloomberg Government, Sept. 4, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: The data centers have got to build the trust of the local community.

members_on_record.name: Jon Husted
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on Blackburn Amdt. 2814 to H.R. 1 striking the 10-year moratorium on state/local AI laws (passed 99-1).

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Wants to end all taxpayer subsidies for data centers; says he will likely introduce federal legislation taxing any state/local data center incentive at 100%. Remarks at Columbus energy-affordability summit (Sept. 3, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: These data centers are going to come into our community and take our water and pollute our environment. They're going to raise our electricity prices. They're eventually going to put us out of work — and our taxpayer dollars are going to support the construction of these things. It's the worst sales pitch in the history of sales pitches.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Proposed 100% federal tax on state/local data center tax incentives; said Ohio's $2.3B already given cannot be recouped.
members_on_record.quote: I most likely am going to introduce federal legislation that says if a state or local government gives a data center a tax incentive, the federal government will tax that incentive at 100%. You can take that out of the equation. No more taxpayer dollars. Period.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Told The Dispatch the critics are right; opposes tax breaks, criticized the data center business model at a June 2026 Senate hearing, wants open-source U.S. AI models.
members_on_record.quote: I think that 70% of the country is against giving taxpayer money to trillion-dollar companies, having them come in and raise electricity prices, suck up our natural resources and then ultimately produce a product that un-employs us all.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Letter to Carlyle Group demanding it give up a $4.5M Ohio sales-tax exemption for Ark Data Centers' 10-job expansion, sign the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and create more jobs.
members_on_record.quote: When corporations like Carlyle demand massive amounts of electricity to fund their projects, it's everyday Ohioans who get stuck with the bill. Without protections, these costs are quietly dumped onto families and small businesses through higher utility rates, while taxpayers are left to subsidize grid upgrades necessary to accommodate private projects.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Condemned Ohio EPA draft permit allowing data centers to release untreated wastewater and stormwater into rivers and streams.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Spectrum News interview (March 2026): data centers should take no taxpayer money, clean discharged water, invest in workforce, not take prime farmland.
members_on_record.quote: They shouldn't be taking a dime from the taxpayer. That's just grotesque.

members_on_record.name: Bernie Moreno
members_on_record.position: Cosponsored S. 465, GRID Power Act (Hoeven) to prioritize dispatchable generation in interconnection queues (cosponsored Apr. 28, 2025); voted Yea on stripping the state-AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1, July 1, 2025).

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of three data center bills: H.R. 6529 Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act (Dec. 9, 2025; FERC conference on protecting residential ratepayers; ordered reported 44-0 by E&C July 21, 2026), H.R. 8033 No Harm Data Centers Act (Mar. 20, 2026; data centers >50 MW pay full grid costs via FERC ratemaking, no NDAs with officials, environmental study), H.R. 9629 Protecting Communities from Data Center Impacts Act (July 9, 2026; EPA/NASEM study of noise, air, water, waste). Also original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act.
members_on_record.quote: You're either with Big Tech or with our towns. A handshake and a promise from these tech companies is not enough. That's why we're leading the data center effort to make sure they pay, and that they negotiate their deals in public – no more NDAs.

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Argues federal framework needed because Ohio won't act; his bill would move data-center ratemaking to FERC (Ohio Consumers' Counsel supports no-cost-shift but objects to displacing PUCO).
members_on_record.quote: These deals need to be entirely transparent. Not a little bit transparent, not kind of transparent, not mostly transparent, but entirely transparent. And that means no NDAs.

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Campaign framing in OH-1 race against Eric Conroy: federal government must make data centers pay for everything, not pollute, and negotiate publicly.
members_on_record.quote: What our towns need is the federal government to come in and say this is going to stop. If they're going to come in, they're going to come in, they're going to pay for everything. They're not going to pollute. You're going to have a say. They're going to treat workers well. They're going to pay them well. And they're going to do everything above board, all of it public.

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Summarized his three bills for FOX19.
members_on_record.quote: One forces the data centers to pay for everything. There's no reason our taxpayers should pay for anything of this. They have so much money. The second is getting rid of these NDAs. Everything should be done publicly. And the third, this most recent bill, requires there to be a national standard in terms of the environmental impact.

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Letter to Gov. DeWine backing Hamilton County Commissioner Reece's request for a moratorium on further Duke Energy rate increases and $1M in utility assistance.
members_on_record.quote: Local folks need help. At a time when families are already paying more for gas, groceries, healthcare – they shouldn't have to worry about another big bill. We have to act now before it gets worse.

members_on_record.name: Greg Landsman
members_on_record.position: Voted Nay on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), which contained the 10-year moratorium on state/local AI regulation; voted Nay on GRID Power Act (Sept. 18, 2025) and Reliable Power Act (Dec. 17, 2025).

members_on_record.name: Marcy Kaptur
members_on_record.position: Spoke on the House floor (late 2025) questioning what data centers will cost citizens in power and water; campaign against Derek Merrin centers on his 2017 state vote on data center tax breaks; campaign statement says data center companies should pay their fair share.
members_on_record.quote: How much more will our citizens be forced to pay for power and water? They have a right to know. Will our building trades be true partners in economic growth or just temporary labor while facing higher utility bills at home? And how many permanent jobs will these largely opaque facilities actually provide? … The American people deserve to know how AI data centers will affect their communities.

members_on_record.name: Marcy Kaptur
members_on_record.position: As ranking member of Energy-Water Appropriations, linked data center proliferation to rising electricity bills during FY27 defense/energy spending debate.
members_on_record.quote: This Congress has an obligation to defend our people — not stick our heads in the sand or pretend it's 1946.

members_on_record.name: Marcy Kaptur
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 9700, Ratepayer Justice and Commercial Power Accountability Act (utility-corruption/FirstEnergy ratepayer refund fund; not data-center-specific but aimed at electric bills). Voted Nay on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) and Nay on GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act.
members_on_record.quote: I will not stand for FirstEnergy increasing any Ohioan's electricity bills until justice is delivered to ratepayers and we have a full accounting of the criminality that occurred at the expense of our people.

members_on_record.name: Bob Latta
members_on_record.position: As E&C Energy Subcommittee chair, co-signed (with Chairmen Guthrie and Joyce) a letter to PCAST and FBI Director Patel requesting investigation of alleged foreign (CCP-linked) influence campaigns behind data center opposition; letter calls Sanders' moratorium bill 'disastrous.'

members_on_record.name: Bob Latta
members_on_record.position: At Ohio Manufacturers' Energy conference (Columbus, late Aug. 2026) said data centers, not customers, should bear costs they cause.
members_on_record.quote: We want to make sure that the ratepayers aren't paying for a data center that comes into the area. If you've got costs that are being incurred, that data center should be the one doing it, not the customer.

members_on_record.name: Bob Latta
members_on_record.position: May 13, 2026 hearing: demand rising faster than ever, need much more generation and transmission. Sponsor of H.R. 3638 Electric Supply Chain Act (passed House 267-159, Dec. 11, 2025) and H.R. 7257 SECURE Grid Act (passed House; in Senate July 2026).
members_on_record.quote: Demand for reliable energy is rising faster than at any point in history. Clearly, we will need more generation and transmission, and a great deal more of it.

members_on_record.name: Troy Balderson
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of H.R. 1047 GRID Power Act (passed House 216-206, Sept. 18, 2025; prioritizes dispatchable generation in interconnection queues), H.R. 3616 Reliable Power Act (passed House 225-203, Dec. 17, 2025), H.R. 9332 Load Forecasting Enhancement Act (E&C 47-0, July 21, 2026; aimed at speculative data center load inflating ratepayer costs). Chairs House Energy Action Team.
members_on_record.quote: This is especially concerning for Central Ohio, which has become a national hub for data center construction. These facilities are powering the American AI revolution, but we must ensure we can keep them running while also providing reliable, affordable energy to Ohio families.

members_on_record.name: Troy Balderson
members_on_record.position: At Zanesville event said data centers must find their own power source.
members_on_record.quote: These data centers are going to have to find their own power source. We cannot put that on the backs of our constituents.

members_on_record.name: Troy Balderson
members_on_record.position: Load Forecasting Enhancement Act press release: better forecasting prevents overbuilding for speculative projects that raise ratepayer costs.
members_on_record.quote: Our nation is using more electricity each year, and for our grid to meet that growing demand, we need to know where infrastructure investments are needed to keep the lights on and keep America moving forward. By giving states and utilities the tools they need, we can ensure we expand and improve our grid as efficiently as possible—saving Ohio families money while boosting our nation's energy security.

members_on_record.name: Jim Jordan
members_on_record.position: Supports PUCO's approach that data centers cannot drive up costs for other consumers; supports state study bill; cosponsored H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act on Sept. 1, 2026.
members_on_record.quote: The Public Utilities Commission of Ohio has said that if data centers come into a community, they can't drive up the cost of electricity for the other consumers, for residents and other users. I think that's a good thing.

members_on_record.name: Jim Jordan

states.summary: Michigan's fight is anchored by the Oracle/OpenAI/Related Digital 'Stargate' campus in Saline Township (1.4 GW, $16B construction plus ~$40B Oracle fit-out, ~$56B total), where the township board rejected rezoning in Sept. 2025, settled after being sued in Oct. 2025, DTE sought a fast-track PSC approval (opposed by Dingell and state Democrats), AG Nessel appealed the PSC approval, the treasurer resigned after death threats (May 2026), and Gov. Whitmer's June 1, 2026 groundbreaking appearance with Sam Altman drew fury from progressives including Rep. Tlaib. More than 50 municipalities have passed moratoria; at least 17 hyperscale proposals are pending (Saline, Washington Twp., Bay City, Lowell, Frenchtown/Dundee, Dowagiac, U-M/Los Alamos $1.2B Ypsilanti Twp.). Data centers dominated the Aug. 4 primaries (El-Sayed beat Rep. Stevens for the Senate nomination; Sunrise co-founder William Lawrence won MI-7 Dem primary against Rep. Barrett, who then introduced two local-control/NDA bills; GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers backed a one-year moratorium). State legislature: bipartisan pause bill (Feb. 2026), Senate Dem 8-bill package (June 18, 2026), repeal-the-tax-break push.

fights.issue: 1.4 GW Stargate campus ('The Barn'): rezoning rejected Sept. 2025, lawsuit and settlement Oct. 2025, DTE asked PSC to skip public hearings (Nov. 2025), AG Nessel appealed PSC approval of DTE contracts, treasurer resigned after death threats (May 2026), Whitmer/Altman groundbreaking June 1, 2026, Saline River discharge permit comment period (July 2026).
University of Michigan / Los Alamos National Laboratory $1.2B computing center sited over township opposition; Rep. Dingell repeatedly demanding transparency and a real town hall (Sept. 9, 2026).
fights.status: Site confirmed Aug. 2026; township vows fight

fights.issue: Hyperscale Data campus partnering with Shanghai-based AGIBOT on humanoid robotics; Rep. Walberg asked Commerce Sec. Lutnick to investigate (July 28, 2026).
Cloverleaf Infrastructure proposals dominated Rep. Walberg's Jan. 5, 2026 town hall.

50+ local moratoria; bipartisan House bill to pause approvals until April 1, 2027 (Feb. 2026); Senate Democrats' 8-bill package (SB 1046-1051, 762, 763) on water caps, 20-year contracts/90% renewables, NDA ban, community benefit agreements (June 18, 2026); push to repeal 2024 sales/use tax break.

El-Sayed (anti-tax-break, 'terms of engagement') defeated Rep. Stevens in Aug. 4 primary; Rogers (R) backs 1-year moratorium; Sunrise co-founder Lawrence won MI-7 primary on data-center opposition, prompting Barrett's local-control bills.

members_on_record.name: Debbie Dingell
members_on_record.position: Joined Democrats' letter to Michigan PSC Chair Dan Scripps opposing DTE's request to skip public hearings on Saline Township data center contracts; says approval should be predicated on no ratepayer increases.
members_on_record.quote: The community deserves and must have a seat at the table, so you need a transparent process.

members_on_record.name: Debbie Dingell
members_on_record.position: Statement criticizing U-M's selection of Ypsilanti Township for the Los Alamos data center.
members_on_record.quote: I have repeatedly urged the University to listen to the impacted community, be transparent, and answer basic questions about the impact of this project. Instead, they have rebuffed these concerns and are ignoring the pleas from residents that do not want this.

members_on_record.name: Debbie Dingell
members_on_record.position: Letter to U-M leadership demanding the Sept. 9, 2026 town hall be a genuine two-way forum; raised water use, grid impact and who bears costs.
members_on_record.quote: Key concerns include water use, such as how much water the facility will require, where it would come from, and what safeguards are in place to protect long-term regional supply. They also include energy demand and infrastructure strain, particularly how the data center will impact the electrical grid, who would bear the costs, and how it aligns with renewable energy commitments.

members_on_record.name: Debbie Dingell
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (Casten; data centers pay their own costs); voted Nay on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) and Nay on GRID Power Act, Electric Supply Chain Act and Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Rashida Tlaib
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 9939, No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act (permanent ban on large AI data centers on federal land incl. military bases, removal of existing ones); cosponsors include Ramirez (IL), Pocan (WI), later Carson (IN). Also offered as amendment to Defense appropriations (rejected).
members_on_record.quote: Everywhere I go in our district, our residents tell me loud and clear, data centers are not welcome in our communities. AI data centers bring noise, light, air, and water pollution, and can increase energy costs by as much as 267%.

members_on_record.name: Rashida Tlaib
members_on_record.position: Publicly attacked Gov. Whitmer's appearance at the Saline Township groundbreaking, calling her support 'disgusting' (post on X).
members_on_record.quote: So disappointed in Governor Whitmer's support of data center expansions in our state especially when so many Michiganders are opposed

members_on_record.name: Rashida Tlaib
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 9442 AI Data Center Moratorium Act (Ocasio-Cortez, June 24, 2026), H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act (Apr. 23, 2026), H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (Mar. 5, 2026), H.R. 8568 Lowering Utility Bills Act (Apr. 29, 2026), H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; introduced 'Make DTE Pay Act' (May 2026, per CBS headline, not opened). Voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Tom Barrett
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (bars federal agencies from overriding local zoning/siting) and H.R. 10118 No Data Center NDAs Act (bars members of Congress from signing data center NDAs); touts his state-House vote against Michigan's data center tax breaks. Cosponsors of 10119 include Moolenaar, Shreve, Wied. Also cosponsored H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Sept. 10, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: Families in my district are rightly concerned about the effect data centers could have on their utility bills, as well as the land and water in their neighborhood. They deserve to know all the facts and have the final say over any proposed project. That starts with stopping federal overreach and preventing the secrecy pledges that have plagued Michigan and undermined the power of local residents.

members_on_record.name: Tom Barrett
members_on_record.position: Campaign ad: 'I believe you should decide on data centers, not Washington'; 'I stood up to my own party.' Critics (CAP, American Prospect) note he voted for H.R. 1 with the state-AI-law moratorium (May 22, 2025) and backed the SPEED Act permitting bill; Speaker Johnson called a federal moratorium a 'dangerous prospect' while campaigning with him in Lansing (Aug. 18, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: I believe you should decide on data centers, not Washington.

members_on_record.name: Haley Stevens
members_on_record.position: Senate candidate (lost Aug. 4 primary to El-Sayed); opposed a moratorium, wants data centers in Michigan but paying utility/water bills and taxes; introduced H.R. 7926 Stop Unfair Electricity Prices Act (Mar. 12, 2026; bars DOE financial assistance to investor-owned utilities that raise residential rates above Jan. 1, 2026 levels). Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act.
members_on_record.quote: I want to force these data centers to pay their utility bills and to pay water bills for folks.

members_on_record.name: Haley Stevens
members_on_record.position: Called for federal laws governing data centers; declined follow-up on Saline Township specifically.
members_on_record.quote: I support tackling why we have 50-some data centers and one being built right now and no federal laws ... governing them, ensuring that the money goes into the communities, ensuring that the costs of the consumers in those communities and the states that they're in don't continue to go up.

members_on_record.name: Haley Stevens
members_on_record.position: Open to Congress preempting state AI regulation (a patchwork is 'not good for the long term'); prioritizes worker training and auto-industry protections.

members_on_record.name: Hillary Scholten
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 10005 Data Center Resource Disclosure Act (NTIA annual survey of data center energy/water use, public dashboard) and the Defending Our Energy and Water Act (DoD data center water-efficiency standards); offered a related NDAA/appropriations amendment. Original cosponsor of H.R. 10321 Responsible Data Center Siting Act (Sept. 8, 2026) and H.R. 7977.
members_on_record.quote: Accountability starts with transparency. As data centers continue to come online across Michigan and the country, people deserve to know how these facilities are affecting the water and power they rely on, so we can best advocate for our communities to prevent exploitation.

members_on_record.name: Tim Walberg
members_on_record.position: Local control; opposes state/federal incentives; at Frenchtown Township town hall on Cloverleaf proposals.
members_on_record.quote: Local control is where I stand. There are communities in my district that want centers. Others don't. I'd like to see both of them impacted in a positive way. Data centers are going to be here. They are valuable in their use. Whether in local neighborhoods, that's up to the local community.

members_on_record.name: Tim Walberg
members_on_record.position: Letter to Commerce Sec. Lutnick urging review of Hyperscale Data's Dowagiac robotics program with Shanghai-based AGIBOT on national-security grounds. Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025).

members_on_record.name: John James
members_on_record.position: GOP gubernatorial nominee; calls state approach 'crazy,' wants 'transparency and local control by default,' guardrails so data centers don't raise rates, build on blighted sites not farmland; opposes moratorium. Cosponsored Latta's H.R. 7257 SECURE Grid Act (Mar. 3, 2026). CAP notes he voted four times (E&C markup and floor) for the H.R. 1 state/local AI-law moratorium in May 2025; Michigan Democrats say he 'voted 4 times against local control.'
members_on_record.quote: We have to diversify Michigan's economy. Data centers are just one tool, but they're not the whole plan.

members_on_record.name: John James
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) after voting three times in E&C markup (May 13-14, 2025) to retain the state/local AI moratorium, including against Pallone amendment COMM19 (29-24).
members_on_record.quote: Number one, local control.

members_on_record.name: Shri Thanedar
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Landsman's H.R. 6529 (Dec. 16, 2025), H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (original, Mar. 5, 2026), H.R. 8568 Lowering Utility Bills Act (original, Apr. 29, 2026), H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; lost Aug. 4 primary. Voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Aug. 27, 2026) and original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025).

members_on_record.name: John Moolenaar
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Barrett's H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (Aug. 31, 2026) and H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Sept. 2, 2026); voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025).

members_on_record.name: Bill Huizenga
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Sept. 10, 2026); voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025). No data-center statement located.

members_on_record.name: Lisa McClain
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Jack Bergman
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Elissa Slotkin
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1). Legislating AI guardrails for military 'kill chain' decisions; frequently frames AI as a tech race with China. No Saline Township or data-center-specific statement located.
members_on_record.quote: If we were functioning like a healthy democracy, we would be talking about AI every single day in the US Senate and the US House.

members_on_record.name: Gary Peters
members_on_record.position: Retiring; voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1, July 1, 2025); backed Stevens in the primary. No data-center statement located.

states.summary: Roughly 60-70 hyperscale proposals in two years; Indiana's 2019 50-year sales-tax exemption (HEA 1405, which Rep. Messmer helped pass as a state legislator) and HEA 1007 (2025) fast-tracked approvals. Flashpoints: Meta's $10B+ LEAP campus in Lebanon (10 data centers, ~1 GW; MISO estimates 1.2 GW; up to 25 MGD of White River water piped to Lebanon), Amazon's 2,400-2,800 MW New Carlisle campus (909 diesel generators; NIPSCO GenCo gas plant), Google/Amazon in Fort Wayne (I&M), Google in Monrovia (AES). Citizens Action Coalition documents hundreds of millions in grid costs shifted to Duke/I&M customers (IURC cases); DOE emergency orders kept coal plants running. Indianapolis City-County Council voted 23-1 (Aug. 10, 2026) to bar new data centers through 2027 (reported; not independently opened). The legislature did little in 2026 (HB 1245 study died; HB 1210 advanced). Rep. Spartz (R) asked DOE/Interior for an independent federal review (Sept. 9, 2026); Rep. Carson (D) joined the Sanders/AOC moratorium; Rep. Mrvan sought a FERC probe of NIPSCO after mass outages.

fights.issue: Meta $10B+ campus, 10 planned data centers, ~1 GW (MISO: ~1.2 GW total LEAP load); hundreds of millions in transmission upgrades; plan to supply up to 25 MGD from White River watershed; FERC (June 2026) preliminarily found MISO lacks protections against shifting large-load transmission costs.
fights.status: Announced Feb. 2026; federal review requested Sept. 2026

fights.issue: Amazon campus 2,400 MW growing to 2,800 MW on NIPSCO; 909 backup diesel generators; NIPSCO contract lets Amazon cut demand to 1,200 MW by 2029; wetland loss; county council candidates calling for moratorium.

City-County Council voted 23-1 (Aug. 10, 2026) to bar new data center construction through 2027 (per aigridwatch/datacenterbans search results; not independently opened); Sabey proposal; People's Hearing Feb. 24, 2026.

Cost shifting: Duke (Cause 45647 TDSIC-5) $216M Meta upgrades; I&M (46301) $400M+ for Google/Amazon; NIPSCO/I&M plan 5.6 GW gas by 2030; DOE emergency orders keeping CenterPoint/NIPSCO coal plants running.

2026 session: HB 1210 (data centers pay 1% of electric-bill savings for tax break) advanced; HB 1333 (bypass local zoning) died; HB 1245 (IURC study of data center rate impacts) never got a hearing; LEAP water bills failed.
Mass NIPSCO outages (Aug. 2026); Rep. Mrvan requesting FERC investigation of NiSource.

members_on_record.name: Victoria Spartz
members_on_record.position: Letter to Energy Sec. Wright and Interior Sec. Burgum requesting an independent federal review of LEAP and other Indiana data center projects (Google, Amazon, Meta): energy/water needs, infrastructure costs, who pays, blackout risk. Says she has raised these concerns for two years.
members_on_record.quote: We cannot retire firm generation, add massive new loads, spend hundreds of millions on infrastructure, and then leave Hoosiers guessing who will pay for it. We must ensure Hoosiers are not left paying higher utility bills while facing increased risks of blackouts. Hoosiers deserve substantiated answers before these commitments are made.

members_on_record.name: Victoria Spartz
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) including the state/local AI-law moratorium (opponent J.D. Ford cites this); Yea on GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: André Carson
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 9442 AI Data Center Moratorium Act (Sanders/Ocasio-Cortez); announced support for a federal moratorium in April 2026 amid primary challenges.
members_on_record.quote: Data centers cannot come at a cost to American families, who are already facing high grocery, gas, and housing costs. Data centers have the potential to create good union jobs, but they also have the potential to eliminate jobs. We need to make sure workers, families, and neighborhoods aren't forced to pay the burden of this rapidly rising technology without guardrails. Our bill would enact a pause until we can guarantee common sense protections.

members_on_record.name: André Carson
members_on_record.position: Co-introduced H.R. 8488 AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act (180-day public disclosure, outreach, NDA limits) with McIver and Foushee.
members_on_record.quote: Data centers are often shrouded in mystery, with plans moving forward before meaningful public input. Our bill will change that, requiring data centers to be transparent. Neighborhoods have to deal with the consequences of data centers – and so neighborhood input should be central, not an afterthought.

members_on_record.name: André Carson
members_on_record.position: Statement to E&E News backing a federal moratorium and cost/environmental disclosure bills, after challengers accused him of silence (AES Indiana donations).

members_on_record.name: André Carson
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Landsman's H.R. 6529 (Apr. 14, 2026), Menendez's H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act (Apr. 14, 2026), Tlaib's H.R. 9939 (Aug. 3, 2026), Subramanyam's H.R. 10321 (Sept. 8, 2026), and original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Frank Mrvan
members_on_record.position: Drafting request for FERC investigation of NiSource/NIPSCO after mass outages; original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act and H.R. 8568 Lowering Utility Bills Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: We'll use every leverage that we have on the federal side to make sure that we are looking into and investigating what went right, what went wrong and what needs to be improved upon.

members_on_record.name: Mark Messmer
members_on_record.position: Helped pass Indiana's 2019 data center tax break as a state legislator; now tells Courier & Press he supports federal legislation mandating data centers pay full infrastructure-upgrade costs to protect ratepayers, and AI-disclosure rules for ads (paraphrase; no 2026 verbatim quote). Voted Yea on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: The tax structure changes in this bill will put Indiana in the top five in the country on data center tax policy. This bill could be the biggest economic development bill in this session.

members_on_record.name: Rudy Yakym
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 1047 GRID Power Act (May 15, 2025); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act. Amazon's $15B northern Indiana expansion is in his district; no data-center statement located.

members_on_record.name: Jefferson Shreve
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Barrett's H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (Sept. 1, 2026), Fedorchak's H.R. 6633 High-Capacity Grid Act (Jan. 20, 2026) and H.R. 3843 Baseload Reliability Protection Act (June 23, 2025); voted Yea on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Erin Houchin
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 3843 Baseload Reliability Protection Act (Oct. 8, 2025); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act. Indiana Daily Student reported IN-9 candidates discussed data centers (Apr. 15, 2026; page not retrievable).

members_on_record.name: Marlin Stutzman
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Jim Baird
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Todd Young
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of S. 465 GRID Power Act (Hoeven; Feb. 6, 2025; ENR subcommittee hearing Apr. 15, 2026); advocated the administration's permitting reform for data center construction as a bipartisan near-term opportunity (Nextgov, Jan. 28, 2026); voted Yea to strip the state-AI moratorium (99-1).

members_on_record.name: Todd Young
members_on_record.position: Opposed S.J.Res. 60 (CRA to reinstate limits on Indiana power plants), framing it as raising Hoosier energy costs; not data-center-specific.
members_on_record.quote: Hoosiers should not pay more because government insists on regulating yesterday's grid instead of today's realities.

members_on_record.name: Jim Banks
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1, July 1, 2025); co-led AI DATA Act (workforce data) and a Schiff-Banks AI distillation antitrust bill (July 2026). No data-center statement located.

states.summary: Illinois (ComEd territory in PJM) is ground zero for the capacity-price shock: PJM's Independent Market Monitor attributed the 2025 capacity price spike entirely to data center demand; CUB says consumers are paying 40-50% more than two years ago; ComEd has spent $3B+ since 2021 connecting large loads (data centers covered ~25% via deposits); NRDC projects up to $70/month increases by 2028. Illinois ranks 4th with 262 operating/planned data centers. Gov. Pritzker paused new data center tax incentives and joined five governors' letter to PJM; the POWER Act (interconnection costs, bring-your-own capacity/clean energy) is pending. Local fights: Yorkville 'Project Cardinal' 1,000-acre campus, Granite City/Troy (Metro East), McLean County guidelines, Lockport. Federal delegation is active: Durbin's S. 4213 disclosure bill, Underwood's House companion H.R. 9825, Casten's Energy Bills Relief Act (161 cosponsors), Mary Miller's farmland bill H.R. 10169, Sorensen's build-your-own-power stance, and Durbin/Duckworth cosponsoring Van Hollen's Power for the People Act.

fights.issue: PJM capacity price spike (IMM: caused entirely by data center demand); bills 40-50% higher than two years ago; ComEd $3B+ interconnection spend since 2021; June 2025 and June 2026 rate jumps.
POWER Act would make data centers cover interconnection costs, supply capacity or cut peak use, and provide new clean energy; Pritzker paused tax incentives and proposed consumer protections.
Developer interest prompted Sen. Duckworth's Feb. 6, 2026 meeting with mayors; mayor wants jobs but fears 'sky-high' rates; state Rep. Stuart calls for statewide rules.
City gave final approval to 1,000-acre 'Project Cardinal' campus (March 2026; per WSPY headline, not opened).
County proposing stricter data center guidelines while waiting for state; Rep. Sorensen laid out conditions (no rate increases, own renewable power, gray water, industrial siting).

members_on_record.name: Dick Durbin
members_on_record.position: Introduced S. 4213, Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act (report energy/water use to states; 5-year projections; EPA/DOE/USDA regional reports; fines). 0 cosponsors per govinfo. House companion H.R. 9825 by Rep. Underwood.
members_on_record.quote: If you've noticed a sharp increase in your utility bills lately, it may be from the growth of energy-hungry data centers. Illinoisans deserve an honest analysis of the electricity and water needs of these data centers as they crop up around the country.

members_on_record.name: Dick Durbin
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Van Hollen's Power for the People Act (data center load queues, own power, pay for transmission upgrades) per DCD and LoudounNow; voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).

members_on_record.name: Tammy Duckworth
members_on_record.position: Says data centers should not raise utility or water bills, should use wastewater, bring their own generators/co-locate with nuclear; calls Illinois' approach 'thoughtful.'
members_on_record.quote: Data centers shouldn't be able to raise utility prices and water bills, and should be using wastewater, not fresh drinking water.

members_on_record.name: Tammy Duckworth
members_on_record.position: Convened Madison County mayors/legislators on data centers eyeing Granite City and Troy.
members_on_record.quote: I would love to have one down here for the jobs that are created, but we just need to make sure that what they're consuming isn't going to hurt the local population.

members_on_record.name: Tammy Duckworth
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Van Hollen's Power for the People Act (Jan. 2026); voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).

members_on_record.name: Sean Casten
members_on_record.position: Lead sponsor (with Rep. Mike Levin) of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (161 cosponsors, all Democrats, incl. 32 from the 12 states), which would ensure facilities like data centers pay their own costs; also sponsor of grid bills H.R. 603, 6176, 6177 and cosponsor of H.R. 9945. Voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Lauren Underwood
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 9825, Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act of 2026 (House companion to Durbin's S. 4213); original cosponsor of H.R. 7977; voted Nay on H.R. 1. Yorkville 'Project Cardinal' is in her district.

members_on_record.name: Eric Sorensen
members_on_record.position: Three conditions for Illinois data centers: no utility-cost increases for residents, generate own renewable power and use gray water, site in industrial corridors; helped introduce Energy Bills Relief Act but says 'guard rails' needed.
members_on_record.quote: We're going to have to make sure that there's guard rails in place

members_on_record.name: Eric Sorensen
members_on_record.position: Data centers that would raise bills should build their own solar, wind and nuclear; supports more nuclear reactors.
members_on_record.quote: As a coal power plant gets taken off, we've got to make sure that that energy source is replaced with something else.

members_on_record.name: Mary Miller
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 10169 to prohibit federal financial benefits for constructing, expanding or rehabilitating data centers on prime farmland; cosponsor of Fedorchak's Baseload Reliability Protection Act (Sept. 18, 2025); voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025); did not vote on GRID Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Robin Kelly
members_on_record.position: Says Illinoisans statewide are complaining about utility bills and Congress should look at data centers; original cosponsor of Energy Bills Relief Act.
members_on_record.quote: A lot of people in Illinois from all over the state are complaining, so we definitely do need to look at that because people do feel like their utility bills have gone up and they need to be responsible neighbors.

members_on_record.name: Bill Foster
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Energy Bills Relief Act (Apr. 27, 2026); working with Rep. Lieu and Leader Jeffries on a House select committee on AI; voted Nay on H.R. 1; voted Yea on Latta's Electric Supply Chain Act.
members_on_record.quote: Leader Jeffries understands that we can't repeat Republicans' mistake of letting Congress sit on the sidelines while AI rapidly shapes our future.

members_on_record.name: Mike Quigley
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Landsman's H.R. 6529 (Dec. 10, 2025), McIver's H.R. 8488 Site Selection Transparency Act (May 21, 2026), Subramanyam's H.R. 10321 Responsible Data Center Siting Act (original, Sept. 8, 2026), and H.R. 7977; voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Jesús "Chuy" García
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 9442 AI Data Center Moratorium Act (June 24, 2026), H.R. 8568 Lowering Utility Bills Act and H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Delia Ramirez
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of Tlaib's H.R. 9939 No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act (July 23, 2026) and H.R. 7977; skeptical of AI ('move fast and break things is not acceptable'); voted Nay on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: This whole move fast and break things is not acceptable innovation strategy when we know that the things that end up being broken are not just a computer, a laptop, a cell phone. It's people's lives, their rights and their privacy.

members_on_record.name: Raja Krishnamoorthi
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; Senate candidate (lost March primary); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Jan Schakowsky
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Brad Schneider
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1; Yea on Electric Supply Chain Act.

members_on_record.name: Nikki Budzinski
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Jonathan Jackson
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (Apr. 22, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Danny Davis
members_on_record.position: Voted Nay on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Electric Supply Chain Act and Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Darin LaHood
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act; discussed data centers in a May 11, 2026 Central Illinois Proud interview (page blocked; content not verified).

members_on_record.name: Mike Bost
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Electric Supply Chain Act and Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement located.

states.summary: Wisconsin has ~$46B of proposed or under-construction data centers: Microsoft's Fairwater in Mount Pleasant (Racine County; $7B+ growing toward $20B; first building online June 2026; 400 MW Phase 1 rising toward 900 MW, ~16% of We Energies capacity; neighbors suing over noise), the $15B Vantage/OpenAI/Oracle 'Lighthouse' Stargate campus in Port Washington (1.3 GW; 672 acres; ATC $1.4B transmission line; a protester arrested), Meta's $850M Beaver Dam site, an $8B Janesville proposal, $1B Cassville/Grant County, and a $1.6B Menomonie project halted by ordinance (Jan. 2026). The PSC approved We Energies' large-load tariff (data centers pay 100% of dedicated infrastructure) and then had to override Microsoft contract terms (Aug. 2026); We Energies wants a $1.8B Kenosha County gas plant (Red Oak Ridge). The Legislature debated SB 729/AB 722 (very-large-customer class, 70% renewables), AB 840/SB 843 (passed Assembly 53-44) and SB 969 (NDA ban) but ended the 2025-26 session without passing any data center bill; the LFB says the sales-tax exemption forgoes $2B+. Data centers now define the governor's race (Rep. Tiffany vs. David Crowley) and the WI-3 race (Van Orden).

fights.issue: Microsoft Fairwater AI campus on former Foxconn land; Phase 1 400 MW (~7.5% of We Energies capacity) rising toward 900 MW; 2.8M gal/yr Lake Michigan water; PSC rate plan requires data centers to pay 100% of dedicated infrastructure; Microsoft's 15-year contract contained geographic generation limits PSC had rejected; noise lawsuit by neighbors (July 2026).

$15B Vantage 'Lighthouse' Stargate campus for OpenAI/Oracle (1.3 GW, 902 MW of IT capacity, 4 buildings, 672 acres); ATC $1.4B transmission line; residents object to water, energy, property values; only Midwest Stargate site besides Michigan.
We Energies seeks PSC approval to buy the Red Oak Ridge Energy Center natural gas plant for $1.8B, with Microsoft as anchor buyer.

Menomonie $1.6B project halted by city ordinance over secrecy (Jan. 2026); at least four communities signed NDAs (Beaver Dam Meta $850M, 150 MW via Alliant); Janesville $8B hyperscale at former GM site; Cassville $1B.

SB 729/AB 722 (Democrats: very-large-customer class, biennial rate cases, 70% renewable), AB 840/SB 843 (Republicans: on-site renewables, water recycling, bonds; passed Assembly 53-44), SB 969 (NDA ban); session ended without passing any; LFB: $2B+ sales tax exemption cost for Beaver Dam, Port Washington, Mount Pleasant.
Transmission line town hall (Aug. 2026) with Rep. Van Orden and state Sen. Pfaff; Van Orden proposes siting data centers on Fort McCoy/military bases instead of farmland.
Rep. Tiffany brands opponent 'Data Center David Crowley,' pledges to end all data center subsidies and protect farmland; Crowley wants 100% renewable requirement and no cost pass-through.

members_on_record.name: Tammy Baldwin
members_on_record.position: Wants constituents' questions answered before projects proceed; developers must commit that communities won't shoulder energy/water costs; says any moratorium is for the state Legislature to consider first. Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: I want my constituents to get their questions answered before these projects move ahead

members_on_record.name: Tammy Baldwin
members_on_record.position: Ratepayer protection commitments from developers.
members_on_record.quote: The developers of these need to have commitments to the local community that they won't see, that they won't have to shoulder the costs of the energy use and water use by these data centers

members_on_record.name: Ron Johnson
members_on_record.position: Calls grid impact a 'very serious concern,' doubts local officials have 'really factored it in properly'; treats energy/water demands as local issues. Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: I'd be concerned about that, as well

members_on_record.name: Derrick Van Orden
members_on_record.position: Data centers should self-power or pay for rising utility rates; cosponsored H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (July 20, 2026); 'non-negotiables' for Wisconsin development (Sept. 9, 2026); wants data centers on military bases (worked with Department of War on RFPs), closed-loop cooling, no farmland, no rate increases.
members_on_record.quote: The average Wisconsinite should not have to subsidize the power or water for a commercial entity

members_on_record.name: Derrick Van Orden
members_on_record.position: Campaign stop in West Salem laying out conditions.
members_on_record.quote: I support putting these on military bases and the requests for proposals that we worked with the Department of War to do so have all of those conditions in them. So I do not want a data center sitting in that cornfield. I do not want a data center that doesn't have a closed loop cooling system. I do not want a data center where it can bother people with the noise. And if any company is going to increase the electric rates, I will not stand for it.

members_on_record.name: Derrick Van Orden
members_on_record.position: At transmission-line town hall: increase baseload (nuclear, coal, gas) rather than long-distance lines; condemned eminent domain for a single corporation; proposed Fort McCoy siting.
members_on_record.quote: No increase in your rates. The ratepayer protection is written in that.

members_on_record.name: Derrick Van Orden
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor, H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act; voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025).

members_on_record.name: Tom Tiffany
members_on_record.position: GOP gubernatorial nominee; opposes statewide moratorium but would end all data center subsidies (incl. 2023-25 sales tax exemption), ban NDAs, require data centers to bring own energy per Ratepayer Protection Pledge, protect farmland; attacks Crowley as 'Data Center David.'
members_on_record.quote: We should end all subsidies for data centers. These are some of the wealthiest companies in the world, and the people of Wisconsin should not be subsidizing them.

members_on_record.name: Tom Tiffany
members_on_record.position: Ratepayer protection framing (Jan. 2026).
members_on_record.quote: Existing ratepayers and commercial users should not have their rates go up as a result of someone that's coming in using massive amounts of electricity

members_on_record.name: Tom Tiffany
members_on_record.position: Claims Crowley's renewable plan for Mount Pleasant and Port Washington would need ~100,000 acres; 'Protect Our Farmland Tour.'
members_on_record.quote: David Crowley's plan to make Wisconsin a data center hub for the 'entire globe' comes with a price, and Wisconsin farmers and taxpayers would be left paying it

members_on_record.name: Tom Tiffany
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) with state/local AI moratorium (Crowley attacks this as the 'Big Ugly Bill'); Yea on GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Bryan Steil
members_on_record.position: Attended Microsoft's Washington announcement of a plan shifting energy, water and infrastructure costs onto the company rather than homeowners; said it could set a national standard (WTMJ interview; paraphrase, no verbatim quote captured). Voted Yea on H.R. 1; did not respond to Wisconsin Watch in Dec. 2025.

members_on_record.name: Mark Pocan
members_on_record.position: Data centers should pay all related infrastructure costs; Congress needs AI regulation; original cosponsor of Tlaib's H.R. 9939 (July 23, 2026) and H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: The focus should be more on if they're going to build something, they should have to pay for all the infrastructure costs related to it. That means power lines, that means a lot of other infrastructure.

members_on_record.name: Mark Pocan
members_on_record.position: Dec. 2025 comment on Foxconn's AI pivot.
members_on_record.quote: All the more reason Congress should get its act together because we need to do the proper regulation that's good on all fronts related to AI

members_on_record.name: Glenn Grothman
members_on_record.position: Represents Port Washington; declined comment to Wisconsin Watch (Dec. 2025) and 'hedged' when asked whether residents should bear data center energy costs (Jan. 2026). Voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Tony Wied
members_on_record.position: Declined comment on data centers (Dec. 2025); cosponsored Barrett's H.R. 10119 Protecting Local Control of Data Centers Act (Sept. 2, 2026); voted Yea on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Gwen Moore
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act (Menendez) as of Sept. 8, 2026; voted Nay on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Scott Fitzgerald
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act and Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

states.summary: Minnesota's boom is 'on shaky ground' (Reformer): Google's Hermantown ('Project Loon') campus with Minnesota Power's 67-mile Grand Rapids-Hermantown line, Google's 482-acre 'Project Skyway' in Pine Island (halted by court TRO), Meta's Rosemount campus (city then imposed a moratorium), Farmington, Faribault (court-ordered review), North Mankato (moratorium hearing), Monticello, and Nobles County's 3-2 rejection of Geronimo's 400 MW project (Apr. 21, 2026). A 2025 law made large data centers cover full service costs (PUC 'very large customer' definition, Xcel proposes 100 MW); 2026 bills for NDA bans, water permits and a two-year moratorium failed after industry/union lobbying. Polls: 63% oppose data centers in their community (Star Tribune/KARE); DFL delegates backed a moratorium 64%. Most proposals sit in GOP districts (Finstad, Stauber, Emmer). Emmer echoes Trump's 'backwards and poor' pro-build line; Finstad and Klobuchar (running for governor) stress local control; Craig wants federal regulation; Stauber and Fischbach declined comment.

fights.issue: Google hyperscale campus (code name 'Project Loon'), 67-mile Minnesota Power transmission line from Grand Rapids (part of MISO's $21.8B tranche); NDAs signed by officials; three anti-data-center council candidates; internal city recordings mocking opponents.

Google/Ryan Cos. 482-acre 'Project Skyway'; construction halted by court TRO pending environmental lawsuit; Google charm offensive (Cheese Festival sponsorship, school funding); protest joined by MN-1 Democratic challenger.
County board rejected 3-2 (Apr. 21, 2026) zoning for Geronimo Power's 400 MW data center despite no-NDA transparency approach.

fights.place: Rosemount / Farmington / Faribault / North Mankato / Monticello
fights.issue: Meta Rosemount built then city moratorium; Farmington opposition uniting left and right; Faribault paused by court order; North Mankato moratorium hearing; Monticello packed hearings; candidate filings up in all six data-center cities.

2025 law: large data centers must pay full service costs and comport with carbon-free standard; PUC setting 'very large customer' threshold (Xcel: 100 MW); 2026 NDA ban, water permit and 2-year moratorium (McEwen) bills failed.

members_on_record.name: Tom Emmer
members_on_record.position: House Majority Whip; embraced Trump's Truth Social post that communities rejecting data centers will be 'backwards and poor'; told Fox Business (Aug. 28, 2026) Congress getting in the way of data centers slows innovation and competition with China. Monticello proposal is in his district. Voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.
members_on_record.quote: President Trump is absolutely spot on. Communist China and our adversaries would love it if the United States was asleep at the wheel and stopped innovating and developing AI and emerging tech. Thanks to President Trump's work, the USA will be a digital LEADER!

members_on_record.name: Brad Finstad
members_on_record.position: Local control; companies must be fully transparent; cosponsored H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Aug. 31, 2026). Pine Island, Faribault, North Mankato are in his district.
members_on_record.quote: Data centers, like those proposed in southern Minnesota, can play an important role in our economic future and national security, but the decision about whether a data center is right for a particular community should be made by the people and local leaders who know their communities best, not handed down by Washington through a blanket, one-size-fits-all approach that treats every community the same

members_on_record.name: Brad Finstad
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor, H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act; voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025).

members_on_record.name: Pete Stauber
members_on_record.position: Hermantown Google project is in his district; office did not respond to MinnPost request for comment (Sept. 2026); challenger Trina Swanson campaigning on NDAs and energy costs. Voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Michelle Fischbach
members_on_record.position: Office did not respond to MinnPost request for comment on data centers (Sept. 2026); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.

members_on_record.name: Angie Craig
members_on_record.position: Senate candidate (lost Aug. 11 primary to Flanagan); wants federal regulation of data centers and an aggressive AI approach; original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act and cosponsor of H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act (Apr. 14, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: I think we have to take an aggressive approach to regulating AI. ... We have to consider a kill switch. And the other side of this is just the data centers. I think we actually have to federally regulate (them). No big tech company gets out of not funding the electricity cost and the water quality and water supply in this country is another concern of mine.

members_on_record.name: Kelly Morrison
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (Mar. 18, 2026); cosponsor of H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act (July 20, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Betty McCollum
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; cosponsor of H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (Apr. 15, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Ilhan Omar
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; cosponsor of H.R. 7858 Data Center Community Impact Act (Mar. 26, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Amy Klobuchar
members_on_record.position: DFL nominee for governor; says data centers raise rates and hurt the environment, backs local control, the 2025 state law, bans on NDAs; would require projects to cover 100% of energy and grid costs; did not directly answer Reformer on local moratoria. Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: (Data centers) Cause people's rates to go up, they have hurt the environment, and that just can't keep happening. So my answer to this is number one, local control. Allowing the locals to make decisions, one data center isn't the same as another one.

members_on_record.name: Amy Klobuchar
members_on_record.position: Statewide candidate survey.
members_on_record.quote: As governor, my focus will be on making sure that Minnesotans — not Big Tech — have the final say on data centers, and that involves strong state standards and local control. If Minnesotans don't want a data center in their community, I don't want it there either.

members_on_record.name: Tina Smith
members_on_record.position: Retiring; cosponsor of Van Hollen's Power for the People Act (data center load queues, own power, pay for transmission upgrades); voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1). No Minnesota-specific data center statement located.

states.summary: Iowa is a long-time data center state (Microsoft West Des Moines, Google Council Bluffs, Meta Altoona) now facing a hyperscale wave: QTS's $10B Cedar Rapids campus (toured by Energy Sec. Wright with Rep. Hinson, Apr. 24, 2026) and proposed Clinton site (city council rejected a moratorium June 2026; residents seek steep restrictions), Google's $7B expansion, MidAmerican and Alliant peaker plants (Marshalltown, Cedar Rapids, Clear Lake, Adams County) with utilities promising Big Tech pays 100%. Multiple Iowa communities have passed moratoria (KGAN); data centers surfaced in the IA-3 race (Altoona water use). Iowa's Republican delegation mostly says 'local decision' (Hinson, Miller-Meeks) while having voted for the H.R. 1 state-AI-law moratorium; Grassley told a Sioux City Q&A nothing is happening in Congress on siting.

fights.issue: QTS $10B Cedar Rapids campus (Alliant); proposed Clinton hyperscale site where council rejected a moratorium (June 2026) and residents requested steep restrictions (July 2026); Alliant accused by an Iowa group of hiding true cost of data center power.
fights.status: Cedar Rapids under construction; Clinton pending

fights.issue: MidAmerican and Alliant building gas peakers (Marshalltown approved; Cedar Rapids, Clear Lake, Adams County proposed) to serve data center load; utilities say tech companies pay 100% of their costs.
fights.status: Ongoing (from search results; not independently opened)

fights.issue: Water consumption concerns about Altoona data center raised by voters in the hotly contested 3rd District (Nunn).
Multiple Iowa communities have passed AI data center moratoria (per KGAN, Aug. 2026).

members_on_record.name: Chuck Grassley
members_on_record.position: Discussed positives and negatives of data centers and possible legislation at a June 30, 2026 Chesterman Company Q&A in Sioux City; per the Journal's headline, said nothing is going on in Congress to address data center locations (article body paywalled; no verbatim quote captured). Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).

members_on_record.name: Joni Ernst
members_on_record.position: Retiring; voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1); no data-center statement located.

members_on_record.name: Ashley Hinson
members_on_record.position: GOP Senate nominee; says data center decisions are best made locally; appeared with Energy Sec. Wright at QTS Cedar Rapids (Apr. 24, 2026). CAP notes she voted for H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025) containing the state/local AI moratorium.
members_on_record.quote: I continue to hear from my constituents that they're also concerned about data centers and what I have said is I believe that these decisions are best decided at the local level.

members_on_record.name: Ashley Hinson
members_on_record.position: KGAN Connect to Congress interview on Iowa's data center boom and local moratoria.
members_on_record.quote: these decisions are best decided at the local level

members_on_record.name: Mariannette Miller-Meeks
members_on_record.position: E&C member; voted three times in May 2025 markup to keep the state/local AI moratorium (incl. against Pallone amendment, 29-24) and Yea on H.R. 1; cosponsor of Balderson's H.R. 3616 Reliable Power Act (July 10, 2025); told Iowa's News Now constituents' concerns are legitimate.
members_on_record.quote: People are rightly concerned about water usage and electricity rates going up.

members_on_record.name: Zach Nunn
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; Altoona data center water concerns are a live issue in his district (NBC, Sept. 6, 2026); no statement located.

members_on_record.name: Randy Feenstra
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; lost June 2026 GOP gubernatorial primary; no data-center statement located.

states.summary: Missouri's fight runs from the I-70 corridor west of St. Louis (Google's $15B, 934-acre New Florence campus and Amazon's $10B site in Montgomery County's 5,000-acre 'Heart of America' megasite, with a 25-year, 70% property tax abatement and an 85%-opposed county survey) to Kansas City (at least eight hyperscale campuses incl. Nebius' 800 MW Independence site, Meta KC) and Festus ($6B project; voters ousted every incumbent council member). SB 4 (2025) forced Ameren/Evergy/Liberty to create large-load rate classes; the PSC approved Evergy's (Nov. 2025) with Ameren close behind; Ameren has 2.2 GW of data center contracts; St. Charles County passed a six-month moratorium (July 2026); 16 lawmakers asked for a special session; nine utilities incl. Ameren/Evergy asked FERC for transmission right-of-first-refusal. Sen. Hawley is the delegation's leading critic (S. 3852 GRID Act with Blumenthal; Ameren letter; Warren-Hawley EIA letter; Free Press op-ed) while Rep. Burlison is the loudest booster (calls opposition disinformation, blames China/solar-wind). Rep. Alford wants a pause; Rep. Jason Smith welcomed Ameren's data center investments; Rep. Onder cosponsors nearly every GOP grid bill.

fights.issue: Google $15B 934-acre campus and Amazon $10B data center in 5,000-acre 'Heart of America' megasite; 25-year 70% personal property tax abatement; Missouri Rural Crisis Center survey: ~85% opposed; farmers losing rented land; at least five data centers proposed along a 30-mile I-70 stretch.

fights.place: Kansas City metro (Independence, Smithville, KCK, Osawatomie)
fights.issue: At least eight hyperscale campuses; Nebius Independence ~800 MW; Evergy's Nov. 2025 large-load plan (up to 20% premium, 17-year exit penalties); Evergy adding 5 GW+ generation through 2032.
fights.project: Evergy large-load tariff / KC hyperscale wave

fights.issue: $6B AI data center approved by council after packed meeting; voters ousted every incumbent up for reelection (per Hawley op-ed).

2025 law (SB 4) requiring large-load rate schedules; PSC approved Evergy's (75 MW threshold) Nov. 2025 with Ameren next; 2026 bills to extend to munis/co-ops and water permits died; 16 lawmakers requested a special session; Amendment 5 fight over 2015 data center sales-tax exemptions; House committee hearing Sept. 16, 2026.
County council unanimously passed a six-month moratorium on data centers (July 2026).

Ameren has 2.2 GW of large-load contracts and plans 50% generation growth; Hawley letter demanded records on rate hikes, shut-offs and data center deals; Missouri Times reports fake anti-data-center Facebook pages.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Introduced S. 3852, Guaranteeing Rate Insulation from Data Centers (GRID) Act with Sen. Blumenthal: no consumer price increases due to data centers, consumers get grid priority, new data centers must use off-grid generation (10-year off-ramp for existing), public disclosure of usage. Cosponsored by Sen. Marshall (Aug. 7, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country. This is unacceptable. I am introducing legislation that will protect American citizens by requiring data centers to use energy from sources that are separate from the U.S. grid and publicly report their electricity usage.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Skeptical of data centers' economic benefit; opposed to ratepayer subsidies (interview after Rep. Jason Smith and Gov. Kehoe welcomed Ameren's data center plans).
members_on_record.quote: I don't want Missouri ratepayers to be paying to foot the bill for data centers. If data centers are going to come into the state, fine. If they're going to create jobs? Hey, wonderful. But if they're going to suck up a bunch of electricity, they need to pay for that.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Sent letter to Ameren CEO Martin Lyons demanding communications on rate increases, disconnections, data center expansion and cost allocation; rebuffed Missouri Senate President Pro Tem O'Laughlin's criticism.
members_on_record.quote: told me to stop asking questions about data centers and higher electricity rates. Not a chance.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Says tech companies can afford their own power; wants Trump's ratepayer pledge written into law.
members_on_record.quote: These people are making outrageous sums of money. I mean they're just making trillions of dollars. They can absolutely afford to pay for their own electricity, and they should.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Wants the Ratepayer Protection Pledge codified.
members_on_record.quote: I think we ought to say in the law that the data centers have to pay for their own electricity, the data centers have to pay for their own water supply.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Bipartisan letter with Sen. Warren to EIA Administrator Tristan Abbey demanding mandatory annual energy-use reporting by data centers and other large loads (response requested by Apr. 9, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: Comprehensive information regarding the operations of data centers and other large loads is essential for accurate grid planning and will support policymaking to prevent large companies from increasing electricity costs for American families

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Free Press op-ed citing Festus; demands binding legal requirements that data centers supply own power, protect residential rates and local water.
members_on_record.quote: The companies building these facilities can afford to supply their own power, protect residential rates, and safeguard local water. We must hold them to that with binding legal requirements, not hollow promises.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Asked whether Congress has momentum to act on data centers.
