members_on_record.quote: Only with voters.

members_on_record.name: Josh Hawley
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1); called data centers 'massive electricity hogs' (E&E, Oct. 2025).
members_on_record.quote: I'm concerned about what data centers are doing — even in my state — to costs

members_on_record.name: Eric Schmitt
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1, July 1, 2025); no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Eric Burlison
members_on_record.position: Strong data center booster; frames opposition as disinformation from solar/wind interests or foreign actors; says data centers pay for infrastructure and reduce peak load. Sponsor of H.R. 3751 Reliable Grid Act (June 5, 2025). Voted Yea on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: The only thing that I can I can think of is that if you are in the solar or wind industry, or if you're really a foreign actor, that's the only group that makes sense for them to demonize data centers, because the truth is, this is a national security issue of critical importance. I cannot stress this enough, you do not want your data being housed in China

members_on_record.name: Eric Burlison
members_on_record.position: Says water concerns are overblown and warns of Chinese influence on opposition.
members_on_record.quote: From what I understand, most of them use less water than a car wash

members_on_record.name: Eric Burlison
members_on_record.position: Social media post blaming China for anti-data-center sentiment.
members_on_record.quote: China absolutely wants you to hate them. They know the future runs on AI and data centers, and they want the edge.

members_on_record.name: Eric Burlison
members_on_record.position: After a subcommittee roundtable on AI and China, said communities should judge data centers on measurable impacts, not AI fears.
members_on_record.quote: Whether it's a data center or any other business, I think we should approach them all the same way

members_on_record.name: Mark Alford
members_on_record.position: Supports pausing data center expansion pending facts (KSHB voter guide); voted Yea on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: This is a serious issue that deserves serious research and serious attention to facts over emotion. Until we determine those facts, we think it wise to pause the expansion on data centers as we listen and learn together for the betterment of Missouri.

members_on_record.name: Jason Smith
members_on_record.position: Ways and Means chair; welcomed Ameren's data center investments on Facebook while calling for oversight of taxpayer-funded projects; voted Yea on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: while there should be oversight into any massive project that is funded by taxpayers, Ameren's desire to invest in data centers in Missouri would be a win for the 8th District and the hardworking people that live here.

members_on_record.name: Robert Onder
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (July 13, 2026), H.R. 1047 GRID Power Act (July 22, 2025), H.R. 3616 Reliable Power Act, H.R. 7257 SECURE Grid Act (Apr. 22, 2026), H.R. 3843 Baseload Reliability Protection Act (Oct. 8, 2025), H.R. 9339 Affordable Innovation for the Grid Act (June 23, 2026); authored RealClearEnergy op-ed 'Why Missouri's 3rd District Should Lead America's Data Center Revolution' (Oct. 7, 2025; page blocked). Voted Yea on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Emanuel Cleaver
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; voted Nay on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; KC-area data centers in/near his (redrawn) district.

members_on_record.name: Wesley Bell
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act; sponsor of H.R. 7197 Home Energy Relief Act (Jan. 22, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Ann Wagner
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

members_on_record.name: Sam Graves
members_on_record.position: Retiring; voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement located.

states.summary: Kansas's data center wave (De Soto's third campus by Digital Realty, Meta and others on the Kansas side of KC, Compass Datacenters in Topeka, proposals in Wichita and small towns) has triggered what Sen. Marshall calls constituents 'on fire': 'several dozen counties' have adopted moratoria (Marshall), Topeka's council debated one (July 14, 2026), and the governor's race turned on it (state Sen. Holscher won the Democratic nomination on a statewide-moratorium pledge, costing her a union endorsement). Evergy's large-load tariff (up to 20% premium, exit penalties) was approved in Missouri and discussed in Kansas; residents blame Evergy rate hikes (~$8/month) on data center plans; Panasonic's De Soto plant is cited for rate pressure. Marshall opposes tax incentives and backs county moratoria; Davids sets a 'no rate increase' standard; Moran, Mann, Estes and Schmidt have said little.

fights.issue: Digital Realty's third data center for the suburb (1,000 construction jobs, 250 permanent); residents divided; Panasonic plant cited for higher electricity rates nearby.
fights.status: Proposed (page not opened; from search results)

fights.issue: 'Several dozen counties' have placed moratoriums on data centers (Marshall, July 2026); Topeka City Council debated a moratorium July 14, 2026; Compass Datacenters open house July 28.

Evergy large-load rate (hyperscalers pay up to 20% more, cover all grid upgrades, 17-year exit penalties); residents tie ~$8/month hikes to Evergy's 20 data center projects; Evergy adding 5 GW+ by 2032.
State Sen. Cindy Holscher (D) won nomination backing a statewide moratorium; SMART-TD union endorsed Republican Ty Masterson over her because of it; Gov. Kelly says guardrails already exist.

members_on_record.name: Roger Marshall
members_on_record.position: Says constituents are 'on fire' against AI data centers; supports county moratoriums (not statewide bans); opposes tax incentives; cites Panasonic-area rate increases; cosponsored Hawley's S. 3852 GRID Act (Aug. 7, 2026), Hoeven's S. 465 GRID Power Act (Feb. 26, 2025) and Rick Scott's S.Con.Res. 30 endorsing the Ratepayer Protection Pledge (original, Mar. 25, 2026).
members_on_record.quote: Several dozen counties have placed moratoriums [on data centers]. I certainly support their moratoriums.

members_on_record.name: Roger Marshall
members_on_record.position: KSHB voter guide statement.
members_on_record.quote: Kansas isn't going to hand over our land, water, or power grid to Big Tech companies that turn a profit while local families foot the bill with taxpayer giveaways. I support the counties in Kansas who are standing up and saying NO to data centers.

members_on_record.name: Roger Marshall
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of S. 3852 GRID Act (Hawley-Blumenthal); voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1). His July 22, 2026 press release 'AI Will Not Replace Us—It Will Assist Us' could not be retrieved (senate.gov blocked; not archived).

members_on_record.name: Jerry Moran
members_on_record.position: Original cosponsor of S. 3499 Electric Supply Chain Act (Cortez Masto; Dec. 16, 2025; grid equipment supply); voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1). No data-center statement located.

members_on_record.name: Sharice Davids
members_on_record.position: Standard: no data center should proceed if it raises electricity costs, wastes water or shifts burdens; cosponsor of H.R. 6984 Data Center Transparency Act (May 12, 2026) and H.R. 7977 Energy Bills Relief Act (June 23, 2026); voted Nay on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: Data center decisions are primarily made at the state and local level, but the standard should be clear: no data center should move forward if it raises electricity costs for families, wastes our limited water resources, or shifts the burden onto Kansas communities.

members_on_record.name: Tracey Mann
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of Balderson's H.R. 1047 GRID Power Act and H.R. 3616 Reliable Power Act (July 10, 2025); did not respond to KSHB data center voter guide; voted Yea on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Derek Schmidt
members_on_record.position: Gave Topeka Capital-Journal 'three tips' for Kansas towns weighing data centers (June 10, 2026; page blocked, content not verified); did not respond to KSHB voter guide; voted Yea on H.R. 1.

members_on_record.name: Ron Estes
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; no data-center statement or cosponsorship located.

states.summary: Nebraska's public-power model is being reshaped by data centers: Google (Papillion, Omaha, Lincoln) and Meta (Papillion) load kept OPPD's North Omaha coal units running; Google's 2023 Lincoln data center buys 423 MW of wind; EPRI projects data centers could exceed 20% of state electricity by 2030. The biggest fight is a leaked proposal for a Google data center needing 1,000-3,000 MW from a privately built Tenaska natural gas plant with carbon capture, enabled by Gov. Pillen's LB 1261 (private generation for a single large customer), with Tenaska optioning 2,600+ acres in southeast Nebraska and donating to Pillen. Otoe County enacted a temporary ban (May 2026), Madison County added special-permit requirements, Gage County scheduled a moratorium hearing, and Nebraska City residents posted 'Stop the Data Center' signs. Sen. Ricketts (facing Dan Osborn) frames data centers as national security but insists on local control, negotiated rate and water protections; Rep. Flood cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act; Fischer, Bacon and Smith have little on record.

fights.issue: Leaked OPPD-meeting documents show Google/Tenaska/Tallgrass proposal for a 1,000-3,000 MW data center powered by a private gas plant with carbon capture, online as early as 2029, dependent on LB 1261; Tenaska optioned 2,600+ acres and gave Pillen $65,000 in 2025.
County board banned new data centers for up to a year (May 2026); Madison County added special-permit oversight; Gage County planning commission scheduled moratorium hearing (June 2026).
Google and Meta load growth kept North Omaha coal units from retiring; OPPD receiving more data center power requests.
LB 1261 (Governor's bill) to allow privately built 1,000 MW+ generation dedicated to a large industrial customer with grid interconnection and excess sales; endorsed by OPPD, NPPD, LES.

members_on_record.name: Pete Ricketts
members_on_record.position: Frames AI data centers as national security (July 2026) but says local control is 'the name of the game'; communities should negotiate rate and water protections and property-tax benefits before approving.
members_on_record.quote: When it comes to data centers, local control is the name of the game. If communities are considering a data center, what they should do is negotiate first. They are in charge. They're in the driver's seat. They should make sure, 'yes, you shouldn't impact my power rates. You should conserve water – closed-loop systems.' But then they can ask for more [in property taxes]

members_on_record.name: Pete Ricketts
members_on_record.position: Broken Bow campaign stop: communities should set water and rate protections and seek property tax relief and school/road investments before approving; flagged transformer supply constraints.
members_on_record.quote: Communities are in the driver's seat. They should decide, before they allow the data center to come in, what they want to be able to get from that data center.

members_on_record.name: Pete Ricketts
members_on_record.position: Classified AI data centers as a matter of national security (Panhandle News Channel Nebraska, July 8, 2026; page opened but body not extractable); voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).

members_on_record.name: Deb Fischer
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea to strip the state/local AI-law moratorium from H.R. 1 (99-1, July 1, 2025); Senate Commerce examined AI's impact on network infrastructure (July 2026); no data-center statement located.

members_on_record.name: Mike Flood
members_on_record.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act (Sept. 10, 2026); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; Lincoln Google data centers in district; July 28, 2026 town hall coverage contains no data center remarks.

members_on_record.name: Don Bacon
members_on_record.position: Retiring; pro-data-center remarks at a Lincoln Google data center announcement (quoted in a Jan. 24, 2025 Nebraska Examiner commentary by Brett Lindstrom); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.
members_on_record.quote: The importance of innovation in national security and AI between the public and private sectors cannot be understated, and we're working on that right here in Nebraska.

members_on_record.name: Adrian Smith
members_on_record.position: Voted Yea on H.R. 1 (May 22, 2025), GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act; sponsor of hydro bill H.R. 2160; no data-center statement located.

states.summary: North Dakota is courting AI data centers with cheap power, cold climate and a large-load rate structure (Rep. Fedorchak says it saved customers $30M+), but local fights are emerging. Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale; repurposed from crypto to CoreWeave/AI) and Polaris Forge 2 ($3B, 280 MW, Harwood/Cass County, leased to Oracle, financed with a $2.15B bond in March 2026) spurred an annexation battle and power-upgrade fights near Fargo; the company eyes Oliver County for a third campus; Geronimo Power is scouting Cass County; Mapleton held a public forum (Sept. 2026); Grand Forks got a modular data center at GrandSKY; southwest ND weighed ratepayer burdens. Columnists dispute 'hysteria' vs. 'propaganda.' The all-Republican delegation is pro-build but focused on cost causation and state authority: Fedorchak (E&C) backs the Ratepayer Protection Act and local decision-making and sponsors grid bills (H.R. 6633 High-Capacity Grid Act reported 49-0; FAIR Act; Baseload Reliability Protection Act); Cramer is wary of FERC's large-load interconnection push; Hoeven sponsors the GRID Power Act.

fights.issue: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 2: $3B, 900 acres, 280 MW, liquid-cooled, leased to Oracle, $2.15B bond (Mar. 2026); power via Cass County Electric Cooperative; annexation battle (ENR); developer backing power upgrades near Fargo.
fights.status: Under construction; ops 2026-27 (pages blocked; from search results)

fights.issue: Polaris Forge 1 converted from crypto hosting to AI/HPC under CoreWeave deal.
Applied Digital eyeing Oliver County for third campus (July 2026); Mapleton public forum on impacts (Sept. 9, 2026); Geronimo Power exploring Cass County project (Sept. 10, 2026).

North Dakota large-load rate structure requires data centers to cover costs they impose (Fedorchak: $30M+ saved); delegation guards state PSC autonomy against DOE/FERC large-load interconnection proposal (Oct. 2025).

members_on_record.name: Julie Fedorchak
members_on_record.position: E&C member; voted for H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act in 52-0 committee vote; cites North Dakota's large-load cost-causation model.
members_on_record.quote: No American should pay higher utility bills because of the infrastructure needed to serve new, large electricity users like data centers. Republicans and Democrats are united in this belief and support the commonsense principle: those who cause costs on the system must pay for those costs—not hardworking families, seniors on fixed incomes, or small businesses.

members_on_record.name: Julie Fedorchak
members_on_record.position: Local decision-making on siting; companies must be transparent on noise, roads and energy.
members_on_record.quote: The decision-making should be local because the local people are best able to ferret out what is right and what is wrong for their community. They need to make the decisions in a thoughtful manner based on the facts. Not based on what people think or read on the internet, but based on the facts of each and every project.

members_on_record.name: Julie Fedorchak
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of H.R. 6633 High-Capacity Grid Act (E&C 49-0, July 21, 2026), H.R. 6336 Fair Allocation of Interstate Rates Act (Dec. 1, 2025), H.R. 3843 Baseload Reliability Protection Act (June 9, 2025), H.Res. 290; created an AI-power working group (Feb. 13, 2025); original cosponsor of Balderson's Reliable Power Act and cosponsor of GRID Power Act.
members_on_record.quote: America's electricity demand is growing at the fastest pace in decades. To meet this demand, we must optimize our existing transmission infrastructure.

members_on_record.name: Julie Fedorchak
members_on_record.position: Axios Live: data center customers should pay for the energy they need.
members_on_record.quote: The people who need the energy need to pay for the energy, and they're willing to do it

members_on_record.name: Julie Fedorchak
members_on_record.position: Welcomed DOE's large-load interconnection proposal to FERC while defending state authority; voted Yea on H.R. 1.
members_on_record.quote: While I'm still evaluating the details of this proposal, I fully support testing new approaches to large-load interconnection. This is an entirely new challenge, and our existing regulatory system is not equipped with the tools to handle it.

members_on_record.name: Kevin Cramer
members_on_record.position: Former PSC member; 'uncertain' about Energy Sec. Wright's push for FERC jurisdiction over large-load (data center) interconnection; wants states to retain planning authority and an appeal pathway. Sponsor of S. 3287 Fair Allocation of Interstate Rates Act (Dec. 1, 2025). Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: We have to strike a balance that doesn't completely dismiss a state's rights or, you know, reduce the importance of or diminish the importance of a planning process.

members_on_record.name: John Hoeven
members_on_record.position: Sponsor of S. 465 GRID Power Act (Feb. 6, 2025; prioritize dispatchable generation in interconnection queues; cosponsors Young, Marshall, Moreno; ENR subcommittee hearing Apr. 15, 2026); original cosponsor of Cramer's S. 3287 FAIR Act; delegation 'steadfast in preserving the state's planning autonomy' (E&E). Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1). No direct data center quote located.

states.summary: South Dakota rejected data center incentives and instead enacted restrictions: SB 239 (equipment write-offs) failed 16-17 twice (Feb. 2026), and on March 25, 2026 the governor signed laws requiring 10 MW+ data centers to prove water use won't overburden local supplies, to pay attributable electric infrastructure costs, letting the PUC bill review costs, and barring the state from overriding local ordinances. Sioux Falls rezoned 164 acres for Gemini Capital's first hyperscale campus (7-0, Jan. 2026, after a five-hour hearing), Lincoln County commissioners rejected a moratorium and NDA ban 3-2 (Aug. 25, 2026), a Leola project and Rapid City backlash (Meta cash, EPA rules) are in the news, and 19 legislative candidates signed a Data Center Accountability Pledge. Majority Leader Thune broke with Trump's 'backwards and poor' line (data centers must be self-sufficient and welcomed locally); Rounds says the long-term answer is data centers in space and that projects must be welcomed locally; Rep. Dusty Johnson (running for governor) has a 'Data Centers Done Right' plan with four tests.

fights.issue: Council rezoned 164 acres (Six Mile Rd./Veterans Pkwy.) 7-0 for Gemini Capital hyperscale campus (~50,000 homes' worth of power) after five-hour hearing; Lincoln County commission later rejected a data center moratorium and NDA ban 3-2 (Aug. 25, 2026); joint meeting set for October.

SB 239 incentive (equipment write-off) failed 16-17 on Feb. 23 and 24, 2026 (Sen. Carley absent); governor signed restrictions March 25, 2026 (water, infrastructure cost responsibility, PUC fees, local ordinance protection).
Rapid City backlash over EPA rules, Meta money and a proposed project; Leola data center in news (SDPB, Sept. 9, 2026).

19 legislative candidates signed the Data Center Accountability Pledge (D-CAP); independent Senate candidate Brian Bengs attacks Rounds over AI/data center donations ($80,000+ more than all SD donors combined, per Bengs).

members_on_record.name: John Thune
members_on_record.position: Senate Majority Leader; distanced himself from Trump's 'backwards and poor' remark: data centers must be self-sufficient on power and go only where locally supported (to a South Dakota TV station, Aug. 31/Sept. 1, 2026). Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: These entities need to be self-sufficient. They ought to be able to take care of their own utilities, their own power, and that ought to be a given any place they go in the country. But they shouldn't be going places where there isn't support for them at the local level.

members_on_record.name: Mike Rounds
members_on_record.position: Says data centers must go only where actively welcomed today and that long-term most new data centers will be in space; opponent Bengs attacks his AI/data center donations. Co-sponsored Schiff-Rounds AI literacy bill (Apr. 2026). Voted Yea to strip state-AI moratorium (99-1).
members_on_record.quote: Long-term, I believe that the vast majority of new data centers will probably be based in space. And the reason for that is that they have an immediate—permanent supply of solar power available to them. And when you put them in space, the cooling systems aren't nearly as tough to do.

members_on_record.name: Dusty Johnson
members_on_record.position: GOP gubernatorial candidate; 'Data Centers Done Right' plan with four tests (rates, water, taxes, jobs); says state has a role filtering proposals; cosponsor of Fedorchak's H.R. 3843 Baseload Reliability Protection Act (Oct. 8, 2025); voted Yea on H.R. 1, GRID Power Act, Reliable Power Act.
members_on_record.quote: We're not going to welcome data centers to our state unless they can prove four things. 1, Not going to hurt our electric rates, 2, not going to hurt our water, 3, they're going to pay millions and millions of dollars in taxes to reduce the burden on the rest of us, and 4, they're going to create good jobs

midwest.coverage_notes: METHOD AND LIMITS. WebSearch budget was exhausted early (shared session cap), so discovery ran through Google News RSS (decoded via news.google.com batchexecute), Wayback CDX/id_ snapshots, the GovTrack v2 API, govinfo BILLSTATUS XML (sponsors, cosponsors with state, actions, committee vote tallies) and GovTrack roll-call CSV exports. Every quote in members_on_record was copied from a page I opened (press release, article text, bill XML, vote roster); where a page could not be opened the quote is null and the position says so. Dates are press-release/article dates unless a specific action date is given; 'null' dates mean the source did not give one (e.g., Tlaib's X post, Emmer's X post, Kaptur's late-2025 floor speech). Fight-level facts marked 'from search results' or 'not independently opened' came from search-result summaries and should be re-verified before publication (Indianapolis 23-1 moratorium vote Aug 10 2026; Yorkville Project Cardinal approval; MidAmerican/Alliant peakers; OPPD coal; several ND project details; De Soto Digital Realty). PJM capacity numbers ($329.17/MW-day for 2026-27; $16.1B) come from Ohio Capital Journal Dec 2025 search summary and CUB (opened). BLOCKED SOURCES (Cloudflare/Akamai/paywall; also blocked in Wayback): all senate.gov sites directly (worked only via Wayback: Hawley GRID Act, Hawley Oct 17 2025 and Jun 9 2026 releases, Husted Jul 20 and Mar 4 2026 releases, Moreno Mar 17 and Feb 27 2026 releases, Durbin Mar 25 2026, Warren-Hawley Mar 26 2026, Young Sept 2025; Marshall Jul 22 2026 release and Hawley Ameren letter page were not archived); cleveland.com (5 relevant stories incl. Latta FBI briefing and 'Ohioans are mad at data centers' naming Carey/Miller), Politico (6), Detroit News (James Aug 1 story; two others opened via Googlebot UA), NYT Kansas primary, WaPo (GOP-turned story opened but only Husted 2024 quote extracted), KELOLAND (Thune and Dusty Johnson Q&A), KFOR (Dusty Johnson), Central Illinois Proud (LaHood), Lima News (opened via Wayback), Daily Advocate (opened via Wayback), WTHR (Carson, Spartz), IndyStar Carson story, News-Leader Burlison op-ed, RealClearEnergy Onder op-ed, Topeka Capital-Journal Schmidt piece, WTOL Husted rally, Missouri Independent Jul 22 FERC ROFR story, MinnPost (429 on WebFetch; opened via curl), Star Tribune (429), Michigan Democrats' James page. VOTES: Senate roll call 363 (Jul 1 2025, Blackburn Amdt. 2814 striking the state/local AI-law moratorium, 99-1): all 24 senators from the 12 states voted Yea. House roll call 145 (May 22 2025, H.R. 1 with the moratorium, Sec. 43201): every Republican from the 12 states voted Yea except Warren Davidson (OH-8, Nay); every Democrat Nay. House roll 279 (H.R. 1047 GRID Power Act, Sep 18 2025, 216-206): party-line among the 12 states, Mary Miller and Mike Turner not voting. House roll 347 (H.R. 3616 Reliable Power Act, Dec 17 2025, 225-203): party-line. House roll 324 (H.R. 3638 Electric Supply Chain Act, Dec 11 2025, 267-159): Democrats Foster, Schneider, Quigley, Casten, Mrvan, Stevens, Scholten, McDonald Rivet, Davids, Sykes and Kaptur voted Yea. H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act was reported 52-0 by E&C on Jul 21 2026 and placed on the Union Calendar Sep 10 2026; Politico Pro (Sep 10) and USA Today (Sep 11) report a House floor vote is scheduled but none had occurred as of GovTrack/govinfo on Sep 12 2026. COSPONSOR ROSTERS from govinfo are current as of Sep 11-12 2026 update dates. NOT FOUND / GAPS: no data-center statements located for Sens. Peters, Slotkin (AI only), Schmitt, Ernst, Fischer, Moran (grid supply chain cosponsorship only), Banks (AI bills only), Hoeven (bills only); House: McClain, Bergman, Turner, Joyce, Carey, Max Miller, Stutzman, Baird, Fitzgerald, Estes, Wagner, Graves, Adrian Smith, Danny Davis, Bost, Nunn, Feenstra (votes only). Grassley's June 30 2026 Sioux City remarks are paywalled (headline only). The 'Hawley says he was asked to sign data center letter, declined' headline (Jul 15 2026) is NY Assemblyman Steve Hawley, not Sen. Josh Hawley, and was excluded. Van Hollen's Power for the People Act (Senate) bill number was not confirmed via GovTrack/govinfo; Midwest cosponsors (Durbin, Duckworth, Smith) are per DCD (Jan 27 2026) and LoudounNow (Jun 9 2026). Stevens' Defending Our Energy and Water Act, Tlaib's 'Make DTE Pay Act', and Carson's Tonko/Van Hollen companion status were not confirmed with bill numbers. Kaptur's H.R. 9700 concerns utility corruption refunds (FirstEnergy), not data centers specifically; included because it targets electric bills. Bacon's quote is second-hand via a Nebraska Examiner commentary that attributes it to him at a Lincoln data center announcement. Emmer's X post text is as reproduced by MinnPost (Sep 3 2026), which links to the post.

states.summary: Phoenix metro has the largest data center concentration outside Northern Virginia (176 sites per Data Center Map) and the issue dominates the 2026 governor's race between Gov. Hobbs and Rep. Andy Biggs. Fights: Tucson's Project Blue (city council rejected it Aug 2025, Amazon Web Services pulled out Dec 2, 2025, but ACC approved TEP's power deal Dec 4, 2025, Pima County approved Dec 16, 2025, Marana rezoned Jan 2026, construction began Apr 2026, Tucson adopted data center rules Aug 2026); Chandler unanimously rejected a $2.5B Sinema-backed data center Dec 2025; Maricopa County approved Project Baccara near Luke AFB 4-1 in May 2026 over protests; Hobbs signed a three-year pause on the 2013 data center tax exemption in the June 2026 budget (through 2029) and pledges permanent repeal; AG Kris Mayes called for a statewide data center moratorium Aug 31, 2026; APS is seeking a ~14% rate increase and TEP a 13% hike partly to cover $1.7B of data-center-linked infrastructure; Arizona led the nation in electricity consumption growth in March 2026 (+19.4% y/y); Noble Predictive Insights found 57% of voters oppose new large data centers. Both senators are on record: Kelly is drafting a community-benefits bill and Gallego calls data centers a 'necessary evil' while backing an end to their tax breaks.

fights.issue: Water, secrecy (NDAs), TEP power deal; Tucson council rejection overridden by county/Marana approvals; ACC approved TEP electric service agreement Dec 4, 2025
fights.status: Under construction since April 2026; Tucson adopted data center regulations Aug 2026; AG Mayes sought new ACC hearing Jan 2026

fights.status: Paused until 2029 (signed June 15, 2026); Hobbs pledges permanent end

fights.issue: Water use and electricity demand
fights.status: Mayes called for statewide pause Aug 31, 2026; Biggs/Kerr ticket opposes an outright moratorium

members_on_record.name: Mark Kelly
members_on_record.position: Pro-buildout with community guardrails; previewed legislation to force developers into early, enforceable community-benefit agreements (local hiring, paying for infrastructure, keeping rates low); cosponsored S. 4506 Advancing Water Reuse Act (07/15/2026); voted Yea on 99-1 vote to strip state AI-law moratorium (07/01/2025)
members_on_record.quote: Communities across the country have been left out of the AI boom. Giant companies are proposing planning and building large infrastructure projects without local input.Decisions get made. Plans get drawn up. And then communities are told what's coming with no real answers about how it's going to impact their utility bills or quality of life.That's just wrong. And it's not going to work.

members_on_record.name: Mark Kelly
members_on_record.position: Warned local data center rejections (Chandler, Tucson) threaten US-China AI race; says AI buildout must not raise locals' electricity bills
members_on_record.quote: If we see that become a trend across the country, it's going to be hard to win against China in this race to develop intelligent models where we can reap some significant benefits in scientific discovery and cures for diseases and material science and chemistry

members_on_record.name: Ruben Gallego
members_on_record.position: Calls data centers a 'necessary evil'; supports ending Arizona's data center tax exemption; says residents must be held harmless on electricity bills and developers should bring their own power; released 'Fostering American Energy Innovation and Affordability' plan (12/03/2025); Risch-Gallego nuclear bill (Feb 2026)
members_on_record.quote: Your local resident should be held harmless. We shouldn't be paying more in electricity bills because data centers are here

members_on_record.name: Ruben Gallego
members_on_record.position: Fears water and generation shortfalls from data center volume; called some Valley data centers 'abusive'
members_on_record.quote: The amount (of data centers) that are coming in is a problem to me. I fear that we may not have enough water and we may not have enough power generation to be able to hold harmless everyone else.

members_on_record.name: Andy Biggs
members_on_record.position: GOP nominee for governor; in June 17, 2026 debate agreed with Hobbs' three-year moratorium on data center tax breaks, said taxpayers will not pay for data center infrastructure and he would force data centers to produce their own power; running mate Sine Kerr rejects an outright moratorium; voted Yea on H.R. 1 (Roll Call 145, 05/22/2025) and Yea on SPEED Act (Roll Call 356, 12/18/2025)

members_on_record.quote: If I can, I would.

states.summary: Project Jupiter, the $165B Oracle/OpenAI data center campus in Doña Ana County (Santa Teresa) approved in 2025, is the state's defining fight: NDAs and shell companies, a $50M water-infrastructure pledge, arrests at a rowdy July 28, 2026 county meeting, the Pueblo of Acoma forcing a developer rename, the State Land Commissioner blocking a related pipeline on state land (July 16, 2026), and the NM Supreme Court halting water use from a Project Jupiter well and pausing permitting (Aug 24-25, 2026) while site work continued. State lawmakers are planning a moratorium. Socorro County adopted a yearlong moratorium (June 9, 2026) after Rep. Vasquez urged it. Sen. Heinrich, ENR ranking member, has made data center cost-allocation a signature issue (GRID Savings Act) while rejecting moratoriums; Reps. Stansbury and Vasquez have escalated on water transparency.

members_on_record.quote: If a company is driving the need for expensive new facilities, that company should pay for it — not families and small businesses. That's the basic principle behind my GRID Savings Act

members_on_record.name: Martin Heinrich
members_on_record.position: Opposes data center moratoriums; says water will be a giant issue and hyperscalers must not push costs onto consumers (POLITICO Energy podcast)
members_on_record.quote: I'm not a fan of the moratorium approach because it will simply push them to the places with the lowest standards, and we don't want to race to the bottom

members_on_record.name: Martin Heinrich
members_on_record.position: Says data center developers should learn from SunZia by front-loading community engagement
members_on_record.quote: I worry that the data center developers are not doing that well. There's a healthy dose of arrogance in some of these budget proposals rather than starting from a position of humility and really trying to partner with local communities.

members_on_record.name: Martin Heinrich
members_on_record.position: Chaired questioning at ENR grid hearing on meeting data center demand without offloading costs (03/26/2026); introduced Grid Connection and Congestion Management Act / 'Grid for Growth' (07/18/2026); pressed FERC at 07/22/2026 oversight hearing

members_on_record.name: Ben Ray Luján
members_on_record.position: Introduced S. 4506 Advancing Water Reuse Act with Sen. Britt (05/13/2026): 30% investment tax credit for onsite water recycling incl. at data center facilities
members_on_record.quote: As demand for freshwater continues to grow, we need smart and forward-looking solutions to protect our vital resources and strengthen long-term water security.

members_on_record.name: Gabe Vasquez
members_on_record.position: Represents Project Jupiter's district; cosponsored H.R. 9655 FAIR Data Act and H.R. 9825 Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act (08/13/2026; announced 08/25/2026); condemned security guard's use of force at July county meeting; voted Nay on SPEED Act
members_on_record.quote: New Mexico's water, air and resources belong to us, not to billionaires from coastal states who see an opportunity to extract profit from our land. I've been appalled at the backroom deals, silencing of dissenting voices, shady NDAs and shell companies, and the overall lack of transparency from those who seek to do business in our state.

members_on_record.name: Gabe Vasquez
members_on_record.position: Called on Socorro County to adopt a data center moratorium against the Green Data proposal
members_on_record.quote: offers limited transparency and a lack of clear answers

members_on_record.name: Melanie Stansbury
members_on_record.position: Sent letter to NM AG Torrez, State Engineer, Environment Secretary and others demanding Project Jupiter water consumption, water rights, permits and Rio Grande Compact analysis by Aug 28, 2026; later called for investigation
members_on_record.quote: The scale of Project Jupiter makes this an important test case for how New Mexico evaluates major industrial water users in a water-scarce future.

members_on_record.quote: Our electricity grid faces ever-growing challenges from increased data center demand to wildfire-caused blackouts. As utilities across the country race to address these challenges, Americans' energy bills only go up

states.summary: Colorado is the home of the House's flagship data center bill: Rep. Gabe Evans (CO-8) sponsors H.R. 9340 Ratepayer Protection Act, which cleared Energy & Commerce 52-0 on July 21, 2026 and is set for a House floor vote the week of Sept 14, 2026; all four CO Republicans (Evans, Boebert, Crank, Hurd) are now sponsors/cosponsors. State-level: Denver City Council passed a unanimous one-year moratorium (May 2026), Xcel proposed a data center rate class to shield customers (Apr 2026) amid a ~33% cumulative rate request, dueling Democratic data center bills stalled in the legislature (Apr 2026), Weld County is courting projects, Elyria-Swansea residents fought a Denver project, and Energy Secretary Wright toured the Ray Nixon coal plant with Evans and Crank (Sept 2026). Data centers scrambled Democratic primaries: DeGette (E&C member) lost to Melat Kiros, Hickenlooper's challenger Julie Gonzales backed a moratorium, and gubernatorial nominee Bennet's platform demands data centers pay their fair share.

members_on_record.name: Gabe Evans

states.summary: Kevin O'Leary's Stratos Project in Box Elder County (originally ~20,000-40,000 acres, 9 GW of on-site gas generation, approved through the Military Installation Development Authority in May 2026 during a drought emergency) triggered viral protests, forced Gov. Cox's data-center framework executive order (May 29, 2026), a 75% scale-back demanded by Senate President Adams, and a lawsuit against O'Leary over 'China' claims. The backlash reshaped GOP primaries (Lisonbee vs. Moore, Lyman vs. Maloy; incumbents won June 23, 2026), while Sen. Curtis called for federal transparency standards and Sen. Mike Lee, who chairs the Senate ENR committee where every major data center bill sits, said the issue was not a priority. Other fights: Eagle Mountain tax fight, Dugway Proving Ground Army data center (CyrusOne), Spanish Fork off-grid campus, water-use reporting law, Operation Gigawatt, and ~$1.3M in AI super PAC spending in Utah primaries.

states.summary: Nevada's flashpoint is the Townsite data center outside Boulder City, the first data center approved on BLM land (June 2026) via an amended solar right-of-way without public review; Rep. Titus's letters to BLM and Gov. Lombardo preceded an Interior Board of Land Appeals stay (Sept 1, 2026) and a judge halting construction. Nye County banned data centers in an over-appropriated basin (Aug 2026) after a moratorium; Henderson chose new rules over a moratorium (July 2026); the state is reviewing its data center tax abatements ($225.6M in sales/use tax breaks FY23-24) with counties 'out of the loop'; gubernatorial candidate Aaron Ford pledged to pause new abatements; an Emerson poll (Sept 10, 2026) found a majority oppose new data centers; teachers' union pushed back on a moratorium. Northern Nevada (TRIC/Storey County: Switch, Google, Microsoft, Tract) continues to build. All three southern Nevada House Democrats answered a Nevada Independent survey; senators have been comparatively quiet.

states.summary: Cheyenne is weighing 40-70 proposed data centers. The Crusoe/Tallgrass 'Project Jade' AI energy campus (1.8 GW data center, 2.7 GW new gas generation) was approved by Laramie County in January 2026 as potentially the largest in the US, though Crusoe exited in June 2026 (reportedly under Google pressure) and Tallgrass continues. Microsoft announced a 3,200-acre expansion (Apr 2026) on land largely owned by Sen. Lummis's family; the City Council approved the ~3,460-acre annexation 7-3 after an eight-hour session (July 13-14, 2026). A Meta ('Project Cosmo') subcontractor's closed-loop cooling discharge put rare bacteria into Cheyenne's wastewater (July 2026), prompting Rep. Hageman's letter to Zuckerberg and a city ban on such discharges; the council rejected a moratorium. Black Hills Energy is planning for the load surge, and developers are eyeing public lands. The delegation is uniformly pro-buildout (Lummis, Barrasso frame it as beating China with Wyoming coal/gas/nuclear) but Lummis authored the first GOP bill for federal large-load interconnection rules and Hageman cosponsored the Ratepayer Protection Act.

members_on_record.quote: Whoever powers the AI revolution will win the AI arms race. As we unleash affordable, reliable, American energy, America will lead the world in AI.

members_on_record.quote: Water is a precious resource in our state, so it is of immense concern to learn the system marketed to reduce a data center's water consumption caused this contamination.

states.summary: Montana's fight centers on Quantica Infrastructure's 'Big Sky Digital Infrastructure', a nearly 8-square-mile campus near Broadview in Yellowstone County: 14,000+ voters signed a ballot initiative requiring voter approval of data centers (failed on a deadline error, may return in spring 2027), residents flooded rowdy county meetings (Aug 2026), opponents sought interim zoning, and Montana Free Press found Quantica executives made matching donations to nine state candidates in 2024 before the 2025 Legislature passed a data center power-plant tax break (HB 424) and the Right to Compute Act. NorthWestern Energy is in talks with 11 developers and its large new load tariff case is before the PSC (Gov. Gianforte intervened, signed the ratepayer protection pledge); its $16B merger with Black Hills touts data center profits; Atlas Power in Butte is being supplied. A Daily Montanan column called the delegation's silence 'deafening'; Daines and Zinke are retiring.

states.summary: Oregon passed the POWER Act (2025) requiring data centers to pay their own cost of service; the PUC approved PGE's 29.7% rate increase for data centers under it (July 7, 2026) while residential rates fall. The Dalles fought 13 months to keep Google's water use secret, then records showed the campus used roughly a third of the city's supply; the city now seeks more Mt. Hood forest water. Amazon paid $20.5M to settle Morrow County nitrate-contamination claims (Mar 31, 2026) and bought 1,300 more acres; petitioners sought an Eastern Oregon pause; Oregon DOJ alleged local officials' data center 'scheme.' Hillsboro faces power constraints; property tax breaks save the industry ~$450M in 2026; Gov. Kotek's Data Center Advisory Committee drafted recommendations and she will back a 2027 bill. Sens. Wyden and Merkley wrote the committee (July 2, 2026); Wyden pressed Google/Apple/Meta/Amazon on water (Apr 30, 2026), cosponsored the AI Environmental Impacts Act and floated an excise tax on AI data centers (Aug 6, 2026); Reps. Salinas and Dexter introduced/cosponsored tax and cost-shift bills; Rep. Bentz (E&C) warns of a power shortfall.

states.summary: California's data center backlash 'exploded' in August 2026: San Jose residents pushed a moratorium, Pittsburg residents protested at City Hall, Tulare County temporarily firewalled data centers, Imperial County weighed a moratorium after Rep. Ruiz opposed projects, Eureka scheduled a moratorium vote, Monterey Park's Measure NDC went to the June ballot, Oakland split over billionaire-backed proposals, and Big Tech spent heavily against state bills; lawmakers reached a late-session deal on data center regulation (Aug 29, 2026) after 2025 efforts (SB 57 ratepayer bill, water disclosure) faltered or were vetoed. The CEC projects data centers' share of peak demand rising from 2% to 9% by 2040 as PG&E rates climb. The Central Valley battleground (Valadao vs. Villegas) and CA-4 (Thompson vs. Jones) feature moratorium calls. Federally, Sen. Schiff's S. 4559 would make data centers bring their own power and pay 100% of grid upgrades; Khanna's Data Center Bill of Rights, Levin's SHIELD Act, Costa's rural AI study bill, Obernolte's measurement-standards bill and the Pentagon-base data center fight (Garamendi, Calvert, Levin) round out an unusually active delegation.

states.summary: Alaska's delegation is pitching the state as an energy-rich data center destination: Sen. Sullivan pressed the Air Force to issue a request for information for AI data centers on Alaska bases (which it did) to build demand for the Alaska LNG pipeline, and Rep. Begich introduced the House DATA Act (H.R. 8400) to let data centers run isolated 'grid-of-one' power systems. On the ground: Stak Energy's $500M gas-powered North Slope data center drew a flood of opposition comments to state land managers (July 2026), the military's plan to lease base land for AI data centers drew community reaction (June 2026), an East Coast firm proposed an underwater data center in Cook Inlet (Aug 2026), Anchorage demonstrators called for a pause (Aug 13, 2026), and a state bill requiring data centers to cover their own grid costs died in committee (May 2026). The Sullivan-Peltola Senate toss-up features data centers only at the margins; Murkowski has not been located on record.

members_on_record.quote: I'll give you an example of something we've been pressing on, and we just made really important progress yesterday on: new federal data centers on Air Force bases in Alaska for AI computing.

members_on_record.name: Nick Begich
members_on_record.position: Introduced H.R. 8400 DATA Act of 2026 (04/21/2026) with Crenshaw and Owens (House companion to Cotton's S. 3585) allowing data centers/manufacturers to run fully isolated off-grid power systems; op-ed urging Alaska to capitalize on the 'AI gold rush'; voted Yea on SPEED Act and H.R. 1
members_on_record.quote: The DATA Act allows manufacturers to operate on fully self-contained, 'grid-of-one' power systems, so innovation can scale without forcing households to subsidize massive new energy demands or straining local utilities. For Alaska, this approach is especially critical.
